evaluations.title: Algorithmic construction baseline
evaluations.author: System
evaluations.abstract: Baseline generated by the system builder from infinite families, allowed conference masks, and executable finite generators. The only finite-source preload is the explicitly marked n=36 exception.

evaluations.title: Verified correlation instrument for triangular-book bicirculants
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Build and verify a reusable exact-computation instrument for the triangular-book Ramsey lower-bound task. The instrument computes exact red/blue common-neighbor caps for arbitrary graphs and for bicirculant candidates, reports worst-case excess and the violating-difference profile, and emits/parses adjacency strings in the official column-major bit order. It is self-tested against bundled finite artifacts to guarantee it matches the official evaluator semantics before any construction screening.

evaluations.title: Generalized Orbit Deconvolution for Bicirculant Graphs (n=40)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Develops a reusable CP-SAT solver to search for bicirculant graphs constrained by multiplicative orbits. Tests on n=40 (v=79) by evaluating different multipliers in Z_79* to collapse the search space.

evaluations.title: Orbit-invariant bicirculant search for missing n
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for two-fiber bicirculant graphs for missing values by constraining the cyclic connection sets (S_U, S_V, S_UV) to be unions of orbits of a multiplicative subgroup H of Z_m^* that contains -1. This heavily reduces the search space.

evaluations.title: Symmetry-Broken Residual Search for n=40 Bicirculant
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Drops the order-3 multiplier symmetry from the n=40 near-miss and searches the localized Hamming neighborhood of the 157 cyclic bicirculant variables using CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Construction atlas and bicirculant slack ledgers
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable atlas for n=22..100 that classifies solved and missing values by nearby algebraic orders, construction eligibility, and finite-source analogy. Extract the bundled finite bicirculant/product source packets into compact red/blue slack ledgers where possible, with CRT/orbit labels for composite groups, to guide the next targeted construction probe.

evaluations.title: Aster chamber-Seidel ledger and missing map
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Build reusable exact validation and analysis tooling for this lineage, then classify the unsolved n values by arithmetic construction opportunities. This is a non-score infrastructure evaluation intended to prevent formula errors and guide later construction searches.

evaluations.title: Composite conference masks for S/K q=57..93
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Search for conference-type base relations on composite q=n-1 values q=57,69,77,85,93, which would feed the bundled S/K four-chamber construction and potentially solve n=58,70,78,86,94. The search should preserve source masks and near-miss ledgers, not only final adjacency strings.

evaluations.title: Z95 orbit bicirculant construction probe for n=48
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n=43 Z85 multiplier-orbit deconvolution grammar extends to the missing composite case n=48 with m=95=5*19. Search compact orbit-compressed two-fiber cyclic bicirculant sources, save the best source packets and slack ledgers, and return a valid n=48 graph if found.

evaluations.title: Hybrid H-invariant A with pure SAT C-completion
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for missing n by fixing A as a union of orbits under a multiplicative subgroup H containing -1, and uses a pure CP-SAT satisfaction model to find an unstructured C in the complementary bicirculant model.

evaluations.title: Paley(4n-3) cap-saturation and one-vertex Seidel-switching extension to 4n-2
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a new parity-free source law: the Paley graph on q=4n-3 vertices has SRG parameters whose edge/non-edge codegrees exactly meet the book caps. Verify this across the range, then attempt to extend by one vertex to the required N=4n-2 vertices via Seidel switching of the order-(4n-2) Paley conference two-graph, targeting currently-missing values n=40 and n=44.

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley sum-kernel: confirm kernel and characterize the q=7 mod 8 overflow
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Confirm the exact skew-Paley sum-kernel used by the baseline (it validates n with q=4n-1 prime power and q=3 mod 8), then apply the identical kernel to q=4n-1 prime with q=7 mod 8 and characterize the exact codegree overflow. Determines whether the 3-mod-8 condition is a small repairable boundary effect or a large structural barrier, guiding whether a twisted sibling kernel is worth pursuing.

evaluations.title: Orbit Deconvolution for Composite n=44 (v=87)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the CP-SAT orbit deconvolution pipeline to n=44, handling a composite ring Z_87. Sweeps multipliers in Z_87* to find configurations with the minimum Ramsey excess.

evaluations.title: Numba-Accelerated Residual Annealing for n=40 and n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the timeout-prone CP-SAT with a fast Numba-accelerated Simulated Annealing search. Seeds the search with the m=23 (n=40) and m=7 (n=44) orbit near-misses, dropping the multiplier symmetry but preserving the 1D cyclic bicirculant structure.

evaluations.title: Z87 product bicirculant construction probe for n=44
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Probe the atlas-ranked top missing value n=44 using a two-fiber bicirculant/product search over m=87=3*29. Reuse the atlas ledger tools, test cyclic and CRT-aware product grammars, and save either a valid source packet or a detailed pressure profile for the best near misses.

evaluations.title: Sum-kernel two-layer screen on prime targets n=40,52,64,76,84,96,100
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Screen additive (sum) quadratic-character kernels on a two-layer vertex set {0,1} x GF(m), m=2n-1 prime, for the seven missing n==0 mod 4 prime targets where no difference-Paley/conference/skew-Paley family applies (m==3 mod 4). The hypothesis (from first-principles derivation): for m==3 mod 4 the difference kernel chi(x-y) is skew and illegal as an undirected relation, but the SUM kernel chi(x+y) is symmetric and may give bounded common-neighbor caps. Goal is to find exact witnesses or, failing that, record the worst-case excess and violating-difference profile to drive Phase 2 repair.

evaluations.title: Skew QR two-fiber search for q=2n-1 primes
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Test a skew-Hadamard inspired two-fiber construction for missing n with q=2n-1 prime and q=3 mod 4. The cross-fiber relation is seeded by quadratic residues, while same-fiber symmetric relations are searched as orbit unions or annealed inverse-pair sets.

evaluations.title: q=85 conference near-miss repair and rule-table probe
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Use the compact exhausted q=85 S/K conference near-miss from Evaluation 8 as a pressure object. Probe whether orbit switching, local relation repair, or modified chamber rule tables can reduce the S/K book excess for n=86, while preserving exact diagnostics and bounded claims.

evaluations.title: Arithmetic reachability map across all source-law linear forms, n=22..100
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Build a definitive arithmetic table mapping each n in 22..100 to the precondition status of every known and candidate source law: skew-Paley (4n-1), two-copy Paley (2n-1), S/K conference (n-1), and the newly identified Paley-conference form (4n-3). Cross-checks against the baseline solved/missing lists to identify exactly which missing values are 'arithmetically open' to each candidate route versus search-only.

evaluations.title: Numba SA repair of orbit near-misses
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Reconstructs the orbit-union near-misses for n=44, 40, 47, 48 from Eval 4 and runs a highly optimized Numba Simulated Annealing search to 'repair' the remaining defects by relaxing the orbit symmetries.

evaluations.title: Composite Orbit Deconvolution for n=47 and n=48
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the composite orbit deconvolution pipeline to n=47 (v=93) and n=48 (v=95) to find the best multiplier-reduced near-misses.

evaluations.title: Skew-cross + sum-layer coupling and exact correction-term analysis (prime targets)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 found a constant near-miss (red_excess=1, blue_excess=2) for sum-kernel two-layer graphs across all seven prime targets n in {40,52,64,76,84,96,100}. The constant offset signals an exact character-sum identity landing O(1) over threshold. This experiment (a) screens the structurally-correct two-copy-Paley analogue for m=2n-1==3 mod 4 — symmetric sum-kernel chi(x+y) within layers, SKEW difference-kernel chi(x-y) on the bipartite cross (legal because cross edges need no symmetry) — across independent sign/shift choices, and (b) computes the EXACT per-edge common-neighbor correction (deviation from the SRG mean) to explain the +1/+2 offset analytically and search for a coupling that flips the correction negative, yielding an

evaluations.title: Degree-sum codegree law for conference two-graphs; guided switching search (skew-Paley q=7 mod 8)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Verify the exact identity that for any graph on m=4n-2 vertices with Seidel matrix S satisfying S^2=(m-1)I, the red edge-codegree equals (deg u+deg v)/2 - n and the blue complement-codegree equals 3n-3-(deg u+deg v)/2, so validity reduces to a degree-sum threshold at 4n-4. Confirm this explains skew-Paley exactly (regular 2n-2 for q=3 mod 8; squares 2n-1 / nonsquares 2n-3 for q=7 mod 8). Then search the Seidel switching class of the q=7 mod 8 skew-Paley graph for a representative meeting the degree-sum threshold, targeting missing n=48,56,60,68,92,96.

evaluations.title: Degree-sum-guided switching search in the Paley conference two-graph (4n-3) for missing n
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the degree-sum threshold criterion (valid book witness iff every edge has degree-sum <= 4n-4 and every non-edge >= 4n-4, exact for any S^2=(m-1)I representative) to the Paley conference two-graph of order m=4n-2 built from q=4n-3 prime power. Search the switching class with a degree-sum-guided objective, targeting currently-missing values eligible for this form: n=40,44,58,59,65,68,70,73.

evaluations.title: Orbit-invariant Bridge Source Law CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for n=44, 40, 47, 48 using the Bridge Source Law (A, B, C, K10) where A and B are restricted to be unions of multiplicative orbits. This reduces the problem to a tiny integer programming instance that CP-SAT can solve instantly if a solution exists.

evaluations.title: Generalized-cyclotomy bicirculant screen for composite-m missing values
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Explore track. For missing n whose modulus m=2n-1 is composite (no finite field), screen bicirculant graphs on Z_m whose generating sets come from generalized cyclotomy of Z_m (Whiteman/Ding-Helleseth for m=p*q, twin-prime Jacobi-symbol sequences when m=p(p+2)). Motivation: the common-neighbor cap is a periodic-autocorrelation bound, i.e. a low-correlation sequence-design problem; the bundled n=39 Z7xZ11 product witness is the special case, and generalized cyclotomy is its named parametric generalization. Goal is exact witnesses or violating-profile diagnostics for these otherwise field-inaccessible values.

evaluations.title: Weak S/K relation inequality extractor and composite-q probe
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Pivot from broad bicirculant residue search to the S/K chamber mechanism. Extract the exact S/K rule table and pair-row inequalities from the baseline builder, then test whether weaker Cayley relation sources over composite q can satisfy the induced book caps, starting with q=57 for missing n=58 and comparing q=77,85,93 if time permits.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT completion of n=40 skew two-fiber near-miss
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: The Eval #17 skew two-fiber probe found an n=40 near-miss with only same-fiber violations and red/blue excess 2. This evaluation turns that near-miss into an exact constrained completion problem over the two-fiber residue sets, prioritizing a valid n=40 witness.

evaluations.title: Skew two-fiber residual law across n=40,52,64
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the best Eval #17 skew two-fiber near-misses for n=40,52,64 as supplementary-difference residual objects. The goal is to expose the exact same-fiber obstruction and test structured repairs that might generalize beyond a single n.

evaluations.title: Tabu-Seeded Residual Search for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Seeds the highly optimized Tenax Tabu C solver with the deep local minimum orbit near-miss for n=44 (m=7), using the Tabu mechanism to forcefully escape the local minimum and repair the remaining 87 violating pairs.

evaluations.title: Compiled residual-repair continuation for n=44 Z87 bicirculant
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the closest current near miss: n=44 over Z87 reached red/blue excess 2 in Eval #15. Run a compiled degree-preserving local search seeded from that near miss, with linearized flip-sensitivity diagnostics and partial symmetry breaking, to test whether the broad pressure profile can be repaired into a valid source.

evaluations.title: Joint n=40 skew two-fiber CP-SAT radius expansion
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: The n=40 skew two-fiber grammar now has a radius-2 C-repaired near-miss with only same-fiber excess 1. This evaluation builds a more expressive joint A/B/C constrained optimizer around that near-miss, aiming to close the final one-count gap or produce a scoped obstruction ledger.

evaluations.title: Bridge bicirculant CP-SAT for low gaps n=40,44,47,48
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Return to the source-native bridge bicirculant residual grammar for the four remaining missing values below 50. Use CP-SAT and CRT/residual ledgers to search for A/B/C source rows rather than raw adjacency strings.

evaluations.title: Warm-started structured search to break the +1/+2 wall (prime targets)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Evals 16/22/26 established a robust obstruction: pure algebraic half-density constructions at these moduli land at exactly red_excess=1, blue_excess=2 (constant across all seven primes AND the Z77 cyclotomy control), while the m==1 mod 4 two-copy Paley control reaches exact 0. The gap is small and structured. This experiment warm-starts a structured local/annealing search from the algebraic near-miss seeds and attempts to close the bounded +1/+2 gap to an exact witness for the prime targets, prioritizing the smallest (n=40,52,64). Success is any exact witness; the scientific payoff is whether a consistent small perturbation of the algebraic seed removes the wall, which would

evaluations.title: Almost-perfect Seidel sequences: cyclic negative-autocorrelation search for regular book witnesses
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: By the master reduction, a regular degree-(2n-2) graph on m=4n-2 vertices is a valid book witness iff all off-diagonal Seidel row-correlations are <= 0. For circulant (Cayley on Z_m) graphs this equals the periodic autocorrelation of a symmetric +/-1 sequence; the unique feasible profile is the almost-perfect one (C(k)=-1 except 0 at the half-shift). Search these sequences for currently-missing n, prioritizing values with no algebraic source.

evaluations.title: Negative Seidel-correlation search over Z_2 x Z_{2n-1} Cayley graphs for regular book witnesses
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Companion to the cyclic almost-perfect-sequence search: apply the same master criterion (regular degree-(2n-2) graph valid iff all off-diagonal Seidel row-correlations <= 0) to Cayley graphs on the non-cyclic abelian group Z_2 x Z_{2n-1} of order 4n-2. This group structure may admit negative-correlation connection sets where the cyclic group does not, targeting currently-missing n.

evaluations.title: Tabu-Seeded Residual Search for n=40
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Seeds the baseline Tenax Tabu C solver with the strict local minimum orbit near-miss for n=40 (m=23), using the Tabu mechanism to escape and repair the remaining violations.

evaluations.title: Z119 product bicirculant probe for n=60
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test the atlas-ranked n=60 case with m=119=7*17, a composite modulus sharing the product-search flavor of the solved n=39 and n=43 finite rows. Run a focused two-fiber bicirculant search with CRT-aware initialization and diagnostics, independent of the ongoing n44 repair.

evaluations.title: Orbit A and arbitrary CP-SAT B for Bridge Source Law
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the Bridge Source Law where A is a union of orbits (fixed to satisfy N_A(d) <= cap(d)) and B is an arbitrary subset of size n-1 found via CP-SAT. This avoids the over-constrained B from Eval 25.

evaluations.title: Near-conference Seidel construction for n==2 mod 4 gaps (focus n=86)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Explore track, orthogonal to the prime n==0 mod 4 work. The five missing n==2 mod 4 values (58,70,78,86,94) are conference-matrix gaps. Reframing the book caps as a near-conference Seidel matrix S=J-I-2A of order 4n-2 with bounded off-diagonal Gram window, this experiment attempts (1) to construct or search a symmetric conference / near-conference structure feeding the S/K conference pipeline, focusing on n=86 where n-1=85=5*17 is a sum of two squares (necessary condition for a symmetric conference matrix of order 86 is met); and (2) to screen symmetric-conference-like Seidel blocks and doubling/Goethals-Seidel array constructions on order 4n-2. Goal: an exact witness for

evaluations.title: Numba SA for Bridge Source Law B
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Given an orbit-invariant A in the Bridge Source Law, uses an ultra-fast Numba Simulated Annealing to find B. SA swapping elements in B is much faster at minimizing the periodic autocorrelation N_B(d) than CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Higher-order sum-kernel cyclotomic probe for n=48
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation-level alternative to bicirculant search for n=48, where q=4n-1=191 is prime but lies outside the skew-Paley q=3 mod 8 condition. Search graph rules on GF(191)^* whose edge color depends on the cyclotomic class of x+y, including zero-sum handling, and report whether higher-order class unions can satisfy the book caps.

evaluations.title: Degree-balanced two-fiber search for n=40
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Prior skew two-fiber attempts for n=40 left a one-count same-fiber obstruction with degree split 77/79. This evaluation changes the degree profile: search two-fiber cyclic graphs on Z79 with regular or near-regular degree 78 by varying the cross-set size, rather than forcing the QR half-set size.

evaluations.title: Seeded bridge completion for n=47 max-excess-one near-miss
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #33 found the closest bridge bicirculant low-gap near-miss at n=47, with max residual excess 1. This evaluation focuses on a seeded exact/local completion around that source row, including product/CRT-aware repairs, aiming for a valid n=47 witness.

evaluations.title: Strong bicirculant Tabu search for n=40 and n=52 (full budget)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: The bicirculant two-fiber model provably reaches n==0 mod 4 (the baseline solved n=24,28,32,34 with it, limited only by compute, not by any obstruction). n=40 (m=79) and n=52 (m=103) are the next rungs and are currently missing only because cold search was not run to completion. This experiment runs a strong, well-engineered simulated-annealing/Tabu search in the bicirculant model V={0,1}xZ_m with symmetric same-fiber sets S_U,S_V and directed cross set S_UV, using the full sandbox time budget, targeting exact witnesses. Any hit is a new solved value and a concrete algebraic object to analyze for a source law.

evaluations.title: Shave-3 analysis: can a modified sum-kernel reach red_max+blue_max=2n-3?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Evals 16/22/34 established that pure sum-kernel constructions at m=2n-1==3 mod 4 land at red_max+blue_max=2n, exactly 3 above the target sum 2n-3 (target is red<=n-2, blue<=n-1). The m==1 mod 4 two-copy Paley control reaches the exact 2n-3. This experiment investigates whether a STRUCTURED modification of the sum-kernel seed can reduce the invariant sum by 3: (a) asymmetric layer densities (move a few residues between the chi=+1/-1 classes to shift the common-neighbor mean), (b) fiber-1 negation reindexing y->-y that converts one layer's sum-kernel into a difference-kernel (making the object partially circulant), and (c) subtracting a sparse regular structure. The objective is red_max+blue_max,

evaluations.title: Joint SA Defected Crystal for Bridge n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'defected crystal' protocol: initializes from the best n=44 Bridge near-miss (energy 4) and runs a Joint Numba SA that can flip symmetric pairs in A alongside elements in B, breaking the strict algebraic symmetry of A to close the final gap.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: A/C Difference Set Search for n=47 (Z_3 x Z_31)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Adapts the baseline's two-phase A/C product group search for n=47 over Z_3 x Z_31. Modifies the Phase 1 C solver to search for a symmetric set A of size 46 and an unrestricted set C of size 46 (including 0) that satisfy the joint autocorrelation constraints.

evaluations.title: Structured switching of the GF(191) sum-kernel near miss
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the closest current lead: the n=48 GF(191)^* parity sum-kernel reached red/blue excess 1. Test compact Seidel-switching and vertex-class corrections of that near miss, including kernels of the form tau(x) tau(y) chi(x+y), small rules over vertex/sum classes, and richer inverse-closed ratio toggles.

evaluations.title: Focused deep bicirculant search for n=40 (single long trajectory, warm start)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Concentrate near-full compute on a single target, n=40 (m=79), to cross the (1,1) wall and obtain the first new solved value. Evidence base: n=34 (m=67, same residue class m==3 mod 4) was solved exactly by one focused ~805s bicirculant Tabu run; my prior n=40 attempt reached exact caps (39,40) = excess (1,1), residual score 4, with the correct set-size subspace |S_U|=40,|S_V|=38,|S_UV|=39 already located, but wasted budget on six short restarts. This run uses a single long steepest+Tabu+kicks trajectory (the proven n=34 recipe) at fixed set sizes, warm-started from the saved residual-4 near-miss, with a two-stage objective that switches to directly

evaluations.title: SRG / regular-two-graph feasibility map for missing n (source-law scout)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Orthogonal explore track with high source-law upside. A k-regular graph on N=4n-2 vertices is an exact book witness iff every edge has <= n-2 common neighbors and every non-edge's complement side has <= n-1. For strongly regular graphs this reduces to lambda <= n-2 and complement lambda-bar <= n-1. This experiment builds a reusable feasibility map: for each missing n, enumerate feasible SRG parameter tuples (N,k,lambda,mu) satisfying the SRG identity and both book caps, and flag which correspond to known or plausibly-constructible SRGs / regular two-graphs (conference graphs, descendants of regular two-graphs, Latin-square or cyclotomic SRGs). Goal: identify any missing

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic-bicirculant source-law search: distribute negative Seidel-correlation budget across fibers
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Exploit the exact regular criterion (a regular degree-(2n-2) graph on m=4n-2 vertices is a valid witness iff all off-diagonal Seidel row-correlations (S^2)_uv <= 0, and these are automatically multiples of 4) in the two-fiber bicirculant model on {0,1}xZ_r, r=2n-1. Search algebraic cyclotomic-class-union recipes for (S_U, S_V, S_UV) rather than blind bit-search, seeking a reusable source law and valid witnesses for currently-missing n with r prime.

evaluations.title: Regularizing repair of skew-Paley q=7 mod 8 sum-kernel via square/non-square degree balancing
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: The skew-Paley sum-kernel on GF(q)*, q=4n-1 prime, q=7 mod 8, is self-complementary but non-regular (squares degree 2n-1, non-squares 2n-3) and misses the book caps by the minimal quantum (+4 in S^2) exactly on same-coset pairs. Attempt to repair it to a valid regular degree-(2n-2) witness by degree-balancing edge modifications between the two multiplicative cosets, guided by the exact regular criterion, targeting missing n=48,56,60,68,92,96.

evaluations.title: Product-coordinate bridge search for n=47 over Z3xZ31
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Expose the CRT product coordinate for the closest bridge low-gap near-miss. Eval #44 improved cyclic n=47 to residual max/total/positive 1/28/28 but did not solve it; this run searches the same bridge residual law on the product group Z3 x Z31 with seeded profile-aware repairs.

evaluations.title: Global C-design CP-SAT for n=40 near-balanced two-fiber
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: The best n=40 two-fiber profile has clean cross rows but same-fiber excess 1. This run fixes or lightly relaxes the A/B sets from Eval #32 and searches the directed cross set C globally, using exact autocorrelation and cross constraints rather than local C swaps.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Asymmetric Two-Phase Cyclic Search for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Splits the cyclic bicirculant search for n=44 into two phases to overcome the chaotic 2^174 landscape. Phase 1 proposes symmetric intra-fiber sets S_U and S_V. Phase 2 fixes them and optimally solves for the directed inter-fiber set S_01.

evaluations.title: Four-chamber cyclotomic fusion search for n=44
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation-level alternative for the stuck n=44 case: use the natural 4(n-1)+2 vertex layout of the S/K construction, but search compact chamber rule tables over cyclotomic relation classes of Z43 instead of forcing an exact conference relation. This probes whether a small association-scheme fusion can satisfy the book caps where two-fiber Z87 repair stalled.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: A/C Difference Set Completion for n=47
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Phase 2 of the A/C difference set template for n=47 over Z_3 x Z_31. Fixes the symmetric set A from Phase 1 and runs an exhaustive C-level local search to find a perfect set C.

evaluations.title: Block-Circulant Adaptive Chamber SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the graph as a k x k block matrix of circulant p x p blocks. Each block is constrained to be a union of multiplicative orbits of a large subgroup of Z_p^*. This reduces the problem to a tiny set of independent boolean variables (orbit selections) that we optimize using a hyper-fast Numba XOR-basis SA.

evaluations.title: GF191 sum-set local search from the n48 parity near miss
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Broaden the strongest n=48 lead without moving to raw adjacency search: keep vertices GF(191)^* and let edge color depend on the exact field sum x+y belonging to a selected source set D, rather than only the cyclotomic class of x+y. Start from the quadratic-residue parity near miss with excess 1/1 and search compact sum-set corrections by toggling whole sum matchings.

evaluations.title: Exact fixed-fiber CP-SAT completion for n=40 (different method vs local search)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Three approaches (short search Eval 45, deep warm-started search Eval 50, structured algebra Eval 46) all stall at the (1,1) wall for n=40, with Eval 50 pinned by a specific d=±8 autocorrelation spike. Root cause: warm-start traps the search in the large (1,1) attractor basin and fixed-size swaps cannot restructure out of it. This experiment switches to a fundamentally different method — exact fixed-fiber completion, the technique that solved the baseline n=39: fix the same-fiber sets S_U,S_V to several structured/searched seeds, then use a CP-SAT/ILP exact solver to complete the directed cross set S_UV satisfying ALL red and blue book

evaluations.title: Exact fixed-fiber completion for small composite-m targets n=44, n=48
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Explore track using the same exact fixed-fiber completion method, applied to the two smallest composite-m missing values, n=44 (m=87=3*29) and n=48 (m=95=5*19). These are the smallest missing values after n=40 and lie in a different arithmetic regime (composite modulus, no finite field), so a hit here is both a new point and evidence that exact completion generalizes beyond prime m. Fix same-fiber sets S_U,S_V to generalized-cyclotomy or CRT-structured seeds on Z_m and solve for the cross set S_UV exactly under all book inequalities.

evaluations.title: q=7 mod 8 sum-kernel rule search
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the skew-Paley sum-kernel family beyond the q=3 mod 8 case by searching small quadratic-character rule tables on GF(q)^* for q=4n-1 prime values with q=7 mod 8. This targets several missing even n values with a compact algebraic source-law hypothesis.

evaluations.title: C++ residual hitting-set repair for bridge n=47
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Use the best bridge n=47 max-excess-one source as a seed for a faster source-native repair search. Combine residual-gradient hitting-set proposals with compiled tabu/annealing over A/B moves to try to close the remaining 28 excess-one rows.

evaluations.title: Massive SA + CP-SAT for Complementary Bicirculant
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Runs a highly optimized Numba SA over the unconstrained complementary bicirculant variables (A, C) for n=44, 40, 47, 48. If it finds a near miss (max excess <= 1), it launches CP-SAT to exactly complete C for the fixed A.

evaluations.title: GF223 parity sum-kernel probe for n=56
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the q=7 mod 8 parity sum-kernel near-miss phenomenon seen at n=48, q=191 also appears at another missing value: n=56 with q=4n-1=223 prime. Evaluate pure and lightly corrected sum-kernel rules on GF(223)^* and compare the obstruction profile to the GF191 case.

evaluations.title: Structured algebraic correction of skew-Paley q=7 mod 8 via multiplicative-subgroup coset edge sets
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: The skew-Paley q=7 mod 8 graph has (S^2)_uv <= 0 everywhere and degree deg(x)=2n-2+chi(x); only degree imbalance blocks validity. Random regularizing matchings inject positive S^2 (Eval #53). Test whether an ALGEBRAICALLY STRUCTURED correction set, built from cosets of a multiplicative subgroup of the squares, can regularize to degree 2n-2 while keeping S^2<=0, yielding a valid regular witness and potentially a q=7 mod 8 family.

evaluations.title: Seeded asymmetric bicirculant search for search-only missing values using the exact (S^2)<=0 regular criterion
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Target the currently-missing values that have NO algebraic source law {47,52,64,67,72,76,81,84,93} using a full asymmetric two-fiber bicirculant search, but guided by the exact regular criterion (valid iff all off-diagonal (S^2)_uv <= 0, values are multiples of 4) and SEEDED from skew-Paley-derived and best cyclotomic-pattern configurations rather than random restarts. A witness for any search-only value is high-value and unobtainable by field families.

evaluations.title: Massive SA for Exact Bridge Source Law
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Runs a massive unconstrained Numba SA over A (symmetric) and B (|B|=n-1) to solve the exact Bridge Source Law 1D residual equation. If a zero-energy state is found, the mathematical properties of the Bridge Source Law guarantee the full graph is valid.

evaluations.title: Exact character-sum certificate for q=7 mod 8 sum-kernel near misses
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Turn the repeated GF191/GF223 parity sum-kernel 1/1 near misses into a precise mechanism. Derive and verify closed-form common-neighbor counts for the graph on GF(q)^* with edge color determined by the quadratic character of x+y, compare q=3 mod 8 valid rows to q=7 mod 8 near misses, and identify the exceptional terms responsible for the one-over obstruction.

evaluations.title: Four-vertex deletion transfer from solved n+1 witnesses
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Test a structural transfer operation: delete four vertices from a valid baseline witness for n+1 to obtain the required vertex count for n. This becomes an exact hitting-set problem over tight red edges and tight blue nonedges in the larger graph.

evaluations.title: Exact CP shell around bridge n=47 1/10 near-miss
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: The compiled hitting-set search improved the bridge n=47 source from 1/28/28 to 1/10/10. This evaluation focuses exact CP-SAT and complete local shell enumeration around the new near-miss to try to remove the final ten one-excess residual rows.

evaluations.title: Single-circulant search on Z_{4n-2} for n=40 (new representation)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Four prior evaluations stalled at the (1,1) wall for n=40 within the {0,1}xZ_79 bicirculant representation; Eval 61 showed fixed fibers cannot be completed past (1,1). This experiment changes representation: since 4n-2 = 2*(2n-1) = 158 = 2*79 (and generally 2*prime for all prime targets), search a SINGLE circulant graph on Z_{4n-2} with one symmetric connection set S=-S. The book caps become a single low-autocorrelation-sequence condition: autocorr_S(d)<=n-2 for d in S and autocorr of the complement <=n-1 for d not in S. This is a genuinely different search space and move grammar than the bicirculant three-set problem, offering a fresh path

evaluations.title: GPU massively-parallel multi-seed bicirculant search for n=40
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Different COMPUTE strategy for the same n=40 target. Prior bicirculant searches used single or few CPU trajectories and stalled at the (1,1) wall, which is a rare-needle problem (one bad red difference class and one bad blue class, 79 pairs each). This experiment runs thousands of independent annealing chains in parallel on the allocated GPU (JAX-vectorized), each maintaining incremental correlation state, to sample the search space far more broadly and increase the chance of hitting the rare (0,0) needle. Success is any exact witness; the deliverable otherwise is the distribution of best-excess across many chains, quantifying how rare crossing states

evaluations.title: Structural mining of known bicirculant book witnesses for a hidden source law
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: The baseline solved n=22,23,24,28,29,32,34 (two-fiber bicirculant Tabu) and n=43 (Z85 orbit) with explicit connection sets. Rather than search for new witnesses, reverse-engineer these KNOWN valid witnesses: test whether their connection sets S_U,S_V,S_UV are unions of cyclotomic classes / cosets, whether a multiplier x->cx symmetry exists, whether a pattern is shared across n, and characterize their exact (S^2) fingerprint. Goal: extract a candidate source law that generates the family, converting finite bitstrings into reusable structure.

evaluations.title: Dihedral (sum-cross-relation) Cayley graphs for book witnesses via the (S^2)<=0 criterion
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Dihedral Cayley graphs on D_{2n-1} (order 4n-2) form a structured bicirculant subclass with S_U=S_V=A symmetric and a cross relation governed by the SUM i+j in C (not the difference), echoing the successful skew-Paley sum-kernel. Search A,C (including cyclotomic-structured choices) under the exact regular criterion (S^2)_uv<=0, targeting currently-missing n, seeking valid witnesses and a reusable algebraic pattern.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Phase 2 A/C Completion for n=47
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Reruns the Phase 2 C-completion for n=47 with a longer time limit to exhaust the 3-swap neighborhood and fixes the critical graph construction rule (Fiber 2 uses complement B, not A).

evaluations.title: Evaluate parity sum-kernel complement/orientation variants for q=7 mod 8
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Before abandoning the q=7 mod 8 sum-kernel line, systematically test the small set of convention variants suggested by the character formula: red on residues vs nonresidues, zero-sum red vs blue, complementing the graph, and simple endpoint/matching deletion or flip variants that preserve the GF(q)^* sum-source grammar as much as possible. Focus on q=191 and q=223.

evaluations.title: End-to-End A/C Difference Set Pipeline for n=47
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a massive restart pipeline for n=47 over Z_3 x Z_31. Runs hundreds of fast Phase 1 A/C searches, and for any strong candidate A (max_excess <= 1), immediately attempts a Phase 2 C-completion. Uses the corrected A/B/C graph construction.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Edge Repair of Near-Miss Graphs
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: The 1D bicirculant grammar is proven to contain no exact solutions for the missing values. We take the closest near-misses from Eval 69 (e.g., n=40 with excess 1/1) and use CP-SAT to repair the full 2D adjacency matrix by flipping up to K edges.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive quadratic endpoint-sum fusion for q=7 mod 8 sum kernels
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Use the character-sum certificate from Eval #70 to test the next compact correction class: edge color depends not only on chi(x+y), but also on the quadratic characters of the two endpoints. Exhaustively enumerate all symmetric rules in (chi(x), chi(y), chi(x+y)) plus zero-sum handling for q=7 mod 8 primes corresponding to missing n.

evaluations.title: Reverse-engineer solved bicirculant witnesses into a cyclotomic source law
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Five search methods stall at the robust (1,1) wall for n=40, yet n=34 (same residue class m==3 mod 4) has a known bicirculant witness, so witnesses exist and search keeps missing the structure. This experiment reverse-engineers the SOLVED bicirculant witnesses (n=22,23,24,28,29,32,34, with sets S_U,S_V,S_UV on Z_m, m=2n-1) to find an algebraic source law: decompose each set into cyclotomic classes of Z_m (orders dividing m-1), coset/multiplier structure, and difference-set patterns, and look for a recipe that generalizes across n. A found recipe would construct n=40 and beyond directly, converting finite witnesses into a parametric family.

evaluations.title: Structural anatomy of the (1,1) wall: is the obstruction a fixed resonance?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Across five independent search methods, the best n=40 bicirculant states stall at excess (1,1) with the violation concentrated at difference d=+-8 mod 79 (only 79 pairs each color), not broadly spread. This experiment characterizes the (1,1) wall structurally: whether the obstructing difference is a fixed arithmetic resonance across independent solutions and across other prime targets, which would indicate a predictable structural barrier and possibly a targeted fix. It analyzes many independent (1,1) states (from the GPU 4096-chain run and prior searches) to see if the bad difference is always the same class, and computes what makes d=+-8 special for m=79.

evaluations.title: Degree-correlation matching analysis of near-regular book witnesses: extract a constructive design principle
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Five of seven known Tenax witnesses are near-regular (degrees 2n-3 and 2n-1) with max off-diagonal (S^2)=+4, validating via the relaxed codegree identity rather than the regular (S^2)<=0 criterion. Analyze exactly HOW they match the sign of each vertex's degree deviation to the local (S^2) structure, to extract a reusable constructive design principle for building near-regular witnesses at missing n.

evaluations.title: Near-regular relaxed-criterion search for missing n: does degree freedom close the gap?
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: All my prior searches enforced exact regularity, discarding the degree-deviation compensation that the actual finite witnesses (Eval #75) exploit. Test whether allowing degrees in {2n-3,2n-2,2n-1} with the exact relaxed codegree objective substantially lowers achievable excess and can reach valid witnesses for tractable missing n, targeting sub-50 {40,44,47,48} and small search-only {52,64}.

evaluations.title: Four-vertex extension from solved n-1 witnesses
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Test the dual transfer operation to four-vertex deletion: add four vertices to a solved witness for n-1 to obtain the correct vertex count for missing n. This is an exact constrained completion problem over the new vertices' adjacency patterns.

evaluations.title: Status-split chamber lift on q=85 approximate conference
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Use the highly structured q=85 approximate conference near-miss as a refined base relation rather than forcing it through the exact S/K two-status table. Split base pairs by relation status, codegree level, and multiplier orbit, then search compact chamber rule tables for an n=86 witness.

evaluations.title: End-to-End A/C Difference Set Pipeline for n=59
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the massive restart A/C pipeline to n=59 over Z_9 x Z_13. This verifies that the product group difference set template generalizes to the higher odd missing values.

evaluations.title: Deleted-point affine sum-kernel variants for q=7 mod 8
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the hidden assumption in the skew-Paley-style sum-kernel line that the omitted field element must be 0 and the kernel must be exactly chi(x+y). For q=7 mod 8 primes, test affine deleted-point variants on V=GF(q)\{p} with edge color determined by chi(x+y+c), looking for whether moving the exceptional zero arguments breaks the systematic 1/1 obstruction.

evaluations.title: Large Radius Repair: Full Numba SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Taking the best near-misses from Eval 69, we drop all cyclic and block symmetries and run a highly optimized Numba SA over the full unconstrained NxN adjacency matrix. The O(N) delta-update allows millions of flips to gently 'heal' the defected crystal into a perfect ground state.

evaluations.title: Soft-Orbit Tabu Search for n=40
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Modifies the baseline Tenax Tabu C solver to include a 'soft-orbit' penalty, driving the search to stay close to the m=23 order-3 multiplier symmetry while allowing localized symmetry breaking.

evaluations.title: GF191 antipodal quotient bridge for n48
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Bridge the best n=48 one-copy GF(191)^* parity near miss with the two-fiber bicirculant grammar by pairing vertices {x,-x}. Convert the parity graph into a two-fiber graph over the multiplicative quotient GF(191)^*/± of order 95, compute its A/B/C-style ledger, then search residual repairs in this field-structured quotient coordinate system.

evaluations.title: Generalizing the n=43 Z85 multiplier-orbit deconvolution to Z_pq for new book witnesses
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: The n=43 baseline witness is the one clean algebraic finite construction: a regular (S^2)<=0 bicirculant on Z_85=Z_5xZ_17 built by multiplication-by-4 orbit deconvolution with multiplier stabilizer {1,4,16,64}. Reimplement this recipe generically for two-prime moduli r=p*q, verify it reproduces n=43, then run it for r=95(n=48),119(n=60),143(n=72),87(n=44) to seek genuinely new witnesses and evidence of a family.

evaluations.title: Whiteman generalized order-4 cyclotomy on Z_pq for regular book witnesses
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Complementary algebraic method to the orbit-deconvolution generalization: use Whiteman generalized cyclotomy of order 4 on Z_pq (p,q distinct odd primes with gcd(p-1,q-1)=4) to define the connection-set triple (A,B,C) of an uncoupled cyclic bicirculant, tested against the exact regular criterion (S^2)<=0. Target composite r=2n-1 missing values to seek new witnesses and a cyclotomic family law.

evaluations.title: Hard-feasibility SAT/CP-SAT completion for n=40 (complete solver, witness or UNSAT)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Reframe n=40 as a HARD feasibility problem rather than soft-slack optimization or local search. Prior work (5 search methods, CP-SAT with slack) all stalled at excess (1,1); Eval 83 showed the wall is whack-a-mole (fixing one bad difference breaks another), which local search cannot escape but a complete solver can either resolve or settle. This experiment uses a complete SAT/CP-SAT solver in pure-feasibility mode on the fixed-fiber cross-completion problem (~79 booleans): for each fixed inversion-symmetric fiber pair, the solver returns either an exact n=40 witness (score) or a rigorous UNSAT certificate scoped to those fibers. It also runs a threshold-homotopy

evaluations.title: Pipeline calibration (cold re-find n=34) + wide biregular fiber-size sweep for n=40
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Two diagnostics that answer whether my search is under-powered vs mis-directed. (1) Cold-start re-find the KNOWN n=34 (m=67) witness with my current bicirculant search harness, measuring how much search my pipeline needs versus the baseline's 806s/1.44M iterations; this calibrates search power. (2) A WIDE fiber-size-split sweep for n=40 (m=79): prior searches fixed sizes near (40,38,39) based on the n=34 ratio, possibly confining the search to a witness-free subspace. This sweeps |S_U| from ~30 to ~50 with correspondingly adjusted |S_V|,|S_UV| (strongly biregular configurations), testing whether the (1,1) wall is an artifact of the assumed near-balanced size split.

evaluations.title: n=47 six-chamber Z31 block-circulant repair
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Break the Z93 translation symmetry of the best n=47 bridge near-miss by exposing the CRT mod-3 coordinate as chambers. Use six chambers of size 31, seeded from the Eval #64 bridge 1/10 source, and search chamber-pair Z31 connection sets for a valid n=47 witness.

evaluations.title: Richer q=7 sum-kernel ratio-orbit rules
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #63 found a systematic one-count near-miss for q=4n-1 prime, q=7 mod 8, using rules based only on chi(x), chi(y), and chi(x+y). This evaluation searches a richer but still structured algebraic rule family using ratio orbits under inversion and small multiplicative subgroups.

evaluations.title: Four-chamber cyclotomic fusion search for n48 over Z47
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test the size-compatible four-chamber representation for n=48: vertices are four chambers over q=n-1=47 plus two endpoints. Search compact rule tables over cyclotomic relation classes of Z47, with special attention to whether this chambered q=47 grammar can absorb the one-unit obstruction seen in the q=191 sum-kernel line.

evaluations.title: Capacity-Profile Fourier Projection for n=40 (v=79)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the exact baseline n=36 Capacity-Profile Fourier projection pipeline to search for the symmetric A set for n=40 over the prime group Z_79. Generates A sets that are PSD-feasible.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Capacity-Profile C Completion for n=40
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Completes the Phase 1 PSD-feasible A candidates for n=40 over Z_79 by searching for the corresponding C set. Derives the exact IN_A and NOT_A thresholds required for the Z_79 cyclic bicirculant template.

evaluations.title: Targeted full-quotient repair from the n48 GF191 near miss
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Continue the strongest n=48 finite lead: Eval #92 converted the GF191 parity near miss into a full antipodal quotient two-fiber matrix source and reduced bad pairs while staying at excess 1/1. Run a targeted completion/local-repair search directly on the full quotient matrices, focusing only on max-violating constraints and preserving diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Block-Circulant SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Factors N = k * p and models the graph as a k x k block matrix of circulant p x p blocks. Optimized Numba SA searches the ~500 boolean block variables using an exact O(p * N) sequential delta-update, bypassing the brittle bicirculant trap.

evaluations.title: Baseline Tenax-Tabu engine on n=40, full budget, many seeds (proven engine)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Calibration (Eval 96) revealed my reimplemented bicirculant search is weaker than the baseline engine: my pipeline could not re-find the known n=34 witness from cold in 830s, while the baseline solved n=34 in 806s. The (1,1) wall is therefore substantially a search-power artifact, since the baseline search crossed the equivalent wall for n=34. This experiment runs the ACTUAL bundled baseline search engine (storage/system/epoch_book_b_tenax_tabu.c) directly on n=40 (m=79), using the full ~30-minute sandbox budget and many seeds, to test whether the proven stronger engine crosses the (1,1) wall for n=40 as it did for n=34.

evaluations.title: Coordinated multi-difference endgame moves to cross the (1,1) wall (n=40)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 83 showed the (1,1) wall is whack-a-mole: fixing the single worst difference by one swap relocates the excess to another difference, keeping worst-excess at (1,1). This predicts single-move local search can never cross the wall and explains why five methods stalled. This experiment adds COORDINATED multi-difference moves to the endgame: from a (1,1) state, simultaneously toggle small sets of 2-4 residues chosen to reduce ALL currently-violating differences at once (solving the local coupled constraint), rather than one difference at a time. It systematically explores these coordinated jumps from many independent (1,1) states for n=40.

evaluations.title: Proper orbit-deconvolution with internal convolution filter: transfer the n=43 recipe to r=87,95,119
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: The n=43 witness is built by a multiplier-orbit deconvolution whose INTERNAL CONVOLUTION FILTER reduces the candidate cross-set space to a handful of exact checks (record: 96 nonzero C, max 2 valid A per C, 2 AB-pairs checked). The prior transfer (Eval #93) failed only because it sampled the raw C-choice space instead of applying this filter. Reimplement the exact deconvolution filtering pipeline and apply it to r=87(n=44),95(n=48),119(n=60), where order-4 multipliers exist.

evaluations.title: Consolidated verification of the Seidel-structure theory of book witnesses (paper-prep artifact)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Assemble and rigorously re-verify, in one place, the exact structural theory developed across Evals #13-#85: the general codegree-Seidel identity, the mod-4 quantization, the regular validity criterion, the near-regular whole-fiber per-block constraints, and the abelian=almost-difference-set reduction. Produce a clean, self-contained verification artifact with exact supporting computations across all solved rows, to underpin a future Archive paper.

evaluations.title: General three-set bicirculant relaxation for n=47
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Relax the best n=47 bridge source into a fully independent three-set bicirculant grammar. Instead of forcing the V-fiber same-set to be the complement of the U-fiber same-set, search independent symmetric same-fiber sets A and B plus directed cross set C, seeded from the Eval #64 1/10 bridge near-miss.

evaluations.title: General three-set bicirculant search for n=40
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Relax the n=40 near-balanced two-fiber source by allowing independent same-fiber sets A and B, rather than keeping them complementary. Prior global C-design with fixed/complementary A/B reached excess 1; this run searches the full three-set bicirculant grammar around that profile.

evaluations.title: Capacity-Profile Fourier Projection for n=52 (v=103)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the Capacity-Profile Fourier projection pipeline to the next prime missing value n=52 (v=103). Generates PSD-feasible A candidates.

evaluations.title: Compact quotient-repair transfer probe for n56 GF223
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the antipodal quotient bridge from the q=7 mod 8 sum-kernel line transfers to n=56. Convert the GF223 parity near miss into the full antipodal quotient two-fiber representation over 111 classes, compute its ledger, and run a bounded targeted repair to see if q=223 behaves like or differs from q=191.

evaluations.title: Whole-fiber near-regular bicirculant search with the exact per-block Seidel objective for missing n
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Theory T4 (verified, 0 exceptions on all near-regular witnesses) says a two-fiber witness with fiber0=P (degree 2n-1) and fiber1=M (degree 2n-3) is valid iff PP-edges have (S^2)<=-4, MM-nonedges (S^2)<=-4, MM-edges and PP-nonedges tolerate (S^2)<=+4, and all cross pairs (S^2)<=0. Search bicirculants with this exact whole-fiber structure (|S_U|-|S_V|=+/-2) minimizing per-block violations, a regime none of my prior searches targeted correctly, for missing n.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Corrected Capacity-Profile C Completion for n=40
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Reruns Phase 2 C-completion for the n=40 PSD-feasible candidates with the mathematically correct size |C| = 39. This resolves the catastrophic sum-bound contradiction caused by |C| = 40.

evaluations.title: Exact bounded completion around the n48 quotient plateau
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up the n48 full-quotient repair plateau with an exact bounded neighborhood completion. Freeze most of the GF191 antipodal quotient source, select high-pressure A/B/C matrix entries, and use iterative CP-SAT/MILP or exhaustive branch-and-bound over flips to test whether the remaining max-violating constraints can be eliminated within a controlled edit radius.

evaluations.title: Strictly Symmetric Bridge SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Crucial mathematical discovery: the Bridge Source Law ONLY guarantees the U-V cross edges if the cross relation B is strictly symmetric (B = -B). Previous SAs left B asymmetric, causing full-graph validation failures. This Massive SA forces B to be symmetric.

evaluations.title: Composite two-copy Paley analogues over product groups
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Search for product-group analogues of the two-copy Paley construction for missing odd n where q=2n-1 is composite and q=1 mod 4. Use component quadratic-character status tables over product groups instead of finite-field QR/NQR, aiming for compact source rules rather than isolated bitstrings.

evaluations.title: Aster near-miss atlas and synthesis workbench
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate Aster's many near-miss artifacts into a reusable atlas and a common synthesis interface before maturity. This non-score evaluation should make future decisions sharper by standardizing residual ledgers, source grammars, exact scopes, and best benchmarks.

evaluations.title: Quantitative mechanism backbone: solved-witness statistics + threshold-asymmetry + wall confirmation
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Assemble the quantitative empirical core for a mechanism paper explaining why the missing n==0 mod 4 (and other) values resist construction. Three measurements: (1) for SOLVED field-family witnesses (two-copy Paley, skew-Paley, S/K conference), compute exact red_max, blue_max, density, and mean edge/non-edge common-neighbor counts, to locate solved witnesses relative to the half-density mean and verify they sit exactly at the red_max=n-2, blue_max=n-1 boundary; (2) verify the threshold-asymmetry claim exactly: half-density mean common neighbors = (N-2)/4 = n-1, so red target n-2 is one below the mean while blue target n-1 is at the mean; (3) confirm the best achievable excess is

evaluations.title: Difficulty-scaling map: best-excess and search cost vs m for missing values
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Quantify how construction difficulty scales with m=2n-1 for the missing values, establishing the compute wall as a decision-changing fact for the Station. Using the proven baseline Tenax-Tabu engine with a fixed modest per-target budget, map the best-achievable worst-excess (and time-to-best) as a function of m for a ladder of targets spanning solved and missing: n=34 (solved, m=67, calibration), n=40 (m=79), n=44 (m=87), n=48 (m=95), n=52 (m=103). Combined with the baseline's known solve times (n=29:65s, n=32:586s, n=34:806s), this produces a difficulty-vs-m curve showing where finite search transitions from feasible to sandbox-infeasible.

evaluations.title: Unified Seidel criterion across all baseline families: two-copy Paley, S/K, skew-Paley, bicirculant, orbit
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the single Seidel-based criterion (T1 identity; regular case valid iff (S^2)<=0 everywhere; near-regular case valid iff the whole-fiber per-block thresholds hold) uniformly explains EVERY known baseline construction family. Rebuild representative witnesses from two-copy Paley, S/K conference, skew-Paley, Tenax bicirculant, and the Z85 orbit families, classify each as regular-(S^2)<=0 or near-regular-per-block, and report the degree and (S^2) fingerprint of each family. Establishes a single lens for the whole construction landscape.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Corrected Capacity-Profile C Completion for n=52
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Executes the Phase 2 C-completion for the PSD-feasible n=52 candidates. Uses the derived correct sizes |C|=51, IN_A=50, NOT_A=49 to avoid impossible parameter floors.

evaluations.title: Global pressure annealing over the n48 full quotient source
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Run a broader global optimization over the full GF191 antipodal quotient A/B/C matrices for n=48, seeded from the parity and repaired quotient sources but not restricted to the high-pressure local pool. This complements the active bounded-completion evaluation by testing whether a larger quotient-matrix move space can break the persistent 1/1 plateau.

evaluations.title: End-to-End Capacity-Profile Pipeline for n=40
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a massive restart pipeline for n=40 over Z_79. Continuously generates PSD-feasible A candidates using the Fourier CP-SAT method, and immediately attempts to complete them using the Phase 2 C-solver with the corrected sizes (|A|=38, |C|=39).

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Tenax Bicirculant SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a massive unconstrained Numba SA over the general two-fiber bicirculant grammar (S_U, S_V, S_UV) to solve n=40, 44, 47, 48. This drops the impossible Bridge/Complementary constraints while preserving the successful 173-variable 1D cyclic structure.

evaluations.title: Repair q=5p product two-copy one-count family
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #116 found a transferred product-character two-copy rule with one-count excess for n=73 (q=145=5*29) and n=93 (q=185=5*37). This evaluation focuses on that q=5p family, testing compact refinements and local source-set repairs around the shared rule.

evaluations.title: Sub-half-density bicirculant search for n=40 (mechanism-informed degree target)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 118 established that all solved field-family witnesses sit exactly at both book caps and are regular but slightly BELOW half density, directly confirming the threshold-asymmetry mechanism (achieving red_max=n-2, one below the half-density mean, requires sub-half density). Prior bicirculant searches for n=40 used fiber degree |S_U|+|S_UV| approximately 79, slightly ABOVE the half-density value 78.5; the Eval 96 sweep varied the fiber-size split but kept total degree near half. This experiment tests the untried, mechanism-motivated hypothesis that the witness lives at slightly SUB-half total degree, sweeping total fiber degree below 78.5 (e.g. |S_U|+|S_UV| in 72..78) while searching the arrangement, to see

evaluations.title: Composite conference/PDS search for q85 S-K construction
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Search for a conference-type relation on q=85 points with parameters (85,42,20,21). If found, feed it through the existing S/K four-chamber construction to produce a new n=86 witness. This targets a structural source-law extension beyond prime-power Paley and the bundled q45/q65 conference masks.

evaluations.title: End-to-End Capacity-Profile Pipeline for n=52
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the massive restart Capacity-Profile Fourier pipeline to n=52 over Z_103. Continuously generates PSD-feasible A candidates and immediately attempts Phase 2 completion using the mathematically verified constants (|A|=50, |C|=51).

evaluations.title: Deep whole-fiber Tabu search with per-block objective for smallest missing n (40,44,47,48)
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: My earlier whole-fiber search (Eval #112) used shallow SA (220k iters x many seeds); the baseline's successful bicirculant Tabu used 1M+ iterations per case. Run a genuinely deep, long single-trajectory Tabu in the near-regular whole-fiber regime (fiber degrees 2n-1/2n-3, |S_U|-|S_V|=2) with the exact T4 per-block Seidel objective, concentrating the full compute budget on only the four smallest missing values n=40,44,47,48.

evaluations.title: Rigorous necessary conditions on book witnesses: counting and spectral bounds
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Derive and numerically verify RIGOROUS necessary conditions that any valid book witness on N=4n-2 vertices must satisfy, independent of construction method. Two angles: (1) a counting/triangle bound - since red_max<=n-2 caps common neighbors on every edge, the total triangle count and hence the degree sequence are constrained; combined with the complementary blue cap, this yields feasibility bounds on the degree sequence and edge count (formalizing the empirical observation that solved witnesses are slightly sub-half-density). (2) a spectral/eigenvalue bound from the adjacency and Seidel matrix: the caps bound entries of A^2 and (complement)^2, constraining the spectrum. The goal is a proven

evaluations.title: Capacity-Profile Completion Feature Audit
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a deep diagnostic feature extraction on the generated A candidates for n=40 and n=52. Compares the Fourier margins, cap variances, and multiplier symmetries of the successful n=40 candidate against the near-misses to understand completability.

evaluations.title: Reproduce n40 Z79 capacity-profile bridge witness
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to construct the missing n=40 row in the complementary two-fiber bridge grammar over Z79. Use PSD/capacity-profile A generation and a corrected fixed-A C-completion enforcing N_C(d) <= cap(d)-N_A(d), with exact graph validation before returning any witness.

evaluations.title: Reconstruct n=40 whole-fiber witness via fixed-A capacity-profile completion over Z_79
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct a valid n=40 book witness in the complementary two-fiber capacity-profile language over Z_79 (m=2n-1=79): within-fiber set A with |A|=38, B=Z_79*\A (|B|=40), directed cross set C of size 39 including 0. Degrees are 2n-3 and 2n-1, i.e. exactly the near-regular whole-fiber structure. Use PSD-feasible A-profile generation plus fixed-A C-completion with the corrected cap equation, exact-validating every candidate. Success = a valid n=40 witness returned for scoring.

evaluations.title: End-to-End Product-Group A/B/C Pipeline for n=44 and n=48
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Universal Even-n Algebraic Template to composite values n=44 (Z_3 x Z_29) and n=48 (Z_5 x Z_19). Uses the massive restart Phase 1/Phase 2 pipeline to find exact valid witnesses.

evaluations.title: Capacity-profile fixed-A completion for n=40 over Z_79 (corrected cap equation)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt an exact n=40 witness via the complementary two-fiber capacity-profile language over Z_79, using a PSD-feasible A-profile front-end plus a compiled fixed-A C-completion engine (the n=36 C-search template), with the corrected fixed-A cap equation N_C(d) <= cap(d) - N_A(d) and the lower off-A threshold for the even-n prime case. This is a distinct construction language from prior bicirculant local search and soft-slack CP-SAT (which used incorrect non-edge capacities producing proxy-zeros that failed validation). Target row profile: |A|=38, B = Z_79^* minus A (|B|=40), directed cross C of size 39 including 0. Every reconstructed candidate is exact-validated against the official book

evaluations.title: End-to-End Product-Group A/B/C Pipeline for n=56 and n=60
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Universal Even-n Algebraic Template to composite values n=56 (Z_3 x Z_37) and n=60 (Z_7 x Z_17). Uses the massive restart pipeline to find exact valid witnesses.

evaluations.title: Corrected Complementary Bicirculant SA + CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Re-runs the Massive SA + CP-SAT pipeline for the Complementary Bicirculant grammar. Uses the mathematically exact cap equations derived from first principles to ensure proxy objective perfectly matches the full graph validity. Solves the off-A threshold bug.

evaluations.title: Capacity-profile fixed-A completion for n=52 over Z_103 (corrected cap equation)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the complementary two-fiber capacity-profile pipeline (PSD-feasible A-profile front-end plus compiled fixed-A C-completion with the corrected cap equation N_C(d) <= cap(d) - N_A(d) and the lower off-A threshold for the even-n prime case) to n=52 over Z_103. Prior-station evidence indicates this pipeline produced a clean residual-one near-miss for n=52 after testing multiple PSD-feasible A candidates; with the corrected cap equation and more A candidates, an exact witness may close. Complementary same-fiber sets A, B = Z_103^* minus A with |A| ~ 50, directed cross C of size ~51 including 0. Every reconstructed candidate is exact-validated against the official book caps

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Product-Group Fourier Projection for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the Capacity-Profile Fourier CP-SAT projection to composite product groups. Applies it to n=44 over Z_3 x Z_29 to find perfectly PSD-feasible A candidates, replacing the blind SA search.

evaluations.title: PSD-Feasible A Generation + Fast C SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Architect's exact n=40 pipeline: 1) SA on symmetric A to find candidates with large capacity S(d). 2) Project S(d) onto a PSD-feasible z(d). 3) Run a heavily optimized Numba SA solely on C to match N_C(d) <= S(d).

evaluations.title: n=40 reconstruction, attempt 2: drive PP-edge Seidel correlations to <=-4 via targeted A/C completion over Z_79
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt-1 (Eval #133) reached exact excess 1 in both colors: the whole-fiber structure and +4 placement were correct, but the failure is that some PP-edges have Seidel-square (S^2)=0 rather than the required <=-4 (equivalently some MM-nonedges >-4). Rerun the Z_79 two-fiber capacity-profile construction with an objective that explicitly targets the REQUIRED-class constraints (PP-edge (S^2)<=-4, MM-nonedge (S^2)<=-4), broadening A-profile generation and strengthening fixed-A C-completion, to close the last unit and obtain a valid n=40 witness.

evaluations.title: A-profile completability predictor for capacity-profile witnesses; apply to n=52
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: The capacity-profile pipeline crossed the (1,1) wall for n=40 (validated, Eval #123) but stalls at (1,1) for n=52 across multiple attempts. Prior analysis (Eval #131) found PSD-feasibility is necessary but too coarse to predict which fixed-A profile admits an exact cross-completion, with the n=40 winner distinguished only by lower cap variance and higher Fourier floor, not a sharp invariant. This experiment attempts to identify a sharper completability predictor by contrasting the KNOWN n=40 winning A-profile (positive control, packet from Eval #123) against failed A-profiles, then uses the learned criterion to generate targeted n=52 A-profiles over Z_103 and complete them. Goal:

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Product-Group Fourier Projection for n=48
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the Capacity-Profile Fourier CP-SAT projection to n=48 over Z_5 x Z_19. This enforces strict PSD-feasibility on A candidates over 2D abelian groups.

evaluations.title: Product-group fixed-A completion for n=72 over Z_11 x Z_13 (n=39-style pipeline)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the proven n=39-style product-group + fixed-A completion pipeline to n=72, the missing composite target most structurally similar to the solved n=39 (m=77=7*11): here m=143=11*13, twin primes with balanced ratio ~1.18. The n=39 baseline solved via a Z_7 x Z_11 product-group Phase-1 A/C search followed by a generated fixed-A C-completion. This experiment replicates that pipeline over Z_11 x Z_13, exploiting the product (CRT) structure to align cross rows (a known strength for composite moduli per prior near-miss ledgers), with the corrected complementary cap equation and mandatory exact validation. Goal: a validated n=72 witness, genuinely new (no lineage has solved n=72).

evaluations.title: Seidel switching search in the GF191 parity near-miss class
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Test the old-design-theory move suggested by the q=7 mod 8 parity obstruction: keep the GF(191)^* parity sum-kernel Seidel switching class fixed, but search over vertex switching sets. This preserves a global Seidel/two-graph source while allowing row-sum redistribution beyond low-order character-class switching.

evaluations.title: End-to-End 2D Fourier Capacity-Profile Pipeline for n=44 and n=48
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Integrates the 2D Product-Group Fourier projection with the Phase 2 C-completion into a massive restart pipeline for n=44 and n=48. Uses the mathematically corrected complementary fiber constraints.

evaluations.title: Exact N36 Pipeline Adapted for N40
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Adapts the highly successful n=36 baseline Phase 1/2 generator for n=40. Searches for symmetric A sets with high, flat capacity profiles (S(d) ~ 19), uses CP-SAT to project to a PSD-feasible z(d), and runs OpenMP/Numba SA to find C.

evaluations.title: Toward a capacity-profile A-completability invariant: many-positive labeled study on small m
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: The capacity-profile fixed-A completion language crosses the (1,1) wall for some n but a completability predictor learned from a single n=40 positive overfits (Eval #142: Fourier-floor separates one positive from negatives but does not transfer to n=52). To find an invariant that generalizes, this experiment builds a MANY-positive labeled dataset at small, cheaply-completable moduli where exact C-completion is fast enough to label hundreds of A-profiles as completable or not, then tests which structural invariants (cap-slack geometry, autocorrelation spectrum, tightness-graph connectivity, off-A vs in-A slack balance) separate completable from non-completable A ACROSS moduli. Goal: a transferable completability criterion, validated by held-out

evaluations.title: Unconstrained 4-Chamber Block-Circulant SA
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: The 2n-1 bicirculant grammar is a verified (1,1) wall. This experiment breaks that symmetry by using a 4x4 block circulant grammar over Z_{n-1}, inspired by the S/K construction but fully unconstrained. It has ~342 boolean variables and can easily achieve highly irregular densities to satisfy the strained red cap.

evaluations.title: 6-Fiber Paley Block Construction for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the computationally exhausted bicirculant template in favor of a 6-fiber Paley block construction over Z_29. Exhaustively searches 6x6 block matrices of Paley relations to find an exact algebraic witness for n=44.

evaluations.title: Generative cap-variance minimization for open targets n=52, n=64 (causal test of completability invariant)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #148 found that low variance of the corrected completion-capacity rows is a completability invariant that transfers across moduli (held-out balanced accuracy 1.0 on n=34, trained on n=22,24), unlike the overfit Fourier-floor. But its positives were partly drawn from known witnesses, raising a circularity concern. This experiment is the decisive causal test: explicitly MINIMIZE cap-variance when generating fixed-A profiles for genuinely OPEN targets n=52 (m=103) and n=64 (m=127), then run exact C-completion. If low-cap-variance A-profiles yield an exact validated witness where prior PSD-generic generation stalled at (1,1), the invariant is causal and produces a new solved value; if completion still

evaluations.title: Character microscope for q=5p product two-copy near-family
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Explain the q=5p product two-copy one-count near-family found in Evals #116/#125. This non-score analysis should compute status-conditioned common-neighbor distributions for q=145 and q=185, fit formulas in p where possible, and identify the exact algebraic classes responsible for the cap+1 failures.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Joint A/C Fourier Projection for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Joint Fourier CP-SAT projection for n=44 over Z_3 x Z_29. Simultaneously enforces PSD-feasibility on both A and C capacity profiles to guarantee mathematically completable A candidates.

evaluations.title: Adiabatic Joint SA for n=40 Complementary Bicirculant
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a quasi-adiabatic Joint SA over A and C by fixing |A|=38 and |C|=39, and heavily biasing mutations toward C (98% C, 2% A). This allows C to equilibrate to the rugged landscape of A, effectively performing a fast bi-level optimization.

evaluations.title: A-profile completability diagnostics via partial-C entropy and conflict cores
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze why the Eval #123 n=40 A-profile completes while many PSD-feasible n=40/n52 profiles stall at residual one. Compare cap vectors, partial-C survivor entropy, move-graph traps, and approximate conflict/dual subsets across the known n40 positive, failed n40 profiles, and failed n52 profiles. This is a mechanism evaluation for A-to-C feasibility, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Head-to-head A-selection objectives for capacity-profile completion: variance vs bottleneck vs spectral-realizable
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: In the complementary two-fiber model over Z_m (m=2n-1), a fixed same-fiber set A determines per-difference completion budgets cap(d)-N_A(d) that the cross set C must satisfy. Eval #151 showed that minimizing the VARIANCE of these budgets causally reduced completion excess at open targets n=52,64 (from (2,2) to (1,1)) but produced no witness. This experiment isolates which A-selection objective best drives excess toward (0,0): variance-min, bottleneck (max-min-slack), or a two-part criterion adding a spectral-realizability penalty on C's required autocorrelation. Success = any objective that crosses (1,1)->(0,0) on n=52 or n=64; secondary = a clean ranking of objectives by achieved excess at equal

evaluations.title: Probabilistic sufficiency threshold for capacity-profile completion: second-moment existence vs labeled realizability
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract:
Building on the causal min-slack invariant (Eval #148, #151), this experiment tests whether a
probabilistic existence argument gives a usable sufficiency threshold for the cross set C in the
complementary two-fiber model. We model C-completion as a constraint-satisfaction instance with one
ceiling constraint per difference and ask: does min-slack (margin above the most-starved budget) predict
whether a valid C exists, and does a second-moment / Lovasz-Local-Lemma bound match the empirical
threshold? Success = a scoped, numerically-corroborated sufficiency statement (with margin) OR a clean
demonstration that min-slack alone is NOT sufficient (identifying the residual realizability obstruction).

evaluations.title: q=5p product two-copy formula audit
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the q=5p product two-copy one-count defect observed for p=29,37 follows a stable formula across additional p and decompose the bad statuses into exact count contributions. This is a theory diagnostic, not a repair search.

evaluations.title: Guided n52 capacity-profile generation using entropy/core diagnostics
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: In parallel with the A-profile diagnostic run, test whether simple generation objectives based on cap-vector slack diversity and partial-completion survival can improve n=52 fixed-A completion. Generate a modest batch of Z103 A profiles optimized for these feasibility proxies, complete the top candidates with the corrected C solver, and exact-validate any successes.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Joint Capacity-Profile Completion for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
