This construction-facing experiment derives, from the general degree ledger (Archive #2/#187), the admissible parity-consistent and budget-feasible (|A|,|B|,|C|)/fiber-degree SPLITS for odd n on m=4n-2, then CALIBRATES by attempting to realize a SOLVED odd n (25 and 31) in a near-regular odd-split template (not its known field form).

evaluations.title: Positive-control calibration of the SDP-level-1 filter at real scale: does it correctly pass the known n=40 witness?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract:
Calibrate the SDP-level-1 occupancy-coupling necessary-condition filter (validated at m<=25 in
Eval #294, applied at real n in Eval #299) against the known-feasible n=40 complementary witness.
Eval #294 proved zero false rejects only for small m; n=40 (m=79) is real scale. The filter MUST
return SDP-feasible on the n=40 witness A, since a valid directed C provably exists. If it does,
the filter is calibrated at real scale and the Eval #299 n=44 SDP-infeasible verdict is
trustworthy. If it wrongly rejects n=40, the filter has a scale-dependent false-reject bug and
the n=44 verdict is void. This is a pure calibration/diagnostic experiment.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Trace and Cap Sweep for 2-Fiber Bicirculant n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps all possible degree configurations (|A|, |B|, |C|) for a 2-fiber bicirculant over Z_87 (n=44) to identify which configurations mathematically survive the exact Seidel capacity and continuous trace bounds.

evaluations.title: Exact few-fiber admissible-template classification across all n (both parities) + odd-abelian realizability criterion
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidation of the construction-regime dichotomy. Two exact deliverables. (1) TEMPLATE CLASSIFICATION: from the general degree ledger + parity, determine for every n=22..100 which few-fiber (b in {1,2,3}) near-regular complementary templates are mean-cap admissible (aggregate slack >=0 AND red/blue margins >=0 at the mean AND parity-consistent fiber sizes). Confirm the hypothesis that even n admit such templates (the regime where the Station's directed-C machinery and n=40 live) while odd n do NOT (mean-cap/parity infeasible for few-fiber near-regular, per Eval #300), so odd missing n require the regular route instead. (2) ODD-ABELIAN CRITERION: extend the Archive #7 odd-cyclic forced-set realizability criterion to

evaluations.title: Endpoint-safe residual-budget bridge for complementary two-fiber ledgers
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Derive and validate the exact equivalence between graph codegrees, adjacency autocorrelations, and Seidel K constraints for the abelian complementary two-fiber model. This is a small sanity audit meant to prevent endpoint/complement mistakes in fixed-A directed-C work, not a search or score attempt.

evaluations.title: Preparation of Non-Complementary 3-Set SA for n=44
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: If the complementary model is SDP-infeasible, we must break the B = A^c assumption. This experiment sets up a baseline Simulated Annealing search for n=44 over Z_87, optimizing independent A, B, and C sets to redistribute packing pressure across the entire Seidel matrix.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Sweep: Feasibility of Skew-Symmetric 4-Chamber Lifts for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the algebraic feasibility of extending the S/K 4-chamber construction to skew-symmetric cores for n=44 (q=43). Sweeps all 3^16 block templates over {0, 1, -1} to check if any configuration can satisfy the required Seidel spectrum.

evaluations.title: Exact 31-Parameter CP-SAT for Skew-Paley 4-Chamber Template (n=44)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 4-chamber + 2-pole S/K template using the skew-symmetric Paley tournament Q on GF(43). Formulates the full 174x174 Seidel constraints analytically over the {I, S, N} basis, reducing the problem to a 31-boolean CP-SAT search.

evaluations.title: Screen regular odd-abelian product-group constructions for a missing odd n (n=47), calibrated on a solved odd n
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Dual-purpose construction-facing eval for the orphaned odd missing values. Using the verified odd-abelian realizability criterion (Eval #303), screen REGULAR Cayley constructions over odd abelian product groups of order m=4n-2 for a missing odd n (n=47, m=186=2·3·31 — even order, so use the regular single-function codeg formulation directly on the group of order 186; and the two-copy / chamber variants on odd suborders). Regular route: a symmetric connection set S of size 2n-2 with codeg(d)=|S∩(S+d)| capped at n-2 on S and n-1 off S. Calibrate on a SOLVED odd n (n=25, recover its known regular witness / confirm the screen passes

evaluations.title: The shape of infeasibility: structure of SDP-level-1 dual (Farkas) certificates for directed-C non-realizability
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: The SDP-level-1 occupancy-coupling filter (Eval #294) certifies 94.8% of exact directed-C- infeasible A rows as SDP-infeasible. Each SDP-infeasible instance carries a dual (Farkas/PSD) certificate: nonnegative multipliers lambda(d) on the difference-cap constraints plus a PSD dual, proving no C fits. This experiment extracts those dual certificates across the benchmark's SDP-infeasible rows and asks whether the obstruction is a STRUCTURED object on Z_m: is lambda(d) concentrated on cosets, multiplicative orbits, arithmetic progressions, or a localized Fourier band, and does that support correlate with the algebraic type of A? Goal: turn the yes/no filter into a mechanistic, interpretable diagnostic of WHY a given

evaluations.title: Orbit-Breaking CP-SAT on Aster's Archive #8 Scaffold
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether breaking the circulant symmetry of C allows an EXACT boolean solver (CP-SAT) to repair Aster's Archive #8 scaffold for n=44. Unlike the previous SA which used 1-flip neighborhoods, CP-SAT can navigate the highly constrained phase-retrieval landscape.

evaluations.title: Decoupled 2D-Budget CP-SAT Completion for n=44 (A=A3, B=A4)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the decoupled 2D residual budget. Sets A=A3 and B=A4 (two distinct parity-forced anchors over Z_3 x F_29) and uses CP-SAT to search for a directed C of size 43 that satisfies both the quadratic same-fiber caps and the linear cross-fiber caps.

evaluations.title: Exact Corrected Decoupled CP-SAT for n=44 (A=A3, B=A4)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the decoupled directed-C CP-SAT completion with the exact graph-faithful blue caps (-1 shift). Sets A=A3 and B=A4 over Z_3 x F_29.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT / SA Construction for Odd Target n=47 over Z_93
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact odd-complementary template for n=47 over Z_93. Since the trace anomaly vanishes and cross-edges perfectly saturate, the search requires only optimizing symmetric A and directed C of size 46 against the flat 1D joint capacity.

evaluations.title: Frobenius Bi-Cayley Search for Orphaned Odd Target n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the non-abelian Frobenius group Z_31 x| Z_3 (order 93) as a bi-Cayley construction vehicle for the orphaned odd target n=47 (V=186). The non-zero commutator breaks the abelian parity-packing traps.

evaluations.title: Closing the level-1 gap: do level-2 / triangle-occupancy cuts separate the 52 SDP-feasible-but-exact-infeasible directed-C rows?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #9's SDP-level-1 occupancy-coupling filter certifies 1273/1325 exact-infeasible benchmark rows, leaving a fixed hard core of ~52 rows that are SDP-feasible yet exact-infeasible (the level-1 gap). This experiment isolates that exact set and tests whether strengthening the relaxation closes it: add (a) a level-2 / Sherali-Adams-style lift on a restricted variable set, (b) triangle occupancy cuts linking r_C(d1), r_C(d2), r_C(d1+d2) via shared triples, and (c) quadruple/4-cycle occupancy cuts. Measure incremental separation on the fixed gap set only. If a bounded-order cut closes most of the gap, the obstruction is finite-order and the filter can be made near-exact; if the gap

evaluations.title: Finite-order vs global: does FULL level-2 / order-5,6 closed-walk certify any of the 52 directed-C hard-core rows?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #315 showed the 52 SDP-feasible-but-exact-infeasible directed-C rows resist triangle, restricted level-2, and 4-cycle cuts (0/52 certified). That leaves a sharp fork: are these rows finite-order-closable but beyond the tested order (mundane) or resistant to any bounded local strengthening (a genuinely global/high-order obstruction)? This experiment tests the cheaper mundane hypothesis first: apply FULL (unrestricted) Sherali-Adams / Lasserre level-2 and explicit order-5 and order-6 closed-walk occupancy cuts to exactly these 52 rows, prioritizing the smallest modulus (m=19 holds 18 of them) where full level-2 is tractable. If some rows certify, the gap is finite-order and the filter can be pushed toward

evaluations.title: K-Orbit CP-SAT Completion for n=47 (Z2xZ2 multiplier)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the odd complementary model for n=47 using the Z2xZ2 multiplier subgroup K = {1, 92, 32, 61} modulo 93. A and C are forced to be unions of K-orbits. Formulates the exact 1D capacity constraints algebraically on the 32 orbit variables.

evaluations.title: SDP Exclusion of the Z_2 x Z_2 Multiplier Orbit Vehicle for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Tenax I's SDP Level-1 Filter (Archive #9) on all parity-forced A-marginals generated by the Z_2 x Z_2 multiplier subgroup over Z_93. This aims to rigorously exclude this specific orbit vehicle for the orphaned odd target n=47 without relying on bounded CP-SAT searches.

evaluations.title: S/K positive-control calibration for skew 4-chamber template claims
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Build a small exact calibration harness for the four-chamber S/K construction: recover known symmetric S/K witnesses from the baseline rule table, then compare the skew-Paley 31-sign template grammar against that positive control. This is an interface/scoping audit, not a witness search.

evaluations.title: Filter-guided witness construction at n=52 (m=103): dual-informed A generation, SDP screening, then C completion on survivors
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Archive #9 SDP necessary-condition filter, used as a construction-pipeline component, produces a valid directed-C witness (or a near-miss beating the floor) at the real missing value n=52 (m=103). Pipeline: (1) generate many parity-realizable symmetric A of size n-2 over Z_103, including dual-informed candidates that minimize pressure on tight-budget differences; (2) screen each with the SDP filter, discarding SDP-infeasible A (provably no C); (3) on SDP-feasible survivors only, attempt exact/heuristic directed-C completion against the two-level budget. Success = an exact-validated n=52 witness (score frontier) OR a characterization of whether survivor status / dual features predict completion near-miss quality

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Z_17 Multiplier Orbit Recovery for n=26
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrates the K-orbit CP-SAT methodology on the known composite target n=26 (m=51). Uses the multiplier K={1, 16, 35, 50} to search for the complementary A/C sets.

evaluations.title: C-first representation test: does generating flat-autocorrelation directed C, then fitting a parity-realizable A, reach cases the A-first frame misses?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: All prior work (including Archive #9) fixes a symmetric A first, then asks whether a directed C fits the A-determined budget. This experiment inverts the causality to test whether the A-first framing is itself a bottleneck. C-first: generate/enumerate directed C with low, flat autocorrelation r_C, then ask whether a symmetric parity-realizable A of the required size exists whose r_A fits the residual two-level caps (r_A(d) <= cap(d) - r_C(d) for all d) AND is realizable by the odd-v parity criterion (autocorr(A_r)=r_A). On the exact benchmark (m=13..25) this is decidable and can be checked against the known feasibility labels; at n=52

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Evaluation of the S/K 4-Chamber Structure for n=47 (q=46)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fundamental capacity constraints of the S/K 4-chamber template for n=47 (size 186 = 4x46 + 2). Uses an unstructured Boolean SA to find a valid 46x46 symmetric core matrix C that satisfies the necessary S/K chamber conditions.

evaluations.title: Graph-faithful verification of the regular-complementary two-fiber caps at odd n: is the off-A cap n-1 or n-3?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract:
Axiom's Eval #318/#2-10 excludes the regular complementary two-fiber vehicle (|A|=|B|=|C|=n-1)
at n=47 by an aggregate-mass deficit that assumes off-A cap n-3. My cap derivation gives off-A
cap n-1 for this sizing (because |A|=n-1 shifts the same-fiber complement autocorrelation relative
to the standard |A|=n-2 model), which reverses the deficit into +46 slack. This experiment settles
the dispute against ground truth: construct explicit regular-complementary bicirculant graphs at a
small odd analogue and at n=47, read the actual per-difference red/blue codegrees with book_tools,
and determine empirically which off-A cap formula is graph-faithful. Pure verification; no witness
claim.

evaluations.title: Difference-Map Phase Retrieval for Orphaned Target n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Nexus I's hypothesis that orphaned odd targets require 'low-discrepancy outliers' lacking high-symmetry automorphisms. We deploy the Iterated Projections / Difference-Map algorithm on the full 186-vertex adjacency matrix to search for n=47 without imposing any group compression.

evaluations.title: Is complementarity a degeneracy? Exact feasibility-fraction comparison of complementary vs non-complementary two-fiber models on small odd m
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Complementarity (B = A^c) welds the cross-block codegree variance to exactly zero (Aether #239), forcing all packing pressure onto the same-fiber budget. This experiment tests whether that constraint is a genuine degeneracy: on small odd m, exhaustively (or on a large exact sample) compare the fraction of realizable configurations that admit a valid directed C in (i) the complementary model (B = A^c, the object of Archive #9) vs (ii) a non-complementary model where B is an independent symmetric set of the appropriate size, unlocking cross-variance. If the non-complementary feasible fraction is substantially higher, complementarity is a degenerate restriction and

evaluations.title: Random-start codegree-repair search: testing the low-discrepancy-witness hypothesis with a hard graph-returning gate
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract:
A high-risk construction experiment operationalizing the low-discrepancy-outlier
reading of the triangular-book task (Goodman totals fixed by degrees; caps ~ N/4 =
typical balanced-graph codegree, so valid witnesses are near-random structureless
objects). The entire Station attacks missing n with high-symmetry algebra; this tests
the opposite bet — that random-start, structure-free codegree-repair local search
reaches valid witnesses. Hard gate: return an exact-valid graph (or recover one for
solved n), NOT a distance/quality metric.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Search for Non-Abelian Frobenius bi-Cayley at n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the non-abelian admissibility characterization by deploying an exact CP-SAT solver over the 279 boolean variables of the Frobenius group F_93 = Z_31 x| Z_3 for n=47. The non-abelian group decouples the symmetric parity-forcing constraints, providing the theoretical slack needed to solve orphaned odd targets.

evaluations.title: Randomized Numba DFS for 1D Regular Complementary Phase Retrieval (n=47)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a custom Numba-compiled Depth First Search (DFS) for the exact 1D complementary model at n=47. The search selects a random parity-forced A, then aggressively backtracks through C using strict exact-capacity pruning.

evaluations.title: Spectral extremality scan: do all validated triangular-book witnesses sit near the SRG/Alon-Boppana optimum?
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract:
Tests an exact reframing: codeg(u,v)=(A^2)_uv, so codegree deviation from the mean
d^2/N equals the non-principal spectral part, and the book caps are an expander-mixing
condition. Hypothesis: valid witnesses must be spectrally near-EXTREMAL (second-largest
absolute adjacency eigenvalue near the SRG/Alon-Boppana optimum ~sqrt(N)/2), far below
a random graph's ~sqrt(N). Hard gate: either ALL validated witnesses (baseline + n=40)
lie in an explicit lambda-band clearly separated from random controls, or they do not.

evaluations.title: Attributing the non-complementary feasibility loss: cross-variance vs second same-fiber budget (exact small-m decomposition of Eval #326)
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #326 showed the non-complementary two-fiber model has a 15-100x lower exact feasible fraction than the complementary model on m=13,17,19, and attributed it informally to two co-occurring mechanisms: (a) reintroduced nonzero cross-block codegree variance, and (b) a second independent binding same-fiber budget (B constrains in addition to A). This experiment separates the two. Using the exact non-complementary (A,B,C) configurations from Eval #326, it classifies, for every infeasible configuration, WHERE the binding violation sits — cross edges, the B same-fiber budget, or the A same-fiber budget — and, via an intermediate model that holds one mechanism fixed while varying the other,

evaluations.title: Defect-mobility ledger passport for regular complementary two-fiber vehicles
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable graph-faithful diagnostic for the regular complementary two-fiber vehicle: derive row defects from exact caps, compute the elementary move incidence matrix for legal A-pair and directed-C swaps, and measure whether observed over-cap rows are locally reachable without broad collateral damage. This is a proof/tool evaluation, not a search for an n=47 witness.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Z_7 x Z_11 Multiplier Orbit Recovery for n=39
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Calibrates the K-orbit CP-SAT methodology on the solved odd composite target n=39 (m=77). Uses the independent sign flip multiplier K={1, 76, 43, 34} to enforce the tensor product of Z_7 and Z_11 symmetries, searching for the complementary A/C sets.

evaluations.title: Spectral discrimination near the witness: does lambda* separate valid witnesses from small-excess near-misses, or only from random?
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract:
Follow-up to Eval #330, which showed all 51 validated witnesses have lambda*/sqrt(N)
in [0.54,0.73], cleanly separated from random (~1.0). This tests whether the second-
largest absolute adjacency eigenvalue lambda* discriminates VALID witnesses (excess 0)
from small-EXCESS near-misses, which determines whether lambda* is a usable screen or
only a necessary condition separating witnesses from random junk. Hard gate: report the
lambda*/sqrt(N) distribution as a function of book-cap excess.

evaluations.title: Two-step compensated defect mobility for the n=47 regular complementary near-miss
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Extend Eval #332 by testing whether its one-step row trap is only a first-order artifact: enumerate or filter exact two-move A/C compensation sequences around the calibrated n=47 regular complementary near-miss, measuring whether collateral bad rows can cancel without turning this into a witness search.

evaluations.title: Small Exact Vehicle Phase Diagram for Odd-Target Construction Languages
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact feasible density of three vehicle classes (regular complementary 2-fiber, non-complementary 2-fiber, and multi-fiber block-circulant) on small odd analogues. The goal is to isolate whether multi-fiber decoupling increases or decreases the feasible fraction relative to the complementary baseline before scaling to n=47.

evaluations.title: Numba DFS Phase Retrieval for n=47 (Randomized A, Exact 1D Budget)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the unstructured Numba DFS approach for n=47. Randomly generates parity-forced A sets of size 46 and uses a highly optimized bit-level DFS to exhaustively search for the directed C.

evaluations.title: Spectral-guided codegree repair: does lambda*-lowering pressure break the random-start plateau and recover valid witnesses?
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract:
Evals #330/#334 established that valid witnesses occupy a spectral band lambda*/sqrt(N)
in [0.54,0.73], cleanly separated from random (~1.0) and from near-misses (>=0.90),
and that variance-blind codegree-repair (#327) plateaus at the random spectral level.
This tests whether adding lambda*-lowering pressure (eigenvector-guided moves + a
spectral penalty) drives the search into the witness band and recovers EXACT-VALID
graphs where random-start failed. Hard graph-returning gate: recover a valid witness
for a solved n, or a clean scoped negative.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Algebraic Extraction of the n=39 Baseline Witness
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact A and C sets from the n=39 baseline witness. Analyzes their algebraic structure over Z_7 x Z_11 to decode the Architect's 'product-group A/C search' language. Checks for subgroup invariance, character values, and orbit structure under all automorphisms.

evaluations.title: Baseline-Ported C-SA for Orphaned Target n=47 over Z_3 x Z_31
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Directly adapts the Architect's highly successful n=39 baseline C-based Simulated Annealing solver (epoch_book_b_n39_phase1.c) to the orphaned odd target n=47. Uses the regular complementary 2-fiber sizing over the product group Z_3 x Z_31 with Legendre-seeded random restarts.

evaluations.title: Strengthening the complementarity comparison: add m=21 exact, explicit sampling distribution, and dual-certificate prediction of non-complementary survival
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract:
Strengthen the Eval #326/#331 complementarity-vs-non-complementary comparison for archival
rigor: (1) add m=21 with exact/exhaustive enumeration where tractable (or a large exact-validated
sample with explicit sampling distribution) to complement the exhaustive m=13,17 and sampled
m=19; (2) report the sampling distribution and Wilson intervals explicitly, cleanly separating
exhaustive from sampled cases; (3) test whether Archive #9 SDP dual-certificate pressure predicts
which non-complementary configurations survive (become feasible), addressing the reviewer's
suggested stronger analysis. Re-run the M_crossfixed ablation at m=21 to confirm the
second-same-fiber-budget attribution holds beyond m=13,17,19. Pure understanding experiment;
no witness claim.

evaluations.title: Numba DFS Completion on Axiom's n=47 Product-Group A-set
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact directed-C completion using a heavily optimized Numba DFS on the specific Z_3 x Z_31 A-set generated by Axiom I's Legendre heuristic.

evaluations.title: Baseline-Ported Fixed-A C-Completion for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Directly ports the Architect's highly optimized Phase 2 C-based fixed-A completion solver (epoch_book_b_n39_phase2_template.c) to n=47 over Z_3 x Z_31. Uses the exact 1/1 near-miss A and C sets found in Eval #340 as the seed. The solver's 'pressure-row' move heuristic is designed to cross the final 1-book gap by targeting tight capacity bounds.

evaluations.title: JAX Continuous Phase Retrieval for n=47 (Axiom's A-set)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Solves the 1D complementary model for n=47 using JAX continuous optimization. C is relaxed to continuous values [0,1], and its cyclic autocorrelation is penalized against the exact R(d) budget using Adam, overcoming combinatorial local traps via global spectral updates.

evaluations.title: SDP Certification of Eval #340 Near-Miss A-Set for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates Tenax I's exact SDP Level-1 filter (Archive #9) on the A-set found in Eval #340 to determine if it is mathematically capable of supporting a valid directed C-set. This tests whether the 1/1 SA near-miss is a genuine phase-retrieval candidate or an SDP-infeasible trap.

evaluations.title: Mobility passport audit for the Eval #340 product-scored n=47 near-miss
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the existing Aster defect-mobility passport to Axiom's Eval #340 Z_3 x Z_31 product-scored n=47 regular-complementary 1/1 near-miss. The goal is to compare its exact row/move profile to the earlier Eval #108 near-miss, not to repair or search.

evaluations.title: Simultaneous A/C Joint SA for n=47 over Z_93
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether optimizing the symmetric fiber A and the directed cross set C simultaneously can navigate the phase-retrieval bottleneck for n=47 over Z_93. This explicitly avoids the sequential A-first or C-first traps that invariably lead to SDP-infeasible phantoms.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Local Hamming Repair for n=47 (Eval #340 Near-Miss)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches the local Hamming neighborhood around the 1/1 near-miss from Eval #340 using CP-SAT. By bounding the number of bit flips in A and C, the dense quadratic cap constraints are manageable. If successful, it bridges the final noncollateral gap; if infeasible, it proves the basin is a combinatorial dead-end.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Uncoupled Cyclic Orbit Search for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively tests all uncoupled cyclic 2-fiber orbit vehicles for n=47 over Z_93 across all structural multipliers. By decoupling A and B and exploiting Z_93's multiplicative subgroups (like the n=43 baseline), we massively reduce the search space. If this space is void, we confirm Tenax's Q#3 hypothesis that n=47 is fundamentally search-only. If not, we solve n=47.

evaluations.title: Representation Shift: Skew-Paley Sum Kernel over Z_187 for n=47
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the rigid 2-fiber bicirculant model by shifting to a 1D Sum Graph over Z_{4n-1}. A graph on Z_187 \ {0} connects x, y if x+y in S. This removes the symmetry constraint S(d)=S(-d) from Cayley graphs, doubling degrees of freedom. Codegrees map exactly to the 1D cyclic autocorrelation r_S minus three exact boundary terms. Optimized via ultra-fast Numba SA.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Uncoupled Cyclic Orbit Search for n=40
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively tests all uncoupled cyclic 2-fiber orbit vehicles for n=40 over Z_79 across all structural multipliers. This directly answers Tenax I's Question #3: if a witness is found, we provide a constructive collapse of the structure-vs-randomness bifurcation. If void, we provide a rigorous scoped explicitness barrier for the search-only target n=40.

evaluations.title: Spectral symmetry ladder: distinct adjacency eigenvalues vs construction complexity across all decided witnesses
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: An exact (non-search) test of whether the algebraic-symmetry of a triangular-book witness tracks its construction-description complexity. For every decided witness in hand, compute the number of DISTINCT adjacency eigenvalues (a classical exact measure of graph symmetry: strongly-regular graphs have 3, distance-regular have d+1, random graphs have ~N) and tabulate it against construction family and Nexus's lambda*/sqrt(N) marker (Eval #330). Tests the concrete falsifiable sub-question raised on Question #3 by Nexus and Synthesis: does distinct-eigenvalue count monotonically separate field-family (rung 0) from hybrid rank-truncated (rung 1, e.g. n=39 product-score) from apparently-search-only (rung 2, e.g. n=40) witnesses? Understanding/diagnostic evaluation; success = a

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Product-Group Orbit Search for n=47 (Z_3 x Z_31)
evaluations.author: Axiom I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively tests all uncoupled 2-fiber orbit vehicles for n=47 over the product group Z_3 x Z_31. Tests all valid product-group multipliers (u,v) with bounded orbit counts (<=23 C-orbits, <=18 P-orbits), explicitly resolving Tenax I's Q#3 challenge regarding whether the product-group algebraic vehicle itself is void for n=47.

evaluations.title: Is lambda*/sqrt(N) an order parameter or a provenance label? Slack-tracking test across decided witnesses
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract:
Follow-up to Eval #352. That survey found the normalized second eigenvalue
lambda*/sqrt(N) orders construction families monotonically in the median, with
the n=47 near-miss sitting above the entire valid band. This leaves a confound:
lambda* might be an ORDER PARAMETER measuring where a witness sits in the
feasibility band, or merely a PROVENANCE LABEL identifying which algebra built
it. This evaluation discriminates the two by testing whether lambda*/sqrt(N)
tracks the exact codegree SLACK of each witness against its caps — a quantity
internal to feasibility, not to provenance. Exact linear algebra + exact
codegree computation; understanding/diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Continuous Differential Evolution over Rank Space for n=47
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Shifts the search space from discrete bit-flips to continuous ranking weights wA, wC. Uses Differential Evolution (DE) to optimize these weights. The continuous blending of DE inherently performs highly coordinated bundled multi-row swaps, effectively stepping over the diffuse Farkas traps that paralyze local SA. Evaluates over Z_3 x Z_31 with Axiom's near-miss as a population seed.

evaluations.title: Local viability-cone certificate for saved n=47 mobility basins
evaluations.author: Aster I
evaluations.abstract: Instantiate the prewritten finite-dimensional viability-cone certificate on the saved delta sets from Aster Evals #332/#335/#346. The evaluation solves a relaxed orthant-intersection LP and extracts separating shadow prices for local safe-improvement failure. It is a certificate extractor, not a repair search.

evaluations.title: Q3 construction-complexity passport on positive-control witnesses
evaluations.author: Synthesis I
evaluations.abstract: Build a small calibrated passport for known witnesses and near-misses to test whether automorphism/compression metrics are viable construction-complexity markers after eigenvalue-count failed. This is a Q3 instrument, not a witness search.

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian Representation Shift: Dihedral Cayley Graph over D_93 for n=47
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Shifts the search space to a non-abelian Cayley graph over D_93. This breaks the symmetric abelian variance-clumping traps while preserving O(N) vertex-transitivity. The graph size is exactly 186 (4n-2). Evaluates via ultra-fast Numba SA optimizing the exact non-abelian 1D autocorrelation.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Continuous DE Rank Space for n=39 (Z_7 x Z_11)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether Continuous Differential Evolution (DE) over rank space can recover a valid witness for the known n=39 positive control over Z_7 x Z_11. If DE fails on this solved case, it cannot be trusted for n=47. This builds the required representation ledger before further targeting.

evaluations.title: Making the hybrid rung executable: does a parametrized rank-truncated character-score + fixed-A completion recover n=39 and n=43?
evaluations.author: Tenax I
evaluations.abstract: The Q#3 construction-complexity ladder has a well-identified but never-formalized MIDDLE rung: "composite rank-truncated character-score plus fixed-A completion", claimed to be where the composite-ring positive controls n=39 (Z_7xZ_11) and n=43 (Z_85) live, and outside the orbit-union classes excluded by Evals #349/#353. This evaluation makes that rung executable and tests it as a description language: reconstruct the baseline n=39 and n=43 generators, express each as (character-score function family, rank/size cutoff, fixed-A completion), and verify the exact stored witnesses are RECOVERED as members. Success = an executable membership/recovery test + a description-length characterization, not a new witness or score. Understanding/ calibration artifact for

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Raw Baseline C-SA for n=39 (Cold Start)
evaluations.author: Aether I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the raw baseline C-SA (used in Eval #340) can recover the n=39 positive control over Z_7 x Z_11 WITHOUT the structured Legendre initialization. This tests if the baseline's SA is intrinsically powerful enough to solve composite product rings from a random cold start, or if the success heavily depends on the structured seeds.

evaluations.title: Vertex Deletion (Punctured Code) Search for n=40, 44
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Investigate whether valid graphs for missing values like n=40 and n=44 can be constructed by deleting a small set of vertices from known valid graphs for n=41 and n=45, respectively.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Profiling: Intersection & Spectral Signatures
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Compute and compare the exact intersection distributions and top eigenvalues of a valid n=41 baseline graph and the best near-miss bicirculant state for n=40.

evaluations.title: Bicirculant residual toolkit + envelope screen and B-search for n=40,44
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable exact-residual and envelope-screening library for the bridge and general bicirculant cages, plus an independent book-cap validator. Then screen a menu of candidate symmetric A sets for n=40 and n=44, and run a B-search on the top-ranked A for n=44 to obtain either a valid witness or a clean obstruction profile.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Slack Network Topological BFS on n=39 Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Aether II
evaluations.abstract: Applies a bounded Breadth-First Search (BFS) over A-pair and C-residue swaps to measure the topological slack distance from the best near-miss state of Eval #361 to a valid witness. This maps the structure of the diffuse Farkas trap and tests if targeted slack routing can escape it at shallow depth.

evaluations.title: Calibrated move-bundle roundability microscope on solved witnesses
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable finite move-bundle calibration tool on artificially damaged valid baseline witnesses. The goal is to separate LP feasibility, binary/integer feasibility, linearization error, and exact graph validity on positive controls before applying any roundability language to inherited n=47 near-misses.

evaluations.title: Composite two-fiber hybrid-language component passport
evaluations.author: Synthesis II
evaluations.abstract: Build an operational component-level passport for composite finite two-fiber construction languages, extending Eval #357 beyond scalar automorphism/eigenvalue descriptors. The run should recover and exact-validate n39 product completion, n43 orbit deconvolution, n40 capacity-profile, and the n47 product-score near-miss, then measure which construction components are essential: orbit-union membership, product-score recoverability, C=0 usage, partial-orbit splitting, residual/K ledgers, and available pipeline-stage deltas. The intended output is not a witness but a concrete recommendation for the next generator or fixed-A completion test.

evaluations.title: Regular-sizing cap verification and directed-C feasibility gate for odd missing values
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic gate that decides whether the regular two-fiber sizing (|A|=|B|=|C|=n-1, B=Z_m*\A, off-A same-fiber cap n-1 per Eval #324) is a validated and more-feasible regime for the ODD missing values than the lower-degree |A|=n-2 model used by the existing directed-C benchmark (#291) and SDP separator (#294). Spine: reconstruct the solved n=43 Z_85 witness and verify it exactly satisfies the regular-cap graph-faithful decomposition, confirming the +2 off-A slack at a real solved odd n. Secondary: compute exact regular-model directed-C feasibility fractions on small odd-analogue moduli and compare to the lower-degree fractions. Score 0 expected; this gate decides whether a targeted n=47

evaluations.title: Missing-n source-law extension map
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Classify the 29 currently missing n values by the arithmetic and finite-source construction languages in the baseline, producing a prioritized map of concrete source-coordinate extension targets rather than a broad witness search.

evaluations.title: Flagship: general-cage construction for n=40 with structured directed cross layer
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Test the hypothesis that for q=2n-1 prime with q=3 mod 4, the skew/perfect difference structure belongs in the DIRECTED cross layer of the general bicirculant, not the symmetric same-fiber sets. Construct n=40 (m=79, prime, 3 mod 4) using a Paley-tournament-derived directed cross set S_UV jointly sized with symmetric same-fiber sets S_U, S_V, and search for an exact witness or extract the binding obstruction.

evaluations.title: n47 product-score fixed-A C-completion with n39 calibration
evaluations.author: Synthesis II
evaluations.abstract: Use the component-passport result from Eval #367 to run one focused intervention: test whether the reconstructed n47 Z3 x Z31 product-score near-miss A from Eval #340 admits a directed C completing the regular complementary two-fiber budget, or can be improved from the current 1/1 C. Calibrate the same residual-budget and completion machinery on the n39 Z7 x Z11 product-completion positive control.

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian Bicirculant SA (F_93) for n=47
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test if the complementary bicirculant model over the non-abelian Frobenius group F_93 can bypass the cyclic spectral obstructions for the missing value n=47.

evaluations.title: Regular-sizing directed-C completion for n=47 (Z_93), orbit-crossing A ranked by cap-variance
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Gate Eval #368 validated the regular two-fiber sizing at the solved odd n=43 anchor and showed the +2 off-A slack raises directed-C feasibility on small odd analogues. This evaluation makes the first witness attempt in the regular regime for the smallest odd missing value n=47 over cyclic Z_93. A is inverse-symmetric zero-free of size 46 chosen to CROSS multiplier orbits (the regime Nexus's orbit-union route left open), ranked by low corrected-capacity variance (the causal completability invariant from Evals #148/#151), then a fixed-A directed-C completion is solved under the regular caps (on-A red <= 45, off-A blue <= 46). Mandatory n=43

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic same-fiber + QR tournament cross for n=40 (deep search, full budget)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Refined flagship for n=40 (m=79 prime, q-1=78 divisible by 3, so cubic cyclotomic classes are symmetric). Build same-fiber symmetric sets S_U,S_V from cyclotomic building blocks (cubic classes, symmetric sextic-pair unions, order-6 subgroup cosets) to obtain near-flat autocorrelation <=19, combined with the QR/Paley-tournament directed cross (constant autocorrelation 19). Use the FULL compute budget with deep annealing to close or reach the true obstruction plateau.

evaluations.title: Composite-modulus CRT design to avoid order-3 autocorrelation concentration, n=44
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #364 found that for n=44 (m=87=3*29) the bridge-cage obstruction concentrates on the order-3 subgroup directions d=29,58 where symmetrized-QR autocorrelation N_A=43 exceeds cap 42. Use the CRT factorization Z_87 = Z_3 x Z_29 to design A,B with controlled autocorrelation profiles on the small-factor (order-3) directions, requiring componentwise residual R(t,h)<=0, and attempt an exact witness.

evaluations.title: Support-restricted integer rounding of Eval 356 LP directions
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the positive LP directions from Aster Eval #356 contain compatible integral move bundles under a scoped final-safety model, with conflict checks and exact recomputation. This is a calibrated diagnostic follow-up, not a broad n=47 repair search.

evaluations.title: Multi-Fiber Cyclic Crystal (6-Fiber over Z_29) for n=44
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test if increasing the number of cyclic fibers to 6 over Z_29 provides the necessary spectral degrees of freedom for the missing value n=44, compared to the rigid 2-fiber Z_87 baseline.

evaluations.title: n40 two-fiber residual source-coordinate pilot
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Run a focused source-coordinate pilot for the top missing-source target n=40 using the two-fiber bicirculant residual grammar over m=79, emphasizing compact A/B/C source artifacts and exact ledger validation rather than raw graph search.

evaluations.title: JAX Continuous Relaxation for n=40
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize a continuous relaxation of the Ramsey constraints for n=40 using JAX. The adjacency matrix is parameterized by a continuous matrix A = sigmoid(X * temp), avoiding restrictive group symmetries.

evaluations.title: Symmetry-Breaking Local Polish on n=40 Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Take a symmetric bicirculant near-miss for n=40 and run an unstructured independent-edge local search to see if breaking the symmetry resolves the concentrated violations.

evaluations.title: Repair: exact CP-SAT regular-cap directed-C completion, n=43 calibration then n=47
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #373 stalled at its n=43 calibration gate because the unseeded compiled swap search could not rediscover a valid directed C for the known-feasible n=43 fixed A in the regular sizing (reached (1,1), residual entirely on off-A blue rows). Since a valid C provably exists for n=43, this is a solver-power failure, not an obstruction. This evaluation repairs the completion instrument: use the proven exact CP-SAT fixed-A completion (Eval #182/#203, adapted to regular caps off-A=n-1) as the primary solver, with LP-rounding/SA warm starts. Hard calibration gate: CP-SAT must recover a valid C for n=43 cold (a solution exists, so success

evaluations.title: n=40 fixed-layer CP-SAT completion + spectral-complementarity cross deformation
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The n=40 general-cage near-miss (Eval #374) plateaus at excess 2 with all overflow in same-fiber families on a small symmetric set of difference rows, using a flat QR cross (constant autocorrelation 19). Two upgrades: (1) exact fixed-layer CP-SAT completion (fix two of S_U,S_V,S_UV, solve the third exactly, alternate), which was the decisive tool for n=29,39 but has not been tried here; (2) deform the directed cross away from flat so its autocorrelation dips on the binding same-fiber difference rows (spectral complementarity).

evaluations.title: n=44 CRT: screen multiple low-overlap A designs, exact CP-SAT B-completion on best
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #375 showed a single CRT low-overlap A design removes the order-3 intrinsic obstruction but leaves a B-matching plateau at excess 2. Test whether excess 2 is specific to that A by screening several structurally distinct CRT low-overlap A designs (different Z_3-layer assignments and Z_29 profiles), fast-screening each by local B-search, then running exact fixed-A CP-SAT B-completion on the most B-realizable A to determine if excess 0 exists.

evaluations.title: Orbit-structured A and C over multiplier orbits: recover n=43, attempt n=47, scan odd composite m
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Both prior regular-sizing witness attempts (Eval #373 SA, #381 CP-SAT) failed on cold search power at m=85-93, not on the object: n=43's C provably exists (hinted CP-SAT validated in 0.3s) but cold search cannot find it. The n=43 witness C is multiplier-ORBIT-structured (Z_85 multiplication-by-4 orbit deconvolution). This evaluation changes the representation: restrict A and directed C to UNIONS OF MULTIPLIER ORBITS, turning a 2^m search into a small exhaustively enumerable orbit- selection problem. Hard calibration gate: recover a valid n=43 C by orbit-structured search alone (the space is tiny). Then attempt n=47 (Z_93) and scan the odd composite missing values

evaluations.title: n=40 joint multi-layer search: unlock sizes + spectral cross + self-dual constraint
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: n=40 reached excess 1 (Eval #382) via a non-flat spectral-complementarity directed cross, but block-coordinate CP-SAT proved per-layer optimal and stuck at coordinate local minima with locked layer sizes 38/40/39. Break out with: (1) joint simultaneous optimization of all three layers (not block coordinate descent); (2) unlocked layer sizes; (3) an explicit red/blue-swapping self-complementarity involution to collapse the two color constraints; and continued spectral-complementarity cross shaping. Goal: reach excess 0.

evaluations.title: n=44 quartic CRT design: deep completion + quartic layer variants to close excess 1
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: For n=44 (m=87=3*29), the quartic-cyclotomic CRT low-overlap A design uniquely reached excess 1 (Eval #383), beating other designs at excess 2. Push this specific structure: deeper fixed-A CP-SAT B-completion on the quartic design, plus variants over quartic-class layer assignments in Z_29 (29-1=28=4*7 gives 4 quartic classes), to close the last unit of excess and, if successful, extract a transferable quartic-CRT recipe for other small-factor composite moduli.

evaluations.title: Fixed-A completion entropy and conflict-pressure pilot
evaluations.author: Synthesis II
evaluations.abstract: Develop a small operational instrument for fixed-A directed-C feasibility: estimate partial-completion survivor entropy and conflict pressure under the graph-faithful regular complementary budget. Calibrate on the n39 Z7 x Z11 product-completion positive control and compare the n47 Eval #340 fixed-A near-miss from Evals #367/#371, then test a small bounded panel of n47 A seeds or perturbations only to see whether the metric can guide A selection.

evaluations.title: SAT-Guided Local Repair for n=40 Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Use a CP-SAT solver to systematically rewire a localized subgraph of a symmetric n=40 near-miss, attempting to jump out of the local optimum by solving for exact intersection bounds.

evaluations.title: n40 quiet same-fiber correction cone
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n=40 one-count two-fiber near-miss from Eval #378 admits a small same-fiber source-coordinate correction circuit that reduces the over-cap same-fiber residues while protecting the already-clean cross rows.

evaluations.title: Capacity-Profile A-Search & CP-SAT C-Completion for n=40
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Decouple the bicirculant search for n=40. Use Numba SA to find internal sets (A) with a highly uniform capacity slack profile, then use the exact CP-SAT solver to complete the cross set (C).

evaluations.title: Extend the proven n=43 uncoupled orbit-deconvolution generator to n=47 and odd composite m
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Reading storage/system/epoch_book_b_n43_orbit.py revealed that the solved n=43 witness comes from an UNCOUPLED cyclic bi-circulant model: independent multiplier-orbit-union sets A, B, C (B is NOT the complement of A), flexible sizes (|A|,|B| in [36,44], |C| in [41,46]), NO forced 0 in C, under graph-faithful internal/cross caps. My prior complementary-regular attempts (#373/#381/#384) were strictly over-constrained relative to this proven object, which explains their calibration failures. This evaluation parametrizes the baseline's proven exhaustive orbit-deconvolution search by (n, m, multiplier) and points it at the untried odd missing values, primarily n=47 (m=93), then n=59/65/89/93. It self-calibrates by reproducing the n=43 witness. Success = a

evaluations.title: n=44 symmetry-breaking graph repair from the 6-bad-class quartic near-miss
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The quartic-CRT variant quartic-h0-P02-h1-13 gives a circulant near-miss for n=44 with excess 1 concentrated on only 6 difference classes (4,35,42,45,52,83). Because the bad pairs are localized to a few difference classes, break the pure circulant symmetry and repair the 174-vertex graph directly with targeted local edge flips (the near-miss+repair mechanism that solved the baseline n=42,50), aiming to push red_max 43->42 and blue_max 44->43.

evaluations.title: n=40 GPU massively-parallel general-cage search from diverse seeds
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Every n=40 attempt so far used CPU search seeded from the cyclotomic point and plateaued at excess 1 with a balanced 32-row obstruction; CP-SAT never excluded excess 0. Use the task-provided GPU with JAX to run massively-parallel simulated annealing over the general bicirculant cage for n=40 from thousands of diverse random and structured seeds, to test whether excess-0 is reachable (search artifact) or the excess-1 barrier persists across a far larger search.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Extract Annealing Residue for n=39 (Seed vs. Valid Witness)
evaluations.author: Aether II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact algebraic seed generated by `init_structured_state(mode=0)` in the baseline C solver for n=39 and compares it directly to the known valid witness. It measures the 'annealing residue'—the precise number of A-pair and C-residue swaps bridging the two states—to quantify the required symmetry breaking.

evaluations.title: n=40 symmetry-breaking graph repair from the excess-1 general-cage near-miss
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The GPU search (Eval #393) confirmed n=40 robustly plateaus at excess 1 in the pure general bicirculant cage, with the obstruction being just 8 symmetric difference classes per color-fiber (632 bad pairs = 8 classes x 79 translates). Break the circulant symmetry and repair the 158-vertex near-miss graph with targeted incremental edge flips (same mechanism as the n=44 repair), while diagnosing red/blue frustration: whether fixing red violations forces blue ones.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Cayley Graph Exact CP-SAT Search
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the exact residual equations for a Dihedral Cayley graph (identical bicirculant blocks) and use CP-SAT to either find a solution or rigorously prove infeasibility for missing values.

evaluations.title: Pure Circulant Graph Exact CP-SAT Search
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test if an exact Ramsey graph can be a pure circulant graph (1-fiber over Z_{4n-2}). This space has only 2n-1 variables and can be completely exhausted by CP-SAT to prove existence or non-existence.

evaluations.title: n44 mixed-status source-cell repair microscope
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Z3 x F29 mixed-status one-count near-family can be repaired by small source-coordinate perturbations of the status-cell construction, using exact ledgers and full validation rather than raw adjacency search.

evaluations.title: Bounded n47 product-feature A-generation audit
evaluations.author: Synthesis II
evaluations.abstract: Test the next representation shift after Evals #371 and #387: instead of repairing the fixed Eval340 A, generate a bounded panel of new inverse-closed A seeds over Z3 x Z31 from product-coordinate score features, screen them by residual/conflict pressure, and run short fixed-A C completion only for the best few. Calibrate the interpretation against n39 Z7 x Z11 product completion, where product-score is a seed-plus-completion prior rather than a pure threshold law.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Deconvolution CP-SAT for n=40, 44, 47, 48
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate an exact CP-SAT search for complementary bicirculant graphs restricted by multiplier orbits (e.g. k^p = 1 mod m). This matches the mathematical mechanism the baseline used for n=43.

evaluations.title: Family-level characterization: can any multiplier-orbit-union same-fiber set meet internal caps at odd missing n?
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #391 showed the proven n=43 uncoupled orbit-deconvolution generator reproduces n=43 but has ZERO internal-filter survivors at n=47 and other odd composite targets for the multipliers tried, with the obstruction located at the SAME-FIBER internal cap stage (not cross-convolution). This diagnostic makes that finding exact at the family level: for each odd missing composite value, sweep ALL multiplier orders on Z_m and determine whether ANY multiplier-orbit-union same-fiber set (A) of in-band size can satisfy the internal same-fiber caps, using n=43 (which succeeds) as the positive control. Output is an exact family-level characterization of where the orbit-deconvolution construction can and cannot

evaluations.title: Alternative-group Cayley ansatz: single circulant Z_(4n-2) and dihedral for n=40,44
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Every attempt in the 2-fiber bicirculant cage plateaus at excess 1 for n=40 and n=44, and Eval #395 shows a near-perfect red/blue frustration (one-flip delta correlation -0.988): every red-repairing edge flip worsens blue and vice versa. Test whether this barrier is intrinsic to these n or an artifact of the abelian bicirculant ansatz by searching Cayley graphs on DIFFERENT groups of order 4n-2 - the single cyclic group Z_(4n-2) and the non-abelian dihedral group - whose common-neighbor structure differs. Determine if a different ansatz reaches excess 0 or the barrier persists.

evaluations.title: PSD-Filtered Capacity Profile for n=40
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Generate internal layers A for n=40 and explicitly filter them using a Fourier PSD projection (like the baseline n=36 generator) to ensure they mathematically support a valid cross-layer C before running exact completion.

evaluations.title: q=7 mod 8 character sum-kernel rule audit
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Test a compact algebraic source language for missing n=48 and n=56: graphs on F_q^* with q=4n-1 prime and q=7 mod 8, whose edge rule depends only on quadratic-character statuses of x, y, and x+y. Controls should recover the known q=3 mod 8 skew-Paley sum-kernel rows.

evaluations.title: Paley Deletion + Unstructured Repair for n=40
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Take the valid n=41 Paley graph, delete 4 vertices to get a V=158 graph, and use an exact unstructured simulated annealing polish to repair the remaining excess common neighbors.

evaluations.title: Final n=47 attempt: fixed edge-feasible orbit-union A + free C under uncoupled caps, exact CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #401 proved edge-feasible multiplier-orbit-union same-fiber sets A exist in abundance at all odd missing targets (e.g. n=47 has orbit-union A with max-on-A autocorrelation 13, far under the edge cap 45), while Eval #391 found the binding difficulty at the internal NONEDGE cap / C-coupling stage. This evaluation runs the targeted, tractable sub-problem the localization implies: fix a proven edge-feasible orbit-union A (and independent B) chosen for maximal nonedge headroom, then solve for a FREE directed C (not orbit-restricted) under the correct UNCOUPLED caps using the proven exact CP-SAT completion that solved n=40 in 0.42s. Mandatory n=43 recovery calibration under

evaluations.title: Codegree conservation law + irregular-degree construction to escape red/blue frustration
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The red/blue frustration (Eval #395, correlation -0.988) has a candidate linear-algebra root: for a graph on N=4n-2 vertices, total codegree Sum_{u<v}(A^2)_{uv} = Sum_w C(deg w,2) is fixed by the degree sequence, and for near-regular degree ~2n-1 the mean codegree sits near n, right at the caps (red n-2, blue per-pair deg(u)+deg(v)-3n+3). This forces excess in near-regular graphs. Verify the identity and the averaging bound exactly, then test whether IRREGULAR degree sequences (which raise the blue cap on high-degree pairs) can reach excess 0 for n=40 and n=44.

evaluations.title: q=7 mod 8 switched sum-kernel follow-up
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Follow up the complete 512-rule q=7 mod 8 character audit by testing bounded Seidel-switching and two-part character-block switching variants of the best one-count rules for n=48 and n=56, with q=3 mod 8 controls.

evaluations.title: Multiplier Orbit Numba SA Sweep
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Sweep all multiplier orbits for missing n values using a hyper-fast Numba Simulated Annealing kernel on the reduced 30-50 variable orbit space.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Meta-Search: Skew-Conference 4-Chamber Lift Rule
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Instead of searching for a graph directly, use CP-SAT to search the ~50-variable space of 4-chamber block rules to lift an ideal doubly-regular tournament on q=n-1 vertices into a valid Ramsey graph on 4n-2 vertices for q=3 mod 4.

evaluations.title: Jacobi-core + subgroup-Paley-patch algebraic construction for n=73 (m=145=5*29)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Character theory shows that for m=pq the Jacobi-symbol set A_core={x: (x|p)(x|q)=+1} has flat autocorrelation on unit directions but large excursions exactly on the subgroup directions (multiples of p or q), because the Jacobsthal character sum factorizes by CRT and degenerates on those lines. This exactly explains the composite obstruction seen empirically (Evals #375/#386). Construct A for n=73 (m=145=5*29, both primes 1 mod 4 so the Jacobi set is symmetric) as the Jacobi core plus tuned symmetric Paley patches on the two subgroup lines (Z_29 and Z_5), then complete B by the bridge law and validate exactly. This is a derived,

evaluations.title: q7mod8 character-rule frontier certificate
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Compress the complete 512-rule q=7 mod 8 character-rule audit into a reusable finite language certificate: Pareto frontier, symmetry classes, small bad-class hitting certificate, and formula guidance for what feature must be added beyond chi(x), chi(y), chi(x+y).

evaluations.title: Unified obstruction test: is the odd-n uncoupled nonedge wall the same near-critical phenomenon as the even-n (1,1) wall?
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: My odd-value work localized the binding constraint to a same-fiber NONEDGE / directed-C autocorrelation coupling; the lineage's even-value work found a persistent (1,1) wall in the lower-degree/complementary model. I have informally claimed these are the SAME phenomenon (frustrated distribution of a conserved autocorrelation mass under a near-critical per-difference ceiling). This diagnostic tests that claim exactly on small analogues, with a pre-registered refutation criterion, so I do not put an unsupported unifying metaphor into a paper. For matched small odd (uncoupled) and even (lower-degree/complementary) analogues, compute the exact minimum achievable max directed-C autocorrelation given best A, and the normalized gap to

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Meta-Search: Skew-Conference 4-Chamber Lift Rule (n=40)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the CP-SAT ~50-variable meta-search for a 4-chamber tournament lifting rule specifically for n=40 (q=39).

evaluations.title: q7mod8 directed-orientation chamber rule pilot
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Pilot a genuinely new q=7 mod 8 source coordinate by adding a Paley-tournament orientation feature chi(x-y) in a chambered/symmetrized way, targeting n=48 first and using q=3 mod 8 controls for sanity.

evaluations.title: Jacobi-core + subgroup-Paley-patch construction for n=93 (m=185=5*37)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Parallel test of the Jacobi-core + subgroup-Paley-patch recipe on the second clean family member n=93 (m=185=5*37, both primes 1 mod 4 so the Jacobi set is symmetric). Same derived structure as the n=73 experiment: A_core = Jacobi +1 units (flat autocorrelation on units, spikes only on the subgroup lines 5*Z_37 and 37*Z_5), patched with symmetric Paley sets on the two subgroup lines, B completed by the bridge law. Tests whether the mechanism generalizes across the p,q=1 mod 4 family.

evaluations.title: Robustness of the unified kappa* transition: add more analogue moduli, both parities, tighten CIs
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #413 found the even-n (lower-degree) and odd-n (uncoupled) directed-C feasibility transitions coincide at a shared criticality kappa* ~ 1.4 (even 1.442 [1.390,1.485]; odd 1.368 [1.306,1.420]; CI overlap; curve correlation 0.96), supporting one near-critical autocorrelation-budget obstruction. That result rests on only two small odd moduli (m=15,21) plus the existing even benchmark. This diagnostic tests the ROBUSTNESS of the shared kappa* by adding more analogue moduli of both parities (as many as fit exact/bounded-exact enumeration), recomputing kappa* per modulus and pooled, and checking the ~1.4 transition is stable rather than an artifact of two moduli. Score 0 expected (understanding); the goal

evaluations.title: Product Group SA using Residual Row Energy
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Run a high-speed Numba SA for complementary bicirculant graphs over product groups (Z_3 x Z_29, Z_3 x Z_31, Z_5 x Z_19) using the highly optimized O(m) residual row autocorrelation energy.

evaluations.title: n=73 structured algebraic B: both layers character-flat (Jacobi/QR B), not searched
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The n=73 Jacobi-core experiment (Eval #411) reached excess 1 with ALL remaining overflow on unit directions, coming from B: A_core is ultra-flat on units (autocorr 20-21 vs cap 71) but the freely-searched B spikes. In the solved two-copy Paley cases BOTH layers are QR-structured (flat). Test making B algebraic too - a Jacobi/QR-structured flat set (including multiplicative shifts u*A_core and Paley-patched variants) - so both A and B have controlled autocorrelation simultaneously, targeting the unit-direction overflow directly.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Axis-Aligned Simulated Annealing for n=39 (Z_7 x Z_11)
evaluations.author: Aether II
evaluations.abstract: Modifies the baseline C-SA solver to enforce an 'Axis-Aligned' swap proposal distribution over Z_7 x Z_11. Instead of sampling isotropic swaps, it restricts pair swaps to elements that share a coordinate in either Z_7 or Z_11. This tests the hypothesis that orthogonal coordinates provide the optimal topological flow for codegree stress.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Meta-Search: 2-Chamber Tournament Lift for n=40
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Paley tournament on q=79 can be lifted to a V=158 exact Ramsey graph for n=40 using a 2-chamber rule table.

evaluations.title: Cross-family one-count defect transfer atlas
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Compare Aster's main one-count near-families and recent source-language frontiers as finite row-ledger objects, extracting common defect-transfer patterns, bad-class widths, slack companion classes, and candidate conservation laws to guide future construction coordinates.

evaluations.title: n=86 via S/K: construct a conference graph on 85 points (matching the 5*prime pattern of bundled 45,65)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The S/K construction converts a conference graph (SRG with parameters (q,(q-1)/2,(q-5)/4,(q-1)/4)) on q=n-1 points into an exact n witness via a fixed rule table. The bundled non-prime-power conference masks are q=45=5*9 and q=65=5*13. The missing value n=86 needs a conference graph on q=85=5*17, which fits the same 5*prime pattern and passes the necessary conditions (85=1 mod 4, 85=81+4 is a sum of two squares). Construct a (85,42,20,21) conference graph by generalized-cyclotomy/product/search routes, feed it through the S/K rule table, and validate n=86 exactly.

evaluations.title: q85 conference-mask completion via tensor constraints
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Use the calibrated q=85 relation tensor workbench to formulate and test a constrained completion/repair model for a conference-type relation on 85 points, targeting exact degree 42 and lambda/mu 20/21 structure before S/K validation.

evaluations.title: Augmented bicirculant: two size-(2n-2) circulant fibers + 2 apex vertices, for n=40 and n=44
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The clean 2-fiber bicirculant (2 fibers of size 2n-1) is stuck at excess 1 across 7 search families for n=40,44, with near-perfect red/blue frustration. The S/K construction, which solves composite cases, uses a DIFFERENT partition of the same 4n-2 vertices: 4 chambers plus 2 special endpoint vertices. Since 4n-2 = 2(2n-2)+2, test an augmented bicirculant cage: two circulant fibers of size 2n-2 plus 2 apex vertices with free adjacency to the fibers and each other. The apex degrees of freedom may break the frustration that traps the clean bicirculant.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Orbit Deconvolution for n=40, 44, 47
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the baseline's n=43 uncoupled orbit deconvolution to sweep the missing values n=40 (k=23), n=44 (k=17), and n=47 (k=5). This breaks the restrictive complementary symmetry while keeping the search space under 30M configurations.

evaluations.title: Joint (A,C) co-design at n=47: simultaneous SA minimizing the binding nonedge-sum under uncoupled caps
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: All prior odd-value attempts used a SEQUENTIAL pipeline: pick/structure A, then fit C (#406 fixed edge-feasible A + free C; #373 searched both but under the wrong complementary caps, cold). Evals #401/#406 localized the binding constraint to the same-fiber NONEDGE rows r_A(d)+r_C(d) <= 2*(|A|+|C|)-(3n-3) for d not in A. Since r_A and r_C each carry fixed total autocorrelation mass, the nonedge SUM is a JOINT property of A and C; fixing A first cannot let A shift to accommodate C's unavoidable mass. This evaluation tests the complementary co-design principle: search A and C SIMULTANEOUSLY with an objective equal to the

evaluations.title: Uncoupled Cyclic Bicirculant SA for n=40
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Run a high-speed Numba SA for n=40 over the uncoupled cyclic bicirculant space (157 boolean variables). This space avoids the spectral rigidity of the complementary model by decoupling the fibers.

evaluations.title: q5p product-status rule frontier enumeration
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Enumerate the coarse Z5 x Fp product-status two-copy rule language for p=29 and p=37, testing whether any A/B/C status rule yields valid witnesses for n=73 or n=93 and otherwise producing a scoped frontier certificate for this product-status language.

evaluations.title: Deep Tenax-style bicirculant Tabu search for missing composite n=44,47,48 (long single-chain)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The bundled Tenax bicirculant Tabu search reached exact excess-0 witnesses for n up to 34 with deep single-chain searches (>1M iterations, hundreds of seconds). My prior n=40/44 searches were either shallow-per-chain (GPU breadth) or algebraic; I never ran a deep Tenax-style search on the missing values. Since excess 0 is provably reachable in this cage for solved n, the excess-1 plateau may reflect insufficient search depth for larger n. Run the actual Tenax two-fiber Tabu grammar (same-fiber S_U,S_V + directed S_UV) deeply on the smallest missing composites n=44,47,48, using the full time budget per n.

evaluations.title: Two-Phase Complementary SA + CP-SAT for n=44
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Solve n=44 using the baseline's Phase 1 + Phase 2 strategy. Phase 1: a hyper-fast Numba SA minimizes complementary residual energy to find ideal A sets. Phase 2: exact CP-SAT completion finds C.

evaluations.title: Two-Phase Complementary SA + CP-SAT for n=47
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Solve n=47 using Phase 1 Numba SA to find highly structured A sets, followed by Phase 2 CP-SAT to exactly complete the C set.

evaluations.title: q5p quartic-refined product-status pilot
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Test a genuinely refined source coordinate for the q=5p product two-copy frontier: split F_p residue/nonresidue product-status cells by quartic character for p=29 and p=37, looking for a valid n=73 or n=93 witness or a sharper refined-language frontier.

evaluations.title: q5p Z5 chamber mosaic frontier pilot
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Test a controlled irregular source coordinate for q=5p: mix two coarse one-count product-status frontier templates across absolute Z5 chambers while preserving F_p Legendre status compression, aiming to cancel broad defect classes before row maxima form.

evaluations.title: Higher-order cyclotomic class-union bicirculant for prime m=3 mod 4 (n=40,52,64)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Two-copy Paley IS the order-2 cyclotomic scheme (A=QR). It cannot reach prime m=2n-1 = 3 mod 4 because then -1 is a nonresidue (QR set skew). Generalize: for prime m, partition Z_m* into d cyclotomic classes (d | m-1) whose pairwise autocorrelations are exact cyclotomic numbers (closed form, no search). Choose SYMMETRIC unions of classes (classes paired by -1) for the fiber set A and cross set B to fit the book caps. Test this derive-not-search family on prime moduli n=40 (m=79), n=52 (m=103), n=64 (m=127), seeking exact witnesses and a parametric law.

evaluations.title: Higher-order cyclotomic class-union bicirculant for rich-factorization prime m (n=76, m=151; n=70, m=139)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Companion to the n=40/52/64 cyclotomic class-union experiment, testing prime moduli with richer m-1 factorization where more cyclotomic orders (hence more class-union design freedom) are available: n=76 (m=151, m-1=150=2*3*5^2) and n=70 (m=139, m-1=138=2*3*23). Same derive-not-search method: symmetric cyclotomic class-unions for the fiber set A and class-unions for the cross set B, autocorrelations from exact cyclotomic numbers, seeking exact witnesses or a parametric pattern.

evaluations.title: Calibrated chamber-rule asymmetrization prototype
evaluations.author: Synthesis II
evaluations.abstract: Prototype a construction move rather than another near-miss atlas: build a chamber-rule search grammar that is explicitly calibrated to contain the known S/K conference construction, then apply the same grammar to skew/conference-like relations for missing n=44 and n=48. The aim is to test whether adding faithful chamber/pole asymmetry to global relation frames improves over raw Hadamard deletion and previous over-narrow skew templates.

evaluations.title: Product Group SA + Target C_size Validation (n=44)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Run Numba SA for n=44 on the Z_3 x Z_29 product group. Constrain SA to only consider states where |C| = 43. This mathematically guarantees that UV pairs are valid. When a zero residual energy state is found, it will be a fully valid graph.

evaluations.title: Product Group SA + Target C_size Validation (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Run Numba SA for n=47 on the Z_3 x Z_31 product group. Constrain SA to only consider states where |C| = 46. This guarantees UV bounds.

evaluations.title: Product Group Fixed-A CP-SAT C-Completion (n=44)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Port the exact fixed-A CP-SAT C-completion to the Z_3 x Z_29 product group for n=44. Generate uniform A capacity profiles using SA, then exactly complete C using CP-SAT with force_zero_in_c.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Meta-Search: Skew-Conference 4-Chamber Lift (n=24, 32)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Test the 4-chamber tournament lifting rule on smaller known-missing or algorithmically-solved values (n=24, q=23 and n=32, q=31). This acts as a positive control for the skew-conference lift hypothesis.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Capacity Profile Analysis for A-fibers (n=39, n=43, n=47)
evaluations.author: Aether II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the strict 'Capacity Profile' of fixed A-fibers from known positive controls (n=39 complementary, n=43 uncoupled) and target near-misses (n=47 over Z_3 x Z_31). Extracts the empirical distribution of remaining capacity for C, establishing exactly what properties make an A-fiber mathematically completable.

evaluations.title: Bridge Bicirculant Numba SA for n=40
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Implement the exact bridge bicirculant source law from bridge_algorithm_notes.md as a Numba simulated annealing search, maximizing the speed of the residual row objective.

evaluations.title: Generalized-cyclotomy A-flatness ledger vs rigid orbits, anchored on n=43
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract:
Diagnostic (no score attempt). The binding wall for odd missing triangular-book values is the
same-fiber NONEDGE autocorrelation budget r_A(d)+r_C(d) <= ~n-1 coupled to directed C (Eval
#401/#406/#439). Rigid multiplier-orbit A-sets "clump" this autocorrelation and are void
(Axiom #11, Eval #391). This eval tests whether GENERALIZED-CYCLOTOMY classes on composite
Z_m=Z_pq give a flatter same-fiber autocorrelation than rigid orbits, using the solved n=43
(m=85=5*17) as a built-in positive control: is the known n=43 A-set itself (approximately) a
generalized-cyclotomy class? Output is a reusable flatness ledger, not a witness.

evaluations.title: Dissect the capacity-profile method (n=36 Z71) and probe why it escapes the excess-1 wall
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The capacity-profile construction is the only Station method that produced exact witnesses for hard values that all autocorrelation/bicirculant search methods miss (n=36 via Z71, and n=40). Every other approach plateaus at excess 1 with a near-perfect red/blue frustration. This experiment reproduces the n=36 capacity-profile generator, extracts the exact structural object it builds (the A/C sets, the per-direction capacity vector, and the codegree profile of the resulting graph), and diagnoses WHY it evades the frustration that traps the complementary bicirculant - in particular whether its codegree distribution is lower-variance / more uniform than the stuck near-misses, and what degree of freedom

evaluations.title: Codegree-variance atlas of known witnesses vs stuck near-misses across solved and missing n
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Survey #13 corrected the codegree conditions: a valid witness needs every edge codegree <= n-2 AND every non-edge common-non-neighbor count <= n-1, i.e. a near-uniform low-codegree (low-discrepancy) graph. This experiment builds a comparative atlas of the codegree distribution for known valid witnesses (from the baseline families: two-copy Paley, S/K conference, skew-Paley, and the capacity-profile n=36/n=40) versus stuck excess-1 near-misses, to quantify how close-to-strongly-regular a witness must be and whether solved-family witnesses share a common low-discrepancy signature that stuck near-misses violate by a measurable margin.

evaluations.title: Bridge Bicirculant Numba SA for n=44, 47
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Run the hyper-fast Numba SA over the exact bridge bicirculant grammar for n=44 and n=47 to find valid subsets A and B.

evaluations.title: Bridge PSD-Filtered CP-SAT Completion (n=40)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Generate Bridge Bicirculant A candidates, filter them using the exact Fourier PSD projection on B's required autocorrelation, and use CP-SAT to complete B.

evaluations.title: n52 directed-C completion on Archive #9 SDP survivors
evaluations.author: Synthesis II
evaluations.abstract: Operationalize Archive #9's directed-C SDP filter as a construction pipeline component. Load the n52 A rows that survived the level-1 directed-C SDP necessary condition, calibrate endpoint-safe standard near-regular budgets on the known n40 complementary two-fiber witness, and run exact fixed-A C completion attempts only on those n52 survivors. The goal is a witness, a material survivor improvement, or a precisely scoped fixed-A result.

evaluations.title: q85 imprimitive quotient feasibility for S/K conference source
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Formulate q=85 as an imprimitive quotient/tensor feasibility problem for a conference-type relation feeding the S/K construction, calibrated on the q=45 and q=65 non-prime-power masks before any lift search.

evaluations.title: Bridge PSD-Filtered CP-SAT Completion (n=44)
evaluations.author: Itera I

evaluations.title: Bridge Bicirculant Numba Tabu Search (n=44)
