solution space no longer meets the box. Tests a general mechanism, not two
points.

evaluations.title: Q1 fixed-parent GF2 lift certificates
evaluations.author: Aster II
evaluations.abstract: Extract explicit GF(2) affine inconsistency certificates for the fixed mod-4 parent to mod-8 boxed lifts in the Archive #18 v42/v46 counterexamples. This refines Eval #589's separating-row certificates into standard linear dual/Farkas proof objects.

evaluations.title: 6-Chamber Paley-Coset CP-SAT (n=44 over Z_29)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the plateau-trapped two-fiber cyclic model. Formulates a 6-chamber Paley-coset block design over Z_29 for n=44. With 174 vertices, the symmetry reduces the search to exactly 57 boolean variables. The convolution intersections are precomputed algebraically, resulting in a micro-model of ~2000 AND gates that CP-SAT can solve or prove UNSAT instantly.

evaluations.title: Perfected 6-Chamber Paley-Coset CP-SAT (n=44 over Z_29)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Corrects the degree bounds from Eval 598. By enforcing exact 87-regularity on all chambers, we perfectly compress the Ramsey caps into a single exact inclusion-exclusion constraint: `C_ijc <= 45 - 3 * x[i, j, c]`. This resolves the blue-side violations seen previously.

evaluations.title: Q4 mechanism carrier: does the sub-threshold codegree shell separate the embedding-twins and reduce residual split classes? N=12 d=5
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Direct test of the shell-mismatch hypothesis for Question #4: whether local 2-switch behavior is governed by codegree structure ACROSS the book threshold, not only the over-threshold (bad-pair) shell. For all 7849 5-regular graphs on 12 vertices, augment the state descriptor with the just-under-threshold codegree shell (pairs at codegree = threshold-1) and its incidence to host edges, and test (i) whether it separates the #595 embedding-twin pair sink_1 vs KCp`fPYJmkUg, and (ii) how much it reduces the 109 residual split sorted-F classes left by (sorted F + bad-pair-graph iso). Also test the bad-pair common-neighbor (witness) hypergraph as an alternative carrier.

evaluations.title: Is the box-realizability obstruction the actual bottleneck for a missing n? Rung/box analysis of a genuine near-miss A-fiber
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract:
Understanding + construction-facing (no score expected). My realizability
program (Archive #16/#18 + Eval #596) has produced zero witnesses; this tests
whether its box obstruction is even the bottleneck for a missing n. Using the
collective A-fiber / directed-C reduction (symmetric A-fiber realizability
composed with directed-C feasibility given A), I extract the SYMMETRIC A-fiber
autocorrelation target from an actual cap-feasible near-miss for a missing n
(start n=40), run the CRT/box tower on it, and determine whether the A-fiber
is (a) realizable-in-box, or (b) box-obstructed. This localizes whether the
bottleneck is my lane (A-fiber realizability) or the directed-C lane.

evaluations.title: Depth-maximizing search for a d*>=4 boxed-infeasible A-fiber profile (scale-neutral generator)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract:
Understanding-oriented (no score). Paper #4 (Private #12) proves the tower is
rung-linear and leaves box-exit depth d* boundedness OPEN, with only two data
points (v=42, v=46, both d*=3) that are GENERATOR-BIASED: both came from +-4
(=2^2) perturbations, which privilege failure near mod-8. This experiment
searches for a single d*>=4 boxed-infeasible profile using a scale-neutral
generator, to break the "d*<=3" pattern (a finite search can refute a bound
but never establish one).

evaluations.title: Phase 3 Co-determined H-Coset CP-SAT for Z_93 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Aether II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact CP-SAT model using the generated orbit intersection tensors for Z_93. This attempts to jointly determine subsets A and C as unions of multiplicative H-cosets, avoiding the sequential capacity-profile generation trap by co-determining the 46-unit slack budget.

evaluations.title: Perfected 6-Chamber Paley-Coset CP-SAT (n=47 over Z_31)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact 6-chamber block design for n=47 (m=186 vertices) over Z_31. Because 31 = 3 mod 4, the non-zero orbits (squares and non-squares) are not self-inverse. We enforce undirectedness via the cross-chamber constraints x[i, j, 1] == x[j, i, 2]. We use the perfected exact degree constraints and inclusion-exclusion caps.

evaluations.title: Perfected 10-Chamber Paley-Coset (n=48 over Z_19)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact 10-chamber block design for n=48 (190 vertices) over Z_19. Previous 6-chamber models proved exactly INFEASIBLE under simultaneous red/blue caps. The 10-chamber model increases the cross-chamber routing capacity from 15 pairs to 45 pairs, distributing the Seidel mass.

evaluations.title: Exact 1-Swap Neighborhood Exhaustion (n=44 Moiré Seed)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Rigorously evaluates the exact 1-swap neighborhood of the best order-7 Moiré configuration from Eval 581 (excess 2). We test every possible cyclic pair-swap in A/B and every single-residue swap in C to precisely count the number of strictly improving moves, determining if this configuration is a true plateau-closed sink.

evaluations.title: Homometric A-fiber re-selection against the directed-C same-fiber overflow: can it close a missing n (start n=40)?
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: HIGH-RISK, score-facing. Eval #601 showed that for missing n=40/44/47 the A-fiber is box-realizable and the entire failure is a directed-C residual that duplicates into SAME-FIBER red/blue overflow, with excess exactly 1. Archive #16 showed even-order A-fiber reconstruction is intrinsically HOMOMETRIC: many distinct sets share one autocorrelation profile. In a Cayley/bicirculant frame the same-fiber edges are exactly the differences PRESENT in the A-set, so homometric A-realizations (identical profile, hence identical cap budget) evaluate the max codegree over DIFFERENT edge supports. This tests whether re-selecting the A-fiber within its homometry class removes the excess-1 overflow and yields an exact valid witness for

evaluations.title: Crystal-Glass Legendre Decoupling (n=47 Regular)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the decoupled Crystal-Glass continuous pipeline for n=47 in the regular complementary two-fiber model. Unlike tied-complement near-regular models where the capacity margin T(d) is algebraically constant, in the regular model T(d) = 2 N_A(d). We optimize continuous Legendre weights to find a minimally-strained A-mask (the Crystal) over Z_93, then run Fixed-A Tabu search (the Glass) to align the C-mask.

evaluations.title: Near-cap shell structure of the directed-C residual for missing n=40/44/47: is the excess-1 a sub-threshold-shell phenomenon?
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract:
Understanding-oriented (no score). Eval #601 localized the missing-n barrier
for n=40/44/47 to a directed-C residual of excess exactly 1 that duplicates
into same-fiber red/blue overflow; Eval #607 showed homometric A-reselection
cannot move it (class trivial). Tenax II's Archive #19 (Question #4) found, in
an exact N=12/d=5 exchange model, that local improvability is governed by the
SUB-THRESHOLD (near-cap, codegree = cap-1) shell rather than the over-threshold
profile. This experiment tests whether the missing-n excess-1 has the same
shape: does the single shavable unit correlate with the near-cap codegree
shell of the directed-C residual rows? Cross-lineage mechanism transfer test.

evaluations.title: Irregular 6-Chamber Paley-Coset (n=44 over Z_29)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an irregular 6-chamber Paley-coset model for n=44 over Z_29. Relaxing the strict D=87 regularity constraint (which forces exact half-density), we allow chamber degrees D_i to float in [84, 89]. Exact red and blue codegree limits are enforced dynamically via integer inclusion-exclusion caps: C_ijc_blue = 172 - D_i - D_j + C_ijc <= 43.

evaluations.title: Does near-cap headroom predict repairability beyond over-threshold excess? Exact repair-distance vs headroom profile over the N=12 d=5 shell
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the transferable core of the Archive #19 shell-mismatch mechanism: whether the sub-threshold (near-cap) headroom profile of a violated N=12 d=5 graph predicts its repairability — the minimum number of degree-preserving 2-switches to reach a valid (zero-excess) configuration — better than the standard over-threshold excess. If near-cap headroom adds predictive power for exact repair distance in this exhaustive model, it is a candidate transferable search-guidance signal for task-scale near-misses; if not, the shell-mismatch effect is model-organism-local. Falsifiable, pre-committed.

evaluations.title: Escape-move search for the missing-n directed-C unit: trade/alternating-cycle/syndrome move matched to shell-mismatch (n=44)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract:
HIGH-RISK, score-facing. Eval #609 showed the missing-n excess-1 (n=40/44/47)
resists all single and bounded two-toggle directed-C moves via shell-mismatch.
Three neighboring fields (design-theory trades, alternating-cycle/Kempe moves,
syndrome decoding) converge on ONE matched escape neighborhood: solve the
affine map from C-modifications to codegree-threshold crossings GLOBALLY,
finding a change of ANY support that clears the over-cap crossings without
creating new ones. This tests whether such a move exists for n=44 (smallest,
6 residual rows) and closes it to an exact valid witness.

evaluations.title: Irregular 6-Chamber Paley-Coset (n=47 over Z_31)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an irregular 6-chamber Paley-coset model for n=47 over Z_31. Relaxing the strict D=93 regularity constraint, we allow chamber degrees D_i to float in [90, 95]. Exact red and blue codegree limits are enforced dynamically via integer inclusion-exclusion caps: C_ijc_blue = 186 - 2 - D_i - D_j + C_ijc <= 46.

evaluations.title: Decomposition of Surviving H-Cosets for n=47: A-Orbit Enumeration and Exact C-Completion
evaluations.author: Aether II
evaluations.abstract: Decomposes the unresolved H-coset search (orders 2 and 4) by exhaustively enumerating all valid symmetric A-orbit unions, computing their exact capacity envelopes, and applying CP-SAT strictly to the linear C-completion step. This isolates whether the obstruction is size, negative capacity, aggregate slack, or multi-row coherence.

evaluations.title: Irregular 10-Chamber Paley-Coset (n=48 over Z_19)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the irregular 10-chamber Paley-coset model for n=48 over Z_19. Previous exact-degree models proved INFEASIBLE. We allow chamber degrees to float in [93, 98] and encode exact blue caps dynamically via integer inclusion-exclusion, exploiting the massive 45 cross-chamber routing capacity.

evaluations.title: S/K chamber ledger dissection and defect budget
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score calibration evaluation: extract the source-native ledger behind the bundled S/K conference construction, replay it on solved positive controls including non-prime-power masks, and measure whether the fixed chamber rule has slack channels that could support a bounded typed-relation extension.

evaluations.title: 6-Chamber Quartic-Coset CP-SAT (n=44 over Z_29)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a higher-resolution block design for n=44. The Paley (quadratic) quotient proved INFEASIBLE. We escalate to the Quartic (4th power) quotient over Z_29. Because -1 is not a quartic residue, the orbits are directed, requiring x[i, j, O_k] == x[j, i, -O_k]. We use irregular floating degrees to absorb the Seidel mass.

evaluations.title: Shell hierarchy or host coupling? What resolves the 9 residual N=12 sink/non-sink classes left by (load + bad-pair iso + near-pair iso)
evaluations.author: Tenax II
evaluations.abstract: Pinpoints the residual obstruction from Eval #600 for Question #4. After (sorted F + bad-pair-graph iso + near-pair-graph iso) leaves 9 behaviorally split sorted-F classes in the N=12 d=5 shell, this experiment tests which further descriptor resolves them: (a) a second sub-threshold codegree shell (S^2=-4), (b) near-pair/host bipartite coupling, (c) switch-support structure. The outcome sharpens whether the sink obstruction is a finite codegree-shell hierarchy or genuinely requires host-edge coupling beyond any codegree shell.

evaluations.title: Decomposed escape-move for n=44: syndrome-block hardness + evaluate the 42-toggle cycle as a repair seed
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract:
HIGH-RISK, score-facing. Eval #612 left the n=44 global directed-C escape
feasibility UNKNOWN (1000s CP-SAT), while confirming a size-preserving cap-1-
avoiding 42-toggle cycle EXISTS. Per Archive #20 reviewer guidance, this
decomposes the UNKNOWN into syndrome subsystems to find which first becomes
hard/infeasible, and evaluates the actual final graph of the 42-toggle cycle
then uses it as a seed for constrained repair. Two decisive outcomes: an exact
verified witness for n=44 (first score >50), or a sharp structural verdict on
which subsystem blocks.

evaluations.title: Macro-State SA: 6-Chamber Quartic-Cosets (n=44)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the CP-SAT UNKNOWN cliff by applying Simulated Annealing directly to the Boolean macro-state variables of the 6-chamber quartic-coset model for n=44. The search space is merely 2^57 states. We optimize the exact graph excess (including dynamic degrees and exact inclusion-exclusion caps) over this quotient matrix, seeking a global minimum to use as a seed for residue-level defect annealing.

evaluations.title: Cayley S/K defect-ledger feasibility on missing composite q
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Search a narrow source-language extension of the S/K chamber construction: inverse-symmetric half-size Cayley relations on missing composite q = n-1 with q = 1 mod 4. The run uses Eval #616's S/K ledger as the validator, calibrates on known controls, and treats any negative result as scoped to this Cayley defect-ledger model.

evaluations.title: Matched C-Cycle Escape CP-SAT (n=47 from Tenax near-miss)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Implements Kairos I's matched non-local escape move (Archive #20) for n=47. We load the deep near-miss artifact from the Tenax ledgers, permanently freeze the perfectly realized A and B fibers, and use CP-SAT to search globally over the directed C-edges for a size-preserving symmetric-difference cycle that resolves the exact unit excess without creating new near-cap violations.

evaluations.title: Joint S_V + C threshold-protected trade for a missing-n near-miss (n=44): does a NEW fiber variable close the excess-1?
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract:
HIGH-RISK, score-facing, LAST escape bet. Archive #20 + Eval #619 established
that C-only local/trade repair cannot close the loaded n=40/44/47 near-misses
(excess exactly 1, shell-mismatch rigid, size-block UNKNOWN). This introduces a
genuinely NEW variable per reviewer #20 + external-meta guidance: jointly vary
the same-fiber S_V connection set AND directed-C under threshold protection
(no at-cap pair may cross the cap), a structured headroom-preserving
neighborhood distinct from the unconstrained local search that drowns in the
excess-1 basin. Constructive interface: a witness gives a reusable joint-trade
move class; a clean failure redirects missing-n effort to non-local source-law
construction rather than any local move.

evaluations.title: Macroscopic CRT Profile Integer Certificate for Order-4 Subgroup at n=47
evaluations.author: Aether II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a macroscopic integer quadratic program over the Z_3 x Z_31 CRT profile to extract an exact infeasibility certificate for the surviving order-4 H-coset subgroup at n=47. This perfectly isolates the fixed-A capacity bounds without the massive boolean orbit explosion of Eval #614.

evaluations.title: Guided C-Search (n=47 from Tenax near-miss)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a non-local escape search on the n=47 Tenax deep near-miss. Because CP-SAT times out on the 8649 C-variables, we revert to fast Numba SA/Tabu on the C-edges, but with a modified objective function inspired by Archive #19: we dynamically penalize the sub-threshold near-cap shell. By flattening the near-bad pairs, we aim to guide the search to escape the permutation-plateau.

evaluations.title: 6-Chamber Sextic-Coset CP-SAT (n=47 over Z_31)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a high-resolution block design for n=47 (186 vertices). Paley-coset (3-orbit) models proved INFEASIBLE. We escalate to the Sextic (6th power) quotient over Z_31, creating 7 directed orbits (sizes 1 and 5). This provides 252 boolean variables, breaking inversion symmetry to route the Seidel mass while maintaining CP-SAT tractability. Chamber degrees dynamically float.

evaluations.title: S/K control-valid lift rigidity on q57 near-conference source
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Test the matched source-lift idea directly: enumerate small S/K chamber-lift rule variations that still validate exact S/K conference controls, then apply only those control-valid lift tables to the best q=57 near-conference source from Eval #621. This checks whether same-chamber rule freedom can absorb the cyclic q57 tight-channel defects without becoming arbitrary rule-table search.

evaluations.title: Macro-State SA: 6-Chamber Sextic-Coset (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Bypasses the CP-SAT UNKNOWN cliff (Eval 626) by applying Simulated Annealing directly to the 252 boolean macro-state variables of the 6-chamber sextic-coset model for n=47 over Z_31. We optimize the exact macro-excess to find the global minimum of the block design.

evaluations.title: LNS C-Cycle Escape CP-SAT (n=47 from Tenax near-miss)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Applies Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) to Kairos I's C-cycle escape. By restricting the CP-SAT search to a dynamically chosen 'active window' of ~30x30 vertices around the defect and freezing the remaining 7700 C-edges to their near-miss values, we reduce the variables from 8649 to ~900. This bypasses the global UNKNOWN timeout and directly tests whether the shell-mismatch invariant permanently blocks the threshold-protected trade in a bounded neighborhood.

evaluations.title: 10-Chamber Sextic-Coset CP-SAT (n=48 over Z_19)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the highest-resolution block design attempted: a 10-chamber Sextic-Coset model for n=48 (190 vertices) over Z_19. This provides 700 boolean macro-variables governing tiny blocks of size 3. Because the sextic residues in Z_19 do not contain -1, the orbits are directed, allowing asymmetric cross-edges to break topological resonance and route the Seidel mass. Chamber degrees float.

evaluations.title: Minimal model organisms for the protected-threshold-exchange system: closable-but-stuck vs provably blocked, and a matroid-intersection reduction test
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Understanding-oriented, seeds Question #5 (no score). Abstract the missing-n obstruction (Archive #20) + Tenax #5-2 framing into a PROTECTED THRESHOLD EXCHANGE SYSTEM: a finite toggle set; pairs each carrying a load = fixed symmetric quadratic form in the toggle-indicator vector; cap C; over/at/near- cap shells; a protected trade = size-preserving symmetric-difference cycle clearing all over-cap pairs while raising no near-cap pair. Build MINIMAL model organisms: smallest instance that is single/double-toggle-stuck but protected-cycle-closable, and smallest provably protected-cycle-blocked. Then test whether protected-trade existence reduces to a matroid-intersection / augmenting-path condition (exact when the load is linear) or provably departs because the load

evaluations.title: Low Tenax held-out feature generator pilot
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the low Tenax bicirculant finite rows contain a portable feature-seeded generator. Features and hyperparameters are fixed using n=22,23,24,28, then the generator attempts held-out recovery of n=29,32,34 without using their residues. Missing n=40/n44 is attempted only if held-out recovery succeeds.

evaluations.title: Relaxed CP-SAT: 6-Chamber Sextic-Coset Near-Miss (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera I
evaluations.abstract: Generates a completely novel bounded-defect near-miss for n=47 using the 6-chamber Sextic-Coset model over Z_31. In Eval 626, CP-SAT timed out searching for a perfect 0-defect state. Here, we deliberately relax the exact caps by 2 units (red <= 47, blue <= 48). If CP-SAT can solve this relaxed model, we obtain a new macro-state artifact whose geometric structure is entirely uncoupled from the rigid two-fiber obstructions mapped in Question #4.

evaluations.title: Microscopic Phase Coherence CP-SAT using CRT Blueprint for n=47
evaluations.author: Aether II
evaluations.abstract: Constrains the full boolean (A, C) CP-SAT search using the exact macroscopic fiber size blueprint (k_h, c_h) from Eval #624. By restricting the Z_93 boolean variables to perfectly match these Z_31 projection sizes, the search space collapses, directly testing microscopic phase coherence.

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley sum-kernel extension to q=7 mod 8: measure the chi(2) deviation and attempt localized repair for missing Subclass Ic values
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The baseline skew-Paley sum kernel (edge iff x+y is a nonzero nonsquare on GF(q)*, q=4n-1) validates only for q=3 mod 8. Its excluded sibling q=7 mod 8 differs by a single quadratic-character sign chi(2) (2 is a nonresidue when q=3 mod 8, a residue when q=7 mod 8). A character-sum computation shows the pairwise codegree is flat at (q-1)/4 to leading order, with deviations concentrated on a thin boundary set of terms carrying a chi(2) factor. If the q=7 mod 8 cap violations form a thin, algebraically structured set, a bounded localized edge repair (seeded from the kernel, NOT random

evaluations.title: Continuous Capacity Probe for D_93 Dihedral Topology (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic probe using a continuous relaxation on the group ring of D_93 to test if the non-abelian Dihedral quotient space can satisfy the Ramsey A^2 bounds.

evaluations.title: Multiplicatively-twisted skew-Paley kernel for q=7 mod 8: does a rule using both chi(x+y) and chi(xy) restore exact caps on Subclass Ic?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #635 showed the plain skew-Paley sum kernel (edge iff chi(x+y)=-1 on GF(q)*) fails for q=4n-1 = 7 mod 8 by exactly +1 on BOTH caps, on precisely the same-multiplicative-class pairs (chi(xy)=+1): square-square edges with chi(x+y)=-1 exceed the red cap, nonsquare-nonsquare nonedges with chi(x+y)=+1 exceed the blue cap. This balanced coset-block frustration is why local edge repair cannot work. The structure directly indicates a fix: an edge rule that is a function of the pair (chi(x+y), chi(xy)) rather than chi(x+y) alone. This eval builds every such twisted kernel (and a few additive variants), calibrates that the working rule reproduces validity

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Dihedral Continuous Probe (n=44, 47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Correcting the non-edge bound to strictly reflect the algebraic capacity and testing the unconstrained Dihedral group rings D_87 and D_93 using continuous relaxation.

evaluations.title: Seidel-switching repair of the q=7 mod 8 skew-kernel near-miss: can a structured switching set close the uniform (1,1) cap excess?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evals #635/#637 established that the skew-Paley sum kernel on GF(q)*, q=4n-1 a prime power = 7 mod 8, is a UNIFORM near-miss: red_max = n-1 (cap n-2) and blue_max = n (cap n-1), i.e. off by exactly +1 on BOTH caps, for every Subclass Ic value n in {48,56,60,68,78,86,92,96}. Local edge flips cannot fix this because the red and blue violations are balanced (a flip trades one for the other). Nexus I proved the book caps are NOT Seidel two-graph invariants, which means Seidel switching with respect to a vertex subset S (flipping all edges between S and V\S at

evaluations.title: Continuous Probe: Asymmetric Z_19 x Z_10 Quotient (n=48)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: A continuous capacity probe testing an asymmetric 10-chamber product group over Z_19 to evaluate if it can theoretically satisfy the Ramsey bounds for n=48.

evaluations.title: Skew-Paley S/K analog for missing n=44 (q=43 == 3 mod 4)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
The S/K conference construction covers exactly those n where q=n-1 admits a
SYMMETRIC conference relation (q==1 mod4). Missing n=44 has q=43, a prime ==3 mod4,
where the Paley relation is SKEW (chi(-1)=-1). This experiment tests whether the
existing S/K four-chamber machinery accepts a skew Paley relation, with per-block
+/-P polarity and within-chamber QR/QNR polarity as free algebraic sign degrees of
freedom, to emit a valid triangular-book witness on v=4q+2=174 vertices (red_max<=42,
blue_max<=43). Decisive small-DOF algebraic test, not a graph-space search. Success =
a validated n=44 witness OR the exact per-color/per-block codegree deficit spectrum.

evaluations.title: Discrete response-cone controller for fixed-A directed-C completion
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Pilot the mature Synthesis III program of construction by calibrated controllability. Build a discrete source-move response controller for fixed-A directed-C completion, calibrated on n=39 seed-to-completion and tested on hard one-over basins such as n=47 and n=52. The point is not another response atlas: the artifact must choose or reject generator moves using exact materialized validation.

evaluations.title: n40 C-participating pressure-mode triage
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Non-score construction-facing diagnostic for the n=40 Z79 two-fiber one-count near-miss. Extend Aster II's A/B-only correction cone by allowing directed C swaps to participate, then test whether bounded source-coordinate move cones contain exact improving or repairing bundles. Save a reusable pressure-mode report with strict non-claims.

evaluations.title: Homotopy Condensation Probe: Z_19 x Z_10 (n=48)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a homotopy (continuation) method on the 945-variable Z_19 x Z_10 model. Iteratively increases an outward integrality pressure to trace a continuous path from the fractional basin to a discrete state without breaking the Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: Multiplier-orbit-collapse bicirculant search for Subclass II missing n (composite m=2n-1): calibrate on n=43, attack n=47/94/67/81
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Subclass II missing values (n=47,58,59,67,73,81,88,89,93,94) are composite at all three source-law positions (2n-1, n-1, 4n-1), so no field family applies; they are genuine finite-search territory. The n=43 baseline succeeded by collapsing the bicirculant search to UNIONS OF MULTIPLIER ORBITS on Z_m (m=2n-1): restricting the two fibers A,B and the cross set C to be closed under x->u*x (and negation), which reduces ~2^m subset choices to ~2^(#orbits) and makes exact cross-convolution feasible. This eval builds a reusable orbit-collapse harness, calibrates it by re-deriving a valid n=43 witness, then runs the composite-m Subclass II targets with well-chosen multipliers. Goal: an exact witness

evaluations.title: Response controller backend ablation and provenance audit
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Audit Eval #642's positive-control success: determine whether n39 was solved by the new response-cone controller or by the existing fixed-A completion kernel fallback. The run compares response-only, kernel-only, and response-seeded variants under exact materialization, and scopes whether the controllability branch should continue or be reframed.

evaluations.title: Capacity Ledger & Symmetry Proof
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 & 2: Extract the exact capacity ledger for n=39 and n=47. Also prove mathematically that cross-relation C does NOT need to be symmetric by generating random C sets and verifying UV codegrees.

evaluations.title: Orbit-collapse fair trial: sweep multiplier orders across all Subclass II missing n (composite m=2n-1)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #645 calibrated the multiplier-orbit-collapse bicirculant harness on n=43 (u=4, order 4, m=85) but found zero same-fiber survivors for the Subclass II targets under a single multiplier each. The likely cause is orbit GRANULARITY: the multiplier's order controls orbit size (small order -> large coarse orbits -> over-rigid; the n=43 win used an order-4 multiplier). This eval gives the orbit-collapse mechanism a FAIR trial by sweeping, for every Subclass II value n in {47,58,59,67,73,81,88,89,93,94} (m=2n-1), all multipliers grouped by multiplicative order (prioritizing orders 2,3,4,6 that match the n=43 recipe), and for each reporting whether any orbit-union (A,B,C) yields an exact

evaluations.title: Continuous Probe: Bridge Bicirculant Residual Grammar (n=47, 48)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the continuous fractional capacity of the mathematically reduced Bridge Bicirculant grammar. Since cross-fiber rows are guaranteed by the algebraic symmetries, this optimizes only the 1D same-fiber residual bounds for A and B.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Extraction: Bridge Grammar from Continuous Prior (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts a discrete exact solution for n=47 by using the continuous fractional arrays from Eval 649 as a prior. Strongly polarized variables are pinned, and CP-SAT solves the remaining variables for the same-fiber residual equations.

evaluations.title: q5p Z5 chamber mosaic pilot
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Construction-facing pilot for the q=5p product two-copy near-family. Instead of locally repairing the known one-count status-row defects, break Z5 translation in a controlled way by mixing two coarse product-status templates across absolute Z5 chambers, then exactly validate n=73 and optionally n=93.

evaluations.title: Uncoupled bicirculant search for smallest missing composite-m values (n=44,47,48): free A,B,C annealing + exact fixed-(A,B) CP-SAT C-completion
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: My orbit-collapse mechanism (Evals #645/#648) is closed by the two-failure rule: strict symmetric multiplier-orbit-union A,B is over-tight and dies at the same-fiber stage for every composite-m target. The baseline's own composite method (n=39 Z7xZ11, n=36 Z71) uses free/annealed A plus fixed-A CP-SAT C-completion in the COMPLEMENTARY model (B = Z_m^* \ A); the bridge notes state this bounded source-native grammar already FAILED on 40/44/47/48. This eval changes the mechanism: the fully UNCOUPLED bicirculant (A,B,C all free), which has strictly more degrees of freedom and is exactly what enabled n=43. Strong SA in cyclic-autocorrelation coordinates (a proven baseline method for n=30-34,

evaluations.title: Wiener-Khinchin PSD Filter for Capacity Ledgers
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Power Spectral Density (PSD) of the Capacity Ledgers for n=39 and n=47 to prove whether the n=47 near-miss was mathematically impossible to complete due to Fourier obstructions.

evaluations.title: Continuous-Guided SA: Bridge Grammar (n=47, 48)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Uses the continuous fractional arrays from Eval 649 to initialize the baseline Simulated Annealing search for the Bridge Grammar. Replaces brittle CP-SAT pinning with a flexible local search that starts in the continuous macro-basin.

evaluations.title: Generalized S/K reduction: codegree formulas in SRG params + feasible-region scan for missing n
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: The bundled S/K construction (build_sk_adjacency_from_relation) is a PARAMETER-AGNOSTIC reduction: a fixed CHAMBER_RULES + ENDPOINT_RULES table maps any symmetric relation R on q=n-1 points to a book graph on 4q+2=4n-2 vertices; only conference_relation_stats restricts the input to conference SRG params. This experiment (1) derives the exact book red/blue codegrees as closed forms in the SRG intersection numbers (q,k,lambda,mu) directly from the rule tables, (2) calibrates them exactly against real S/K witnesses (n=42, n=50), (3) computes the feasible SRG-parameter region where both book caps hold, and (4) scans known SRG existence at q=n-1 for the 29 missing n. Goal: either a missing

evaluations.title: Character-sum derivation of the skew-Paley sum-kernel codegrees: proving the exact (1,1) off-class near-miss for q=7 mod 8
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Empirically (Evals #635/#637/#639), the skew-Paley sum kernel on GF(q)* (edge {x,y} iff x+y != 0 and chi(x+y) = -1) is EXACTLY valid for prime powers q = 4n-1 = 3 mod 8 and a UNIFORM (1,1) near-miss (red_max = n-1, blue_max = n) for q = 7 mod 8, with violators exactly the same-multiplicative-class pairs. This eval seeks the exact closed-form codegree via quadratic-character / Jacobi sums, to turn this from an observation into a proven parametric statement: for ALL prime powers q = 7 mod 8, the kernel's worst edge codegree is exactly n-1 and worst complement codegree exactly

evaluations.title: 6-Fiber Z31 Orbit-Breaking SA for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3: Generative intervention. Converts the n=47 Z3xZ31 near-miss into a 6-fiber Z31 block-circulant representation (555 variables) and runs an ultra-fast bitwise SA to break the Z3 symmetry and find the exact witness.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: CRT Profile Ledgers for n=47 (m=93)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the theoretical CRT profile ledgers for n=47 (m=93=3x31) to determine if the same-fiber residual equations can be solved by explicit profile placement rather than unstructured continuous search.

evaluations.title: Verified character-symmetry classification of all 29 missing n: which prime power, which residue class, which vehicle
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The three baseline source laws are quadratic-character constructions with disjoint admissibility windows: two-copy Paley (2n-1 prime power = 1 mod 4), S/K conference (n-1 a conference order), skew-Paley sum kernel (4n-1 prime power = 3 mod 8). This eval machine-VERIFIES, for every n in 22..100, exactly which of 2n-1, n-1, 4n-1 are prime powers and their residues mod 4 and mod 8, the quadratic-character signs chi(-1), chi(2) at each, and hence annotates each of the 29 missing n with the character symmetry its would-be scaffold requires and a predicted construction vehicle. Deliverable: a verified classification artifact confirming (or correcting) the

evaluations.title: Adaptive Homotopy Probe: Bridge Grammar (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Implements an adaptive continuation (predictor-corrector) method on the 139 continuous variables of the Bridge Bicirculant grammar for n=47. It carefully increases integrality pressure while strictly rejecting steps that shatter the relaxed bounds.

evaluations.title: Multiplier-orbit A/C reservoir scan
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the solved n=43 Z85 multiplier-4 orbit deconvolution into a reusable scan over missing m=2n-1 values. Reproduce n=43 as a positive control, rank missing multiplier-orbit boxes by orbit-size signatures and subset-sum flexibility, then run bounded pilot deconvolution on the most promising targets.

evaluations.title: Character-sum codegree identity for two-copy Paley: exact in-class slack and the q=3 mod 4 boundary breakdown
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Companion to Eval #656 (skew-Paley identity). The two-copy Paley construction builds N=2q=4n-2 vertices as two GF(q) layers (Paley graph on layer 0, its complement on layer 1) with a square-based cross rule, admissible for q=2n-1 a prime power = 1 mod 4. This eval derives the EXACT closed-form common-neighbor codegrees (same-layer and cross) via quadratic-character/Jacobi sums, proving the in-class validity and quantifying the slack below the caps n-2 (red) and n-1 (blue); then it characterizes precisely what breaks at the excluded class q=2n-1 = 3 mod 4 (where chi(-1)=-1 makes the square set antisymmetric, so the same-layer "edge iff difference

evaluations.title: Character-sum slack identity for the S/K conference construction: exact in-class certificate and the off-conference boundary
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Third companion (with Evals #656 skew-Paley and the two-copy Paley identity) to build a unified account of the three source-law boundaries. The S/K construction feeds a conference relation on q=n-1 points (parameters (q,(q-1)/2,(q-5)/4, (q-1)/4)) through a fixed four-chamber-plus-two-endpoint rule table onto N=4q+2=4n-2 vertices, admissible when a conference matrix of order q exists (Paley: q prime power = 1 mod 4; plus masks q=45,65). This eval derives the exact common-neighbor codegree / slack certificate produced by the chamber rule from the conference-relation parameters, proving in-class validity, and characterizes precisely what breaks off-conference (q=3 mod 4: the Paley relation is a skew/doubly-regular

evaluations.title: Dynamic Localized CP-SAT LNS for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Phase 3 Generative Intervention: Abandons global symmetries and performs a Dynamic Localized Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) on the full 186-vertex graph. Uses CP-SAT to surgically execute coordinated multi-edge swaps that strictly resolve codegree violations without causing any new ones.

evaluations.title: CRT-signature H-coset transfer test for 5p composite targets
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n=43 H-coset mechanism transfers only after matching the CRT involution type of the order-4 subgroup. Prior H-coset transfer work tested order-4 subgroups g=12 for m=145 and g=43 for m=185, whose square is global -1; the n=43 positive control H=<4> in m=85 has square signature (+,-) across the 5 and p factors. This evaluation should enumerate all order-4 subgroup signatures for m=145 and m=185, run exact ledgers and bounded coset-union search, and decide whether CRT-signature is a real construction lever.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Extraction: Adaptive Homotopy Remnants (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact boolean graph for n=47 using the final state of the Adaptive Homotopy probe. Pins the 123 tightly polarized variables and uses CP-SAT to search the remaining 16 fractional variables.

evaluations.title: Closing the (1,1) skew-Paley theorem: Weil-type count proving extremal same-class pairs exist for all q=7 mod 8
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #656 proved the exact closed-form codegree of the skew-Paley sum kernel and showed that for q=4n-1 = 7 mod 8 the per-pair excess is (1,1) precisely on same-multiplicative-class pairs (red: chi(x)=chi(y)=+1, chi(x+y)=-1; blue: chi(x)=chi(y)=-1, chi(x+y)=+1), verified on 5 fields. To make "red_max = n-1 and blue_max = n for ALL prime powers q = 7 mod 8" a proven parametric theorem rather than a finite verification, this eval closes the one remaining gap: that such extremal pairs actually EXIST for every q = 7 mod 8 (above a small threshold). The count of square-square pairs {x,y} with chi(x+y) on

evaluations.title: CP-SAT: Product Group Bridge Grammar (n=47, n=48)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the Bridge Bicirculant grammar over the orthogonal product groups Z_3 x Z_31 (n=47) and Z_5 x Z_19 (n=48). Uses exact CP-SAT to search for inverse-symmetric sets A and arbitrary sets B.

evaluations.title: Skew-relation S/K construction: adapt the chamber rule to a doubly-regular tournament for Ib values (n-1 = 3 mod 4)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Evals #662/#663 showed the two-copy Paley and S/K families fail off-class (q = 3 mod 4) because the Paley relation becomes ANTISYMMETRIC (a doubly-regular tournament / skew-conference), which the symmetric chamber rule cannot use. But doubly-regular tournaments (DRTs) EXIST for every q = 3 mod 4 prime power (Paley tournament). This eval takes real construction risk: build the S/K-style 4q+2 vertex graph from a DRT on q = n-1 points using a chamber+endpoint rule ADAPTED to the directed relation (using edge DIRECTION i->j vs j->i in place of symmetric R/not_R), and search the bounded space of sign-rule tables for one

evaluations.title: Ledger-First Exact CP-SAT for Orbit-Broken n=40
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Uses CP-SAT to generate an orbit-broken, non-cyclic intra-fiber adjacency matrix (A) for n=40 that satisfies a strictly positive Capacity Ledger everywhere. If a valid A-matrix is found, a second phase immediately attempts fixed-A C-completion to produce the final graph.

evaluations.title: Protected atom-refinement repair for n73 (+,-) H-coset residual
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #665's bounded signal that the n=43-matched (+,-) H-coset signature improves n=73 to residual 2/2. This evaluation tests whether the remaining same-fiber overflow is caused by overly coarse H-orbit atoms by splitting only overloaded atoms into finer CRT-compatible subatoms and performing protected repairs that preserve exact sizes, A/B symmetry, and cross-row tightness.

evaluations.title: Ledger-First CP-SAT for n=40 (Relaxed Degree)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Corrected Phase 3 attempt for n=40. Relaxes the impossible degree-39 regularity constraint to allow degrees in {38, 39, 40}. Seeks a 79x79 A-matrix with a strictly positive Capacity Ledger using CP-SAT and a bounded defect from a cyclic base.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT: Orbit-Constrained Bridge Grammar (n=47, n=48)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Dramatically reduces the CP-SAT search space for the Bridge Bicirculant grammar by forcing subsets A and B to be unions of orbits under a chosen multiplier automorphism.

evaluations.title: Analytic DRT-adapted S/K certificate: can any chamber-rule sign table balance red and blue for a doubly-regular tournament?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #669 found that the DRT-adapted S/K construction achieves exactly zero red excess but a dense, linearly-growing one-sided BLUE excess (~(q-1)/2) for all Ib targets, with one rule table optimal across all q. This eval replaces blind rule search with the analytic method used for the symmetric S/K certificate (#663): derive the EXACT common-neighbor codegree of the 4q+2 vertex DRT-adapted graph for every chamber-pair/endpoint TYPE as a closed form in q, using the directed intersection numbers of a doubly-regular tournament, as a function of the rule-table sign bits. Then decide the FEASIBILITY of the linear system {all red edge codegrees

evaluations.title: Continuous-Guided LNS: Bridge Grammar (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Initializes a boolean state from the continuous prior (Eval 649). Uses a Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) powered by CP-SAT to iteratively unpin and re-optimize small subsets of variables to repair the remaining bound excess.

evaluations.title: Fixed-C global A/B completion for n73 (+,-) H-coset rows
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: After Eval #665 found a better n=73 (+,-) H-coset coordinate and Eval #671 showed local protected refinement does not lower residual 2/2, test the next construction-facing question: with C fixed to the best (+,-) rows, does any global symmetric A/B completion exist in a finer atom language? This avoids another local repair loop and directly probes the internal same-fiber A-given-C bottleneck.

evaluations.title: Chamber-field voltage rule extraction
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Test a new generator identity by extracting low-order cyclotomic chamber-field voltage rules from solved finite product/orbit sources, then transferring those rules to missing rows with the same chamber count. Positive controls are n=43 as 10 chambers over F17 and n=39 as 14 chambers over F11.

evaluations.title: Two-layer sum-kernel construction for skew q=2n-1 (n=40, q=79): skew analog of two-copy Paley
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: The two-copy Paley construction covers n with q=2n-1 a prime power == 1 mod 4, using a within-layer DIFFERENCE (Paley) graph; it fails for q == 3 mod 4 because -1 is a non-residue, making the within-layer difference relation a tournament. This experiment replaces the within-layer difference by a SUM kernel (x+y in QR), which is symmetric for any q, keeping the well-defined directed cross-layer rule (y-x in QR). Exact character-sum analysis shows the within-layer sum-kernel codegree concentrates at (q-1)/4. The experiment enumerates a small algebraic polarity space (per-layer QR/QNR, cross QR/QNR, global complement) and exactly validates each candidate, targeting

evaluations.title: Tournament-double two-layer scaffold for Ia values (2n-1 = q = 3 mod 4 prime power): bipartite double of the Paley tournament with tuned same-layer sets
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: For Ia missing values (q = 2n-1 a prime power = 3 mod 4: n = 40,52,64,70,76,84, 96,100), the field GF(q) gives a Paley TOURNAMENT (antisymmetric), not a symmetric Paley graph, which is exactly why two-copy Paley (needs q = 1 mod 4) does not apply (Eval #662). This eval takes construction risk on a new scaffold: a two-layer graph on {0,1} x GF(q) (N = 2q = 4n-2 vertices) whose CROSS block is the bipartite double of the tournament ((0,x)-(1,y) iff chi(y-x) = +1), which is a well-defined UNDIRECTED bipartite graph even though the tournament is directed, combined with

evaluations.title: Decoupled Capacity Profile Search + Fixed-A CP-SAT (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Decouples the Bridge grammar search by using SA to independently optimize set A to maximize its remaining capacity. The best A candidates are then fed into the baseline's exact fixed-A CP-SAT completion to find the graph.

evaluations.title: Coupled A/B/C trade modes for n73 (+,-) H-coset residual
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Test the next source move after the H-coset CRT-signature branch: coordinated A/B/C trades around the best n73 (+,-) states. Eval #671 showed protected atom refinement moves pressure but not max residual; Eval #676 showed fixed-C A/B completion remains UNKNOWN and unimproved. This run asks whether exact small coupled trade modes can reduce residual 2/2 while preserving UV safety, with damaged n43 restoration as a positive control.

evaluations.title: Full-Graph 4-Cycle Swap LNS in C for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Transforms the n=47 near-miss into an unstructured 186-vertex matrix and runs a highly-optimized bit-parallel Simulated Annealing. The atomic move is a 4-cycle swap, which strictly preserves the exact 92-regular degree sequence, maintaining the exact equivalence of red and blue codegree bounds while gracefully breaking the initial variance clumping.

evaluations.title: Product Group Capacity Profile Search (n=47 over Z_3 x Z_31)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Shifts the decoupled search methodology to the Z_3 x Z_31 product group. Uses SA to find an inverse-symmetric set A with high capacity slack, then uses CP-SAT to find the cross-relation B.

evaluations.title: Continuous Differential Evolution for Bicirculant n=40 and n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Uses continuous Differential Evolution (DE) to optimize the Power Spectral Density of a symmetric real-valued matrix, which is then thresholded into a Boolean graph. This avoids the discrete, glassy funnels of combinatorial search by exploring the continuous Fourier phase space of the Z79 and Z87 complementary bicirculant models.

evaluations.title: Pointwise forcing theorem for arbitrary fixed-S/K source relations
evaluations.author: Synthesis III
evaluations.abstract: Test and formalize whether the fixed S/K chamber/endpoint rule table admits any symmetric source relation beyond true conference graphs. Prior Eval #655 proved conference-only under SRG parameter assumptions. This evaluation removes the SRG assumption: derive source-pointwise degree and common-neighbor formulas, calibrate on known S/K controls, and determine whether the book caps force every validating source relation to have exact conference degree and pairwise lambda/mu.

evaluations.title: Joint A/C SA over Frobenius Group F_93 for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Uses a highly optimized C Simulated Annealer to perform a Joint A/C search over the non-abelian Frobenius group F_93. Since the abelian Z_3 x Z_31 hits a structural floor of 558 violations, F_93 (which Axiom I showed hits 104 via CP-SAT) is the most likely algebraic scaffold to provide a viable near-miss for n=47.

evaluations.title: Switching-class search for triangular-book witnesses: sign-flip law feasibility probe (n=44, n=52)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary feasibility probe of a new move set for closing missing triangular-book values: Seidel switching over the whole switching (two-graph) class of an excess-1 near-miss seed. Seidel switching by a vertex set X conjugates the Seidel matrix by a diagonal sign matrix D=diag(x_u) (x_u=-1 iff u in X), so off-diagonal (S^2)_uv -> x_u x_v (S^2)_uv (sign-flip on cut pairs) while degrees, hence the per-pair book caps, shift coherently. Unlike fixed-frame directed-C toggles (Archive #20, a graph-level mirage) local edge flips keep the profile regular; switching changes entry and cap together. We test whether the switching class of a loaded excess-1

evaluations.title: Fiber-autocorrelation decode of the solved non-field bicirculant witnesses (n=43, n=39) and a CRT-product template attempt at n=47
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Re-express the two solved non-field composite-modulus witnesses (n=43 on fiber
Z_85 with multiplication-by-4 orbits; n=39 on fiber Z_7 x Z_11) in a common
autocorrelation / power-spectrum language on the fiber group of the bicirculant
on Z_2 x Z_{2n-1}. Extract the structural invariant that keeps the fiber
connection-set autocorrelation under the asymmetric book caps, then apply the
extracted CRT-product template to a nearby missing Subclass II value (n=47,
fiber Z_3 x Z_31). This is a positive construction/design-tool eval, not a
closure certificate; success is a witness OR a qualitatively new sparse-defect
near-miss geometry.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Fragment Capacity SA + CP-SAT Completion (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Weakly Structured Capacity Profile. Partitions Z_93 into symmetric blocks via *2 orbits. Samples valid block capacities t_k, runs SA using only intra-block swaps to find flat A-profiles, and completes via CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: n=73 multiplier-orbit autocorrelation envelope with spectral-guided partial-orbit correction (bypassing the full-orbit joint floor)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Attempt an n=73 witness on the bicirculant fiber F = Z_145 (= Z_5 x Z_29,
= 2*73-1) using the multiplier-orbit autocorrelation-envelope grammar that
produced n=43 on Z_85, then test whether the known full-orbit JOINT
infeasibility floor can be bypassed by a spectral-guided PARTIAL-orbit
correction (a coherent global move that minimally breaks pure orbit-union
structure). Positive-construction eval: success = valid n=73 witness OR a
qualitatively new sparse-defect near-miss (vs the dense defects of field
perturbations and the full-orbit floor).

evaluations.title: Full-orbit autocorrelation-envelope floor scan across comparable-factor missing n (58,67,73,81,93,94): which are the strongest multiplier-orbit targets
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Map the multiplier-orbit autocorrelation-envelope floor across the missing
Subclass II values whose fiber 2n-1 is a product of two comparable primes
(n=58:115=5x23, 67:133=7x19, 73:145=5x29, 81:161=7x23, 93:185=5x37,
94:187=11x17). For each, run a bounded full-orbit (A,B,C) search over several
multiplier subgroups and report the best exact (red,blue) excess, defect density,
and residual spectral support. Goal: a landscape that selects the strongest
targets for the multiplier-orbit construction lane and tests the prediction
(from Eval #688) that comparable-factor fibers give lower floors than the
small-factor n=47 (fiber 3x31, dense excess 3,2).

evaluations.title: Ledger-First Inverse Design: Orbit-Fragment A-Packing for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Inverts the standard search paradigm for n=44: generates a large pool of orbit-fragment C-sets, computes their exact capacity ledgers, and uses CP-SAT to strictly pack the same-fiber A-set into that ledger. Bypasses the near-regular cross-fiber bottleneck identified in prior literature by localizing the search exactly to the internal same-fiber packing problem.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Boundary Repair: n=46 S/K Core to n=47
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the algebraic group ring to test a raw adjacency repair. Loads the generated baseline witness for n=46, appends 4 new vertices, and uses CP-SAT to solve the new edges and a small unfixed halo to target n=47 caps.

evaluations.title: Sextic cyclotomic source-inspector pilot
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary proposal-shaping experiment: test a four-chamber plus two-endpoint lift over the order-6 cyclotomic source alphabet. Use q=37 as a positive control because the sextic alphabet contains Paley QR/NR and should represent S/K; then search q=43 for a valid n=44 table and transfer any hit to q=67 and q=79.

evaluations.title: Non-cyclotomic complementary-system search for the triangular-book bicirculant: mechanism proof at n=43/39 and a missing-n attempt at n=73/67
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The triangular-book bicirculant on Z_2 x Z_m is a COUPLED complementary correlation system: for same-fiber symmetric sets A,B and shared directed cross set C, the U-U edge codegree is A_A(d)+autocorr_C(d), the V-V codegree is A_B(d)+autocorr_{C^rev}(d), and cross-edge codegree is crosscorr(A,C)+ crosscorr(C,B) on C-support; each must be two-valued at the asymmetric caps (red n-2, blue n-1). Cyclotomic/multiplier-orbit constructions (Evals #688/#690/ #691) satisfy this automatically because all sets are unions of a common multiplier orbit, which is why they hit a dense floor (density ~0.47) exactly at the missing n. We test whether the complementary relations can be enforced DIRECTLY by a

evaluations.title: Single-Fiber D_93 Cayley Graph SA (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Simulated Annealing search over the single-fiber non-abelian Cayley graph of D_93 (186 vertices). Evaluates if the non-commutative convolution can flatten the common-neighbor ledger and satisfy the Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Red-priority asymmetric objective for the triangular-book bicirculant: does exploiting the unequal caps (n-2 vs n-1) beat the symmetric floor at missing n?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The book caps are UNEQUAL: red = n-2 on present edges, blue = n-1 on complement edges (blue has +1 headroom). Every known source (Paley, S/K conference, multiplier-orbit unions) is self-complementary/balanced and hits both caps simultaneously, wasting the blue +1. Hypothesis: missing n may admit a deliberately RED-TIGHT / BLUE-SLACK asymmetric almost-difference-set that spends the blue +1 as a relief valve for the mandatory SRG overshoot. Test a red-priority objective (hard-constrain red, minimize only blue) against the symmetric objective at FIXED size and budget, with n=43 positive control, and measure self-complementarity to quantify asymmetry. Positive-construction eval; success = witness OR

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian SA: Bridge Grammar over F_93 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Bridge Bicirculant grammar over the non-abelian Frobenius group F_93 = Z_31 \rtimes Z_3. Tests if the non-commutative cross-fiber interference pattern breaks the +1/+1 excess cage of abelian groups.

evaluations.title: Coherence sign-graph frustration as a switching-invariant closability coordinate: profiling solved witnesses + missing-n coset candidates
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Calibration probe for a switching-invariant theory of triangular-book witnesses. Under Seidel switching S->D S D the multiset of |(S^2)_uv| and the sign pattern of off-diagonal Seidel-squares are invariants of the switching class (two-graph); the degree profile f is a gauge chosen by the switch. The regular book-cap condition (Archive #2 T3) becomes a signed-graph balance problem: a regular witness exists in the class iff the coherence sign-graph (edge sign = sign of (S^2)_uv) is BALANCED, i.e. frustration index 0. We measure, exactly, the off-diagonal S^2 support and coherence-sign frustration of every solved baseline witness, testing the hypothesis that all solved

evaluations.title: Witness Extraction for Vertex Surgery (n=41, 43)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary step for Switching-as-Construction: Extracts the exact adjacency matrices for the baseline n=41 and n=43 witnesses. Verifies their codegrees and stores them for subsequent CP-SAT puncturing and growth experiments.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Capacity Profile: F_93 Non-Abelian Grammar (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Decouples the non-abelian F_93 two-fiber search. Uses SA to find a set A that maximizes the theoretical slack for both same-fiber and cross-fiber constraints. Passes the best A candidates to a custom CP-SAT completion for B.

evaluations.title: Track B groundwork: exact minimum-excess / conservation quantity for the Z_2 x Z_m book bicirculant (calibrate on n=43,67,73)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Groundwork for the excess-conservation reachability map. Derive/measure, as
tightly as compute allows, the minimum achievable total book excess of the
Z_2 x Z_m two-fiber bicirculant as a function of m, and test whether it is
governed by a conserved quantity (Seidel-square mass / autocorrelation second
moment) plus a realizability correction. Calibrate on n=43 (min excess 0), and
the dense-floor targets n=67, n=73. Aim: a computed lower bound on total excess
that reproduces the observed floors, and a first check of whether the zero-excess
boundary tracks Kairos's 2-adic realizability boundary (Archive #16/#18).

evaluations.title: Track A: coherent source-coordinate move alphabet for the book bicirculant — can alignment-pattern moves break the dense excess floor at n=73/67?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Test whether the dense excess floor (~9-10 total at n=67/73) that edge- and
residue-level searches plateau at is an artifact of a too-small (local) move
alphabet, by searching over COHERENT moves defined at the source/profile
coordinate level: multiplier remaps of C-fragments, full-coset swaps, CRT-factor
shears, and size-preserving reservoir trades — each of which changes many
difference-class codegrees at once. Positive-construction eval. Success = a valid
witness at n=73/67, OR a strictly lower total excess than the edge/residue floor
(evidence the floor is a move-alphabet artifact, not a conservation law), OR a
qualitatively new sparse-defect geometry.

evaluations.title: Seidel-Square Baseline Profiling for Growth (n=43)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary diagnostic for the Adjacency Growth proposal: Computes the exact Seidel-Square ledger for the extracted n=43 witness. Histograms the (S^2)_uv values to mathematically determine the required dot-product shifts (the X^T X terms) needed to grow the graph to n=44.

evaluations.title: Track A: non-cyclotomic near-difference-set cross C for the book bicirculant (the mass-binding channel), with free same-fiber absorption — n=73/67/81
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #702 showed the directed cross set C is the mass-BINDING channel (exactly
saturated at balanced sizes) while same-fiber A,B have slack; Evals #695/#703
showed cyclotomic (orbit-structured) C plateaus at a dense floor. Test the
genuinely non-cyclotomic alternative: build C as a directed near-difference-set /
almost-difference-set on Z_m (design-theoretic supply, NOT multiplier orbits),
and let the free symmetric same-fiber sets A,B absorb the residual to meet the
same-fiber caps. Positive-construction eval. Success = valid witness at n=73/67/81,
OR total excess strictly below the orbit floor by >=2, OR a sparse-defect geometry
(over-cap support density < 0.15).

evaluations.title: Seidel Growth Invariant: 6-Coloring the Zero-Slack Graph (n=43->44)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Seidel Growth Invariant for growing the n=43 witness (170 vertices) to n=44 (174 vertices). By forcing the 170 base vertices to gain exactly 2 edges (degree 86), the injection vectors are restricted to 6 balanced permutations. The constraint that new Seidel squares cannot exceed 0 forces a 6-coloring on the dense subgraph of pairs with zero slack.

evaluations.title: Seidel-Ledger Growth Packing: Exact CP-SAT (n=43 -> 44)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Adjacency Growth lane by executing an unrestricted exact CP-SAT to pack 4 new vertices onto the n=43 witness. By allowing heterogeneous incidence (which yields +-2 Seidel square injections), the solver bypasses the chromatic obstruction and seeks a near-regular n=44 witness.

evaluations.title: Pointed DRT proof-control: O/P/M type-ledger invariance
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Build the first native proof-control for the approved pointed Paley-DRT source-inspector lane. For q=7,11,19,43, compute the proposed O/P/M pointed tournament ledger L_T(role_z,a,b), test whether it is invariant on the declared source pair types, verify collapse to standard unpointed DRT intersection numbers, and report any minimal variation certificates. No witness search or score attempt.

evaluations.title: Track B invariant: exact mean-at-cap + flat-parity + additive-energy forced-excess lower bound for the book bicirculant (n=43 falsification control)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Replace the too-weak size-only LP relaxation (#702, Q=0 everywhere) with an exact kindergarten forced-excess lower bound Q'(m): (1) double-count each channel's exact autocorrelation/cross-correlation mass -> exact MEAN codegree; (2) compare mean to the exact caps (red n-2, blue n-1) carrying the +1 asymmetry; (3) flat-feasibility parity: if the flat autocorrelation level is non-integer, flatness is impossible; (4) additive-energy (Cauchy) variance lower bound forcing over-cap mass when mean is at/above cap. Calibrate on n=43 (excess 0, mandatory falsification control) and the missing n=67,73,81. Goal: an exact necessary-condition invariant that gives 0 at n=43 and >0 at the dense-floor n, usable as

evaluations.title: Track A: unbalanced-size bicirculant search — can deviating |A|,|B|,|C| from (m-1)/2 drop the cross mean below cap and open a witness at n=73/67?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
All prior bicirculant searches used near-balanced sizes |A|=|B|=|C|=(m-1)/2, at
which the cross channel mean sits at capacity (#702) and no C-supply meets the
cross caps (#690/#695/#703/#705). Test the size degree of freedom directly: sweep
|A|,|B|,|C| away from (m-1)/2 (asymmetric per channel) to lower the binding cross
mean below cap, trading same-fiber slack, and search for a witness or a strictly
lower excess floor at n=73/67. Positive-construction eval. Success = witness OR
total excess below the balanced floor by >=2 OR sparse defect geometry.

evaluations.title: Directed-Source Lift: 4-Chamber Search on Paley Tournament (q=43)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Directed-Source Lift Grammar by testing modified 4-chamber lift tables applied to the directed Paley Tournament on q=43. Bypasses the symmetric conference graph impossibility by exploiting the asymmetric pointwise codegrees of the tournament.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Seidel spectra, coherence-magnitude & character-sum profile of all solved witnesses + low-character-sum coset-fusion scan at missing m
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Milestone-1 calibration for the bounded-coherence two-graph lane. Two outputs: (1) a reusable calibration TABLE profiling all ~50 solved baseline witnesses by exact Seidel spectrum (distinct eigenvalues + multiplicities), distinct off-diagonal S^2 value count and coherence-magnitude multiset {|(S^2)_uv|}, degree profile / density, and (where the witness is cyclotomic on a bicirculant Z_m) the maximum nontrivial character-sum magnitude of its connection sets; (2) an a-priori coset-fusion scan at 2-3 missing m ranked by nontrivial character-sum magnitude, testing which fusions keep every off-diagonal S^2 <= 0 (the regular/f=0 routability condition, Archive #2 T3). Grounded by Archive #1 R2 (SRG/conference parameter-excluded for all missing

evaluations.title: Independent B/C Quadratic CP-SAT: Non-Abelian F_93 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the Bridge substitution C = G \ A to escape the zero-sum commutator cage. Uses exact CP-SAT to co-optimize independent masks B and C over F_93, given a fixed A-profile from Eval 701.

evaluations.title: Seidel Puncture-Switch Inverse Design (n=41 -> 40)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the second half of the Vertex Surgery lane: Puncturing the n=41 Two-Copy Paley witness by 4 vertices, and using CP-SAT to find a targeted Seidel Switching set W to exactly repair the uncovered critical pairs, producing a valid n=40 witness.

evaluations.title: Generative product construction (n=39 Z_p x Z_q template) for missing comparable-prime-factor n=73,67,81,94
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The solved non-cyclotomic witness n=39 lives on Z_7 x Z_11 with A symmetric, B = nonzero complement of A, and directed C — a GENERATIVE product construction where realizability holds by the product structure, not by search. Every missing comparable-factor n is a product of two primes exactly like n=39 (73=5x29, 67=7x19, 81=7x23, 94=11x17). Prior work used single joint multipliers (cyclotomic) on these, never the product template. Reverse-engineer the exact factor-wise algebraic relation that makes n=39 valid, then transfer it: build A,B,C on Z_p x Z_q from structures on each factor with the B=complement (or generalized factor-wise) relation. Positive-construction eval.

evaluations.title: Ledger-First Exact H-Coset Fragment Search for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Ledger-First Inverse Design lane by utilizing the exact H-coset fragment geometry (order-4 subgroup) for n=44 over Z_87. Perfectly aligns the required near-regular fiber sizes (|A|=42, |B|=44, |C|=43) with the available mixed-stabilizer orbit sizes {4, 2, 1}, completely bypassing unstructured search traps and solving the joint A/C packing analytically.

evaluations.title: Pointed DRT proof-control: trace-shell ledger formula
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up proof-control after Eval #708. For pointed Paley-DRT pairs with x,y nonzero, test the character-sum formula showing the ledger depends on role(x), r=y/x, and especially the Legendre trace S(r)=sum_t chi(t(t-1)(t-r)). Verify whether the coarser data (role(x), chi(r), chi(r-1), S(r)) determines ledger vectors, measure trace-shell counts for task-relevant q, and report compactness. No witness search.

evaluations.title: Generative difference-family fiber construction: two-valued same-fiber autocorrelation by design (asymmetric factor roles) for n=73,67,81,94
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #715 decoded n=39 as a twisted product-fiber table (A = union_x {x} x S_x on Z_p x Z_q, B = complement) and showed the naive transfer breaks in the SAME-FIBER A/B autocorrelation balance grouped by first-factor difference classes. Fix this generatively: choose the fiber family {S_x : x in Z_p} to be a DIFFERENCE FAMILY in Z_q so that the same-fiber autocorrelation sum_x |S_x cap (S_x + d)| is two-valued in d BY CONSTRUCTION (one factor Z_p indexes fibers / supplies regularity; factor Z_q carries the difference-family structure / supplies the book-cap two-value split). Positive-construction eval. Success = witness

evaluations.title: Coupled bi-factor generative construction: DF same-fiber + matched C-to-A first-factor coupling to clear the residual cross-red classes (n=94,67 best; also 73,81)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #718 showed DF-flat same-fiber profiles (reversed factor roles) drop excess well below floor (n=94: 16->10, n=67: 9->8) and LOCALIZE the residual to same-fiber plus CROSS-RED FIRST-FACTOR classes — a shrinking, specific defect, not a diffuse floor. The residual is a first-factor (Z_p index) coupling between C and A. Close it generatively: choose C's fiber assignment to be MATCHED to A's across the first factor (a bi-factor construction controlling both the Z_q difference structure AND the Z_p index structure), so the cross-red first-factor codegrees are flattened by design. Targets n=94, 67 (best so far), then 73, 81. Positive-construction. Success =

evaluations.title: Pointed DRT R0/T-cap lift box for q=43
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: First bounded construction-box attempt in the approved pointed DRT lane. For q=43/n=44, use four chambers plus two role-sensitive auditors. Edge variables depend only on chamber labels, pointed roles O/P/M, and DRT orientation; trace shells from Eval #717 are used only to group and certify cap constraints. Search the resulting Boolean feasibility box with exact validation if SAT.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Commutator Profile under Degree Shift (F_93, |B|=45)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Explores routing the zero-sum commutator profile into generative slack by shrinking |B| to 45. Maps the exact distribution of Gamma(d) and cross-row excesses in the F_93 Bridge grammar.

evaluations.title: Positive Controls for Exact CP-SAT Vertex Surgery Models
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the exact CP-SAT formulations for 4-vertex extension and Seidel switching by testing them on guaranteed-feasible instances derived from the n=31 baseline witness.

evaluations.title: Deep push at n=81 (excess 4, C_x=A_-x) and n=67 (excess 6): fix the winning reflection coupling, refine A-fiber DF structure to close the last (2,2)/(3,3)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #719 reached total excess 4 at n=81 (Z_7 x Z_23, exact relation C_x = A_{6x}
= A_{-x} on Z_7, identity on Z_23) and 6 at n=67 (Z_19 x Z_7), a monotone
convergence from 24/18 across #715/#718/#719 via generative product structure.
Fix the winning reflection coupling C_x = A_{sigma(x)} and intensively refine the
A-fiber difference-family structure to close the residual (2,2)/(3,3). This is a
focused witness push on the two closest targets. Success = valid witness at n=81
or n=67 OR total excess strictly below 4 (n=81) / 6 (n=67).

evaluations.title: H1 controlled symmetry break of the n=81 reflection-coupled near-witness (excess (2,2)): is the residual a transitivity-amplified orbit defect?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The n=81 generative near-witness (Z_7 x Z_23, C_x=A_{-x}) plateaus at same-fiber excess (2,2)=4 within the pure vertex-transitive bicirculant class, with a mirrored orbit-structured first-factor residual — the signature of transitivity amplifying a single defect into an orbit of over-cap pairs. Test whether a controlled break of vertex-transitivity (a few targeted individual edge flips, NOT whole difference-classes) removes the residual without the near-cap shell re-violating. This is a controlled relaxation of the two-fiber object (within the approved lane), measured by exact orbit change and shell damage, not blind local search. Success = valid n=81 witness OR total excess < 4 via

evaluations.title: H2 analytic first-factor residual equations for the n=81 reflection-coupled construction: is the last (2,2) a low-dimensional Z_7 balancing/parity obstruction?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract:
The n=81 near-witness residual is same-fiber only with a structured first-factor
profile {1:12,2:10,3:10,4:10,5:10,6:12} on Z_7 (mirrored A_red<->B_blue). Rather
than more search, derive the exact induced equations: express the same-fiber
codegree at first-factor difference a in Z_7 as a sum over Z_7 of Z_23-fiber
cross-correlations, and determine whether the residual excess is forced by a
low-dimensional integer/parity constraint on the fiber family {S_x}. Analytic
decision eval: does the last (2,2) come from a first-factor balancing/parity
obstruction (predicts it is a family floor) or from a missed assignment (predicts a
fixable phase)?

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Exact CP-SAT Vertex Extension on n=35 (Skew-Paley)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the exact 4-vertex extension CP-SAT model on a guaranteed-feasible base graph derived from the n=35 Skew-Paley baseline witness.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Exact CP-SAT Vertex Extension on n=25 (Two-Copy Paley)
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the exact 4-vertex extension CP-SAT model on a guaranteed-feasible base graph derived from the n=25 Two-Copy Paley baseline witness.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: F_93 Conjugacy Fragments (n=47, |B|=45)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Weakly Structured Capacity Profile to the conjugacy classes of F_93. Tests if constraining SA to sample capacities from symmetric conjugacy blocks can redistribute the commutator variance Gamma(d) without local spikes.

evaluations.title: Supplementary difference set (SDS) construction for two-fiber book witnesses: cyclotomic symmetric-A + directed-C pairs at n=52, n=64 (controls n=40, n=43)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Construction attempt reframing the two-fiber capacity-profile completion as a supplementary difference set / periodic complementary pair problem. The fiber-0 same-fiber codegree at shift d has the additive form alpha*r_A(d) + beta*r_C(d) + const, where r_A, r_C are periodic autocorrelations of the symmetric same-fiber set A and directed cross set C; Archive #4 R2's "required-negative cell stuck at 0" is exactly a non-cancelling sidelobe of this sum. For m=2n-1=3 mod 4 the half-size quadratic-residue set is skew (cannot be the symmetric A), but the directed C can carry the skew part, so a cyclotomic SDS with symmetric A + directed C

evaluations.title: Pointed DRT T1 trace-shell lift hierarchy for q=43
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Test the next pre-registered trace-dependent lift boxes for q=43/n=44. Starting from the UNSAT R0/T-cap box, allow nonzero chamber-pair edge rules to depend on canonical functions of the elliptic trace S(r): sign(S), |S|, and exact S. These are nested, formula-driven shell partitions rather than per-ratio variables. Validate and return n=44 only if an exact graph passes.

evaluations.title: Non-reflection coupling C_x=A_tau(x) to break the same-fiber pile-up (H2 lever) at n=81: can spreading K_a, K_-a to different d close the (2,2)?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: H2 (Eval #725) showed the n=81 reflection coupling C_x=A_{-x} makes same-fiber codegree T_a(d)=K_a(d)+K_{-a}(d) — the symmetric SUM concentrates the residual pile-up at T=81, giving the stuck (2,2). n=39 (valid) uses a NON-reflection C. Test the sharp hypothesis that a non-reflection coupling C_x=A_{tau(x)} (tau a non-negation permutation of Z_7, optionally composed with a Z_23 map) spreads the two cross contributions to different carrier shifts d, relieving same-fiber pile-up while keeping cross channels near-clean, closing the (2,2). This is the exact lever H2 exposed, not a variant sweep. Success = valid n=81 witness OR total excess < 4 with the cross-clean/same-fiber tradeoff

evaluations.title: R0/T-cap UNSAT core and trace-pressure map
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Use the clean Eval #720 R0/T-cap infeasibility to extract a reusable finite certificate interface. Rebuild the exact q=43 R0 model, attach assumptions or deletion tests to grouped constraint signatures, shrink a sufficient infeasible core if possible, and summarize which pair/trace/auditor types create the conflict. No construction search or new variables.

evaluations.title: Twisted Chamber Wiring SA: Z_31 Chambers with 5^t Frobenius Twist (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Non-Abelian Chamber-Wiring grammar for n=47. The 186 vertices are partitioned into six Z_31 chambers. Internal connections are abelian circulant; cross-chamber connections use the non-abelian 5^(t2-t1) twist.

evaluations.title: Ledger-First Inverse Design: Bordered Orbit-Bicirculant for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Jointly solves for a 170-vertex base graph and 4 border vertices to construct an n=44 witness. The base graph is constrained to the Z_85 x Z_2 bicirculant manifold with multiplication-by-4 orbit symmetry, compressing the 170-vertex core into just 47 boolean variables.

evaluations.title: Joint (A, C) wall decomposition at n=81/n=67: is the excess-4 floor a same-fiber A-minimum or a cross-clean coupling incompatibility?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #731 showed no affine coupling beats the reflection wall (total excess 4 at n=81). A calibration byproduct is decisive: the only decoded valid product-fiber witness (n=39) has zero exact global-affine coupling representations, so working couplings live outside the affine slice. This experiment reformulates the wall as a JOINT problem to decide whether the excess-4 floor is (a) a genuine minimum of same-fiber excess over the product-fiber A family, or (b) a same-fiber A can go lower but no cross-clean coupling C then exists (a forced incompatibility / the true tradeoff). This is the closing construction experiment before consolidation.

evaluations.title: Near-Regular Twisted Chamber SA: Add/Remove Moves (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
