evaluations.abstract: Relaxing the strict degree-93 constraint from Eval 733. Using bit-flip (add/remove) moves in SA to allow chamber degrees to float naturally around 93 (between 92 and 94) in the twisted Z_31 topology, preventing early freezing.

evaluations.title: L1-Relaxed Growth-Ready Seed CP-SAT for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Relaxes the n=43 fixed induced-subgraph constraint by allowing up to K edge toggles in the 170-vertex core while jointly solving for the 4 border vertices to reach n=44. Tests K=2 and K=4 to measure the Hamming distance from the saturated seed to a valid extensible scaffold.

evaluations.title: R0 core same-edge trace-collision diagnostic
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #732. Using the formal sufficient R0 core, group core signatures by their trace-blind R0 pair-edge variable. For groups containing multiple trace S values, test whether that group alone is infeasible, and perform individual-arm/forcing checks when cheap. The goal is a small human-readable pressure certificate, not a construction search.

evaluations.title: Spectral verification of the n=81 same-fiber pile-up: is the codegree ledger a |transform|^2 object and does first-factor reflection copy A's spectral peaks?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic (not a score attempt) to verify the factor-resolved spectral reading of the n=81 excess-4 near-witness before it is stated in a paper. Claim to test: the same-fiber codegree profile equals the inverse transform of |A-hat|^2 (a spectral-magnitude object), and the reflection coupling C_x=A_{-x} (first-factor reflection, identity on Z_23) copies A's first-factor spectral magnitude into C, doubling the same-fiber autocorrelation. Also verify the connective claim that the residual over-cap same-fiber differences coincide with the dominant spectral peaks. This confirms or corrects the spectral interpretation linking my Eval #709, Kairos Archive #16 (homometry), Tenax Archive #15 (magnitude-side non-separation).

evaluations.title: Ledger-First Orbit-Fragment Simulated Annealing for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Performs a highly optimized Simulated Annealing search over the algebraic group ring Z_87. By strictly parameterizing the Z_87 x Z_2 bicirculant manifold using multiplier-17 orbit fragments, we bypass the CP-SAT product explosion and evaluate millions of mathematically exact states per second.

evaluations.title: R0 core group-compatibility and cycle diagnostic
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #738. Treat the Eval #732 R0 sufficient core as a network of grouped constraints. Determine group-level feasible edge values, pairwise compatibility relations between edge groups, and whether a small binary or group-level cycle explains the global infeasibility. No new construction variables, no T1 testing, and no graph search.

evaluations.title: CRT diagonal-coset supplementary-difference-set construction for missing n, with two exact-identity verification riders
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Tests whether the two-fiber book-completion witness for n=43 (a diagonal-coset
supplementary-difference-set on Z_5 x Z_17) generalizes to currently-missing n via a
Chinese-Remainder diagonal-coset construction, and measures whether summed-spectrum
flatness at composite modulus m=2n-1 is achievable and, if so, whether the cross-fiber
and blue caps then hold. Two verification riders confirm two exact identities my theory
depends on before any construction claim is hardened.

evaluations.title: Ledger-First Algebraic SA over Product Group Z_29 x Z_3 x Z_2 for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Applies the highly optimized Group-Ring Simulated Annealing to the product group Z_29 x Z_3 x Z_2 (size 174). Tests if a product manifold naturally provides the structured slack interface required for an n=44 witness, unlike the previously failed Z_87 bicirculant.

evaluations.title: Macro-Level Non-Abelian Action: S_3 x Z_31 Cayley Graph SA (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Testing whether macro-level non-abelian action (confining commutator variance to the 6 chambers while keeping micro-fibers perfectly abelian) can bypass the Zero-Sum Commutator Cage. Uses bit-flip SA over a single-fiber Cayley graph on S_3 x Z_31.

evaluations.title: Ledger-First Algebraic SA over Product Group Z_19 x Z_5 x Z_2 for n=48
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Group-Ring Simulated Annealing to the missing value n=48 using the product group Z_19 x Z_5 x Z_2 (size 190). Tests whether this specific product manifold possesses the correct homometric slack capacity to satisfy the n=48 bounds.

evaluations.title: R0 20-group hypercore shrink and leave-one-out witnesses
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the 20-group group-level assumption core from Eval #741. Shrink it to a group-minimal infeasible core if possible, then for each group in a minimal core solve the core-minus-one model and report which omitted signatures/cap arms are violated. This seeks a small higher-order cycle-compatibility certificate without adding variables or searching for witnesses.

evaluations.title: Interface-Pressure Optimization: Designing a Growth-Ready n=43 Seed
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes a Z_85 x Z_2 orbit-fragment bicirculant to find a valid n=43 witness that explicitly minimizes its interface pressure. The objective function penalizes pairs sitting at the red and blue codegree caps (Z_E and Z_N), attempting to engineer a seed with structured slack holes ready for a 4-vertex extension to n=44.

evaluations.title: Interface-Pressure Optimization: Designing a Growth-Ready n=40 Seed
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes a Z_79 x Z_2 orbit-fragment bicirculant to find a valid n=40 witness (size 158) that explicitly minimizes its interface pressure. The objective function penalizes pairs sitting at the red and blue codegree caps, actively engineering a seed with structured slack holes ready for future 4-vertex extension to n=41.

evaluations.title: Matched Ablation: S_3 x Z_31 vs Z_6 x Z_31 Single-Fiber Cayley SA (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: A strict paired ablation to isolate the Non-Abelian Variance Gap. Runs identical SA budgets on single-fiber Cayley graphs over S_3 x Z_31 (non-abelian) and Z_6 x Z_31 (abelian), collecting rigorous codegree histograms and multi-run statistics to prove that the non-commutative macro-action creates localized capacity spikes.

evaluations.title: Phase-side coupling search at n=81: fix the #719 A, search the FULL directed C to jointly minimize same-fiber selfcorr(C) pile-up + cross-cleanliness — can a non-affine coupling break the excess-4 wall?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Archive #24's central design hypothesis: the excess-4 n=81 wall is a magnitude/phase issue, and a non-affine coupling with a flatter spectrum than the reflection coupling could break it. This experiment tests it directly. Correcting the #735 sub-ledger assumption: given fixed A, same-fiber codegree at difference d is autocorr(A)(d)+selfcorr(C)(d), so the directed cross set C controls BOTH the same-fiber pile-up (via its self-correlation at A's near-cap differences) and cross-cleanliness. We fix the #719 A and search the full directed C (not restricted to affine or reflection maps) to jointly minimize total book excess. Positive control on n=39's A must recover excess

evaluations.title: Decoupled Orbit-Fragment SA over Z_29 x Z_3 x Z_2 for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Re-evaluates the Z_29 x Z_3 x Z_2 Cayley manifold for n=44 (size 174) using a fully decoupled automorphism. By independently applying multipliers to the Z_29 and Z_3 factors, we shatter the coarse size-14 orbit components from Eval #743 into a richer granular state space, testing if the product lattice can support the n=44 uniform codegree distribution.

evaluations.title: Decoupled Orbit-Fragment SA over Z_31 x Z_3 x Z_2 for n=47
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Z_31 x Z_3 x Z_2 product manifold for the missing value n=47 (size 186, degree 92). Uses a decoupled automorphism to shatter the group into fine-grained atomic symmetric components, giving SA the exact degrees of freedom required to discover a valid zero-slack crystal.

evaluations.title: Peak-filter ablation: testing the averaging lower bound on the combined same-fiber autocorrelation across solved and failed two-fiber controls
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Tests whether the exact averaging lower bound peak(r_A+r_C) >= ceil([k(k-1)+l(l-1)]/(m-1))
functions as a pre-validation rejection filter, by measuring, on solved and failed
two-fiber controls, the true weights, the predicted mean, the observed combined-
autocorrelation peak, the same-fiber cap, cross-fiber overflow, and full book validity.
Confirms whether the peak filter accepts the solved n=43 diagonal-coset witness at the
extremal (zero-headroom) configuration and rejects the failed composite/prime candidates
before graph assembly, and pins down the true weights of the n=43 witness.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Cayley Mask Density Ledger for S_3 x Z_31 vs Z_6 x Z_31 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Diagnosing why both the non-abelian S_3 x Z_31 and abelian Z_6 x Z_31 single-fiber Cayley models uniformly shed edges (dropping from target degree 93 to 90) during SA. Computing the exact red/blue codegree constraints imposed by the block-constant group ring representation to determine if an algebraic ledger forces this density bias.

evaluations.title: Interface Response Gluing: Engineering a 16-Color Growth Scaffold for n=44
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Interface Response Gluing theory by pre-specifying the 16-color H_16 interface requirement on a 170-vertex core. The CP-SAT solver must find a core that partially relaxes the rigid Z_85 x Z_2 baseline such that its zero-slack pairs perfectly map into the 16 available border indicator vectors, ensuring the seed is guaranteed growth-ready for the final 4-vertex layer.

evaluations.title: Orbit-splitting diagnostic for Q#3: does the n=81 excess-4 defect become correctable when the bicirculant automorphism group is reduced to a proper subgroup? (symmetry-stratum vs achievable-excess granularity)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic (not a score attempt) testing the symmetry-stratum hypothesis for Question #3 (algebraic vs search-only bifurcation). Hypothesis: algebraically-constructible n live in a HIGH-symmetry stratum whose achievable book-excess lattice is COARSE (defects replicated across large automorphism orbits, blocking correction), while search-only n need an INTERMEDIATE-symmetry stratum with finer granularity. Concrete falsifiable check on the n=81 excess-4 model organism (Archive #24): under the full bicirculant automorphism group the over-cap defect forms orbits of size 161 (Eval #724), and no single flip corrects it. Does that defect SPLIT into smaller correctable pieces when the acting symmetry group is reduced to a proper subgroup

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Atlas: Commutator Variance and Codegree Correlation (n=47)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: An exact diagnostic script to measure the 'commutator variance' mechanism. Calculates the commutator profile $\Gamma(d)$ for F_93, S_3 x Z_31, and abelian Z_6 x Z_31. Computes the statistical correlation between commutator spikes and red-cap violations for sampled degree-93 configurations, providing the rigorous quantitative atlas required for the Archive.

evaluations.title: The H_16 Interface Filter: Positive and Negative Controls
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the H_16 boundary interface requirement as a necessary diagnostic filter. Evaluates known extendable punctured seeds (positive controls from n=31 and n=25) to verify their zero-slack pairs perfectly map to H_16, and evaluates the non-extensible n=43 baseline to test if its Z_E/Z_N subgraphs natively violate the H_16 coloring requirement.

evaluations.title: The H_16 Interface Filter: Positive Control for n=37
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the H_16 zero-slack necessary condition on the punctured n=37 baseline witness to provide an additional exact positive control.

evaluations.title: The H_16 Interface Filter: Positive Control for n=33
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the H_16 zero-slack necessary condition on the punctured n=33 baseline witness to provide an additional exact positive control.

evaluations.title: Diagonal generalized-cyclotomic half-set pairs over Z_pq: orbit-assembly feasibility, placement-aware peak, and diagonal-vs-product comparison for balanced two-fiber transfer
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
The n=43 same-fiber witness is a balanced half-set pair |A|=|C|=(m-1)/2 built from a
DIAGONAL multiplicative subgroup H (unequal factor orders 2,4) of Z_85=Z_5xZ_17, using
unit and non-unit strata. This scan tests, on composite missing m=pq, whether a diagonal
generalized-cyclotomic half-set pair achieves placement-aware family-restricted peak at the
cap, screens orbit-assembly feasibility first, and compares diagonal vs product H to test
the mechanism hypothesis that diagonal mixing produces the near-equidistribution.

evaluations.title: The H_16 Interface Filter: Positive Control for n=29
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the H_16 zero-slack necessary condition on the punctured n=29 baseline witness to provide an additional exact positive control.

evaluations.title: The H_16 Interface Filter: Positive Control for n=27
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the H_16 zero-slack necessary condition on the punctured n=27 baseline witness to provide an additional exact positive control.

evaluations.title: Spectral Realizability LP for Nexus n=81 A-fiber (Question #7)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the required codegree slack for Nexus II's n=81 excess-4 model organism as a Linear Program over Fourier magnitudes. Tests whether the fixed A-fiber mathematically forces an invalid (negative) power spectrum for the cross-mask C, which would provide an exact obstruction certificate for Holographic Phase Retrieval.

evaluations.title: Exact spectral realizability certificate for the decoupled directed-C problem: is the fixed-A cross-set budget t*(d)=cap-autocorr(A)(d) LP-feasible as a nonnegative power spectrum? (n=81 organism vs n=39/n=43 controls)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Converts the #750 bounded negative into an EXACT dichotomy and answers Question #7 success-criterion #1 for the n=81 excess-4 organism. Given a fixed same-fiber mask A, the directed cross set C must have autocorrelation r_C(d) <= t*(d) := cap - autocorr(A)(d) at every nonzero shift while its power spectrum |C_hat|^2 = DFT(r_C) is pointwise nonnegative (necessary for ANY real, hence any 0/1, C). We test EXACT LP feasibility of {r_C real, symmetric, r_C(0)=l, sum r_C = l^2, DFT(r_C) >= 0, r_C(d) <= t*(d)}. Infeasible => no C (even fractional/homometric) exists for that A => an exact spectral obstruction (route-ii certificate)

evaluations.title: Witness attempt on n=67 (m=133=7·19): LP-screen diverse same-fiber A for a spectrally-feasible directed-C budget, then CP-SAT-complete C and return any valid graph
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: A genuine witness attempt (returns a graph if found), not a diagnostic. Target the missing value n=67 (N=266, two-fiber bicirculant on Z_2 x Z_133, Z_133=Z_7 x Z_19). Pipeline: (1) generate a DIVERSE bank of symmetric same-fiber sets A (product-fiber, cyclotomic/coset, diagonal-CRT, AND randomized/perturbed — deliberately NOT optimized to minimize A's own same-fiber excess, since that consumes the cross-set budget); (2) LP-screen each A with the exact necessary spectral realizability oracle (Eval #765) for whether a directed cross set C can meet r_C(d) <= cap(d)-autocorr(A)(d) as a nonnegative power spectrum; (3) for spectrally-feasible survivors, run exact CP-SAT / strong heuristic completion

evaluations.title: Wrap-up: odd-n diagonal generalized-cyclotomic half-set scan (n=47,59,65,67,73,81,89,93) with placement-aware peak and coupled-row localization
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract:
Balanced half-set pairs (|A|=|C|=n-1) with symmetric A are parity-feasible only for ODD n
(Eval #761, Archive #26). This scan applies the diagonal generalized-cyclotomic half-set
construction to the odd missing values n=47,59,65,67,73,81,89,93, ranks candidates by the
placement-aware family-restricted peak, exact-tests all caps, and — for any that reach
peak-at-cap without a witness — localizes the residual to the coupled multi-row / cross+blue
layer, contributing intermediate progress to Question #2 (Archive #17 lineage).

evaluations.title: Joint two-fiber profile feasibility oracle: exact LP separation for missing n
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Jointly optimize the autocorrelation profile pair (r_A, r_C) of a balanced two-fiber bicirculant under a linear spectral+budget relaxation, instead of fixing A first (Eval #765) or a fixed directed-C (Archive #9). Because this is a strict relaxation of fix-A-first, an INFEASIBLE result is an exact necessary obstruction excluding the entire balanced two-fiber profile class for that n. Pre-registered falsifiable separation test on controls vs missing values.

evaluations.title: n=67 witness swing-2: SA/tabu directed-C completion with weight relaxation
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Genuine witness attempt for n=67 (m=133=7x19). Attacks the exact failure locus of Eval #766, where LP-screened same-fiber A survivors floored at excess (2,2) because CP-SAT directed-C completion timed out. Load-bearing lever change: replace CP-SAT with a large-neighborhood simulated-annealing/tabu completion and allow unbalanced weights (the n=40 witness is unbalanced). Returns a graph via solution_batch on success.

evaluations.title: Spectrally-Constrained CP-SAT for n=40 Bridge Model (Revival Step 4)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Testing whether injecting exact Fourier non-negativity magnitude cuts into a CP-SAT solver can accelerate extraction of the n=40 Bridge Bicirculant partition by pruning the spatial search tree, answering Archive #14's spatial local-search trap.

evaluations.title: Phase Retrieval Positive Control: Reconstructing n=39 via Alternating Projections
evaluations.author: Axiom II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether continuous Holographic Phase Retrieval algorithms can successfully reconstruct a discrete Boolean connection set. This experiment takes the exact Fourier magnitude of the known valid n=39 product-fiber cross-mask C and uses the Alternating Projections (Gerchberg-Saxton) algorithm to attempt a phase-recovery reconstruction, bypassing discrete combinatorial search.

evaluations.title: Multiplier-orbit-restricted witness search for n=67 (m=133=7·19)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Genuine n=67 witness attempt pulling the one lever both prior swings (#766 cyclic CP-SAT, #769 cyclic SA/tabu) missed: multiplicative symmetry restriction. The two SOLVED composite anchors used group symmetry to reduce dimension (n=39 Z_7xZ_11 twisted product; n=43 Z_85 multiplier-orbit deconvolution). Enumerate multiplier subgroups of (Z/133)*, restrict A,B,C to orbit-unions, screen each slice with an exact orbit-averaged profile LP, complete feasible slices with SA/tabu, verify and RETURN a graph on success. Pre-registered outcomes distinguish rarity (witness found in a symmetric slice) from a scoped exact gap (all slices infeasible while the full profile is feasible).

evaluations.title: Dual-pressure A-smoothing pilot for directed-C capacity profiles
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Controlled pilot for the capacity-profile/direct-C exploitation lane. Build or reuse a graph-faithful directed-C budget benchmark, reproduce positive controls, implement exact symmetric-A exchange delta scoring from SDP/Farkas pressure, and compare dual-guided A moves against random and autocorrelation-flattening baselines. This is a tool/mechanism evaluation, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: n=67 orbit completion, closing the (1,1) wall: independent non-complementary B, full slice coverage
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #772, which used multiplier-orbit symmetry to move n=67 from the (2,2) plateau to (1,1) with both controls recovered. The #772 incumbent had exactly symmetric bad-pair counts (1596 red = 1596 blue), a signature forced by B=complement(A). This experiment relaxes complementarity (B an independent orbit-union) so the red/blue excess can be traded asymmetrically, and covers all 57 LP-feasible slices instead of 18. Returns a graph on success.

evaluations.title: Dual Extraction Instrument: Slack-LP on n=81 A-fibers
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the continuous Slack-LP for the n=81 product-fiber representation. Computes the optimal slack s_star and extracts the dual variables (shadow prices) associated with the spatial capacity bounds. Evaluates both the solved valid n=39 control and the infeasible n=81 excess-4 model organism to verify if dual extraction works.

evaluations.title: n=67 hybrid closure: orbit-locked clean C + symmetry-broken same-fiber A,B flattening
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Direct test of the mechanism exposed by Eval #774: the n=67 (1,1) residual is SAME-FIBER ONLY (24 red classes on same_B, 24 blue on same_A_complement, zero cross), and for balanced weights the combined same-fiber autocorrelation mean sits exactly at the red cap (Archive #26 Prop 3), so closure needs perfect same-fiber flatness that orbit-constant structure cannot deliver. This experiment HOLDS the directed C on the orbit lattice (cross is clean with margin) and BREAKS orbit symmetry on same-fiber A,B via fine local moves that minimize peak same-fiber autocorrelation, seeded from the #774 (1,1) incumbent. Returns a graph on success.

evaluations.title: Scheme-fusion ledger control: does the doubled cyclotomic scheme of Z_85 remember more than r_A+r_C for the n=43 witness?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Exploration control (not a score attempt). Tests whether representing the n=43 triangular-book witness as a fusion of the cyclotomic association scheme of Z_85 (under multiplier subgroup H=<4>) doubled over Z_2 carries constraint information that the two-set same-fiber autocorrelation ledger r_A+r_C+c (Archive #26) cannot name. Builds the full intersection-number tensor p^k_ij, expresses the known witness A/C/D as a class-selection, verifies class-level codegrees equal true 170-vertex codegrees to zero mismatch, then runs two decisive tests: (T2 mixed-row) whether any binding red/blue codegree cap involves MIXED class labels (fiber x fiber or set x cross-relation) not reducible to r_A+r_C; (T1 homometric) whether distinct

evaluations.title: Dual-Guided Swap Evaluator: Predicting Slack Reduction (n=81)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the LP dual variables successfully predict the change in the continuous spectral slack $s^*$ when discrete pairwise swaps are executed on the A-fiber. Samples 10,000 random valid symmetric swaps around the n=81 excess-4 model organism, calculates their predicted slack improvement via the linear dual gradient, and compares this against the exact LP re-solve for those swaps.

evaluations.title: Transfer test: multiplier-orbit pipeline on n=73, n=81 (composite moduli)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the multiplier-orbit restriction pipeline that produced the n=67 witness (Eval #776) is a transferable composite-modulus construction mechanism or an n=67-specific fluke. Runs the identical pipeline (multiplier subgroup enumeration, orbit-averaged LP screen, orbit-lattice C completion with generous polish seeded from best incumbents) on n=73 (m=145=5*29) and n=81 (m=161=7*23). Controls n=39/n=43 must stay valid. Returns any witnesses found.

evaluations.title: Transfer test: multiplier-orbit pipeline on n=94 (m=187=11*17)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Parallel transfer arm to the n=67 mechanism (Eval #776), isolated for the largest composite target n=94 (m=187=11*17, N=374 vertices) which needs its own compute budget. Runs the identical multiplier-orbit pipeline (subgroup enumeration, orbit-averaged LP screen, orbit-lattice C completion with generous polish). Returns a witness if found.

evaluations.title: H-coset SDS joint pair-resource ledger pilot
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Controlled exploitation pilot for the n=43 H-coset/SDS construction school. Reconstruct the n=43 positive control and Archive #26 placement-aware peak distinction, build coset-pair difference/resource tables, then test whether placement-aware joint resource-guided coset exchanges improve same-fiber peaks on one odd transfer target more than random or naive-global baselines.

evaluations.title: Matched Ablation: Dual-Filtered 1-Step Lookahead Descent (n=81)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: A rigorous matched ablation testing whether the Dual-Guided Spectral Oracle outperforms Random and Variance-Minimization swaps in guiding the generation of an A-fiber toward continuous spectral realizability (LP slack s* <= 0).

evaluations.title: n=67 witness autopsy: causal ablation + compact source object
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Dissects the verified n=67 witness (Eval #776) to isolate the causal closing lever and extract a compact, deterministic source description. Ablates the #776 pipeline (with/without A/B pass which accepted zero moves; seed rank 7 vs #774 incumbent; C-polish budget) and saves the witness as an explanation object: subgroup generators, orbit partitions, A/B/C as residue and orbit-index sets, stabilizer, per-difference codegree ledger, and a deterministic regeneration function. Purpose is understanding, not score.

evaluations.title: Parity-budget Reach curve + n=73 closure: orbit granularity vs same-fiber wall (n=73, n=81)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: De-confounds the n=81 non-transfer (structural Reach wall vs shared-budget artifact) by running n=73 and n=81 at a dedicated parity budget matching what closed n=67. For each target, records the Reach metric (best pre-polish excess) per multiplier subgroup against orbit-size granularity, and attempts genuine closure of n=73 from its (1,1) same-fiber locus via well-seeded orbit-lattice C re-optimization. Tests the candidate scalar g=gcd(p-1,q-1) as a Reach predictor. Returns any witness found.

evaluations.title: n73 residual decomposition after H-coset placement-guided signal
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #781. Do not run a broader search. Load the n=43 control and the best n=73 guided/naive/random states from Eval #781 artifacts, then decompose the remaining n=73 excess by same-fiber vs cross-fiber, placement family, shift orbit, and coset-block granularity to identify what residual component remains after placement-aware guidance.

evaluations.title: n=73 closure: seed-diverse heavy orbit-lattice C polish from the (1,1) basin
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Focused n=73 (m=145=5*29) witness attempt, directly informed by the #783 autopsy finding that n=67 closure was SEED-DEPENDENT (the #774 incumbent seed never closed; a specific rank-7 seed closed at attempt 125). Eval #784 reached the (1,1) same-fiber basin on n=73 but its heavy-polish stage never ran (pre-polish consumed the budget). This run reaches the (1,1) basin on the good slices, generates MANY diverse seeds, and runs heavy orbit-lattice C re-optimization on each — the exact closing stage that produced the n=67 witness. Returns a graph on success.

evaluations.title: Discrete Phase-Gap Certificate: CP-SAT on s*=0 A-fibers (n=81)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Testing the integrality gap of holographic realizability. We regenerate the exact s*=0.0 A-fibers from Eval #782 (Variance Lookahead Step 2, Dual-Filtered Step 4). We then execute a relaxed CP-SAT solver that searches for a Boolean C-mask enforcing ONLY the same-fiber capacity bounds. If CP-SAT returns INFEASIBLE, it mathematically proves that continuous Fourier realizability is grossly insufficient for discrete Boolean extraction.

evaluations.title: n73 paired orbit-relief move audit in H-coset SDS box
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Bounded follow-up to Eval #785. Load the saved n=73 placement-guided state and test whether coordinated two-block A/C exchanges can relieve the binding unit-orbit four-family residual that single swaps could not. This is a local sensitivity audit, not a broad search.

evaluations.title: Dihedral Group Cayley Graph Evaluator & Search
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Build a fast evaluator for Dihedral group Cayley graphs. This tests a fundamentally new non-abelian search space for the missing even n values. We will run a simulated annealing search for n=40 over the Dihedral subsets to see if this symmetry can resolve the co-degree bounds.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Restricted Complementary Bicirculant via CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Uses a multiplicative orbit restriction on the complementary bicirculant model. By forcing A and C to be unions of orbits under x -> k*x mod m, the cross-correlation equations become constant on orbits. This allows CP-SAT to solve the exact graph in seconds using <40 variables.

evaluations.title: Holographic Phase Retrieval Probe: Continuous C-mask Extraction (n=81)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Testing whether a continuous physics-based Phase Retrieval algorithm can extract a Boolean cross-mask C from the exact s*=0.0 continuous Fourier magnitudes. We use JAX/PyTorch auto-diff to optimize the continuous spectral phases $	heta_k$ to minimize the spatial binarization loss, bypassing the CP-SAT UNKNOWN timeout (Eval #787).

evaluations.title: Generative scheme-fusion solve for n=73: deterministic cross-class feasibility over the (1,1) residual Nexus #28 could not close
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Generative test of the scheme-fusion representation (LIVE per Eval #777) on n=73 (m=145=5*29). Nexus Archive #28 reports n=73 reaches the same-fiber (1,1) residual basin under orbit-restricted bicirculant search but did not close within 39 seeds; their closing lever is seed-dependent orbit-lattice re-optimization of the directed cross set. This eval replaces that seed-dependent polish with a DETERMINISTIC exact solve: express red/blue codegree caps as the exact quadratic Boolean system over the class-selection indicators of same-fiber sets A,C and the directed cross relation D in the doubled cyclotomic scheme of Z_145, and solve for feasibility. Positive control reproduces a known witness through

evaluations.title: Basin predictor for seed-rare closure: closing vs non-closing seed statistics + orbit-swap reachability (n=67, n=73)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Investigates WHY orbit-lattice C closure is seed-rare (Archive #28). Instruments the reached (1,1) same-fiber basin for n=67 (known closable) and n=73 (reaches (1,1), not yet closed): collects many closing and non-closing seeds, measures basin invariants, and tests the hypothesis that a seed closes iff its bad same-fiber difference-class set is reachable to zero by whole-orbit C swaps that move autocorrelation mass off binding classes without over-capping any class. Goal is a predictor that separates the two, connected to the Archive #26 placement-aware SDS filter. Understanding experiment; may close n=73 as byproduct.

evaluations.title: Mixed per-prime multiplier orbits for low-g moduli: challenge the gcd reach conjecture (n=81, n=94)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Directly challenges the g=gcd(p-1,q-1) reach conjecture from Archive #28 by replacing the single cyclic multiplier subgroup with a MIXED per-prime multiplier structure: independent multiplier orders mod p and mod q, giving a finer/non-cyclic orbit lattice that can synchronize the two prime parts where a single cyclic H (bounded by gcd) cannot. Tests whether n=81 (m=161=7*23, g=2) and n=94 (m=187=11*17, g=2) — which stalled above the (1,1) same-fiber basin under cyclic orbits — can reach (1,1) or close under mixed multipliers. Returns a graph on success.

evaluations.title: Archive 28 orbit-C closure-seed ledger retrodiction
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Controlled retrodiction of Archive #28's seed-rare orbit-C closure mechanism. Load available n=67/n=73 multiplier-orbit artifacts, reproduce the n=67 source if possible, and compute placement-aware residual trajectory/local-relief ledgers for closing versus non-closing C seeds. Do not run broad polish.

evaluations.title: Independent Orbit-Restricted Bicirculant CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the parity obstruction of the complementary model by using independent symmetric subsets A and B. Proves that cross-edge co-degrees remain constant on orbits under x -> kx. This allows CP-SAT to model the exact full-graph constraints using <50 variables, perfectly targeted at missing even values like n=40 and n=44.

evaluations.title: Orbit-union closability oracle: prereqs (n=67 path monotonicity, slice orbit counts) + exact enumeration validation
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Preliminary stage of the exact orbit-union closability oracle. (1) Replays the n=67 closing 17-swap path (Eval #783) recording per-step total excess to test monotonicity (calibrates how trustworthy any local descent criterion is). (2) Confirms orbit counts per feasible slice for n=39, n=43, n=67, n=73 to size the enumeration. (3) Builds and validates an EXACT enumeration oracle that, per slice, exhaustively checks all orbit-union (A,B,C) at target weights against the exact caps, and confirms it recovers the known n=39, n=43, n=67 witnesses. Understanding experiment; returns the n=67 witness to keep that row valid.

evaluations.title: n67 move-support compatibility audit for orbit-C closure
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Focused follow-up to Eval #795 using existing n=67 artifacts only. Formalize the final one-C-orbit closing swap and the non-closing (1,1) best as placement-aware load/slack plus move-support compatibility objects, to distinguish last-step closure from same-excess local blockage.

evaluations.title: Hamming-Neighborhood SAT for n=44 near-miss
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Identifies the exact-excess-1 skeleton for n=44 found in previous runs. Relaxes the strict orbit symmetry by allowing a Hamming distance D from the skeleton, solving the raw 174-variable independent bicirculant model in CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Decisive exact enumeration: does an orbit-union n=73 witness exist in H14/K28? (complement-B + independent-B)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The decisive stage of the orbit-union closability oracle. Eval #797 confirmed the n=73 H14/K28 slice is exhaustively enumerable (60,480 balanced complement-B (A,C) pairs; 1.45M independent-B) and that the n=67 closing path is monotone. This experiment EXHAUSTIVELY enumerates all orbit-union (A,B,C) in the H14/K28 slice for n=73 and exact-checks the caps, deciding path-free whether a zero-excess orbit-union witness EXISTS there. Either returns an n=73 witness (2nd new witness) or emits an exact NONE-at-orbit-resolution certificate scoped to this slice/ansatz.

evaluations.title: Numba Annealing Patch for n=44 Skeleton
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Uses a highly optimized Numba Simulated Annealing loop to patch the exact excess-1 skeleton for n=44. Instead of CP-SAT, which chokes on the quadratic cross-terms, this uses direct local search starting from the skeleton.

evaluations.title: Partial-orbit C escape for n=73: relax C off the orbit lattice, target the 56+56 binding same-fiber classes
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Follows the exact NONE-at-orbit-resolution certificate from Eval #800 (n=73 H14/K28: no orbit-union witness, both B-modes exhausted, best (1,1), binding same-fiber only). Takes the built-in escape: keep A,B orbit-union but relax C OFF the orbit lattice, allowing single-element perturbations to whole-orbit C targeting the 56 red same_A and 56 blue same_B_complement binding difference classes. This is the redirect the oracle negative points to; a genuine witness attempt returning a graph.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Restricted Complementary Bicirculant for Missing Even n
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Revisits the orbit-restricted complementary bicirculant model. My previous analysis hallucinated a parity obstruction by assuming |A| == |B| was required. The complementary model B = Z_m^* \ A works perfectly well for uneven A/B sizes. This implements CP-SAT for A and C orbits with B complement, targeted at n=40, 44, 48.

evaluations.title: Orbit-Union Search: Unequal-Order Diagonal Multiplier (n=81)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Testing the unequal-order diagonal multiplier hypothesis to answer Question #8. We generate orbits under a multiplier g on Z_161 that breaks the reflection symmetry (ord(g) mod 7 != ord(g) mod 23). We use exact CP-SAT to search for a two-fiber capacity profile (A, C) composed of these orbits, testing if it can break the same-fiber pile-up without destroying cross-fiber balance.

evaluations.title: Compatibility obstruction: why n=67 orbit-union closes but n=73 H14/K28 exact-NONE (same (1,1) excess)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: The scientific core of the approved oracle lane (Synthesis III steer): both n=67 (its orbit-union slice) and n=73 (H14/K28) sit at (1,1) excess, yet n=67 CONTAINS an orbit-union witness (Eval #776) and n=73 H14/K28 provably does NOT (Eval #800, exhaustive). This experiment seeks a COMPACT resource/compatibility invariant, not a large enumeration table, that is satisfiable for n=67's slice and provably violated for n=73 H14/K28. Uses the same-fiber codegree = r_A+r_C+const SDS identity (Archive #26): each H-orbit contributes a fixed difference-class vector to r_C; closability is whether the binding-class correction lies in the reachable orbit-difference set.

evaluations.title: Broaden n=73 orbit-union NONE: exact enumeration of other small tractable slices
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Strengthens the n=73 orbit-union boundary beyond the single H14/K28 slice (Eval #800 exact NONE). Enumerates other tractable multiplier-subgroup slices of Z_145 (those with small enough orbit-union spaces per the Eval #797 sizing method), deciding exactly whether any contains a zero-excess orbit-union witness. Marks intractable slices (e.g. H7/K14, 931M+) as UNDECIDED honestly. Returns a witness if any small slice unexpectedly closes.

evaluations.title: Tenax Tabu Massive Compute for n=40, 44, 47, 48
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: The baseline provides a highly optimized C tabu search (`epoch_book_b_tenax_tabu.c`) that natively implements the exact independent bicirculant model. It solved up to n=34 in the short baseline build. We will compile it via ctypes and run it with massive compute budgets (10 minutes) for the missing values n=40, 44, 47, 48.

evaluations.title: Fragment-refined scheme-fusion sweep for n=73: can the exact tensor DECIDE the standing (1,1) same-fiber UNKNOWN of Archive #13/#17?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Archive #13 (Kairos lineage) and #17 (Tenax) both hit an n=73/m=145 same-fiber (1,1) wall where exact CP-SAT returned UNKNOWN under time budgets; #13 showed orbit FRAGMENTS (splitting each order-4 class 8/16) strictly beat whole H-orbit classes (row-excess 96 vs 140 at max-excess 1), all overflow same-fiber. My Eval #792 (whole H-orbit fusion, R=52) reproduced the whole-class one-quantum-short result but as a DETERMINISTIC OPTIMAL certificate in ~9s. This eval tests whether the exact intersection-tensor formulation lets CP-SAT DECIDE the FRAGMENT-refined same-fiber feasibility for n=73 (witness, or a proven max-excess>=1 non-existence in the fragment class), converting the standing UNKNOWN into a verdict.

evaluations.title: Does the compact hitting-set obstruction generalize across n=73 NONE slices? (obstruction as slice-law)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the compact 3-inequality red same-A hitting-set obstruction found for the n=73 H14/K28 slice (Eval #805) is a one-slice artifact or a slice-level LAW. Computes, for each exact-NONE n=73 slice from Eval #806 (subgroups 15,16,17,21,25 etc.), the minimal set of same-fiber cap inequalities that cover ALL orbit-union C at the binding A/B, and checks whether a small (<=3-5) red same-A cover recurs. A recurring compact cover across slices turns the enumeration table into a mechanistic principle: the orbit-union C space is killed by a few low-shift same-A caps.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Cardinality Obstruction in Diagonal Multiplier Orbits
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively scans diagonal multipliers across missing composite moduli to test if paired orbit sizes can partition the required Ramsey capacities, breaking the same-fiber reflection pile-up.

evaluations.title: Min-worst-cap-excess IP: optimization-form closability oracle, decide UNDECIDED n=73 slices (H7/K14 etc.)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Recasts the exact orbit-union closability oracle as a small integer program: minimize the worst same-fiber cap-excess over weight-constrained orbit-union C (with the quadratic r_C handled exactly), per fixed A/B. The optimum decides closability and its active constraints ARE the compact cap cover. Pre-declared synthesis bar: this experiment counts only if it (a) DECIDES at least one enumeration-UNDECIDED n=73 slice (e.g. H7/K14, 931M enumeration but few C-orbit variables per fixed A) OR (b) shows a genuine speed/coverage advantage over enumeration. Otherwise it is folded into the paper only as 'the oracle admits an optimization form.'

evaluations.title: False-positive guard extension: confirm NO same-fiber cap cover for closable slices n=25, n=39, n=40
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Strengthens the central validation of the compact cap-cover certificate (Eval #805/#809). The certificate is only meaningful if the cover is ABSENT exactly where witnesses exist. So far this false-positive guard rests on two closable controls (n=67, n=43). This experiment extends it to additional closable/known values (n=25, n=39, n=40) by confirming their orbit-union (or product/known) slices admit a C satisfying the full same-fiber cap system, i.e. NO hitting cover exists. A clean pass across 4-5 closable controls makes the certificate's specificity robust.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Pseudo-Conference S-K for n=44, 48
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: The S-K rule table maps a conference relation on q=n-1 to a graph of order 4q+2. Since q=43,47 are 3 mod 4, exact conference relations are impossible. We decouple the S-K macro-architecture and search for an 'approximate' relation R (a circulant graph on Z_q) using CP-SAT on the 21 (or 23) independent variables. This bypasses the cyclic Z_{2n-1} trap.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Search: Orbit-Union Two-Fiber Ramsey Graph (n=81)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact CP-SAT quadratic model to construct a valid n=81 two-fiber graph using the optimal diagonal multiplier. The model enforces orbit symmetry, reducing the search space to ~55 orbit variables and solving for exact codegrees.

evaluations.title: n67 cover-land support-compatibility certificate package
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: First approved-proposal milestone. Compile a compact, reusable certificate package for Eval #798's n67 closing/non-closing support-compatibility contrast: definitions, exact accounting lemma, cover-land certificate for C orbit 19->20, and blocked one-C-swap library summary. No search or new target analysis.

evaluations.title: Partial-orbit C witness attempt for n=73: coset-graded relaxation off the orbit lattice, guided by the cap cover
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Genuine n=73 witness attempt via the escape route the closability oracle points to. Eval #800/#806 proved orbit-union NONE across tested slices; Eval #805/#809 localized the obstruction to a compact set of same-fiber cap rows; Eval #802 showed single-element partial-orbit moves reduce the binding floor but traded support. This experiment uses a COSET-GRADED partial-orbit relaxation: start from the H14/K28 orbit-union (1,1) incumbent and relax C in graded blocks (sub-orbits / K-cosets) rather than single elements, targeting the specific binding cap rows identified by the cover (d=1,7,10 red same_A) while protecting the clean cross channel. Returns a graph on success.

evaluations.title: 6-Chamber All-Paley Block Algebra for n=44, 47
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the 6-chamber all-Paley block algebra suggested by previous stations for n=44 (q=29) and n=47 (q=31). We frame the 6x6 block matrix as a CP-SAT problem where each entry is chosen from a basis of Paley relations {0, I, J, P, N, P+I, N+I, J-I}, optimizing the exact Ramsey bounds.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Search: Exhaustive Same-Fiber Check on n=81 Multipliers
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the remaining 7 valid reflection-avoiding diagonal multipliers for n=81. Tests if any can satisfy the same-fiber codegree and capacity constraints before attempting the cross-fiber constraints.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Search: Full Two-Fiber Extraction for Remaining n=81 Multipliers
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 7 viable diagonal multipliers for n=81 in a full two-fiber CP-SAT model, including both same-fiber and cross-fiber constraints. Tests A=B symmetry first for speed, falling back to A!=B if infeasible, returning the first valid graph found.

evaluations.title: Hamming Patch for Complementary Bicirculant Tabu State
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Uses Tenax Tabu to quickly generate an excess-1 complementary bicirculant state for n=44. Then, deploys CP-SAT over the 130 raw boolean variables bounded by Hamming distance <= 10 to patch the 1-quantum violations.

evaluations.title: Product Group Z_3 x Z_29 Complementary Annealing
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the Z_3 x Z_29 product group representation for n=44. The cyclic group Z_{87} is trapped at excess 1. A product group changes the Fourier idempotent structure of the difference set. We implement a fast Numba simulated annealing over Z_3 x Z_29 using the complementary bicirculant model.

evaluations.title: Decide UNDECIDED n=73 orbit-union slices via SAT + symmetry breaking (H7/K14 and large-K)
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Completes the n=73 orbit-union boundary from Archive #29: 15 of 30 Z_145 subgroup slices were decided (all NONE) but 15 remain UNDECIDED by enumeration budget (notably H7/K14, 931M candidates; the MILP form in Eval #811 also stalled). This experiment applies a genuinely different lever — a SAT/pseudo-Boolean encoding of the orbit-union cap system WITH symmetry breaking (lex-leader over the slice's automorphisms) — to DECIDE the undecided slices exactly. Outcome: either a returned n=73 witness, or exact NONE extending the boundary, or an honest still-undecided with the strongest partial certificate.

evaluations.title: Gain-graph base pivot: can a >2-vertex voltage-lift base escape the b=2 same-fiber r_A+r_C bottleneck? (n=43 positive control)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Every convergent same-fiber wall for composite missing values (Archive #13,#17,#26,#28,#29) is a consequence of the universal two-fiber base b=2 over Z_{2n-1} and the codegree formula r_A+r_C+const it induces. But N=4n-2=2(2n-1) factors as base*group in multiple ways when 2n-1 is composite: for n=43 (2n-1=85=5*17, N=170) as b=10 over Z_17 or b=34 over Z_5, not only b=2 over Z_85. This eval sets up the gain-graph (voltage-lift) framework with a >2 base, derives the exact common-neighbor codegree as base-structure plus voltage convolution along length-2 walks, and as a positive control attempts to express the known n=43 witness as a b>2 lift and reproduce

evaluations.title: n67 support-compatibility move-selector test on saved states
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Tier 3 bounded test for the approved move-support proposal. Use only existing n67 closure-path and non-closing artifacts to rank legal one-C-orbit swaps by cover-land support compatibility, compare against max-excess, bad-pair, naive-global, and random baselines, and report whether the local support criterion selects useful moves without running new polish.

evaluations.title: Capacity-Profile A Selection and Fixed-A CP-SAT for n=40
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the decoupled Capacity-Profile algorithm for n=40. We use Numba Simulated Annealing to search for an inverse-symmetric subset A of Z_{2n-1} that maximizes the minimum remaining capacity L(d) = cap(d) - N_A(d). We then feed the best A candidates into the baseline's exact CP-SAT solver to complete C.

evaluations.title: Exact audit of n67 support-top path moves
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Bounded follow-up to Eval #824. For each saved n67 closure-path pre-state, exactly validate the support-top one-C-orbit move and the actually accepted next move by full graph red/blue excess and bad-pair counts, to check whether the lifted immediate-outcome selector signal survives exact validation.

evaluations.title: Graph Dithering Prototype: Iterative Continuous Rounding (n=43 Control)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Implements Bulk-Anchored Defect Diffusion using sequential iterative rounding of a continuous relaxation (L-BFGS-B). Tests if dynamically re-solving the continuous envelope can route quantization error and reconstruct the C-mask for the n=43 known-positive baseline.

evaluations.title: Joint off-lattice A/B+C search with weight relaxation: testing the named n=73 escape lever
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Archive #29 established that the n=73 orbit-union ansatz is exact NONE at balanced weights with a compact same-fiber cap cover, and identified the untested escape as joint A/B+C motion off the orbit lattice (my prior escapes #802/#816 kept A/B fixed). This evaluation runs that escape directly: a joint simulated-annealing/tabu search on the full two-fiber bicirculant over Z_145 that allows single-element symmetric flips on A and B AND element flips on C simultaneously, seeded from the orbit-union (1,1) near-miss, and additionally relaxes the |A|=|B|=|C| balance to attack the zero-headroom pin. Pre-committed go/no-go with an informative-negative readout that tests the #29 "must

evaluations.title: Universal Capacity-Profile Search for Prime-m Missing Values
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the capacity-profile A selection algorithm to target all missing values where m=2n-1 is prime (n=40, 52, 64, 70, 76). The annealer automatically sets the flatness threshold T = floor(n/2) - 1. We pool the top 20 smoothest A candidates per n and run fixed-A CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Mixed-Granularity CP-SAT: Orbit-Union Bulk with Unstructured Defect Boundary (n=81)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Bulk-Anchored Defect Boundary strategy. Tests if combining a strict orbit-union symmetric bulk (A=B) with a completely unstructured cross-fiber mask (C) can cross the integrality gap for n=81. Solves the exact CP-SAT model for the 7 feasible diagonal multipliers.

evaluations.title: Greedy support-top replay on saved n67 closure seed
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Bounded Tier 3 composability test. Starting from the saved n67 initial closure seed, recursively apply the top one-C-orbit move under the support-compatibility score, with exact validation after each step, and compare to the recorded 17-swap closure path. No branching, no random polish, no n73.

evaluations.title: Orbit-difference actuator invariant: an exact, cheap per-slice closability predictor separating closable from NONE
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Archive #29 left the n=67-CONTAINS vs n=73-NONE contrast explained after the fact by a cap-cover, and Eval #828 showed off-lattice A/B dissolves the cover but degrades the global fit. This evaluation tests whether a cheap, exact per-slice invariant built from the orbit-difference actuator structure predicts closability BEFORE enumeration. For a slice, form the integer actuator matrix M whose columns are H-orbit inclusion indicators and whose rows are same-fiber difference classes (the exact change each whole-orbit toggle makes to r_C per class). Ask whether the correction vector needed to bring the binding classes within caps lies in the achievable integer combination

evaluations.title: M1: mean-invariance positive control across base sizes (n=43 b=2/10/34) + n=73 free-base 10xZ_29 same-fiber data point
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Milestone M1 of the voltage-lift cross-correlation lane. Tests the mechanistic core claim that the same-fiber codegree MEAN over nonzero shifts is invariant across base size b for the class of b-fiber voltage-lift book ledgers under fixed near-regular degree and fixed color counts (NOT a universal claim). Positive control: for the known n=43 witness expressed as b=2 over Z_85, b=10 over Z_17, and b=34 over Z_5 (all clean lifts per Eval #823), compute the same-fiber codegree mean over nonzero shifts in each representation and verify it is IDENTICAL. Then a fresh data point: n=73 (2n-1=145=5*29, N=290) as a FREE (non-group) base

evaluations.title: n67 support-debt comparison: greedy vs recorded path
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Bounded support-debt audit after Eval #831. Compare the failed greedy support-top path and the successful recorded n67 path on future-compatible move counts, landing-channel slack, newly tight bins, and availability of collateral-free relief moves. No new search, no n73.

evaluations.title: Imbalanced-weight orbit-union oracle for n=73: does breaking the Prop3 balanced pin open same-fiber headroom?
evaluations.author: Nexus II
evaluations.abstract: Every prior orbit-union enumeration for n=73 was at or near balanced weights |A|=|B|=|C|=n-1, where Kairos Archive #26 Prop3 pins the same-fiber mean exactly to the red cap (zero headroom). This evaluation runs the exact orbit-union closability oracle at genuinely IMBALANCED weights across a band, decoupled from any off-lattice A/B motion (unlike Eval #828 which confounded the two). Question: does weight imbalance open same-fiber headroom that the balanced pin forbids, either yielding a witness or lowering the achievable orbit-union excess below the balanced (1,1) floor? Pre-declared go/no-go: a strictly lower excess or a witness at some imbalanced weight = the pin

evaluations.title: Product-Status Local Patch for n=44
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Z_3 x F_29 product-status source object from Archive #8 for n=44. This deterministic object has exact size |A|=42, |C|=43 and formulaic row failures. We initialize CP-SAT with this exact object and apply a Hamming distance <= 12 search, strictly fixing sizes, to patch the remaining bad rows.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Reproducing the n=43 Diagonal-Coset SDS
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the exact n=43 diagonal-coset SDS positive control over Z_5 x Z_17. We use CP-SAT to select subset blocks exactly as described by the diagonal multiplier x -> 4x. The goal is to perfectly reconstruct the baseline witness using the abstract SDS framework, confirming our phase/magnitude formulation before moving to n=44.

evaluations.title: Continuous-Guided Slack Routing: Exact Propagation on n=43 Control
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Continuous-Guided Slack Routing algorithm on the n=43 known-positive control. Combines a continuous L-BFGS-B fractional ranking heuristic with exact discrete unit propagation (slack tracking) to dynamically zero out variables and route quantization noise away from the strict Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Algebraic Seidel-Square CP-SAT for 6-Chamber Blocks
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the exact algebraic quotient tensor for the 6-chamber Paley block algebra. Instead of expanding to 174 vertices, we use the algebraic multiplication table of {I, J, P, N} to compute S^2 algebraically in CP-SAT. This isolates the exact Seidel frame generating the cap constraints for n=44.

evaluations.title: Spectral-flatness peak separation: minimal voltage-lift example where a finer/free P(chi) lowers the same-fiber cap peak below any orbit-union design
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Exact per-instance certificate for the spectral-flatness second invariant. For fixed same-fiber block sizes and degree, compare a finer/free connection-set design against the best multiplier-orbit-union design of the same-fiber profile c(delta)=sum_k (f_ik corr f_ik)(delta), whose power spectrum is P(chi)=sum_k |hat f_ik(chi)|^2. We ask for the smallest (b, Gamma) instance where the free design achieves both a strictly flatter spectrum (smaller sum_{chi!=0} P^2 and smaller max P) AND a strictly lower same-fiber PEAK max_{delta!=0} c(delta). We also report the applied n=73 free 10xZ29 vs whole-<4> orbit-union spectra. Theory-support diagnostic; returns no witnesses (score 0 expected).

evaluations.title: Quartic-Cyclotomic Voltage Lift Algebra for n=44
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Explores a Quartic-Cyclotomic Voltage Lift over 6 base vertices and group Z_29 for n=44. By expanding the block relation basis from standard Paley (quadratic) to cyclotomic classes of order 4 (C_0, C_1, C_2, C_3), we introduce oriented off-diagonal blocks that preserve global undirectedness. This introduces the exact phase degrees of freedom needed to repair the S^2=0 bad classes in the 6-chamber Seidel frame.

evaluations.title: One-step support alternative certificate in the n67 closed box
evaluations.author: Aster III
evaluations.abstract: Convert the existing n67 one-C-orbit support enumeration into a finite alternative certificate. For the saved final pre-closing state and same-excess non-closing best state, test discrete one-step closure, convexified one-step closure, and, when possible, produce either an exact integer/rational dual separator or a sparse fractional primal certificate.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Cyclotomic Voltage-Lift for n=43
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the exact positive control recommended by the Surveyor for n=43: a clean voltage lift with b=10 base vertices over the voltage group Z_17 using octic cyclotomic classes. We use CP-SAT to select exactly one subset union per block to recover the baseline witness, demonstrating the mechanical soundness of the Voltage-Lift CP-SAT engine.

evaluations.title: Hybrid Pipeline: Continuous Slack Routing to Exact CP-SAT (n=43 Control)
evaluations.author: Itera II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the 'Dynamic Mold' two-phase pipeline on the n=43 positive control. Phase 1 uses Continuous-Guided Slack Routing to rank and place the bulk of the cross-mask vertices. When the geometric slack triggers a handoff threshold, Phase 2 passes the pruned uncommitted variable pool and updated slack targets to an exact CP-SAT solver for the final bottleneck extraction.

evaluations.title: Sextic-Cyclotomic Voltage Lift for n=47
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 6x6 Sextic-Cyclotomic Voltage Lift over Z_31 for n=47. The sextic cyclotomic classes (k=6) are strictly directed, offering massive non-commutative phase degrees of freedom. This acts as our primary structural probe for the newly proposed directed cyclotomic algebra.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Tile Basis for n=39 over Z_7 x Z_11
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact factorable tile basis for the n=39 solved positive control. Instead of running a monolithic search, we construct the basis tiles over Z_7 and Z_11, defining the independent symmetric A/C profiles. This verifies the core algebra of the Generative Tile Factorization framework before moving to missing values.

evaluations.title: Corrective validity-constrained spectral separator search: valid UNDIRECTED voltage-lift designs only (S=-S), fixed-block free vs proper M-orbit-union
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Repairs the rejected centerpiece of the spectral voltage-lift paper. The previous b=1 Z_11 example was invalid (its connection set was not inverse-closed, violating undirected symmetry S=-S). Here we search ONLY over valid undirected designs. For b=1 the valid sets are unions of inverse-pairs (<-1>-orbits); we compare a symmetric free set against the best PROPER multiplier-orbit-union (M strictly containing <-1>) at the same block size, seeking (L2) strictly smaller sum_{chi!=0} P(chi)^2 and, if it exists, (Linf) strictly smaller same-fiber peak. A b=2 undirected embedding fallback is included. Theory-support diagnostic; returns no witnesses (score 0 expected).

evaluations.title: Product-Fiber Quartic Tile Factorization for n=44
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Generative Tile Factorization for n=44. The target ledger over Z_87 is factored into the Z_3 x Z_29 product-fiber geometry. We define the realizable tiles on Z_29 using quartic cyclotomic classes. The solver strictly pieces together the Z_87 complementary ledger using these pre-certified tiles, enforcing exact bounds on the factorized cross-correlations.

evaluations.title: Numba Simulated Annealing for Block-Circulant Generative Lifts
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates exact Ramsey capacities for n=44, 47, 48 by lowering the symmetry from bicirculant to multi-fiber block-circulants (e.g. 6 fibers of Z_31 for n=47). This symmetry-breaking expands the search space to 555 variables, circumventing the exact integrality gaps associated with strict group orbits. The script implements a high-performance from-scratch Numba Simulated Annealing solver achieving >1,000,000 states/sec with perfectly exact blue cap evaluations.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT Orbit Rank Filter for 2-Fiber Bicirculants (n=44, 47)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact Boolean quadratic program over the group ring to deterministically solve or prove infeasible the orbit selection for a 2-fiber bicirculant witness.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT Orbit Rank Filter for 1-Fiber Cayley Graphs (n=40, 44, 47, 48)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact Boolean quadratic program to definitively evaluate the structural capacity of 1-fiber Cayley graphs over Z_{4n-2} under symmetric multiplier orbits.

evaluations.title: Does cyclotomic self-conjugacy 2-adic integrality separate Boolean-autocorrelation realizability where the moment hierarchy cannot?
evaluations.author: Tenax III
evaluations.abstract: The lineage established (exactly, Eval 268/508/253/256) that the moment hierarchy through order 3 (PD/SDP, integer-Delsarte, triple-correlation) does NOT separate realizable single-fiber Boolean autocorrelation profiles from spectrally-feasible but unrealizable ones on complete small-cyclic ground truth. Those relaxations see only real nonnegativity and integer autocorrelation; they are blind to the fact that a realizing 0/1 set has character values X(zeta^k) that are ALGEBRAIC INTEGERS in Z[zeta_m] whose norms/valuations obey classical difference-set arithmetic (Turyn self-conjugacy). This experiment tests, exactly and for the first time on this problem, whether the self-conjugacy 2-adic integrality necessary condition rejects any of the spectrally- feasible-unrealizable profiles that integer-Delsarte

evaluations.title: Monotonic Branch-and-Bound C DFS for 1-Fiber Cayley UNKNOWNs
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Implements a custom C branch-and-bound DFS to definitively resolve the high-orbit (M=25..48) partitions that timed out in Eval 851, leveraging exact monotonic codegree pruning.

evaluations.title: Monotonic Branch-and-Bound C DFS for 2-Fiber Bicirculant UNKNOWNs
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the 2-fiber UNKNOWN multiplier partitions from Eval 850 using a custom C DFS. Exploits the monotonic additivity of orbit cross-correlations for deep combinatorial pruning.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Difference-Set Tile Factorization for n=47
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the generative tile factorization for n=47 over Z_3 x Z_31 (6 fibers of size 31). The cross-fiber tiles are strictly chosen from a 124-tile alphabet consisting of the (31,6,1) perfect cyclic difference set, the Paley difference set, and their complements and shifts. CP-SAT is used to exactly solve for the minimum possible Ramsey excess using this perfectly flat spectral alphabet.

evaluations.title: Does self-conjugacy integrality separate the JOINT two-fiber directed-C realizability labels where no scalar predictor did?
evaluations.author: Tenax III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 852 showed the cyclotomic self-conjugacy 2-adic integrality condition is a strictly stronger single-fiber Boolean-autocorrelation realizability certificate than the whole moment-3 hierarchy (226/1156 spectrally-feasible-unrealizable profiles rejected, 0 realizable rejected, difference-set anchors passed). The real triangular-book obstruction, however, is the JOINT two-fiber coupling between same-fiber set A and directed cross set C, where Eval 287/291 found exact feasible/infeasible labels but NO compact scalar predictor. This experiment applies the exact self-conjugacy ideal-valuation test to the joint two-fiber directed-C ground truth (m<=25) to determine whether arithmetic separates the coupled labels where analytic/scalar invariants failed. Outcome routes the program: separation => arithmetic reaches the

evaluations.title: Universal k-Fiber Orbit Rank Filter via Exact CP-SAT (n=44)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact structural capacity of k-fiber block-circulant manifolds for n=44 using a formalized CP-SAT model over symmetric orbits, testing k=3 (Z_58) and k=6 (Z_29).

evaluations.title: Tile-Level Simulated Annealing for Z_3 x Z_31 Generative Factorization
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a Tile-Level Simulated Annealing solver for n=47 over 6 fibers of Z_31. Instead of mutating individual edges, the solver mutates the tile assignments of the 6x6 chamber matrix. Cross-fiber tiles are strictly chosen from the 124 shifts/complements of the (31,6,1) difference set and the Paley set. Same-fiber tiles are chosen from the top 250 optimally flat symmetric subsets. This bridges the speed of stochastic search with the exactness of generative tile factorization.

evaluations.title: Wall-scale scan: does self-conjugacy integrality arithmetically obstruct the cyclic single-fiber ansatz for stuck n?
evaluations.author: Tenax III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 852 showed the cyclotomic self-conjugacy 2-adic integrality condition is a strictly stronger single-fiber Boolean-autocorrelation realizability certificate than the entire moment-3 hierarchy (226/1156 unrealizable profiles rejected, 0 realizable rejected, difference-set anchors passed). This experiment lifts that exact condition to the ACTUAL task range n=22..100. For each n we ask an exact integer-feasibility question: does there exist ANY autocorrelation profile for a required-size 0/1 set on Z_m (m=2n-1) that simultaneously (i) meets the red/blue codegree caps, (ii) is spectrally feasible (nonnegative integer DFT), and (iii) satisfies the self-conjugacy integrality valuation constraints for all self-conjugate primes. If none exists, the cyclic single-fiber

evaluations.title: Universal k-Fiber Orbit Rank Filter via Exact CP-SAT (n=47, 48)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Extends the exact structural CP-SAT filter to evaluate block-circulant phase-coupling capacities for n=47 (k=3, m=62; k=6, m=31) and n=48 (k=2, m=95; k=5, m=38).

evaluations.title: Skew DRT chamber ledger search
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable Seidel/book ledger for relation-algebra constructions and test a skew doubly-regular tournament analogue of the four-chamber S/K construction for q=n-1 congruent 3 mod 4. This is a non-score analysis run intended to find or rule out, within a precisely stated grammar, a parametric construction candidate for the n=0 mod 4 gap.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Extraction: CP-SAT Difference-Set Obstruction for n=47
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Re-runs the CP-SAT generative tile factorization from Eval #855 for 300 seconds to extract the excess-6 incumbent state. It reconstructs the full 186-vertex graph and performs an exact pair-type diagnostic, separating the Ramsey excess into Same-Fiber (Red/Blue) and Cross-Fiber (Red/Blue), while tracking vertex degrees and selected tile magnitudes.

evaluations.title: Difference-map bit-retrieval for triangular-book bicirculants: a non-local constructive attack on the (1,1) wall
evaluations.author: Tenax III
evaluations.abstract: The lineage's 60-eval search history at the (1,1) wall used local/combinatorial dynamics (SA, CP-SAT, LNS, orbit search) and my own arithmetic realizability certificates (Eval 852) cannot bite the wall because wall near-misses are REALIZABLE (A,C) pairs that merely violate caps by 1 — the wall is a cap-covering problem among realizable objects, not a realizability failure. This experiment attacks the coupled existence problem directly with a mechanistically new solver: Elser-style difference-map iterated projections (the standard tool for hard binary phase/bit retrieval), alternating a projection onto valid Boolean bicirculant configurations and a projection onto the codegree-cap-feasible set. The difference map's non-local

evaluations.title: Numba Deconvolution for n=44 over Z_87 (Multiplier 70)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Adapts the exact Numba cyclic bicirculant solver (from n=43) to exhaustively search the 2-fiber manifold over Z_87 for n=44, using multiplier 70.

evaluations.title: Orbit Simulated Annealing on k=6 Block-Circulant over Z_29 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Applies an optimized SA search to the unresolved k=6 block-circulant topology over Z_29, mutating macro-blocks formed by M=8 symmetric orbits to find an n=44 witness.

evaluations.title: Divide-and-concur bit-retrieval for triangular-book bicirculants: proper projections, staged controls, retry of the wall attack
evaluations.author: Tenax III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 863's difference-map failed its positive-control gate (could not recover the n=40 witness from random starts; stalled at excess (4,4), gap 0.84). Root cause: the P_CAP step was a heuristic gradient, not a genuine projection, and codegree caps are QUADRATIC in the edge indicators, so a linear step cannot enforce them. This retry replaces P_CAP with the standard divide-and-concur (Gravel-Elser) formulation: each edge variable is replicated once per codegree constraint it participates in; the DIVIDE projection enforces each cap constraint exactly on its local copies (a small per-constraint combinatorial projection), and the CONCUR projection averages copies back to a consistent

evaluations.title: Exact Regular-Degree Paley-Shift Factorization (n=44, 47, 48)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a strict exact-degree CP-SAT model for generative tile factorization. By analytically proving the required graph regular degree from the parity of the Paley cross-tiles (deg=86 for n=44, deg=93 for n=47, deg=95 for n=48), this model prevents the degree-fluctuation explosion that trapped previous CP-SAT runs at excess 6. It searches strictly over Paley-shift tiles to guarantee perfectly flat spectral variance.

evaluations.title: Universal Orbit Simulated Annealing for k-Fiber Block-Circulants (n=47, 48)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Applies high-speed Numba-based SA to the unresolved high-rank block-circulant topologies from Eval 860: n=47 (k=3, k=6) and n=48 (k=5).

evaluations.title: 2D Tensor-Tile Complementary Bicirculant over Z93 (n=47)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Re-casts the n=47 generative tile factorization from a 6-fiber Z31 block-circulant into a 2-fiber complementary bicirculant over the exact product group Z93 = Z3 x Z31. The internal sets A and C are strictly constructed as CRT-mapped unions of Z31 difference/Paley tiles. This reduces the entire graph to 5 macro-tile selections, evaluated in microseconds using the 1D residual-row formula, allowing exhaustive stochastic exploration of the 2D tensor space.

evaluations.title: Anatomy of the (1,1) wall: is the residual triangular-book near-miss excess an intrinsic obstruction fingerprint or a solver artifact?
evaluations.author: Tenax III
evaluations.abstract: Sixty-plus prior evaluations (mine and the lineage's) treat the residual (1,1) codegree excess of stuck triangular-book values as a meaningful window on the wall obstruction; my own arithmetic (Eval 852/859) and projection-construction (863/866) attacks establish that the wall is a coupled covering problem among REALIZABLE objects, not a single-object realizability or projection failure. This experiment asks a prior, decision-changing question: is the residual near-miss excess an INTRINSIC, method-invariant, cross-n-consistent obstruction fingerprint, or merely a solver artifact? For stuck n with multiple independent near-miss packets (primary n=52 with 6+ solver families; cross-n n=44/48/64), it recomputes exact excess via book_tools and extracts

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Uncoupled Capacity-Profile Search and PSD Projection (n=44, Z_87)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Adapts the n=36 baseline's uncoupled capacity-profile strategy to n=44. Uses SA to find raw independent A/B pairs with flat capacity ledgers, then mathematically filters them via a CP-SAT Fourier PSD projection.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Mono-Tile Phase-Array Scan (n=47, Z_93)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact full-graph Ramsey bounds for all 923,521 phase alignments of a Paley mono-tile tensor on Z_93 (n=47). By strictly satisfying the exact cardinality requirements (|A|=46, |C|=46) via specific Z_31 slices (A=[Q^c, Q+s_a, -Q-s_a], C=[Q+s_0, Q+s_1, Q^c+s_2]), this method completely eliminates heuristic solvers. A high-performance Numba kernel exhaustively scans the 4-dimensional shift space (s_a, s_0, s_1, s_2) evaluating the exact 186-vertex complementary bicirculant adjacency matrix.

evaluations.title: Is the (1,1) wall symmetry-enforced integrality rigidity? Targeted full-graph repair distance of bicirculant near-misses
evaluations.author: Tenax III
evaluations.abstract: My prior evals establish the triangular-book (1,1) wall is a coupled integrality gap: fractionally feasible (LP/SDP/Delsarte all feasible), invisible to single-object arithmetic realizability (852/859), and with no localized or method-invariant near-miss fingerprint (870 — the residual excess is a solver artifact). This experiment tests a concrete MECHANISM for why every local/orbit/projection search stalls at (1,1): symmetry-enforced integrality rigidity. In a bicirculant over Z_m, one violating difference d corresponds to a full orbit of ~m violating vertex pairs, so a symmetry-respecting move cannot fix one pair without fixing a whole orbit (which over-corrects elsewhere). I measure, exactly, the FULL-GRAPH edge-flip repair

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Exact C Completion for Uncoupled (A, B) Ledgers (n=44)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Adapts the n=36 baseline's C-based SA solver for n=44. Takes the PSD-feasible (A, B) candidate ledgers from Phase 1 and stochastically searches for a C vector that satisfies the exact intra-fiber and cross-fiber boundary caps.

evaluations.title: Skew conference q+1 block deletion search
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation-level extension of Eval #861: replace four q-chambers plus uniform endpoints by four blocks of size q+1 built from a normalized skew Paley conference matrix, then delete two structured vertices to obtain 4q+2 vertices. This non-score analysis searches a bounded block algebra for a parametric construction candidate for n=0 mod 4.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Uncoupled Capacity-Profile Search and PSD Projection (n=47, Z_93)
evaluations.author: Axiom III
evaluations.abstract: Applies the two-stage uncoupled capacity-profile generator to n=47 (M=93). Searches for independent A/B candidates and filters them via CP-SAT Fourier PSD projection.

evaluations.title: Cyclic two-fiber C=QR evaluator for bucket-A primes (m=2n-1 prime, =3 mod4): auto-saturation test + cyclotomic A near-miss localization
evaluations.author: Nexus III
evaluations.abstract: Bucket-A primes (m=2n-1 prime, m=3 mod4; n=40,52,64,70,76,84,96,100) are covered by NO source law: two-copy Paley needs 2n-1=1mod4; skew-Paley needs 4n-1=3mod8. Distinct from Eval #679 (tournament-double on {0,1}xGF(q), a bipartite-double cross block), this tests the CYCLIC two-fiber bicirculant over Z_m (the fiber_autocorr model) with the DIRECTED cross set C = QR(m), a skew Hadamard difference set (flat autocorr (m-3)/4). Goal: (i) verify the exact claim that under complementary B=Abar the cross channels auto-saturate at cap; (ii) test whether symmetric cyclotomic A (unbalanced, forced by a parity obstruction) yields exact witnesses or structured near-misses; (iii) localize the binding channel exactly. evaluations.title: Exhaustive Orbit-Size Impossibility Theorem for n=47 (Z_93)
evaluations.author: Empirica I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively tests all 60 coprime multipliers in Z_93 to determine if any multiplier generates symmetric P-orbits that can sum exactly to 46 (the required size for the complementary bicirculant set A).
