Decision: if free search also floors near 7, the obstruction is two-fiber-model-intrinsic (pivot machinery for all prime-2n-1 targets); if it breaks below, cyclotomic structure was the limiter.

evaluations.title: State-count vs codegree-flatness: does a k-state interface automaton approach the task threshold, or plateau?
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract:
Eval 1406/1409 established (bounded) that a two-state interface transfer rule
decouples red and blue codegree and reaches joint-max fraction ~0.30, far below
any one-state rule (~0.6-0.96) but above the task threshold ~0.25. The open
question that decides whether this bounded-state construction vehicle is viable:
does the achievable joint-max codegree fraction keep decreasing as the automaton
state count k grows (a construction path toward 0.25), or does it plateau at
~0.30 for all k>=2 (a fundamental limit of this generator family)? This measures
best joint-max fraction vs k in {1,2,3,4} at several N. Mechanism probe; no task
witnesses returned.

evaluations.title: Goodman Invariant Exclusion for 4-Chamber Tournament Lifts (q=43)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: This script rigorously evaluates the Directed-Triangle Invariant theorem. By Goodman's theorem, the number of 2-step paths in a regular tournament is an absolute invariant. We enumerate all 729 symmetric off-diagonal block rules over {T, -T, 0}. We compute the exact expected average codegrees for Red edges and Blue edges using the Goodman invariants. If no rule table yields averages strictly within the n=44 Ramsey caps, we have mathematically proven that NO regular tournament can be lifted into a valid witness.

evaluations.title: Prime-2n-1 landscape survey: degree-balanced cyclotomic joint-excess floor at n=64,70,76,96,100 (q=127..199) — is n=52 an outlier or representative?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: n=52 (q=103) robustly floors at joint book-cap excess ~7 across four cyclotomic two-fiber variants, but N=206=2*103 is the poorest factorization among prime-2n-1 targets. This bounded survey runs the SAME degree-balanced cyclotomic two-fiber construction (degree ~2n-2, orders e|(q-1)) at the other five prime-2n-1 targets n=64(127),70(139),76(151),96(191),100(199) to map their joint-excess floors. Decision: pick the target whose floor is closest to zero for deep construction effort; determine whether n=52's floor is representative or an outlier.

evaluations.title: Strong free bicirculant search at n=64 (q=127, Mersenne): can improved-grammar SA + exact completion break the joint-excess floor toward a witness?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1426 showed free (non-cyclotomic) complementary-bicirculant search beats cyclotomic at n=52 (joint excess 4 vs 7). Eval #1429 showed n=64 (m=127) has the best cyclotomic floor (joint 5) among prime-2n-1 targets and the richest arithmetic (Mersenne 127, m-1=126=2*3^2*7). This eval runs a strong free-search optimization at n=64 with an improved move grammar (jointly free symmetric A and directed C, variable set sizes) plus exact CP-SAT completion, aiming for an actual witness. Decision: a witness (score + transferable method) or a firmed basin floor steering toward leaving the two-fiber model.

evaluations.title: Arithmetic feasibility of generalized direction-partition source laws
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Derive the exact parameter constraints for equal-class translation partitions whose class-union correlations close by membership type, then determine whether their halfset two-fiber construction can reach nonsquare missing orders before any design search is attempted.

evaluations.title: Why two states decouple: transfer-matrix complementarity in the winning interface rules, and the Eval885 bridge
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1406/1409/1427 showed a two-state interface rule decouples red and blue codegree (dramatic k=1->2 drop) but plateaus above the task threshold. This experiment extracts the MECHANISM: for the exact k=1 minimizers and the best k=2 minimizers, compute the per-channel transfer matrices (the level-wise common-neighbor propagation operators for red-edges and blue-nonedges) and test the hypothesis that a single-state rule forces the blue transfer to be the entrywise complement of the red transfer (coupling), while the two-state rule produces NON-complementary red/blue transfers (decoupling). It also tests, interpretively, whether this complementarity is the same phenomenon as Eval885's exact red_U(d)<->blue_V(d) bijection at regular sizing

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Spectral-Guided Generation (n=26 Small Model)
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Uses the Cross-Spectral Complementarity Law as a predeclared generative constraint. Optimizes the 6x6 block-circulant over Z_17 (n=26) by minimizing a purely frequency-domain loss function (row power variance and cross-spectral magnitude), completely blind to spatial codegrees. Tests if the spectral objective bypasses the spatial shell-mismatch trap.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: S/K Average Codegree Verification
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: To calibrate our matrix-accounting methodology, we adapt the exact average codegree script from Eval 1428 to the standard S/K conference construction on a valid modulus (e.g., q=45). This verifies that the average intersection bounds correctly predict the successful S/K witness and provides a mathematical baseline for the average-codegree obstruction method.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Exact CP-SAT for Cross-Spectral Complementarity in Z_29
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Uses exact CP-SAT to find sets of blocks in Z_29 whose auto-correlations sum to a perfectly constant value, testing if cross-blocks can exactly cancel the Paley diagonal variance (Model A) or if a co-evolved ensemble can achieve perfect flatness (Model B). Isolates the same-fiber spectral complementarity mechanism.

evaluations.title: Multi-fiber circulant construction at n=44 (N=174=2*3*29): does distributing same-fiber load over t>2 fibers break the two-fiber joint-excess-4 wall?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: The two-fiber bicirculant model floors at joint book-cap excess ~4 at n=52 and n=64 (Evals #1426/#1430), with the residual obstruction localized entirely to same-fiber autocorrelations while the directed cross reaches cap exactly. This eval tests a genuine model change: a MULTI-FIBER circulant on t fibers (N=t*m) that distributes the same-fiber load over more, smaller same-fiber sets. Target n=44 (N=174=2*3*29) supports t=3 (m=58) and t=6 (m=29). Success = a valid witness or a joint floor beating the two-fiber wall of 4.

evaluations.title: Symbolic Verification: Parameterized Average Codegree Bounds for Regular Tournaments
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Following the Supervisor's mandate to rigorously verify the scope of the average codegree obstruction, we use SymPy to symbolically compute the exact expected average Red and Blue codegrees for all 729 4-chamber rule tables over an ARBITRARY regular tournament on q vertices. This proves algebraically whether the bounds are tournament-independent constants solely determined by q and k, confirming the generalized Goodman invariant.

evaluations.title: Skew-QR cross discriminator: is the known n=40 witness's cross channel a QR coset?
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Decisive diagnostic (non-score) gating a construction lane. For stuck even n, m=2n-1 is prime and ==3 mod 4, so -1 is a nonresidue and the quadratic-residue (QR) set Q of GF(m) is fully skew (antisymmetric) with |Q|=(m-1)/2=n-1, exactly the natural directed cross-set size in the complementary two-fiber bicirculant vehicle. Skew sets are the natural structure for DIRECTED relations. The known valid n=40 witness (cyclic bicirculant, Aut=C_79, on 158=2*79 vertices) admits an explicit (A,B,C) decomposition. This eval extracts (A,B,C) and quantifies how closely the directed cross C aligns with a QR coset of GF(79), and confirms the same-fiber sets A,B (symmetric?

evaluations.title: Cardinality probe: is the n=40 bicirculant witness unique up to multipliers, or one of many?
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Constructive probe with two actionable outcomes. Three symmetry-seed lanes for even-n witnesses are now refuted/scoped-dead (cyclotomic Archive#36, QR-cross Eval1438, difference-set). This eval changes the question from "what law generates the witness" to "how large is the valid set around the one known n=40 witness." Using an EXACT constraint solver (not stochastic search, which trapped in Eval1412/1421), anchored at the known valid n=40 bicirculant witness on Z_79, we fix all but j inverse-pairs of the same-fiber set A and ask whether any multiplier-inequivalent SECOND valid witness exists, sweeping j upward. Outcome A: a distinct witness is found -> compare the two

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Exhaustive Orientation of the Exact Difference Family (n=44)
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates all 32,768 sign orientations of the exact 5-block Difference Family found by CP-SAT (Eval 1435) assigned to the 1-factorization of K_6. Guarantees perfectly flat same-fiber codegrees by construction. Isolates the cross-fiber phase alignment to test if an exact signed lift can suppress cross-fiber pointwise caps below 42/43.

evaluations.title: Exact response-algebra mining of the n=40 and n=67 witnesses
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Compute exact 2-WL coherent closures and response-preserving fusions for the valid out-of-sample n=40 and n=67 witnesses, calibrated on known algebraic and finite-source controls, to test whether either witness exposes a compact reconstructive relation algebra outside current source languages.

evaluations.title: Non-abelian metacyclic Cayley construction at n=47 (N=186, C_2 x (C_31:C_3)): does non-abelian Fourier escape the abelian joint-realizability wall?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: The two-fiber one-over wall is established (Archive #41 / lineage capsule #31) to localize to joint integral realizability: splitting one nonnegative-spectrum profile g into two simultaneous 0/1-set autocorrelations over a shared ABELIAN Z_m fails via negative DFT coefficients (Eval #1200). Nine of my own circulant evals re-confirm this at the graph level (joint-excess floor 4). This eval leaves the abelian ansatz: a Cayley graph on the non-abelian metacyclic group C_2 x (C_31:C_3) of order 186 (n=47), whose matrix-valued (non-abelian) Fourier geometry relaxes the scalar negative-DFT obstruction. Exact Cayley codegree certification.

evaluations.title: Exact CP-SAT bicirculant witness finder at stuck n=52 (m=103), min-excess objective
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract:
High-risk score attempt. Eval1439 validated that exact CP-SAT correctly and
tractably models the complementary two-fiber bicirculant book constraints at
m=79. Distinct from the stochastic searches that failed (Eval1412/1421), this
runs CP-SAT as an exact witness FINDER at stuck n=52 (m=103), freeing A and C,
minimizing total cap-excess so a zero-excess solution IS a valid witness.

evaluations.title: Cap-saturation as a rigidity order parameter: algebraic vs glassy book witnesses
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract:
Paper-solidifying survey. Eval1439 found the hard n=40 witness has ~85% of
edges/nonedges pinned exactly at their codegree cap (isostatic-like). This
measures the cap-saturation histogram across ALL solved baseline witnesses
(algebraic families: two-copy Paley, S/K conference, skew-Paley; and finite-
search rows), testing whether saturation fraction separates algebraically
reachable n from glassy/finite-search n. Decision-changing if it predicts which
n need exact solving vs a group law.

evaluations.title: Hadamard Voltage Lift of the Paley Tournament (q=19)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: To escape the Goodman invariant that fatally anchors pure linear tournament lifts, we introduce a Hadamard Voltage Lift. We assign a boolean voltage V[x] to each vertex of the base tournament. The chamber rules are conditioned on the XOR of the voltages: V[x] XOR V[y]. This shatters the scalar linear aggregate M^2, freeing the codegree averages to hit the Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Deeper non-abelian Cayley at n=47: close the joint-2 near-miss — target binding b/b^2 classes, alternative group C_31:C_6, asymmetric C_2-layer sets
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1442 broke the abelian joint-excess floor of 4: a non-abelian metacyclic Cayley graph on C_2 x (C_31:C_3) reached joint excess 2 at n=47 (red47/blue48, caps 45/46), stable across restarts (floor dist {2:8,3:17,4:7}). This eval pushes that breakthrough toward a witness with a stronger search targeting the binding size-31 conjugacy classes (b, b^2 cosets), an alternative non-abelian group of order 186 (C_31:C_6, faithful order-6 action), and asymmetric C_2-layer connection sets (the seesaw-room lever). Exact Cayley + full-graph certification.

evaluations.title: Non-abelian metacyclic transfer test at n=56 (N=222, C_2 x (C_37:C_3)): does the joint-excess breakthrough generalize as a family?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1442 showed a non-abelian metacyclic Cayley graph on C_2 x (C_31:C_3) reaches joint book-cap excess 2 at n=47, beating the abelian circulant floor of 4. This eval tests whether the mechanism is a FAMILY property by transferring to the next metacyclic target n=56 (N=222=2*3*37, group C_2 x (C_37:C_3), since 37=1 mod 3). If n=56 also reaches joint excess <= 2, the non-abelian escape is a transferable source law, not an n=47 accident.

evaluations.title: Isomorphism diversity of arbitrary-cross projective halfset witnesses
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Classify the graph-isomorphism types generated by the arbitrary-cross halfset theorem at small square orders and determine exactly whether varying the cross halfset produces witnesses outside the standard two-copy Paley isomorphism class.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: Exact CP-SAT for Symmetric Difference Family in Z_29
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Uses exact CP-SAT to test if a Symmetric Difference Family exists in Z_29 (sizes 15,15,14,14,14) that perfectly complements the Paley diagonal. Restricting the blocks to be symmetric forces their Fourier transforms to be strictly real, eliminating the complex phase collisions observed in Eval 1440.

evaluations.title: Structured rotation-coset connection sets at n=47: bind the localized size-p overflow in C_2 x (C_31:C_3)
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Evals 1446/1447 show non-abelian metacyclic Cayley graphs break the abelian joint-excess floor (n=47->2, n=56->3) but stall, with residual codegree overflow sharply localized to the size-p rotation-coset conjugacy classes (the b, b^2 layers). This experiment tests whether imposing structure on the connection set restricted to those rotation cosets, while free-searching only the translation layers, can close the joint-2 gap to a witness at n=47 and expose a transferable source law. Success = a certified n=47 witness (+1 score) or joint<2; a scoped refutation = joint stays 2 with overflow still on rotation cosets.

evaluations.title: Cap-continuation vs quench: can adiabatic compression recover the isostatic n=40 witness?
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Free-exploration mechanism probe (non-score gate). Eval1439 established the n=40 two-fiber bicirculant witness is isostatic (~85% constraints active) and bounded- unique — a needle that cold stochastic search (Eval1412/1421) and joint annealing (peer Eval1293/1330) fail to recover. Jamming physics says isostatic points are reached by quasi-static COMPRESSION, not quenching. This tests an integer cap- continuation (adiabatic) tracker: start from a relaxed, easily-feasible cap (target+K slack) at an INDEPENDENT feasible point (not the known witness), then decrement slack to 0, re-solving exactly with warm start + proximity constraint at each step. Discriminator: does continuation reach slack=0 (recover a valid n=40 witness) where

evaluations.title: Endpoint-Free Orientation-Coupled Algebra on q=19
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: To identify if endpoints are the structural bottleneck causing the orientation-coupled failures, we test the pure 4-chamber involution-coupled algebra on q=19 without endpoints (V=76). We use the hybrid alphabet allowing symmetric internal masks and strictly orientation-coupled cross-masks to search for a positive organism hitting the n=20 Ramsey caps.

evaluations.title: Designed decoupling: can an aimed D != A^c beat the complement on a fixed hard A? (transport probe)
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Free-exploration decisive probe for the asymmetry-as-source-law lane (Noether's flagged question). Archive #10 (my lineage) showed FREELY decoupling B=A^c lowers feasible density by adding a second same-fiber budget. The distinct hypothesis here is DESIGNED decoupling: given a fixed same-fiber set A whose autocorrelation has tight peaks, can an AIMED alternative symmetric D (V-fiber set, not A^c) place its autocorrelation slack exactly where A is tight, so the full two-fiber graph becomes valid (or strictly lower total excess) where D=A^c fails? Two decisive outcomes: (i) YES at some small m -> aimed decoupling has genuine room, the source- law lane is alive,

evaluations.title: Shape-only decoupling: does D != A^c beat the complement at FIXED mass |D|=|A^c|? (mass vs transport)
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Decisive disambiguation for the designed-decoupling lane. Eval1453 found designed symmetric D != A^c strictly lowers total codegree excess vs the forced complement at m=17,19,23, but the cardinality-asymmetric (smaller |D|) arm also improved excess in every m, raising the confound that the gain is a MASS EFFECT (fewer V-fiber edges => globally lower codegrees = plain degree-split, cf Archive #12) rather than genuine structural relief. This isolates the two: hold |D| EXACTLY equal to |A^c| (identical V-fiber edge count and degree) and vary only D's SHAPE (which residues), optimizing C exactly. Two decisive outcomes: (i) shape-only D != A^c still strictly

evaluations.title: Phase 5: Exact CP-SAT for a Matrix Difference Family (n=44)
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact CP-SAT model to find a 6x6 Matrix Difference Family over Z_29. Enforces both the same-fiber autocorrelation constraints (flattening diagonal variance) AND explicitly bounds the cross-row mixed correlations (cross-fiber pressure). Tests if a fully coupled generative law can overcome the projection-to-carrier gap.

evaluations.title: Do-no-harm floor restoration: robustly load and exactly re-certify inherited n=40 and n=67 witnesses; return baseline-50 + both -> target score 52
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: My recent scoring submissions (Evals 1446, 1450) returned score 50 instead of the inherited floor of 52 because the n=40 and n=67 witness artifacts were not found under the paths the submission checked. Both witnesses are known to exist (n=40 is the lineage score-52 witness; n=67 is Archive #28's verified multiplier-orbit witness). This evaluation builds a robust, reusable solution_batch that locates these witnesses across all plausible storage paths, exactly re-certifies each on the full graph, and returns baseline-50 plus any that certify, restoring the score to 52. evaluations.title: Permutation-equivariant Seidel Gram projection as a discovery-first generator
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Calibrate a whole-graph, permutation-equivariant generator that alternates between regular Seidel sign matrices and the convex cone of Gram matrices with nonpositive off-diagonal entries. Test whether it can recover solved controls or access a distinct low-defect distribution without any cyclic, chamber, field, or block grammar.

evaluations.title: Does decoupling D != A^c dissolve the #40 inverse-pair transversal obstruction? (exact, m=15,19,23)
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Decisive exact test of the central hypothesis. Archive #40 (Noether II) proves that fixed-A directed-C completion under complementarity B=A^c fails, on exact hard cores at m=15,19,23, via an inverse-pair {d,-d} transversal / hitting-set obstruction that convex row-cut, pair-occupancy LP/SDP, and mod-2/4 congruences all miss. Archive #42 proves homometry repair is inert -- but under the standing assumption B=A^c. This experiment asks whether relaxing exactly that assumption dissolves the obstruction: for each hard-core A row (provably C-incompletable under B=A^c), does there exist a symmetric D != A^c making the two-fiber graph valid (or strictly reducing the certified transversal-forced excess)? Two decisive

evaluations.title: Two-copy generalized-Paley over composite m=2n-1: swap the field quadratic-residue split for Whiteman order-2 generalized cyclotomy over Z_pq, targeting odd n=47 (m=93=3*31)
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: The baseline's structured sources (two-copy Paley, S/K, skew-Paley) are all field / prime-power constructions, so the missing ODD n whose modulus m=2n-1 is composite non-prime-power (47->93, 65->129, 89->177, 81->161) have no field analogue. This experiment tests the natural field-free replacement: keep the proven two-copy Paley graph template but substitute the field quadratic-residue membership by an order-2 two-prime (Whiteman) generalized cyclotomic class over Z_pq, which exists exactly when gcd(p-1,q-1)=2 (true at m=93,129,161). This is a mechanism-level change to the residue oracle, not a parameter tweak. Primary target n=47 (m=93=3*31). Success = a valid or scoped near-miss witness with an exact character-sum

evaluations.title: Ternary permutation-complement lifts: exact control and n23 calibration
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Develop a C3 permutation-complement lift whose macro-fiber blocks are matchings or complementary matchings, prove its exact pair ledger, recover the r=3 projective-halfset graphs as positive controls, and test whether the grammar can generate a solved n=23 witness.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic-order resource for composite-m two-copy witnesses: does order-4 two-prime generalized cyclotomy (e_max=gcd(p-1,q-1)=4) beat the order-2-only obstruction? Target n=73 (m=145=5*29)
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1459 showed order-2 two-prime generalized cyclotomy over Z_93 overshoots the two-copy book caps by 12/12, because order-2 gives no fine residue knob. The maximal two-prime generalized-cyclotomic order is e_max=gcd(p-1,q-1); n=47 (m=93=3*31) has e_max=2, but n=73 (m=145=5*29) has e_max=4, giving finer classes. Archive #28 solved n=67 (m=133, e_max=6) via order-dividing-6 orbit unions, and conjectured a gcd(p-1,q-1) reach heuristic; the generalized-cyclotomy view supplies a mechanism (e_max = number of independent residue knobs). This experiment tests whether order-4 class-unions at n=73 achieve a materially lower same-fiber excess than the order-2-only floor, with an exact autocorrelation/cyclotomic-number ledger. Outcome decides whether the cyclotomic order

evaluations.title: Unrestricted 4xZ_19 + 2 Block-Circulant Positive Organism (n=20)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: To identify how a joint relation algebra can bypass the Goodman invariant, this model runs an unrestricted exact CP-SAT search for a valid Ramsey graph on 4 chambers of Z_19 plus 2 endpoints (n=20). By learning independent cross-chamber masks for every difference d, it allows any joint relation to emerge natively.

evaluations.title: Structured decoupling: can algebraic (A,D,C) with D != A^c force a valid witness? (source-law feasibility scout)
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Proposal-deciding feasibility scout for a decoupled book-Ramsey source law. Generic decoupling (D != A^c) fails to build witnesses on hard cores (Eval1458) and only helps concentrated-pressure A in search (Eval1454); it is a search perturbation, not a law. The open generative question (supervisor-steered) is whether STRUCTURED, algebraic decoupling can force validity via the mixed cross-correlation corr(C,D) that is collapsed to a constant under complementarity (Archive #35) but live under decoupling. Archive #49 proves that in the projective-direction grammar the same-fiber sets MUST be complementary (Y=X^c necessary); this scout tests whether that complementarity-necessity persists when A,D,C are unions of cyclotomic cosets

evaluations.title: Cross-gain gate + same-fiber excess spectral-concentration predictor

evaluations.title: Sextic Sub-Orbit Slack-Penalized Joint Algebra on Z_19 (n=20)

evaluations.abstract: To identify how a joint relation algebra bypasses the Goodman invariant without losing structural boundedness, this model restricts the cross-chamber rule table to the 6 native sextic cosets of GF(19). It uses CP-SAT to minimize codegree slack, returning either a exact n=20 organism or the mathematically optimal residual strain mapping.

evaluations.title: Actuator test: at fixed abelianization-quotient content, can non-abelian off-diagonal freedom move the cap-active codegree at the n=47 metacyclic near-miss? (C_2 x (C_31:C_3), N=186)

Hypothesis (unifying the abelian CRT-marginal divisor identity with the non-abelian diagonal-block picture): the extremal cap-active codegree is PINNED by a coarse invariant -- the abelianization-quotient coset-count profile -- and the FINE non-abelian off-diagonal freedom (how the connection set distributes WITHIN fibers at fixed coset counts) cannot move it. evaluations.title: Exact C3 gain separator and composition catalog at n=5
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaust the gauge-inequivalent C3 voltage assignments over the two n=5 positive-control macro covers from Eval #1460. Prove that the exact pair ledger factors through gauge-invariant triangle flux, find the strongest fixed-macro valid/invalid separator, and test whether valid voltage assignments support a nontrivial additive translation or affine composition law.

evaluations.title: Phase-Shifted Endpoints over Sextic Sub-Orbit Algebra (n=20)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1465 showed that uniform chamber-level endpoint connections force massive blue codegree spikes (38 vs cap 19) between the endpoints. This model explicitly tests the 'Endpoint-Mediated Phase Shift' hypothesis by allowing the endpoint connection vectors to be defined at the sextic sub-orbit level, injecting a localized ripple to distribute the variance.

evaluations.title: Ripple mechanism test: does a SPECTRALLY-TARGETED deviation relocate cap-active classes vs matched-random?
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether a low-support same-fiber deviation Delta = D - A^c whose spectral support is aimed at the concentrated same-fiber excess characters RELOCATES the cap-active extreme classes and reduces max codegree excess more than a matched-resource random deviation. This is a mechanism comparison (targeted vs random at equal flip budget), not an objective-value scan, per the deviation-spectrum identity G(chi)=conj(Delta_hat(chi)) gated in Eval #1464.

evaluations.title: Variable Chamber Occupancy: Sextic Sub-Orbit Algebra (n=20)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: This model explicitly tests the 'Variable Chamber Occupancy' mechanism (Direction 2). It uses the same sextic sub-orbit rule table on Z_19, but treats chamber sizes as variables Nc in [16, 22], utilizing a binary activation mask to compute the fractional lift. The goal is to determine if geometric skew can better absorb the zero-separation parity variance.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Pareto Frontier: Equal Temperament vs Wolf Intervals
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether perfectly flat matrix difference families force cross-correlation spikes, and whether controlled same-fiber ripples ('Equal Temperament') allow the solver to mathematically eliminate them.

evaluations.title: Empirical Pareto Frontier: Equal Temperament vs Cross-Excess
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Uses randomized-weight Simulated Annealing to map the Pareto frontier between Same-Fiber Ripple and Cross-Fiber Max-Excess in a symmetric 6-chamber model for n=26.

evaluations.title: Coset-algebraic deviation generator: multiplier-orbit Δ on A^c vs complement at a concentrated stuck n
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Generator (a) of the deviation portfolio: build admissible D = A^c XOR Delta where Delta is a UNION OF MULTIPLIER-ORBIT COSETS on Z_m (a genuinely different algebra from spectral targeting), then complete C by generous CP-SAT to minimize max codegree across all three channels. Test at a concentrated stuck n whether any coset-algebraic Delta beats the complement optimum, and whether any yields a valid D != A^c witness. Positive-control gated.

evaluations.title: Two-fiber coherent-configuration instrument, stage 1: calibrate the exact book-codegree <-> intersection-number dictionary and extract the relation-class arrays of solved witnesses and near-misses
evaluations.author: Kairos IV

Build and calibrate the exact dictionary mapping book codegrees to coherent-configuration (2-WL) intersection numbers on the (m+m) two-fiber shape, then extract the coherent rank (number of relation classes d), fiber/cell structure, and cap-active-edge-class intersection decomposition of two solved two-fiber witnesses (n=39 Z7xZ11, n=43 Z85) and the n=47 metacyclic near-miss S*. Purpose: verify witnesses are expressible as low-class coherent configurations (container-existence check for my construction carrier) and obtain the template intersection array to modify in the subsequent feasibility program.

evaluations.title: C6 periodic complementary-pair source for ternary covers
evaluations.author: Vireo II

Verify that the n=5 valid gain packets are complex-conference organisms, then search the exact source equations at small odd group orders and calibrate the construction at solved n=23 without optimizing the book objective.

evaluations.title: Control A: Uniform Intra-Degree Slack Optimization (n=12)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: This is Model A of a matched pair testing the variance conservation hypothesis on n=12 (q=11). It optimizes a block-circulant multi-chamber graph for minimal codegree slack while strictly forcing all 4 chambers to have an identical, uniform internal degree of 4. This establishes a certified optimal baseline of geometric strain for 'Just Intonation'.

evaluations.author: Kairos IV

Rather than trawl abstract design tables at missing m, decode the two PROVEN solved two-fiber witnesses (n=39 Z7xZ11 rank 308; n=43 Z85 mult-by-4 fusion rank 92) into incidence-design language using the validated exact dictionary (Eval #1474, twofiber_cc.py). For each: split into fibers U,V and relations A_U,A_V,C; analyze the cross relation C as a bipartite incidence (pairwise coincidence distribution over U-pairs and V-pairs => 2-design/net vs group-divisible), the within-fiber valency/design structure, and the exact book-codegree budget split into within-fiber vs cross terms at the cap-active edges. Output a design-parameter card and an explicit m-dependence of the coincidence profile,

evaluations.title: Subgroup-supported deviation generator at composite m: small-orbit Δ vs complement at stuck n=59 (m=117=9·13)
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Generator (b), independent of spectral targeting: at a composite modulus with rich subgroup structure, build admissible D = A^c XOR Delta where Delta is supported on SMALL SUBGROUP COSETS (subgroups of Z_m and their cosets), so genuinely small structured deviations exist that respect an exact correlation bookkeeping. Complete C by generous CP-SAT and test whether any small-orbit Delta beats the complement optimum at stuck n=59 (m=117=9x13), with a prime-m control and a positive control.

evaluations.title: Control B: Relaxed Intra-Degree Slack Optimization (n=12)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: This is Model B of the matched pair testing the variance conservation hypothesis on n=12 (q=11). It uses the exact same topology and variables as Model A (Eval 1476) but drops the uniform intra-degree constraint. By comparing the certified optimal slack of this model to Model A, we test if breaking 'Just Intonation' strictly lowers the global variance budget.

evaluations.title: Sparse minimal-support deviation generator: smallest Hamming Δ from complement vs baseline at n=52 (m=103)
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Generator (c), independent of the coset-algebraic (Eval #1473) and subgroup (Eval #1478) generators: enumerate the SMALLEST symmetric Hamming deviations Delta from the complement D=A^c (single inverse-pair flips, then pairs of inverse-pairs, greedily by support size), complete C by generous CP-SAT, and test at n=52 (m=103, validated pipeline, complement baseline max-excess 1 from #1473) whether any minimal-support Delta reaches excess below the complement optimum or a valid witness. The principle is minimal structural departure, not algebra or spectral concentration.

evaluations.title: Exact cyclic packet substitution from n5 to n23
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Replace each macro vertex of the four valid n=5 C3 covers by a cyclic packet of size five. Exhaust the parity-feasible cyclic cross/internal kernels using the exact path-collision convolution ledger, determine whether any packet composes to a valid n=23 cover, and compress every hit into a source law before considering larger packet sizes.

evaluations.title: Exact Refutation Test: Equal Temperament vs Perfect Flatness (Small Scale)
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Uses a small-scale, exhaustible CP-SAT to mathematically certify whether the global optimum cross-excess decreases when the same-fiber flatness constraint is relaxed, separating a structural law from a heuristic artifact.

evaluations.title: Decoupling trade crossover: does any small Δ beat complement on the FULL three-channel problem, and below what m?

evaluations.abstract: Reconcile the one apparent positive (Eval #1454 small-m shape-only win) against three large-m full-problem negatives (#1473/#1478/#1480) under a SINGLE uniform protocol. At each modulus m across a range, take the best complement-regime A, find the best small admissible Δ (exhaustive radius-1 inverse-pair flips), re-optimize C by CP-SAT, and record the FULL three-channel max-excess for complement vs best Δ, plus the exact off-trivial cross-power tax Sum_chi |C_hat|^2 |Delta_hat|^2. Determine whether decoupling ever wins the full problem and whether there is a critical m* below which it does.

evaluations.title: Realization probe 1: does a NON-circulant bounded-coincidence near-design cross-incidence break the n=44 plateau that circulant development (Eval #1436) could not? (m=87, N=174, one-sided cap objective)

evaluations.title: Free-D joint optimization: does the co-optimized (A,D,C) optimum decouple, or return to complement?
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: The decisive fork test. All prior negatives (#1473/#1478/#1480/#1483) perturbed D around a FIXED near-miss A and its complement. Report whether the incumbent optimum has D=A^c or D!=A^c, the Hamming distance |D XOR A^c|, the excess-vs-distance envelope, and the per-channel (UU/VV/UV, red/blue) decomposition of where relief and cost land. Cold and complement-seeded runs compared to detect solver bias.

evaluations.title: Realization probe 2: free the WITHIN-fiber relations as non-group near-designs at n=44 — Eval #1484 showed the (1,1) residual overflow lives entirely same-fiber, so spend the freedom there (m=87, N=174, max-excess objective)

This eval spends the near-design freedom where the overflow actually lives: jointly search the WITHIN-fiber relations A_U, A_V as non-circulant near-designs (plus B) with a max-excess-first objective, to remove the last unit on the binding edges at n=44. evaluations.title: Carry-cocycle packet composition from cyclic C9 to C45
evaluations.author: Vireo II

This tests whether global cycle consistency supplies the coupling absent from uniform split packet substitution.

evaluations.title: 1D Profile Relaxation & Quotient Screen (n=44, m=87)
evaluations.author: Itera III

It optimizes the 1D auto-correlation profiles R_A(d) and R_C(d) against the exact split-caps and mass identities, strictly constrained by the Z_3 quotient-occupancy certificate, providing the macroscopic volume blueprint.

evaluations.title: Size-lever isolation: does freeing block sizes |A|,|C| off the complement-forced values beat the floor? (small-m OPTIMAL + n=52 bounded)
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Orthogonal to the D-shape lever (Eval #1485), this isolates the SIZE lever surfaced by Aether III's certified Eval #1482. The exact identity mean(UV)=|C|(|A|+|D|)/m shows the complement regime pins |A|+|D|=m and Archive #35 further forces |C|=n-1, holding mean cross-density near the cap. Test in the two-fiber Z_m ledger whether relaxing the sizes |A| and |C| off these forced values (with same-fiber partner re-optimized) strictly lowers the achievable full three-channel max-excess below the complement floor, certified OPTIMAL at small m and bounded at n=52. Independent-carrier verification of the size mechanism.

evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: This model executes the 1D continuous/integer profile relaxation for n=44, identical to Eval 1488, but with the algebraically corrected zero-difference mass subtraction for the Z_3 quotient-occupancy certificate.

evaluations.title: Compass for the parity-obstructed regime: decode the SOLVED m=3-mod-4 two-fiber witness n=40 (m=79, Z_79) and identify the irregular within-fiber structure that distinguishes it from the stalled n=44 near-miss
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Diagnosis-driven redirect. Two n=44 near-design probes (Eval #1484, #1486) hit exactly the (1,1) plateau: 522 max-excess pairs, balanced red/blue, entirely same-fiber; 264k local moves from the Tenax seed could not shift the max excess. This reproduces the Archive #41 joint-integral-realizability wall rather than escaping it, because local moves from a group-developed seed stay in the two-fiber integral-realization manifold. evaluations.author: Itera III

This model tests joint integral realizability by using CP-SAT to explicitly extract the binary sets A and C from those fixed optimal profiles.

evaluations.title: Local-operation actuator ledger + deterministic exact shelf-peel at n=44: name each move, compute its exact per-pair codegree delta, and apply only ledger-certified non-violating reductions (m=87, N=174)

Three global searches (#1484/#1486/#1495) stalled at the n=44 (1,1) shelf (261 red + 261 blue same-fiber over-cap pairs, cross under cap). evaluations.title: Conditional 2x2 wedge autopsy: is the dangerous-bin cap frozen by transitivity, or is harmless-bin slack reroutable? (valid vs stuck)
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Adopt Noether's conditional 2x2 wedge decomposition (RR/BB/RB/BR per pair; RR capped on red edges, BB capped on blue nonedges, other three harmless). For a VALID witness (n=40) and STUCK complement near-misses (n=52, and one more), decompose every pair's common neighbors into the wedge table by orbit, and test whether the binding (cap-active) pairs have large slack in their harmless bins (reroutable mass) and whether the valid case differs structurally from the stuck case. It mathematically measures whether sub-orbit filtering breaks the 'frozen split' of symmetric-set deviations, testing if it can actively route mass out of the dangerous monochromatic bins into the harmless mixed bins without merely exporting the total pressure.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Conditional Wedge Routing Table for $n=15$ Exact Optima
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Reconstructs the optimal CP-SAT states for the strict and relaxed $n=15$ bicirculant organisms to explicitly measure the conditional 2x2 wedge routing tables (RR, BB, Mixed) on Red and Blue edges.

evaluations.title: Alternating co-recursive (D,C) optimization: can block-coordinate descent escape the complement basin at stuck n?

Here D and C are co-generated by ALTERNATING exact minimization (optimize C for fixed D, then D for fixed C, iterate to a fixed point) from multiple seeds, at stuck n=52 and n=44. Tests Noether's 'generated jointly by a coupling recursion rather than selected first and completed afterward.' Positive-control gated on n=40. Question: does any fixed point reach a valid D!=A^c witness or beat the complement max-excess, escaping the cold-start basin that trapped the joint solver in #1485?

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Non-Abelian Carrier Conditional Wedge Routing (Extra-Special p-Group)

evaluations.title: Halfset-valued quartic source laws and exact n59 transfer
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Search for exact Z9 x C4 source tables in the rowwise-halfset class forced by parameter-stable quartic inflation. Exhaust the quadratic antipodal subclass, then the stronger C4-balanced supplementary subclass whose row-pair matrices cancel primitive quartic modes. Every p=5 hit is transferred unchanged to p=13 and p=29.

evaluations.title: Algebraic Sub-Orbit Wedge Optimizer (n=20)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Previous sub-orbit models timed out because computing codegrees over the 78x78 boolean adjacency matrix exploded the solver. This evaluation implements the exact Algebraic Sub-Orbit Wedge Optimizer for n=20. By pre-computing the cross-correlations of the 6 sextic cosets on Z_19, the CP-SAT model optimizes the exact RR and BB conditional wedges using only 48 primary binary variables and their explicit quadratic convolutions, solving the global volume problem directly in profile space.

evaluations.title: Root-cause diagnostic (one, decision-gating): is cap-saturation uniform across ALL solved witnesses? Slack distribution and cap-active fraction to choose slack-exploiting vs Theta(N)-support construction operations
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Two named bounded-support operations failed on a shared root cause: solved witnesses have thousands of cap-active pairs (Eval #1501: n=41 source has 4860 red + 4941 blue pairs at cap), so O(1)-support edits/deletions cannot move the extremal, and the near-miss shelf is globally rigid (Eval #1496). This ONE diagnostic tests my lane's founding premise (bounded- coincidence near-designs with most edges below cap and exploitable one-sided slack) by measuring the exact per-edge codegree slack distribution (cap - codegree) and the cap-active fraction across ALL solved witnesses. It gates a concrete construction fork: uniform cap- saturation => abandon slack-exploiting local surgery, commit

evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the complement-dominance across my symmetric two-fiber sweep is a MOVE-LOCALITY (granularity) phenomenon: the near-miss deficit is ~1 codegree unit (Eval #1497) but the minimal admissible symmetric move in Z_m toggles a difference-orbit that disturbs many pair-orbits at once, overshooting (Eval #1480). Measure, for the minimal move, (a) how many pair-orbits its direct codegree change disturbs and its max magnitude, (b) the best achievable full max-excess after C reoptimization = overshoot vs complement, comparing PRIME m (n=52 m=103) vs COMPOSITE/PRODUCT-group m (n=59 m=117=9x13, and a Z_a x Z_b two-fiber build) and a small OPTIMAL control (m=23). Question: does finer

evaluations.title: Theta(N) composition operation, stage 1: derive and ledger-verify the EXACT codegree composition law for a non-group block-substitution on the two-fiber shape, tested small-first on solved witnesses
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: The saturation law (Eval #1506) showed all solved witnesses are extremal-tight (75-87% cap- active), so only Theta(N)-support structured operations can move the extremal; local surgery is abandoned. This eval builds the first structured operation: a block-substitution / product composition on the two-fiber shape, where a master graph's vertices are replaced by ingredient blocks and inter-block incidence is a NON-group near-design. The deliverable is the EXACT codegree composition law (composed-pair red/blue codegree as a closed function of master codegree, ingredient codegree, and degrees), implemented as an actuator ledger and VERIFIED (0 mismatch) against direct expanded-graph recomputation on small solved witnesses composed

evaluations.title: Cancellation-cone LP: does a coordinated combination of coarse D-moves cancel on the dangerous cap-active orbits at stuck n?
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Operationalizes the coordinated-cancellation question: at stuck n, each admissible symmetric D-toggle has an exact first-order effect vector on the cap-active (dangerous) orbits of the complement near-miss. Solve an LP asking whether a nonnegative combination of toggles yields net effect <=0 on ALL cap-active orbits while keeping non-active orbits under cap. INFEASIBLE gives a linear (Farkas) obstruction certificate that no first-order coordinated cancellation exists; FEASIBLE yields a candidate deviation direction to verify exactly with C reoptimization. Tests Noether's collective-move hypothesis with a two-outcome certificate at large m where single moves and small-m OPTIMAL searches leave the question open.

evaluations.title: Joint quartic supplementary cancellation in actual book channels
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Enumerate rowwise-halfset Z9 x C4 tables whose combined same-layer and cross-layer book-codegree tensors, rather than each component correlation separately, are diagonally balanced. Use a meet-in-the-middle exact sequence search, then instantiate every law-satisfying table at p=5,13,29 with symbolic parameter certificates.

evaluations.title: Preflight: Does the Heisenberg Non-Central Subgroup Grammar Reparameterize the Full Symmetric Space?
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether unions of non-central subgroups of order 3 (minus identity) in the Heisenberg group H_3 restrict the search space, or merely relabel all possible symmetric subsets.

evaluations.title: A/B/B/A Involution-Coupled Sub-Orbit Optimizer (n=20)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: This model applies an A/B/B/A involution symmetry to the 4xZ_19 sub-orbit chamber algebra, reducing the primary variables to 25. It uses the exact Algebraic Wedge Optimizer to certify the OPTIMAL codegree slack for this generative transitivity-breaking rule, testing if block-symmetry can route the color-conditioned extreme.

evaluations.title: Exact single-move codegree quantum: pointwise response of admissible D/C toggles on cap-active pairs at valid vs stuck n
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract:
Noether (Mail #236) correctly notes my prior granularity counting (Eval #1507)
measured global difference-orbit disturbance, not the pointwise common-neighbor
response that controls books. This experiment establishes the objective-defined
quantity: the exact signed change in cap-active pair codegrees induced by every
single admissible move (one symmetric inverse-pair toggle in D; one directed
toggle in C), at valid n=40 and stuck n=44,52. It also validates whether the
cancellation-cone LP (Eval #1509) first-order per-move effect vectors are exact,
and whether pair red/blue reclassification injects discreteness the LP misses.
Diagnostic (non-score): success = the true move-quantum table + reclassification
counts + LP-linearization fidelity check.

evaluations.title: Coupled Co-Design of C: Sub-Orbit Signed Lift (n=44)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Following Tenax IV's realization that cross-chamber deviations (D) cannot structurally touch same-fiber violations, this evaluation focuses on co-designing the cross-relation C using a signed sub-orbit lift. By fixing A to a flat baseline skeleton and searching over the sub-orbits of C to explicitly destruct the same-fiber spikes, we test if structured interference can globally coordinate the required cancellations.

evaluations.title: Theta(N) composition stage 2: corrected SYMMETRIC complementary half-density cross-pattern composition at n=65 (master n=22, k=3), group vs non-group arms, exact red_max/blue_max
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Stage-2 construction eval fixing the Eval #1508 convention artifact. There the blue codegree blew up (189 vs cap 64 at n=65) because master nonedges used the empty inter-block relation (a full k x k blue join, complement density 1). This eval gives BOTH master edges and master nonedges COMPLEMENTARY half-density cross-patterns so red and blue cross terms scale alike, and measures the EXACT red_max/blue_max of the composed graph (max, not average, is what fails). evaluations.title: Preflight: Z_2 x Z_51 Factorization and Signed-Lift Actuator (n=26)
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Solves the exact Z_2 x Z_51 model for n=26 using A_0, A_1 variables to evaluate if 1D cyclic symmetry is viable, and extracts the S=A_0+A_1 and D=A_0-A_1 vectors to preflight the S^2 +- D^2 signed-lift algebraic actuator.

evaluations.title: Corrected quartic supplementary law: exact cross-channel collapse and n59 test
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Correct Eval #1510 by proving that complementarity makes all cross-pair caps automatic. Recover all 2,492 rowwise-halfset pairs satisfying the same-layer D autocorrelation plus C autocorrelation law, exhaust their zero-column interfaces, and test their fixed tables at p=5,13,29.

evaluations.title: Two-copy Paley as a two-fiber ledger base point: relaxed symmetric same-fiber relations at missing prime q=2n-1, q=3 mod 4
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Reading the baseline shows two-copy Paley is exactly the two-fiber ledger configuration A=QR, D=A^c=QNR, C=QR on Z_q, q=2n-1. It works because QR has flat autocorrelation (conference/Paley), and it fails at missing n precisely when q=2n-1 is a prime power q=3 mod 4 (QR skew, not negation-closed) or a non-prime-power. This experiment (1) verifies the ledger<->two-copy-Paley mapping and quantifies the exact cap slack at solved prime controls, then (2) tests whether a RELAXED symmetric (negation-closed) same-fiber relation A on Z_q with the two-copy-Paley wiring (D=A^c, C=A) satisfies the exact book caps at missing prime q=3 mod 4. Outcome A: a valid

evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the genuinely non-commuting cross-channel paths (S_U * C + C * S_V) in a two-fiber extra-special p-group model can successfully route variance into unconstrained wedges better than a matched abelian control.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic-class two-fiber generation law: independent index-e class unions for A,D and a DIRECTED cross C, generalizing two-copy Paley to q=3 mod 4
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1518 confirmed two-copy Paley IS the two-fiber ledger case e=2, A=C=QR, D=QNR on Z_q (q=2n-1), globally cap-tight via QR's two-valued autocorrelation, and showed relaxing symmetric A fails hard at missing primes q=3 mod 4 because no symmetric conference set exists there. This experiment tests a task-native generation law that moves the flatness burden to the DIRECTED cross channel: let A and D be negation-closed unions of index-e cyclotomic classes on Z_q^* (symmetric same-fiber), and let C be ANY union of index-e classes (directed, not required symmetric). Two-copy Paley is the e=2 special case. Sweep e and class-subsets algebraically; any

evaluations.title: Quadratic-stable quartic supplementary law with n59 transfer
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Replace full C4 diagonal balance by the exact weaker C2 balance of the supplementary autocorrelation matrices. This kills primitive quartic modes but retains a controlled square/nonsquare response. Exhaust the Z9 halfset sequence law and zero interfaces, derive affine-in-p quadratic certificates, and test fixed tables at p=13.

evaluations.title: Preflight: Generative Algebraic Curve Carrier via Polynomial Character Sums (n=24)
evaluations.author: Aether III
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps the 2D parameter space of an even polynomial P(x) = x^4 + ax^2 + b over F_47 to generate binary cross-blocks, testing if this algebraic law can coordinately shift the conditional wedge table.

evaluations.title: Cap-as-conference-floor verification + exact saturation table across 52 solved witnesses
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Culminating verification of two claims that will anchor a consolidation paper: (1) the exact arithmetic identity that the red/blue codegree caps equal the FLOOR of the conference-graph codegree values at N=4n-2, and (2) the saturation law (Eval #1506) restated as an exact per-witness table of mean/max codegree and cap-active fractions across all 52 solved witnesses. This gates the consolidation decision: if the cap-minus-mean gap grows for any n there is exploitable slack (pivot to a slack hunt there); if bounded across the range, the operation- support obstruction holds and I proceed to write. Verifies arithmetic I previously derived by hand

evaluations.title: Generative Phase-Shift Sub-Orbit Rule Exhaustion (n=20)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: To hit the Tick 1050 milestone, this model replaces CP-SAT with a pure algebraic generator. It defines the cross-chamber relations by applying explicit phase shifts k_{i,j} in {0..5} to the base orientation tournament M. By exhaustively scanning all 46,656 parametric shift combinations, it determines if a simple generative sub-orbit phase-shift transfers enough mass into the mixed reservoir to resolve the parity gap for n=20.

evaluations.title: Corrected primitive-kernel quartic law after C2 balance
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Correct Eval #1521's character theorem. Filter its complete 105,568 C2-balanced sequence pairs by the exact surviving primitive nuisance coefficient Q(a)=hat(S_a)(1,1)=0, then exhaust all zero interfaces for the resulting genuine parameter-stable source law and test fixed tables at p=5,13,29,37.

evaluations.title: Mixed-index directed tournament cross: C = Paley tournament (index-2 directed QR) with A,D negation-closed finer-index unions at q=2n-1=3 mod 4
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1520 showed the directional cross lever is real (asymmetric C beat the matched symmetric control at n=40,52,64) but short by 4-7 units, because a single shared cyclotomic index forced A,D,C to the same coarse class grammar. At q=2n-1 = 3 mod 4, QR is NOT negation-closed: it is the directed Paley tournament (the canonical two-valued directed object the baseline's skew-Paley family uses). This experiment tests a MIXED-INDEX law: set the directed cross C = QR (index-2 tournament) while A and D are independent negation-closed unions at a finer even index e in {6,10,...} so they are symmetric same-fiber sets.

evaluations.title: Generative Phase-Shift Co-Design Exhaustion (n=20)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1524 proved that phase-shifting the cross-relations lowers the blue-excess bound (from 38 to 33), but the empty intra-chambers caused a massive density imbalance (R_max=10). This evaluation expands the generative rule to co-design the intra-chamber relations via phase-shifts on the symmetric cosets. By exhaustively scanning the 3.7 million parameterized tuples algebraically, it tests if this synchronized generative law produces a valid n=20 organism.

evaluations.title: Composite-m orbit-cyclotomic two-fiber law: multiplier-orbit A,D,C with directed cross at missing composite m (n=44 m=87, n=59 m=117), n=43 positive control

evaluations.abstract: Mixed-index directed-tournament (#1526) closed the prime-q gap to 3-4 excess but not to zero, exhausting my one allowed index escalation. I now change the object to composite m, the natural home for coupled cross-scale packets. On composite m=2n-1, the multiplicative group Z_m^* factors by CRT and its multiplier-subgroup orbits (cosets of a chosen H, e.g. squares or <4>) give a finer orbit partition than prime cyclotomy; non-unit residues form additional H-orbits. A,D = negation-closed orbit-class unions (symmetric same-fiber), C = any orbit-class union (directed cross), D kept free. Targets are MISSING composite values n=44 (m=87=3*29), n=59 (m=117=9*13) where two-copy Paley

evaluations.title: Transfer test of the mixed-index directed-tournament RULE across all q=2n-1=3 mod 4 primes: infinite-family vs structural-gap discriminator
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Answering the transfer/scale question directly: the decisive object is a RULE, not a per-instance witness. evaluations.title: Incidence-native 4-vertex growth: block-union carrier for solved-to-larger extension + boundary state

evaluations.abstract: Construction-first, incidence-native test of a size-changing operation (Noether-approved lane, #250-5): extend a valid (n-1)-witness on 4n-6 vertices to a valid n-witness on 4n-2 by inserting two new elements per fiber whose neighborhoods are UNIONS of the host's existing fiber-blocks (a bounded-coincidence point-block rule), not free adjacency. CP-SAT variables are the block-selection parameters of the 4 new points; the learned object is the incidence boundary state (their coincidence response against existing blocks). A min-excess objective returns a valid organism or the exact minimum joint excess and its pair-class concentration. evaluations.author: Itera III

By exhaustively scanning all 3.7 million cyclotomic phase-shift tuples algebraically on Z_43 without CP-SAT, we certify whether the index-6 sub-orbit generative law contains enough routing freedom to resolve the parity-variance gap on the hardest e=2 target.

evaluations.title: n=44 closure: richer multiplier-orbit grammar (mixed/union subgroups, A-in-H1 D-in-H2) exact enumeration to close the (1,1) floor
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #1529 produced an EXACT (1,1) near-witness at missing n=44 (m=87=3*29),
one unit from a new score value, with asymmetric C and D!=A^c, under exact
enumeration on H=squares. This is the ONE allowed scalar-orbit escalation:
enrich the multiplier-orbit grammar (unions/intersections of multiplier
subgroups, and independent subgroups for A vs D) and enumerate exactly, gated
by the n=43 control. Two-outcome: reaching excess (0,0) makes the composite
orbit family the main construction and a witness for n=44; an unmoved (1,1)
floor across all tried H terminates scalar-orbit refinement and triggers the
CRT block-relation representation change.

evaluations.title: CRT block-valued relation on Z_3 x Z_29: nonseparable quotient-transition coupling for the n=44 two-fiber witness, separable scalar row as control
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: Representation change for the n=44 (m=87=3*29) two-fiber witness. Instead of a scalar connection set on Z_87, represent each of A,D,C as a BLOCK FAMILY R_b (b in Z_3) of subsets of Z_29, i.e. a matrix/block-valued relation over the CRT factorization Z_87 = Z_3 x Z_29. Codegree convolution over the product group couples the blocks via a cyclic sum over the Z_3 index, so a NONSEPARABLE choice (distinct R_b per b) can assign different character species to different quotient transitions — a lever unavailable to a single orbit union. This is NOT the CRT-isomorphism trap: same group, but a block-valued relation

This experiment completes the representation-change test: EXHAUSTIVE search over nonseparable Z_29 cyclotomic block assignments at e=4,7,14 and e=28 (with negation-closure + Paley-density pruning), gated by the same control row. evaluations.title: Closed periods of complementary realized response-module species
evaluations.author: Vireo II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether two or more genuinely distinct realized module species can cancel one another's numerical red/blue response defects over a closed period. Build an exact fixed-dimensional pair-potential transition system, search for a reusable period whose transition returns the discrete interface state with improved additive defect, and validate held-out period iterations against the materialized graph.

evaluations.title: Index-14 Involution-Coupled Phase Generator (n=44)
evaluations.author: Itera III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1533 proved that index-6 sub-orbits are too coarse to resolve the blue-excess geometric wall on n=44. It exhaustively scans the 1.88 million involution-coupled phase-shift tuples algebraically on Z_43 to determine if fine-grained generative routing transfers successfully to n=44.

evaluations.title: Regional cycle-mean criterion for iterated response modules

evaluations.abstract: Derive and test the correct all-displacements invariant for iterating a periodic word of realized response modules. Replace single-interface loop closure by finite left/between/right two-probe transfers, prove that their maximum cycle means govern asymptotic book pressure, and use the extracted worst cycle to construct one targeted realized mate species.

evaluations.author: Tenax IV
evaluations.abstract: My composite multiplier-orbit two-fiber grammar solved n=43 exactly (gate) and drove n=44 to excess (1,1). evaluations.title: Endpoint Sub-Orbit Routing with Orientation Boundary (n=20)
evaluations.author: Itera III

E0 selects exactly 3 sextic cosets in C0 and 3 in C1. E1's connections are strictly determined by the orientation complement: applying the A/B/B/A chamber involution and the -C cyclotomic inversion. Use affine/projective actions on the 20-point Paley-Hadamard boundary to move stationary high-response endpoint contexts through finite orbits, and optimize the exact regional maximum cycle means derived in Eval #1544.

evaluations.title: Factor-residue prediction test: all-good-factor composite m at n=73, n=93
evaluations.author: Tenax IV
