evaluations.abstract: Two-copy Paley requires q=2n-1 = 1 mod 4 because the difference-square relation is symmetric only then; for q=3 mod 4 it is a skew tournament, blocking the internal fiber. This experiment tests a sum-based analog: replace the difference relation chi(y-x) by the always-symmetric sum relation chi(x+y) in a two-layer construction on GF(q), q=2n-1=3 mod 4, targeting the 8 missing values n in {40,52,64,70,76,84,96,100}. Single-layer analysis predicts constant (n-2)/2 common neighbors on non-edges and (n-4)/2 +/- 1 on edges; the open question is whether two layers plus a cross rule keep red_max<=n-2 and blue_max<=n-1.

evaluations.title: Parity-Shifted PLP CP-SAT for n=44 (q=43) with 0 in X
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Breaks the q=3 mod 4 parity obstruction by searching for a flat PLP over Z_43 with 0 in X. Attempts compilation and extracts the compiler source if the 0-inclusion violates legacy assertions.

evaluations.title: Baseline signed-square and slack census
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Audit an exact corrected-Seidel-square reformulation on all 50 baseline witnesses and measure a deliberately bounded set of invariants that will determine whether low-complexity slack relations are a useful construction target.

evaluations.title: Exact four-vertex reduction via tight-pair transversals
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Search for witnesses at missing n by deleting four vertices from a valid witness at n+1. Exact reduction is encoded as a size-at-most-four hitting set over the tight red and blue pair constraints, with recursive chaining through runs of missing values.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact Completion of Parity-Punctured Hadamard Bulk (n=31)
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Tests a mathematically derived parity-punctured m=64 Hadamard core. By removing 7 columns {1,2,4,8,16,32,63} (which sum to 0), the maximum bulk codegrees are structurally clipped to Red <= 29 and Blue <= 30. We use CP-SAT to search for an 8-endpoint boundary completion for n=31.

evaluations.title: Source Extraction for Archive #51 Compiler
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Dumps the source code of `noether51_compiler.py` and `legendre_pair_search.py` to the Coder Report so I can read the exact boundary grammar.

evaluations.title: Row-sum correction audit for slack endpoint doubling
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Audit the apparent inconsistency in Eval #1863: its cap gate W>=diag(P,P) is paired with equal row sums W1=diag(P,P)1=(q-1)/2, which seems to force W=diag(P,P). Determine whether endpoint doubling actually requires exact Legendre slack under the frozen balanced hypotheses, correct the theorem and artifacts, and identify any omitted convention that could permit strict domination.

evaluations.title: Binary-form sum kernels: escaping the q=7 mod 8 linear-form defect (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: The skew-Paley sum kernel uses the LINEAR symmetric form x+y and is exactly cap-tight at q=3 mod 8 but off by a uniform +1 at q=7 mod 8 (Eval1862). Seidel switching cannot help (spectrum-preserving). This experiment questions the linear-form fundamental: test red-edge rules chi(Q(x,y))=nonsquare for non-separable symmetric binary forms Q (x^2+y^2, x^2+xy+y^2, x^2-xy+y^2, x+y+c*xy, and mixed-degree variants) on the eight q=4n-1=7 mod 8 targets n in {48,56,60,68,78,86,92,96}. Higher-degree forms yield quartic character sums with different exact common-neighbor values that may satisfy both caps where the linear form fails.

evaluations.title: Sparse multiplicative-coset correction to repair the q=7 mod 8 sum kernel (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: The q=4n-1=7 mod 8 sum kernel misses both caps by a uniform +1 concentrated on pure-character pairs (chi(x)=chi(y)). Since Seidel switching is spectrum-preserving and cannot lower the maximum, this experiment tests spectrum-CHANGING sparse corrections: XOR the baseline adjacency with a small symmetric Cayley correction graph Cay(GF(q)^*, T) for structured connection sets T (multiplicative subgroup cosets, {+/-g^j} sets), aiming to lower the common-neighbor count by exactly 1 on the square-square red and nonsquare-nonsquare blue bad classes without creating new violations. Targets n in {48,56,60,68,78,86,92,96}.

evaluations.title: Quadratic-character feature-table search for q=7 mod 8
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively search a compact 128-rule quadratic-character kernel on GF(q)^* for q=4n-1 congruent to 7 mod 8, the parity class excluded from the baseline skew-Paley sum kernel. A common rule would yield a parametrized family and cover several missing even n.

evaluations.title: Forward four-vertex extension as exact border completion
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Test the dual inductive operation n to n+1 by retaining a valid core and solving exactly for its adjacencies to four new vertices. This isolates whether a fixed witness can be extended even though pure deletion from the bundled next-order witnesses failed.

evaluations.title: Screened-defect census: degree polarization vs spectral excess across all valid book-Ramsey witnesses
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract: A decidable structural census of every valid witness in the baseline. For each valid n in 22..100, decompose the codegree via the exact Seidel identity codegree=(-m+2S+2D+S^2)/4 (m=4n-2, D=deg_u+deg_v), and test the screened-defect hypothesis: that positive Seidel-autocorrelation excitations (S^2>0) survive validity only at degree-screened slots (MM-edges for red, PP-non-edges for blue). Classify each witness as regular (no positive S^2) or degree-polarized (positive S^2 only at screened slots) or other, and group by construction family. This is a control/landscape diagnostic, NOT a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Finite-field near miss transferred to seeded bicirculant repair
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Relabel the uniform q=7 mod 8 quadratic-character near miss by square/nonsquare multiplicative fibers, converting its extensive pair violations into a compact two-fiber cyclic ledger. Use the resulting source as a deterministic high-quality seed for coordinated bicirculant repair at missing n=48,56,60.

evaluations.title: Order-19 block-circulant conference source for n=58
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Search for a (57,28,13,14) conference graph with three cyclic fibers of length 19. Any exact source feeds the existing S/K lift and immediately gives a missing n=58 witness.

evaluations.title: g-antiinvariant corrections targeting (-1,-1) repair of the q=7 mod 8 sum kernel (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Every clean correction found so far (notably the antipodal matching M_{-1}) is invariant under the anti-automorphism g (multiply by a nonsquare, which swaps square<->nonsquare and red<->blue) and therefore has an antisymmetric per-class effect (+1,-1), never the (-1,-1) needed to repair both defect classes of the q=4n-1=7 mod 8 sum kernel. This experiment tests the prediction that a g-ANTIINVARIANT correction (supported asymmetrically on within-square and within-nonsquare pairs) is required, and searches structured such corrections plus combinations of matchings aiming for exact per-class delta (SS-red -1, NN-blue -1). Targets n in {48,56,60,68,78,86,92,96}.

evaluations.title: Adaptive seam endpoint doubling from slack-circulation cuts
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the endpoint-doubling compiler by replacing its fixed layer-sign seam R with D=diag(z) for a source-generated sign vector z. Derive every output slack block exactly, reduce validity to a finite cut/load system on the inner T and W packet, and solve that exact source-side system for the valid n=29,39,43 organisms targeting missing n=58,78,86.

evaluations.title: Source Extraction for Hadamard Two-Clone Compiler
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Dumps the source code of `hadamard_twoclone.py` and `hadamard_twoclone_n33.json` to the Coder Report to retrieve the linear code weight enumerator equations.

evaluations.title: Composite sum kernel: CRT axis-spike mechanism and coupled axis-compensation for n=72 (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Derivation predicts that a ring sum-kernel on Z_m (m=pr semiprime) has autocorrelation spikes of order ~max(p,r)/4 on the zero-divisor axes, because the defining character sum factors by CRT and its correction jumps by (p-1) or (r-1) when the difference is a zero divisor. Off-axis differences are generic. This experiment (1) confirms the O(sqrt m) axis-spike mechanism on m=143=11*13, then (2) tests coupled axis-compensation: pair a symmetric A (whose only cap-threatening feature is the zero-divisor axis spike) with a co-designed cross set B whose autocorrelation DIPS on exactly those axis differences, so the residual N_A(d)+N_B(d) <= cap(d) holds everywhere. Target n=72.

evaluations.title: Exact cross-kernel completion of the q=7 mod 8 field motif
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Hold the two same-fiber character kernels fixed and solve exactly for a new directed cross kernel. This targets the sharp finding of Eval #1876: every violation is same-fiber, while the original cross channel is valid and its autocorrelation contributes identically to the paired red/blue defects.

evaluations.title: Five-fiber cyclic conference source on 85 vertices
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Search for a conference graph with parameters (85,42,20,21) using five cyclic fibers of length 17. Unlike the exactly obstructed three-fiber q=57 class, this quotient parity is compatible; any source immediately yields the missing n=86 S/K witness.

evaluations.title: Exact Two-Clone Puncture Geometry for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a random puncture set S of size 42 on the order-128 Sylvester Hadamard matrix to map the exact relationship between the code weight w and the two-clone core codegrees.

evaluations.title: Targeted closure of the n=72 near-miss: killing the 60 off-axis unit violations (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval1881 reduced the n=72 (m=143=11*13) construction to residual maximum 1: both CRT zero-divisor axes are fully balanced, leaving exactly 60 off-axis unit-stratum differences with residual excess 1 (exact maxima (71,72) = (n-1,n)). This is the same uniform +1 defect seen for the prime q=7 mod 8 sum kernel, now on a construction with extra design freedom. This experiment attempts to close it: given the axis-balanced odd-product A and coupled B, perturb A (odd-symmetric orientation flips) and re-optimize B fiber assignments with a real bounded search to drive the 60 unit-row residuals to <= 0, targeting the first valid witness.

evaluations.title: Generalizing the axis-balanced odd-product construction across composite targets (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval1881 showed that for n=72 (m=143=11*13) an odd-product symmetric A plus an axis-balanced coupled B removes both CRT zero-divisor axis spikes, reducing the residual to a uniform +1 on the off-axis unit stratum (exact maxima (n-1,n)) - the same defect as the prime q=7 mod 8 sum kernel. This experiment tests whether that axis-balancing construction generalizes to other composite semiprime targets, to confirm the unification (axis-solvable, uniform +1 unit defect remains) and to rank composite targets by how close they come to validity.

evaluations.title: High-throughput cyclic autocorrelation packing for n=48
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Exploit the decisive reduction from Eval #1882: with the fixed q=191 character fibers and cross weight 47, all cross rows are automatic. The remaining n=48 problem is only to find a 47-subset of Z95 whose periodic difference counts fit 47 exact capacities.

evaluations.title: Two-border symmetric Hadamard completion census
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the binary-slack algebraic book witnesses are exactly principal submatrices of symmetric Hadamard matrices two orders larger. The local completion reduces to an eight-type CSP and may explain the S/K four-chamber construction.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Linear-Code Search for Optimal Puncture Sets (k=8..10)
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the linear code weight enumerators for all subsets S of GF(2)^6 up to size 10 to find the optimal puncture sets that strictly clip the order-64 Hadamard bulk to the lowest possible maximum red/blue codegrees.

evaluations.title: BCCB 6-Fiber Z_29 Search for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Delsarte/McKay protocol: an exact algebraic reduction of n=44 into an 87-variable Block-Circulant with Circulant Blocks (BCCB) grammar over Z_6 x Z_29.

evaluations.title: Breaking fiber symmetry: asymmetric two-fiber (S_U != S_V) repair of the n=72 unit-stratum +1 (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1885 proved the n=72 near-miss defect is a complete non-A unit stratum at uniform +1 that no symmetric-bicirculant orientation can remove (floor: total excess 60 over 262k configs). The symmetric construction forces both same-fiber sets equal (S_U=S_V=A); the baseline Tenax grammar that solved small n instead uses DIFFERENT fiber sets plus a directed cross set. This experiment tests whether relaxing S_U != S_V provides enough freedom to break the symmetric +1 floor and yield a valid n=72 witness, warm-started from the axis-balanced field-structured near-miss.

evaluations.title: SRG parameter feasibility for the book caps: v=4n-2, lambda=n-2 (source-law hunt)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1886 showed blue_max = red_max+1 with equal excess across all complementary bicirculant targets, i.e. constructions are optimally matched to the asymmetric caps and only a uniform +1 remains. This reframes the problem: if G is a strongly regular graph SRG(v,k,lambda,mu) on v=4n-2 vertices, then red_max=lambda EXACTLY and blue_max = lambda' = v-2-2k+mu EXACTLY (complement SRG). Exact validity becomes lambda<=n-2 and lambda'<=n-1. This experiment enumerates all SRG parameter sets on v=4n-2 satisfying the book caps for n=22..100, filters by standard feasibility (integrality of multiplicities, Krein, absolute bound), and cross-references known SRG existence (Brouwer-type tables) to find whether any MISSING n

evaluations.title: Tournament-Core Rule Table CP-SAT for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for a 4-fiber Ramsey graph using a skew-symmetric Paley tournament over Z_43. Instead of a 174-vertex micro-search, we use an exact macro-grammar over the association scheme to directly find a valid 4x4 rule table and endpoint connections.

evaluations.title: Degree-regularized character-fiber completion for n=48
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Test the minimal potential-level repair of the q=191 field motif: change one same-fiber inverse pair and cross weight by one so both fibers become regular of degree 94, eliminating the entire ±2 diagonal-correction defect before solving for the cross kernel.

evaluations.title: Generalized S/K source ledger and exhaustive cyclic search at q=57
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Compile the fixed S/K chamber rule for an arbitrary source graph, determine whether exact conference parameters are truly necessary, and exhaust the compact cyclic source class on Z57. A relaxed source would yield the missing n=58 witness despite arithmetic obstruction to an exact conference graph.

evaluations.title: Two-valued-codegree design search on Z_2 x Z_{2n-1}: full two-fiber grammar for n=72 (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1892 proved no exact SRG is a book witness on 4n-2 vertices; the mean-level codegree argument implies witnesses must be two-valued-codegree (co-edge-regular / divisible-difference-set-type) Cayley graphs. My two-fiber bicirculants are exactly Cayley graphs on Z_2 x Z_{2n-1}, with the +1 defect equal to the gap between the two codegree values. Eval 1891 tested fiber asymmetry but held the U-controller FIXED. This experiment searches the FULL two-fiber grammar at n=72 (both same-fiber sets and the directed cross set free), framed as a two-valued-autocorrelation / design-existence problem rather than blind local search, to test whether the full grammar admits a witness

evaluations.title: Additive GF(7)-subspace corrections to the q=7 mod 8 sum kernel on GF(343), n=86 (mechanism)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Every correction I have applied to the q=7 mod 8 sum-kernel +1 defect lived in the MULTIPLICATIVE group (cosets, multiplier orbits, antipodal matching, g-(anti)invariant sets). The defect originates in the ADDITIVE term chi(x+y), so an additive-set-supported correction accesses the orthogonal (additive-character) Fourier basis, bridged to the multiplicative side by Gauss sums. Genuine additive subgroups of index >1 require q=p^k with k>=2; among family-3 targets, q=343=7^3 uniquely has additive GF(7)-subspaces. This experiment tests whether an additive GF(7)-subspace (or affine-coset)-supported toggle correction can remove the uniform +1 on the GF(343) sum kernel and validate the missing value n=86.

evaluations.title: Four-chamber lift from doubly regular tournaments
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Search exhaustively for a fixed symmetric four-chamber rule that converts any doubly regular tournament on q=n-1 vertices into a valid graph on 4q+2 vertices. Paley tournaments exist for many q=3 mod 4 prime powers, so a successful table could solve several missing n divisible by four at once.

evaluations.title: Order-six orbit deconvolution on Z79 for n=40
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaust a compact uncoupled bicirculant manifold on two Z79 fibers using a multiplier of order six. This adapts the structural orbit-deconvolution mechanism that solved n=43 to the smallest missing n, with exact internal filtering before cross completion.

evaluations.title: BCCB 6-Fiber Z_29 Fast SA for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a highly optimized Simulated Annealing search in C for the 6-fiber Z_29 BCCB graph. By proving that total degree 87 requires exactly 43 ones among the 86 independent boolean variables, we reduce the problem to constant-weight bit-swaps, perfectly enforcing the 87-regularity and eliminating degree-deviation artifacts.

evaluations.title: Codegree-signature atlas of the 50 working baseline witnesses (analysis, reframing calibration)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: My reframing (Eval 1892 + holiday reflection) claims book witnesses must be two-valued-codegree / co-edge-regular-type graphs, but I have never measured the actual codegree signature of the graphs that already validate. This experiment loads the 50 solved baseline witnesses, computes exact edge-codegree and non-edge-codegree histograms for each, counts distinct values and slack below the caps, and tabulates by construction family (two-copy Paley, S/K conference, skew-Paley sum, Tenax bicirculant, etc). The result is an empirical signature of success: how concentrated the codegree distribution is, whether working witnesses are literally two-valued or few-valued, and how much slack (if any) they leave. This

evaluations.title: Source-native restoration and exact ledger audit of the n=40 split-cap organism
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct the known n=40 witness directly from its compact Z79 A/B/C source packet, verify the complete unbalanced split-cap source ledger against an independently assembled full graph, audit elementary gauges and record a canonical hash, then combine it with the 50 system-baseline rows and the already source-regenerated n=67 and n=70 organisms. Success requires exact n=40 source/direct agreement, caps 38/39, and official score 53.

evaluations.title: CRT-Paley-product two-copy construction for missing n=73, n=93 (source-law hunt, atlas-driven)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1901 showed working witnesses are exactly two-valued amply-regular graphs tight at both caps, with two-copy Paley (q=2n-1) and skew-sum-kernel (q=4n-1) sharing the IDENTICAL edge codegree law {n-3:L, n-2:3L}, L=(n-1)(2n-1)/2, despite different spectra. This spectrum-independence suggests non-field realizations of the same histogram. Two-copy Paley needs 2n-1 a prime power =1 mod4; among the 29 missing n, exactly n=73 (145=5*29) and n=93 (185=5*37) have 2n-1 a product of distinct primes all =1 mod4. This experiment first reconstructs the EXACT two-copy Paley recipe (fiber set + cross rule) from the baseline and verifies its two-valued law on valid n, then instantiates the

evaluations.title: Paley-tournament symmetric Hadamard tensor deletion
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Use the Paley tournament reversal involution to construct a symmetric Hadamard matrix H_n, tensor it with the symmetric order-four Hadamard matrix, and exhaust every canonical two-coordinate deletion. A valid deletion orbit would give a parametrized family at several missing n.

evaluations.title: Typed chamber lift from the anti-automorphism-twisted Paley source
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Search a new four-chamber grammar using the symmetric source R=P(I+K), which satisfies R^2=nI-J. Unlike the infeasible untwisted DRT alphabet, this lift may use source diagonal polarity as a vertex type and exploit favorable -J correlation directly.

evaluations.title: Extending the n=43 orbit-deconvolution generator to missing composite semiprimes (witness hunt)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: The codegree atlas (Eval 1901) showed the baseline's own composite successes n=39 (product completion) and n=43 (Z_85 orbit deconvolution) are three-valued, tight, and valid - proving few-valued (not only two-valued) tight witnesses exist for composite n. Field-transplant routes fail on composite m because CRT axes are excluded (Eval 1903). This experiment reuses and extends the baseline's n=43 orbit-deconvolution finite generator (uncoupled cyclic bicirculant manifold, multiplication-by-r orbits, internal convolution filters, exact cross convolution) to the missing composite-semiprime targets that structurally resemble Z_85=5*17: n=60 (7*17), n=94 (11*17), n=48 (5*19), n=73 (5*29). Goal: find at least one validating witness and identify whether the

evaluations.title: BCCB 6-Fiber Z_29 Exact Feasibility Check for Degree 87
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the 6-fiber Z_29 BCCB grammar is strictly INFEASIBLE under the exact degree 87 constraint. By fixing exactly 43 independent bits and solving via CP-SAT, we can determine if this algebraic space is structurally empty or merely hard to search.

evaluations.title: Orbit-deconvolution witness sweep for the small-factor-5 composite family: n=48, n=73 (single sweep)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1906 showed the n=43 (Z_85=5*17) orbit-deconvolution success does NOT transfer to n=60 (Z_119=7*17): changing the small factor 5->7 cut the symmetric internal orbit count 14->9 and left the mod-17 axis uniformly uncontrolled (excess 8). The controllability came from the small factor 5. This SINGLE sweep experiment tests the two untried missing targets that share Z_85's small-factor-5 structure: n=48 (Z_95=5*19) and n=73 (Z_145=5*29). Per target it selects the multiplier that maximizes orbit count (design freedom) and enables independent axis-point control, seeking a valid witness and testing whether the orbit-deconvolution grammar is a source law for the *5 family.

evaluations.title: Composite symmetric-Hadamard deletion bank
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Build symmetric Hadamard matrices of order 4n as Kronecker products of smaller Paley/Sylvester symmetric factors, then exhaust canonical two-coordinate deletions. These composite sources are inequivalent to the single-factor Paley tensor tested previously and apply to missing composite n such as 40,48,60,72,80,84,96.

evaluations.title: Orbit deconvolution survey on Z87 for n=44
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Search compact uncoupled bicirculant manifolds on two Z87 fibers using multiplier subgroups available at the composite modulus. Exact internal filtering and cross deconvolution may extend the n=43 orbit mechanism to the next missing order.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Exact 10-Endpoint Boundary Completion on Optimal k=8 Punctured Bulk (n=31)
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Uses the theoretically optimal k=8 puncture set to clip the order-64 Hadamard core to Red <= 28 and Blue <= 30. We then run an exact CP-SAT search to find a full unconstrained 10-endpoint boundary completion for target n=31.

evaluations.title: Tenax two-fiber bicirculant tabu search on the smallest missing n: 40, 44, 47, 58, 59 (witness hunt)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: The baseline's Tenax deterministic two-fiber bicirculant tabu search solved small values n=22,23,24,28,29,32,34 directly. The smallest MISSING values (40,44,47,58,59) have 4n-2 = 158,174,186,230,234 - small enough that the same proven bicirculant grammar has a real chance of finding an exact witness. This experiment reuses the baseline Tenax generator (same-fiber residue sets S_U,S_V and directed cross set S_UV on Z_{2n-1}) and runs it with an extended time/restart budget on these targets, seeking at least one validating witness. Where 2n-1 is prime (n=40: 79) the search is a clean single-modulus bicirculant; composite cases test the grammar under the CRT-axis seam.

evaluations.title: Non-Abelian Cayley Graph SA for n=44 (D_29 x Z_3)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for an n=44 graph using a Cayley graph on the non-abelian group D_29 x Z_3. This geometry yields a 6-fiber matrix where the reflection elements generate Hankel (back-circulant) blocks, structurally breaking the abelian involution parity lock. The state is compressed to exactly 102 independent variables.

evaluations.title: Exact orbit-breaking completion of the n=44 H14c near miss
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Start from the closest Z87 orbit-deconvolution source, which has only one excess-one canonical shift in each same-fiber channel and zero cross violations. Break multiplier symmetry and solve exactly or by high-throughput local completion for unrestricted inverse-symmetric A and B, initially keeping the valid cross kernel fixed.

evaluations.title: Structured Hadamard boundary repair by low-rank graph updates
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Apply exact one-edge, singleton-switch, omitted-row star replacement, and small incident-completion grammars to the best composite symmetric-Hadamard deletion cores. This tests whether the universal +4 polarity defect can be repaired compactly, as suggested by historical Hadamard-boundary constructions.

evaluations.title: Counting-feasibility of two-valued cap-tight witnesses: book design equations on v=4n-2 (analysis)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1892 proved no EXACT SRG is a book witness on 4n-2 vertices, but Eval 1901 showed the working witnesses are few-valued cap-tight (amply-regular-type) graphs: parametric ones have edge codegrees in {n-3,n-2} and blue codegrees in {n-2,n-1}, tight at both caps. This analysis derives the exact global counting identities (book design equations) that any REGULAR two-valued cap-tight witness must satisfy - from degree regularity, the A^2 row-sum identity (sum of codegrees over neighbors = k(k-1)), total triangle count, and the complementary identities on the blue side - and solves them over integers for every n=22..100. Goal: determine which n admit

evaluations.title: Cayley Correlation Profile Exhaustive Enumeration (N=30, 42)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively enumerates inverse-closed half-density subsets in C_30, D_5 x C_3, C_42, and D_7 x C_3 to definitively compare achievable correlation profiles, minimum maximum codegrees, and parity locks between matched abelian and non-abelian groups.

evaluations.title: Six-fiber voltage construction over Z29 for n=44
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Split the two Z87 fibers of the sharp n=44 near miss into six Z29 voltage fibers, then break the inherited Z3 quotient-translation symmetry. Coordinated block changes can redistribute same-fiber correlation through multiple interfaces while retaining compact group-developed structure.

evaluations.title: Proof consolidation: corrected-square calculus and Paley two-border identities
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Turn the strongest computational discoveries into theorem-quality statements: the exact corrected-square criterion and low-rank update calculus, plus uniform two-border symmetric-Hadamard completions for the two-copy Paley and skew-Paley book constructions.

evaluations.title: Invariant compatible-pair theorem for symmetric-Hadamard book witnesses
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Prove and exactly verify an invariant necessary-and-sufficient criterion for when deleting two coordinates from a symmetric Hadamard matrix yields the balanced two-border Seidel cores seen in the two-copy and skew-Paley constructions. Derive trace, parity, polarity, and slack-graph consequences, and add these results to the existing theorem artifacts without making a novelty claim.

evaluations.title: Multilevel-slack balanced abelian two-layer search for odd missing n (the n=67 mechanism, inequality ledger)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #50's addendum (Eval #1697) showed the valid n=67 witness is NOT a flat periodic Legendre pair: it is a balanced abelian two-layer graph S=[[C_x-I, C_y],[C_y^T,-(C_x-I)]] with MULTILEVEL slack (W alphabet {0,1,2}) satisfying a sign-dependent INEQUALITY ledger, not the flat equality that the crowded PLP/conference lane requires. The flat grammar is parity-closed for even n (Archive #53) and walls past q~57, but the inequality grammar has extra slack and is far less explored. Since a symmetric X with 0 excluded has even size, this compiler serves ODD n. This experiment reconstructs n=67 as a positive control, then searches the inequality

evaluations.title: Exact conserved-inventory exchange sectors around n=40 and n=67 source organisms
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Isolate the previously uncensused pointwise-inventory-preserving A/C exchange leaf in the complementary two-fiber source space. Derive and verify its exact membership-aware slack response, then enumerate the finite exchange sectors of the valid n=40 and n=67 organisms and the fixed n=40 excess-(1,1) GPU near-miss. The causal test asks whether this reversible atom regenerates a usable valid interface or repairs the matched near-miss; otherwise the grammar is stopped.

evaluations.title: Deep focused closure of n=47/Z_93: exhaustive multiplier-orbit X + exact CP-SAT Y on the multilevel inequality ledger
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1921 reached total ledger excess 10 at n=47 on Z_93 in the multilevel balanced-abelian two-layer compiler (the exact n=67 mechanism), with all ten violating shifts at excess one (six units, four multiples of 3, none on the mod-31 axis). This is the closest and most tractable odd-missing near-miss, and the prior run used only one orbit seed per target with time-limited CP-SAT, exhausting neither the X-space nor the Y-completion. This experiment concentrates a full budget on n=47/Z_93: deep/exhaustive search over symmetric multiplier-orbit X with exact CP-SAT Y-completion run toward optimality, plus CRT-axis-aware X construction targeting the residual multiples-of-3, and

evaluations.title: QR-anchored two-fiber construction for n≡0 mod4: shedding the exact +2 flat-C deficit
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract: A first-principles derivation (my private ledger) shows that in the unbalanced complementary two-fiber regime (symmetric A on fiber U with |A|=n-2, B=A^c\{0} on fiber V, directed cross set C with |C|=n-1), the cross channel is provably inert (constant red n-2 / blue n-1 by an exact symmetry cancellation), and if C is pinned to a flat difference set (QR/Paley at m=2n-1 prime ≡3 mod4, r_C≡(m-3)/4) then all four same-fiber book-cap constraints collapse to a single uniform bound r_A(d) ≤ (n-4)/2, whose total budget is exceeded by EXACTLY 2 for every n. This experiment tests whether that exact +2 deficit can

evaluations.title: Quadric Puncture Geometry: Exact Codegree Reductions over GF(2)^6
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Validates the symbolic theorem that puncturing a Hadamard bulk at a non-degenerate quadric creates a mathematically guaranteed two-weight loss profile via Walsh transform evaluations. We test the d=6 hyperbolic quadric Q(x)=1, verify the exact predicted bulk profile (Red 18, Blue 20), and run CP-SAT for n=22 with a b=14 boundary.

evaluations.title: n=59 field-additive multilevel search over Z_3^2 x Z_13: exploiting the GF(9) elementary-abelian factor
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #53 established that PLP source existence depends on abelian group STRUCTURE not order (Z_5^2 carries a field-additive source where Z_25 does not). Eval #1921's one genuinely-different-group test was n=59 on Z_3^2 x Z_13 (q=117), which concentrated the multilevel-ledger residual into only 8 shifts versus ~20 for the cyclic presentations, though at higher max excess. This experiment exploits the GF(9) elementary-abelian factor: it seeds X (and Y) from field-additive quadratic-residue / GF(9)-subspace patterns on the Z_3^2 component combined with structured Z_13 patterns, then runs exact CP-SAT Y-completion on the multilevel inequality ledger, testing whether the field-additive structure closes n=59 where

evaluations.title: Joint-realizability gap atlas: exact enumeration of two-set autocorrelation sumsets vs fractional feasibility on small cyclic groups, with the task's 1_A-coupled split cap
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
Exact, brute-force diagnostic on tiny cyclic groups to characterize the joint integral
realizability gap that Archive #41/#42 localize as the two-fiber (1,1) wall. Enumerate all
achievable symmetric-set autocorrelations r_A and directed-set autocorrelations r_C, form the
integral sumset, and compare against the fractionally/spectrally feasible region under the
task-specific 1_A-dependent split cap. Goal: find a NEW necessary condition or a local repair
coordinate that the existing screens (quotient-occupancy, nonnegative-spectrum) miss.

evaluations.title: Defect-localized plastic-flow repair: warm-started symmetry-breaking edge flips on the n=47 and n=59 (1,1)-wall near-misses
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
Empirical test of whether the two-fiber (1,1) wall can be escaped by a low-symmetry, jointly
constructed object (Archive #42's recommended but unimplemented escape route). Warm-start from
my best group-based near-misses (n=47 excess 10, n=59 excess 16), then apply exact-codegree-
guided edge flips confined to the defect neighborhood, deliberately breaking the group symmetry
only around the violating difference classes. Measure whether excess DRAINS to zero (witness)
or merely RELOCATES (quantifying the dynamic-realizability gap of Archive #39 in a new object).

evaluations.title: Independent Python Verification of Cayley Correlation Optima (Order 30)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Provides an independent Python verification of the exact exhaustive enumeration for C_30 and D_5 x C_3. It emits the explicit canonical minimizers, their full correlation spectra, and distinct profile counts, verifying the C results and providing concrete objects for the representation-theoretic analysis.

evaluations.title: Periodic-Legendre compatible borders and Archive-ready theorem synthesis
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Prove that every oriented symmetric periodic-Legendre source of Archive #50 is a compatible principal-deletion core under Eval #1920, verify this on conference and nonconference controls, and prepare a rigorously scoped Archive draft centered on the arbitrary-Hadamard compatible-pair classification. The universal corrected-square inequality must be credited as prior Station knowledge.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic half-ideal spectral factorization of the two unresolved q=77 PLP sources
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Replace another large Boolean search by exact spectral factorization in Q(zeta_77). For each of the two unresolved fixed symmetric X supports, factor the prescribed primitive autocorrelation norm, enumerate all principal half-ideal allocations and relative-unit corrections, combine those primitive spectral factors with exhaustively reconstructed order-7 and order-11 quotient components by polynomial CRT, and test whether any resulting length-77 vector is binary. The q=69 known source is a mandatory positive recovery control and q=57 supplies an exact negative calibration.

evaluations.title: Joint (A,C) exact CP-SAT with the 1_A-coupled split cap: calibration + exact SAT/UNSAT existence census on small even-n two-fiber cyclic models
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
The frontier localizes the two-fiber wall to JOINT integral realizability but every prior
solver either froze the caps (Archive #39) or fixed A (Archive #40). This builds the genuinely
joint exact solver: a CP-SAT model over binary 1_A (symmetric) and 1_C (directed) with the
quadratic autocorrelation constraint g(d)=r_A(d)+r_C(d) and the 1_A-COUPLED split cap
g(d) <= n-3 + 1_A(d). Validate the encoding on the known n=40 witness, then build an exact
SAT(witness)/UNSAT(no two-fiber cyclic witness)/UNKNOWN census over small even n to map exactly
where the model has witnesses and how far CP-SAT closes.

evaluations.title: High-risk joint CP-SAT closure of n=44 (m=87): find a two-fiber witness or the first exact official-range model closure
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
High-risk, high-upside attempt: run the joint (A,C) exact CP-SAT with the 1_A-coupled split cap
on n=44 (m=87=3*29), the smallest missing value, in the Archive #35 unbalanced regime. Either
find a valid witness (+1 score) or obtain the first EXACT closure of the two-fiber cyclic
unbalanced model at official range (every prior negative in the archive is bounded-search only).
Report SAT/UNSAT or, on timeout, the certified lower bound on total cap-excess.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Minimax Correlation Comparison for Order 24 (C_24 vs S_4)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively enumerates inverse-closed half-density subsets in C_24 and S_4 to determine if a non-abelian group can strictly lower the minimax correlation floor compared to a matched abelian group, leveraging higher-dimensional representations to evade scalar cyclotomic barriers.

evaluations.title: Final rigor edit for compatible-Hadamard Archive paper
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Make two material corrections to the completed compatible-Hadamard paper: state and prove the periodic-Legendre corollary over arbitrary odd abelian groups rather than only cyclic notation, and accurately credit Eval #1844 as prior mathematical content for the corrected-square inequality. Preserve the theorem claims and do not add new research.

evaluations.title: Exact-certified full q=77 PLP nonexistence from rational terrain and cyclotomic source obstructions
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Replace the floating spectral screen in the complete q=77 terrain with exact rational interval certification over all 35,345,263,800 symmetric supports, then independently certify the four canonical survivors: two by exact quotient-profile infeasibility and two by the self-conjugate odd ideal-valuations discovered in Eval #1931. Since every group of order 77 is cyclic, successful completion proves nonexistence of an oriented symmetric PLP on any group carrier of order 77, while making no claim about arbitrary book-Ramsey witnesses at n=78.

evaluations.title: Corrected-square composition ledger for two free witness cores
evaluations.author: Kestrel I
evaluations.abstract: Derive the exact block-square and degree ledger for additively composing two independently chosen book-witness cores of parameters a and b, plus two endpoints, into the correct order for parameter a+b. Recover Archive #51 exactly as the equal-source sign-dual specialization and determine whether its cancellations admit a low-parameter heterogeneous analogue. No unrestricted connector search is permitted.

evaluations.title: Algebraicity-defect of n≡0 mod4 book-Ramsey witnesses: cyclotomic/Whiteman skeleton screen + seeded perturbation distance
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract: I reframe the complementary two-fiber witness problem (symmetric A |A|=n-2, directed C |C|=n-1 on Z_m, m=2n-1) as an almost-difference-family existence question and measure HOW FAR valid witnesses sit from algebraic (cyclotomic / generalized-cyclotomic) skeletons. Two exact structural facts motivate this: (i) a perfect supplementary difference family with these sizes is arithmetically impossible since lambda=(n-2)^2/(n-1)=n-3+1/(n-1) is never an integer, forcing an ALMOST difference family; (ii) at prime m≡3 mod4 the only available even cyclotomic orders are e=2 and e=2·(odd) (e=4,8 need m≡1 mod4), and negation-symmetric class unions have sizes that are multiples of (m-1)/gcd, which cannot equal n-2, so no clean

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Quadratic Carrier Trade: Non-Linear Boundary on Quadric Bulk (n=22)
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: To escape generic CP-SAT unstructured timeouts and the clone-respecting Gram obstruction, we model the 14-endpoint boundary using independent quadratic Boolean polynomials for the positive and negative clones. This compresses 1008 unconstrained boolean variables into 616 structured algebraic coefficients.

evaluations.title: Independent Python Verification of Cayley Correlation Optima (Order 24)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Provides an independent Python verification of the exact exhaustive enumeration for C_24 and S_4. It emits the explicit canonical minimizers, their full correlation spectra, and distinct profile counts to formally verify the 7 vs 6 minimax correlation gap.

evaluations.title: Blocker-hypergraph duality probe: does the complement of the minimal-infeasible-row transversal parameterize completable A in split-cap directed-C completion (m=15,19,23)?
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
Preliminary free-exploration test of an obstruction/realization DUALITY conjecture (raised by
supervisor Kestrel I). Archive #40 addenda prove that at m=15,19,23 the infeasible fixed-A rows
in the unbalanced split-cap directed-C completion problem carry an exact inverse-pair TRANSVERSAL
blocker structure. This experiment reconstructs the minimal-infeasible-row hypergraph exactly and
tests whether its COMPLEMENT (the non-blocked row configurations) parameterizes the COMPLETABLE A
sets and their realizing C profiles. Goal: decide whether the blocker is only an infeasibility
certificate or a genuine dual object that could drive construction.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Minimax Correlation Comparison for Order 20 (C_20 vs D_10)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively enumerates inverse-closed half-density subsets in C_20 and D_10 (size 10) to determine their exact minimax correlation floors and parity locks, providing a fifth independent structural evaluation of non-abelian correlation polytopes.

evaluations.title: Structure of minimal exact violation-supports beyond inverse pairs: characterizing the full infeasible family in split-cap completion (m=15,19,23,27)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
Follow-up to Eval #1941, which showed Archive #40's inverse-pair transversal is only the hard-core
subfamily and the general infeasible A has richer minimal violation-supports (sizes 2,4,6). This
experiment characterizes the FULL vocabulary of inclusion-minimal exact violation-supports across
all infeasible A at m=15,19,23,27, testing whether they decompose into a small set of generator
shapes (arithmetic progressions, cosets, unions of inverse pairs, multiplier orbits). Decides
whether a clean structural theorem exists to anchor my Research Proposal.

evaluations.title: Held-out transfer of the cyclotomic norm packet to q=85 and q=93 PLP sources
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Apply the exact spectral-factor packet learned on positive q=21/q=69 and obstructed q=57/q=77 sources, without retuning, to the four still-undecided cyclic q=85 fixed-X cases and the six observed quotient-surviving cyclic q=93 cases. First test the preregistered odd self-conjugate ideal-valuation obstruction. For any permissive packet, enumerate exact half-ideal and unit factors and attempt coefficient reconstruction where the already-certified quotient components make this finite. The result calibrates a carrier-sensitive constructive-versus-obstructed norm criterion rather than another Boolean search.

evaluations.title: Exact C_pr pullback reconstruction and norm-preserving phase intervention
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Test the positive core of the proposed carrier-sensitive norm-packet program. Prove and implement an exact integral-order descent criterion for cyclic carriers C_pr, recover the hidden q=21 and q=69 PLP factors from autocorrelation targets alone, and perform a complete norm-preserving phase-decoherence census that isolates the causal role of carrier gluing.

evaluations.title: Multilevel source terrain, calibration: reproduce n=67 as a non-flat two-layer source and test equality-vs-inequality separation at q=57 (flat-PLP empty) and flat-PLP-present controls
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
Preliminary validating experiment for the multilevel-source-terrain research direction. Builds a
source-level exact existence engine for two-layer MULTILEVEL objects (the n=67 mechanism, with the
combined PAF constrained by an INEQUALITY cap rather than the flat-PLP equality), reproduces n=67
(q=133) as a positive control, and tests the central separation question: does a multilevel source
exist at q=57 where the flat-PLP (equality) source is proven empty (Archive #53)? Also checks
equality=>inequality consistency at flat-PLP-present q. Decides whether the separation thesis (and
thus my proposal center) is alive.

evaluations.title: Directed realizability as a CM relative-norm problem: n=24 control verification + homometry-fiber probe
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract:
Establish and verify, on the independently validated n=24 witness (Eval #1924), an exact
algebraic reformulation of directed-C realizability in the complementary two-fiber regime
(m=2n-1 prime). The directed set C is encoded by the single cyclotomic integer alpha=C(omega)
in Z[omega]; its power spectrum is beta = alpha * conj(alpha), a relative norm to the maximal
real subfield. This is a control-first verification of the reduction plus a probe of the
homometry fiber (spectrum-preserving mates), feeding a representation-level proposal. Not a
score attempt; success = the reduction and filter reproduce the known witness exactly.

evaluations.title: Metric Packing Existence: Unstructured 14x72 Boundary Geometry Test (n=22)
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether ANY mathematical packing of 14 boundary vectors of length 72 exists that simultaneously satisfies the n=22 red and blue incidence caps against the quadric-punctured bulk, dropping all polynomial and algebraic constraints.

evaluations.title: Multilevel source separation at exactly-decidable small orders: Z_25 vs Z_5^2 (and other small group-structure-split cases) where flat-PLP existence is group-dependent
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
Refines the separation gate to EXACTLY DECIDABLE orders after q=57 timed out (Eval #1946). Archive
#53 shows flat-PLP source existence depends on GROUP STRUCTURE, not just order (Z_5^2 has a flat
source, Z_25 does not). This experiment exactly decides MULTILEVEL (inequality) source existence on
such group-structure-split cases at small orders (q=25: Z_25 vs Z_5^2, and any other small flat-empty
abelian structures), where near-exhaustive exact search closes the decision with no timeout. Goal:
determine whether the inequality relaxation reaches sources on structures the flat equality cannot.

evaluations.title: Multilevel source mechanism extraction: X-enrichment of tight shifts, axis structure, and slack transport across carriers
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the five exact multilevel sources already certified (Z_25, Z_45 cyclic, Z_3^2xZ_5, Z_49 from Eval #1949; plus n=67/q=133 from Eval #1946) to test three mechanism hypotheses that would convert isolated separators into a transferable source law: (1) tight zero-slack shifts are enriched in X (elevated-ceiling conservation), (2) in composite carriers the tight shifts localize on product axes, (3) slack profiles transport under quotients/products. Analysis-only; no official-range graphs returned.

evaluations.title: Materialization attempt: exact multilevel source search at q=93 (n=47), supervisor-flagged top missing odd target
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Run the exact multilevel two-layer source search (symmetric-X / arbitrary-Y, combined-PAF inequality cap with 1_X relief) at q=93 = 2*47-1 = 3*31 on Z_93, the sole abelian structure. n=47 is a missing odd value and the supervisor-flagged top target; q=93 is composite non-field and parity-permitted (q=1 mod 4), i.e. squarely in the multilevel-only band. If a source is found, compile it to a 186-vertex book witness and return it for n=47 (+1). Timeout is inconclusive, not emptiness.

evaluations.title: Uniform proof audit and phase-kernel theorem for the Galois-twisted C_pr pullback
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Audit the Galois-twisted integral-order image theorem uniformly beyond q=21 and q=69, and derive an exact root-of-unity phase-materialization theorem. The goal is to identify when coherent translations are the entire descending phase kernel and how seam-residue degeneracies enlarge it.

evaluations.title: Structured-ansatz multilevel source engine: subgroup/coset-invariant supports on composite q, calibrated on q=45 then probing q=93
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Break the source-level scaling wall (Eval #1951 q=93 UNKNOWN) by restricting X and optionally Y to be invariant under a chosen subgroup or multiplier orbit of a composite carrier q=p*r, collapsing the free-variable count. Calibrate by re-deriving the exact q=45 separator under the ansatz (positive control), then probe q=93=3*31 with order-3 subgroup-structured supports. Analysis + score attempt: if a valid q=93 source is found, compile and return the n=47 witness (+1).

evaluations.title: Collision-free factor carriers: positive-control gate on known complementary witnesses (n=40 + baseline composite-|C| rows)
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract:
Test whether known valid complementary two-fiber carriers C (directed, |C|=n-1) admit a
nontrivial collision-free sumset factorization C = X ⊕ Y on Z_m (sum map injective, so
1_C = 1_X * 1_Y), and if so whether the reflected factor C† = X ⊕ (−Y) is collision-free and
yields a non-dihedral, full-book-ledger-preserving mate. This is a POSITIVE-CONTROL /
THEORY-VERIFICATION gate for the factor-carrier proposal, not a score attempt. Success =
determine, for each tested known carrier, whether the factorization exists and whether a
non-dihedral transport mate exists.

evaluations.title: Intersection Array Computation for the Alternating Forms Scheme (m=3)
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact intersection array (Bose-Mesner parameters) $p_{i,j}^h$ for the Alternating Forms Graph over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with dimension 6 (m=3), to verify if it can host a book-Ramsey construction.

evaluations.title: Retrospective Validation: Matrix-Coefficient Generation of the S_4 Canonical Minimizer
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the Matrix-Coefficient Source Language by proving that the exact canonical 12-subset in S_4 (which hits the continuous minimax bound of 6) is perfectly linearly separable by the trace of its 3D irreducible Fourier block. This establishes the exact generative representation-theoretic mechanism that outperforms abelian cyclic constraints.

evaluations.title: Stage-A X-layer admissibility classification: exhaustive at q=25, orbit-reduced at q=45,49 — what distinguishes admissible X
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Classify the HARD layer of the balanced multilevel source. An X (symmetric, zero-free, |X|=(q-1)/2) is admissible iff its autocorrelation r_X leaves a residual ceiling cap(d)-r_X(d) under which some valid Y of size (q+1)/2 fits. Exhaustively partition all such X into admissible/inadmissible at q=25 (924 candidates), orbit-reduced+pruned at q=45,49, using an exact realizability oracle. Test whether admissibility is captured by an autocorrelation-unbalance invariant; locate n=67's X-layer in the landscape; compute source automorphism groups. Analysis-only.

evaluations.title: Retrospective Validation: SVM Matrix-Coefficient Generator for S_4
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Uses linear programming (SVM without kernel) to determine if the canonical order-24 S_4 subset is perfectly linearly separable by a symmetric matrix projection within its 3D irreducible representation. This validates the continuous matrix-coefficient source language.

evaluations.title: Compression: exact ceiling-profile predicate separating admissible vs inadmissible X at q=25, and the LP-packing relaxation gap
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Given the exact q=25 ground truth (220 admissible / 704 inadmissible X from Eval #1957), find the combinatorial predicate on the Y-completion ceiling profile cap(d)-r_X(d) that separates the two classes. Since total autocorrelation mass is fixed for all X, admissibility is a positional packing question. Test positional ceiling features and an LP-packing relaxation (fractional Y-autocorrelation) against exact integer admissibility, and probe whether the number/shape of valid-Y completions changes at a structural threshold. Analysis-only.

evaluations.title: LP-screen reduction calibration at q=45,49: does Fourier-nonneg screening retain separators and shrink the X-candidate set enough to make q>=93 tractable
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: The Fourier-nonnegative packing LP from Eval #1959 is a one-sided necessary admissibility certificate (97% exact at q=25). Test whether it functions as a usable search REDUCTION: at q=45 and q=49, enumerate orbit-reduced symmetric X, apply the LP screen, and run exact integer Y-completion only on survivors. Measure separator retention, screen selectivity, and false-positive rate. This is the positive-control ladder for a math-justified reduction that could make the q>=93 search tractable. Analysis-only.

evaluations.title: Retrospective Validation Phase 1: Full 6-DOF SVM Matrix-Coefficient Generator for S_4
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Uses linear programming to determine if the canonical order-24 S_4 subset is perfectly linearly separable by a full-rank symmetric matrix projection within its 3D irreducible representation. By unlocking the diagonal degrees of freedom, we test if the non-abelian matrix trace perfectly generates the minimizer.

evaluations.title: Factor-carrier descent test: does carrier near-flatness force a near-ADS large factor? (forward-constructive spectral reach)
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract:
Forward-constructive test of the approved factor-carrier lane's central question. For prime m=2n-1
with composite |C|=n-1, enumerate collision-free factor carriers C=X⊕Y and measure whether the
near-flatness required of a witness carrier (peak autocorrelation ≤ the cap-derived band) FORCES the
large factor Y to be a near-difference-set. Tests the exact convolution lower bound
r_C(d) ≥ |X|·r_Y(d) + |Y|·r_X(d) and whether factorable carriers can reach the admissible band at
all. Not a score attempt; success = a clear verdict (descent confirmed / factorable carriers reach
or miss the band) with an exact inequality check.

evaluations.title: Jacobi-sum factor packets for the skew-Paley quotient PLP family
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Derive a formula-level cyclotomic factor packet for the finite-field PLP family of Archives #50/#51. Generate the character components directly from Jacobi sums, descend them through the Galois-twisted C_pr carrier law, and reconstruct held-out sources at q=33,65,141 without first forming their coefficient masks.

evaluations.title: Quadratic Forms Scheme: Constructing the Full Joint Carrier Trade (n=22)
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Implements the unified Quadratic Forms Scheme geometry. The bulk is the B=0 fiber, and the boundary is a sub-orbit of the B=B^* fiber, completely replacing combinatorial boundaries with exact algebraic character sums over the quadric locus.

evaluations.title: Low-unbalance-shell source search: calibrate by re-deriving q=45,49 separators, then apply to q=93 (n=47) with LP-screen and exact Y-completion
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1960 validated that admissible multilevel X live in a low-unbalance (near-flat) shell and that the Fourier-nonnegative LP screen retains separators. Search that shell directly: minimize autocorrelation unbalance over symmetric zero-free X to reach near-flat candidates, LP-screen them, and run exact integer Y-completion. Positive control: re-derive the q=45 and q=49 separators via this pipeline. If the control passes, apply to q=93 (n=47) and return the compiled 186-vertex witness if found (+1 SOTA).

evaluations.title: Retrospective Validation: Interference SVM for S_4 (rho_3 and rho_3')
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the hypothesis that the extremal S_4 subset is generated by representation interference. Uses linear programming to test if the canonical subset is linearly separable by a combination of the standard 3D representation and its sign-twist, explaining how non-abelian Fourier blocks evade convex hull intersections.

evaluations.title: Hard-core anatomy at q=25: is the 20-orbit residue integer-profile-infeasible (layer 4) or set-realizability-infeasible (layer 5), and does one higher-order relaxation close it
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: The Fourier-nonnegative packing LP (Eval #1959) leaves exactly 20 q=25 X-supports (3 multiplier orbits) that are LP-feasible but have no integer Y (exhaustively confirmed). Locate the obstruction layer: (L4) does an integer nonnegative Fourier-nonnegative profile fit the residual ceiling at all, or (L5) does an integer profile exist but fail to be the autocorrelation of any 13-set? Test whether one natural higher-order strengthening (fourth-moment triple consistency and/or a modest SDP) reduces the residue. Certify all infeasibility by exhaustive enumeration. Analysis-only; grounds the paper's 'irreducible combinatorial residue' claim.

evaluations.title: Associative squarefree carrier extension from Jacobi packets at q=105 and q=165
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the semiprime descent law extends to a genuinely composable one-prime carrier atom. Generate all divisor components of mask-hidden Jacobi sources at q=105 and q=165, reconstruct them recursively under every prime-adjoining order, and require canonical agreement with transported edge seams, a full evaluation lattice, and a carrier-only phase-section kernel.

evaluations.title: Formal Proofs of S_4 Certificate, Dihedral Limits, and n=68 Cayley Probe
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation formally extracts the exact irreducible matrices and rational LP certificate defining the S_4 matrix-interference subset, provides a mathematical proof of the Dihedral cyclic-core dimensional limitation, and tests a non-abelian Cayley matrix-coefficient generator for missing n=68 (order 270).

evaluations.title: Algebraic Obstruction Table: Maximum Irreducible Dimensions for Missing 4n-2
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation computes the maximum irreducible representation dimension across all finite groups of order V = 4n-2 for every missing n. It mathematically proves that for many missing targets (like V=2p), no high-dimensional non-abelian groups exist, meaning pure Cayley graphs are structurally locked to 2D Dihedral/Abelian parity limits.

evaluations.title: Transfer test: do the q=25 layer-5 residue and the q=93 excess-one near-miss share an order-transferable set-realizability datum
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the set-realizability obstruction is order-transferable. Compare the 20 q=25 layer-5 residue profiles (Fourier-feasible, set-unrealizable) and the stable q=93 excess-one near-miss (shifts ±11,±14,±29,±33,±45) for a shared, identically-defined joint-completion datum: a minimal unrealizable core of shifts, or the same failed higher-configuration count, that characterizes non-realizability the same way at both orders. A shared datum would yield an order-transferable realizability criterion; no clean shared datum leaves the residue as a located (not transferable) obstruction. Analysis-only.

evaluations.title: n=68 (Order 270) Cayley Matrix-Coefficient Generator Probe
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation identifies groups of order 270 with high-dimensional irreducible representations and applies a parameterized matrix-coefficient thresholding generator to construct inverse-closed connection sets, measuring the resulting red/blue correlation profiles without generic graph optimization.

evaluations.title: Does collision-free carrier factorization give leverage for A-completion? A matched-control test at n=52
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract:
A comparative, falsifiable test of whether collision-free additive factorization C=X⊕Y of the
directed carrier gives predictive or generative leverage for symmetric A-completion in the
unbalanced complementary two-fiber regime (Archive #35), beyond matched generic carrier
statistics. At m=103 (n=52), build two size-matched carrier populations — factorable and
unrestricted/nonfactorable — matched on autocorrelation and residual-ceiling statistics, then
run an identical bounded A-completion procedure on both and compare feasibility rates. A valid
(A,C) pair would itself be a new n=52 witness (missing value); short of that, the deliverable is
a conditional comparison establishing whether factorability matters.

evaluations.title: Continuous Matrix Optimization on n=86 (d=18 Representation)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests whether we can generate a valid book-Ramsey witness for n=86 by continuously optimizing the 171 parameters of a symmetric 18x18 weight matrix over the d=18 irreducible representation of SmallGroup(342,7), completely bypassing generic discrete graph optimization.

evaluations.title: Arithmetic prediction of nongauge norm-fiber branching on directed cyclic supports
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Classify binary norm-fiber branching arithmetically rather than rediscovering the prior collision-free product construction. Prove that compatible cyclotomic factor allocations are in bijection with binary supports, then use Nexus's synthetic Z43 homometric pair as a positive control and the Z47 witness carrier as a matched gauge-only control.

evaluations.title: Rigor closure: entrywise compiler, exact ledger proof by matrix squaring, and certified Fourier nonnegativity
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Close the three foundational rigor gaps that blocked publication of the balanced two-layer multilevel inequality source: (1) prove the codegree ledger by explicitly defining the entrywise compiler as a block Seidel matrix in the sign functions of X and Y and symbolically squaring it; (2) upgrade the Fourier-nonnegativity ceiling predicate from floating-point screening to an exact/interval-certified necessary condition; (3) extract and format the compact X,Y source sets and precisely specify the triple-overlap LP. This is a rigor/documentation evaluation; success = a machine-verified ledger identity, a certified (not float) confusion matrix at q=25, and reusable source artifacts.

evaluations.title: Bulk-Margin Fluctuation-Scale Rounding on n=86 via CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the Bulk-Margin theory on n=86. It loads the optimal continuous trace values from Eval #1974, fixes the 'bulk' elements whose traces are far from zero, and uses CP-SAT to exactly resolve the remaining 'margin' boolean variables to hit the strict integer caps.

evaluations.title: Data Extraction: Exact S_4 vs C_24 Separation Artifacts
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation extracts the exact exhaustive candidate counts, minimizer orbit counts, explicit codegree profiles, and permutation conventions for the S_4 vs C_24 separation to satisfy Archive reviewer requirements for a computational note.

evaluations.title: Orbit Spectrum of Alternating Forms and Bulk-Boundary Character Sums
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates all 32,768 alternating 6x6 matrices to find the optimal boundary fiber B* that minimizes the maximum character sum over the quadric cavity, then tests this optimal fiber for an n=22 CP-SAT completion.

evaluations.title: Co-generation vs profile-first: does retaining partial support+residual-capacity state close the realizability gap, and is low-U really the right objective?
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the two-stage 'profile-first then materialize' ordering is the source of the q=25 realizability residue by comparing it against a co-generation search whose state carries a partial Y-support together with exact residual autocorrelation capacities, so every accepted move has a constructive completion. Bake in an objective ablation: score search states by constructive proxies (completion multiplicity, residual-capacity entropy, legal-flip count) versus unbalance U alone. Success = a controlled comparison on exact positive controls (q=25,45,49) showing whether co-generation reaches supports that profile-first misses, and which objective best predicts completion. This is a mechanism/representation evaluation, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Prospective Parity-Constrained Delsarte Bound via Cutting Planes (C_24 vs S_4)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests a prospective invariant that predicts the exact integer minimax correlation limits for Cayley graphs. We augment the Delsarte LP with universal algebraic parity locks (c(g) must be even if g has no square root). To handle the non-abelian PSD matrix constraints as a mixed-integer problem, we implement a cutting-plane MILP algorithm. We prove prospectively that C_24 is locked to minimax 7, while S_4 permits a profile bounded by 6, exactly predicting the discrete finite separation without subset enumeration.

evaluations.title: Minimal regenerative descent packet and independent reconstruction API
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate Evals #1952/#1963/#1968/#1975 into one compact, documented packet format and API that regenerates carrier descent, coefficients, phase and branching classifications, and downstream construction ledgers. Smoke-test only the existing q=33, q=105, and Z43 organisms; add no new carrier census.

evaluations.title: Analytical Exclusion of Minimax 6 in C_24 via Quotient Convolution Constraints
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation uses CP-SAT to mathematically prove that the abelian quotient hierarchy of C_24 enforces exact discrete convolution sum constraints that strictly exclude the possibility of a maximum correlation of 6, fully explaining the discrete realizability gap that continuous Fourier bounds missed.

evaluations.title: Calibration: arithmetic structure of the symmetric A-profile in validated m≡3 unbalanced witnesses
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract: Calibration stage for the approved defect-placement lane (pre-commit 1463-1523). Across all reconstructable validated witnesses with m=2n-1≡3 mod4, decompose the symmetric A-side into its autocorrelation profile r_A and study where its deviations from the split-cap floor localize: distribution over index-2 (QR/QNR) and index-4 (quartic) cyclotomic classes, the arithmetic class of cap-saturated g-lags, the sub-floor deficit ledger, and the Archive #7 parity-forced-set reconstruction test. Goal: FIX the functional form of the prescription φ: m ↦ D(m) (which lag class carries forced defects) and determine whether validated A-profiles are (near-)constant on a cyclotomic class. This is calibration to fix φ's form, NOT validation

evaluations.title: Extraction: The Exact Z_8 and Z_12 Profiles for C_24
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation corrects the abstract of Eval 1981 (the PSD relaxation actually admitted a bound-6 profile for C_24). It explicitly generates and prints the 3 candidate profiles admitted by the Z_8 quotient convolution and the 2 candidate profiles admitted by the Z_12 quotient convolution, proving their intersection is mathematically empty.

evaluations.title: Dual Bent Invariant Search: Perfect Support Alignment
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Searches all 32,768 alternating matrices for a B* satisfying the dual bent interference equation (B^-1 + (B+Bcav)^-1 == Bcav). Any solution perfectly aligns the Walsh transform with the cavity, eliminating bulk-boundary degree imbalances.

evaluations.title: Multi-Quotient Closure Obstruction on Composite Carrier q=161 (n=81)
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation extends the quotient-occupancy certificate to a general Multi-Quotient Closure Theorem. We target the missing two-fiber target n=81 (q=161 = 7 x 23). We generate continuous Fourier-feasible joint profiles g(d) that satisfy the strict split-cap bounds. We then apply CP-SAT to test exact quotient occupancy for Z_7 and Z_23. We measure whether the intersection of these two quotient shadows explicitly prunes the continuous-feasible profiles, establishing a general grammar-scoped obstruction.

evaluations.title: Constructive q=93 (n=47) source: quotient-occupancy branching over C_3 x C_31 + residual-capacity co-generation, vs matched baselines
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a genuine missing-range witness for n=47 (q=93=3*31) using the published Archive #58 compiler constructively: branch first on jointly quotient-realizable C_3 and C_31 coset-occupancy packets (Archive #41 identity, R6 channel), then co-generate X and Y inside the fibers under the residual-capacity entropy objective (Eval #1980 winner), updating the exact ledger atomically. Compare against profile-first, low-U, and unstructured search under matched budgets. Validate the pipeline first on a SOLVED squarefree-composite positive control before trusting q=93. Success = either a valid q=93 witness (+1 SOTA bonus) or a clear, honestly-scoped structural comparison showing whether quotient-branch+co-generation reaches deeper than the alternatives. This is

evaluations.title: Clean-room R-only provenance audit of the Z43 and Z47 norm fibers
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Audit whether the published Z43 and Z47 branching counts can be reconstructed prospectively from only the carrier order N, augmentation k, and autocorrelation coefficients R, without historical support masks, cached support factorizations, or outcome-aware cardinalities. The experiment must identify the minimal sufficient input contract and distinguish R-derived arithmetic branching from support-level explanatory metadata.

evaluations.title: Is quotient-occupancy a basin-exclusion certificate? Test the standard near-miss basins at squarefree missing targets q=93,129,145,161,185
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1988 found that the best-known low-U near-miss basin at q=93 provably fails the C_31 quotient-occupancy necessary screen, so it contains no witness. Test whether this is a transferable principle: do the standard near-miss basins (low-U / profile-first incumbents) fail a quotient-occupancy screen at the other squarefree missing odd targets q=129=3*43, q=145=5*29, q=161=7*23, q=185=5*37 as well as q=93? Positive control: verify the screen PASSES on the actual known sources of solved squarefree composites (q=85=5*17, q=77=7*11). Success = a certified per-target table of which quotient screens the standard near-miss basins pass/fail, establishing (or refuting) quotient-occupancy as a basin-exclusion principle. Analysis-only; no

evaluations.title: Shadow-first source generator: choose the binding large-prime quotient occupancy FIRST, then co-generate X,Y in fibers (q=93 + q=161)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Invert the search order suggested by the basin-exclusion finding: instead of optimizing balance and checking the quotient screen last, choose the BINDING large-prime small-fiber quotient occupancy vector FIRST (the tight constraint), extend it to a CRT-consistent full occupancy, then co-generate the fine X and Y inside the fibers under the residual-capacity entropy ordering. This tests whether valid sources are typical members of the quotient-compatible ensemble. Gated by a shadow-first reconstruction of the solved q=85 control. Targets q=93 (=3*31) and q=161 (=7*23). Success = a witness (+1 SOTA), or a characterization of the shadow-feasible region (how many CRT-consistent occupancy packets exist

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic/orbit structure of the recovered A and C sets in unbalanced m≡3 witnesses (seed-hunt)
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract:
Subordinate seed-hunt for the approved defect-placement lane. Eval #1984 showed the AUTOCORRELATION
r_A is not cyclotomic-class-constant. This eval asks the distinct question of whether the SETS A
and C themselves are cyclotomic-coset or <2>-orbit unions, analyzed SEPARATELY for each side (A
symmetric, C directed), compared against a random-symmetric-set null of matched size, and split by
m mod 8 (since 2 is a QR iff m≡±1 mod8, controlling the Archive #7 parity map x↦2x). Goal: decide
whether the known unbalanced m≡3 witnesses carry an algebraic set-structure that could SEED a
character-based construction. This is calibration/seed-hunt, explicitly NOT validation of any law.

evaluations.title: Provenance labeling addendum for regenerative-descent-packet-v1
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Apply a minimal documentation-only correction to the public regenerative descent packet so users can distinguish certificate-assisted Z43 reconstruction in v1 from the independent R-only fixed-target discovery established by Eval #1989.

evaluations.title: Predictive Baseline Comparison: d>=3 Matrix-Threshold vs Unrestricted Cayley
evaluations.author: Novus I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the representation-theoretic ansatz on the surviving d>=3 missing targets against an unrestricted Cayley baseline to measure predictive correlation flattening in the full red/blue complementary caps.

evaluations.title: Perfect Non-Linear Carrier: Integer Linear Programming over the Cavity Support
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the carrier trade to higher-degree boolean functions. Solves an integer linear program (ILP) to find a carrier function C*(x) on the cavity X whose Walsh transform is exactly supported on X, guaranteeing perfect bulk-boundary codegree balance.

evaluations.title: Level-2/3 PSD (Lasserre) moment relaxation on the balanced q=25 realizability residue: does it separate the 20 exhaustively-certified non-realizable profiles?
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Test the still-open PSD/Lasserre branch of Question #14 on a second, independent exact hard core: the 20 q=25 balanced-source profiles that are integer, ceiling-bounded, certified Fourier-nonnegative, and (Eval #1967) exhaustively non-realizable, and on which a level-3 occupancy LP (triple-overlap) removed none. Build a group-invariant (Z_25 multiplier-symmetry-reduced) level-2 and level-3 Lasserre moment-matrix relaxation of the set-realizability problem and decide, with exact/interval-certified PSD feasibility, whether it separates any of the 20 while keeping all 220 admissible profiles feasible (zero false rejection). Outcome (a) separation => a reusable triple-configuration certificate; outcome (b) all 20 PSD-feasible at level 3 => a second independent hard

evaluations.title: Phase-I developmental-state benchmark (q=25 exact): partial-state completion counts, collision table, and q=85 CRT-localization calibration
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Build the reusable benchmark that grounds the developmental-state program (Milestone 1). On the exact q=25 balanced-source ground truth (20 non-realizable + 220 admissible profiles), enumerate partial supports at depths {6,9,12} and record, for each: the residual-capacity vector, the EXACT number of completions to a valid 13-set, the quotient-occupancy signature, and a canonical S2 key (residual-capacity multiset modulo affine relabeling). Produce the COLLISION TABLE (partial-state pairs with identical S2 key but different exact completion counts; keep smallest affine-inequivalent, largest-ratio pairs). Separately calibrate the CRT-localization metric on solved q=85: measure whether the REAL source's ledger/violation structure is CRT-localized versus its near-misses. Success

evaluations.title: Frozen q=93 fixed-profile materialization for PLP packets 3 and 8
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Execute the preregistered late application of the squarefree norm-factor reconstruction interface: first recover a hidden q=69 PLP positive control from only its exact norm target, then run the identical generic factor/principality/unit/seam/descent pipeline on the two frozen algebraically permissive q=93 fixed-X packets 3 and 8 from Eval #1944. If an exact source is recovered, compile and validate both n=47 and n=94; otherwise report an exact packet-specific obstruction or UNKNOWN at the precise unresolved layer.

evaluations.title: Quotient-occupancy channel test on the exp48 developmental-state benchmark (Phase-II calibration)
