evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Phase-II calibration of my 60-tick program. Eval #1997 built an exact q=25 developmental-state benchmark (3,600 partial states at depths 6/9/12 with exact completion multiplicities) and found that the canonical residual-capacity state predicts completability at depth 6 with accuracy 0.9992 but leaves at least two exact collision pairs: a depth-6 pair with identical 24-shift residual-capacity vectors yet completion counts 0 vs 19 (their C_5 quotient occupancies differ: [1,1,2,2,0] dead vs [1,2,1,2,0] live), and a depth-9 pair with counts 3 vs 4. This eval tests one preregistered hypothesis: does augmenting the residual-capacity state with a C_5 quotient-occupancy signature (a) raise depth-6 completability

evaluations.title: Constructive transfer: does the quotient channel improve BLIND completion beyond residual-cap entropy (q=45, q=49)?
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Phase-II/III transfer test and the falsify half of my two-eval rule. Eval #1999 showed that augmenting the residual-capacity developmental state with a C_5 quotient-occupancy signature (STATE_RESQ) resolves every different-completion-count collision on the fixed q=25 exp48 benchmark and lifts depth-6 completability prediction to 1.0. But residual-cap ALONE was already 0.9992 there, and the q=25 state dimension is large relative to support size, so this may be predictive sufficiency rather than constructive value, and possibly a small-carrier artifact. The objective is a state that MEASURABLY IMPROVES BLIND COMPLETION. This eval runs matched-budget blind support search on the larger solved carriers q=45 and

evaluations.title: Delsarte-Fourier Obstruction Check for the Bridge Ansatz on n=40
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the bridge source-law grammar for n=40 (m=79) is structurally blocked by a continuous Fourier power spectrum contradiction. Uses MILP to test if any valid boolean subset A and continuous non-negative power spectra for A and B can satisfy the residual bridge inequalities.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Profile of the Skew-Paley Sum Kernel for n=48 (q=191)
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the standard Skew-Paley sum kernel on F_191^* (q = 191 = 4(48)-1) to exactly measure the co-degree violations caused by the q=7 mod 8 boundary parity. Analyzes whether the defects are concentrated on specific higher-order cyclotomic cosets.

evaluations.title: Trade-algebra verification: exact Δr closed form + commutation law + ≥2-generator repair control (n=24)
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract: First evaluation of the approved compositional trade-algebra lane. Verifies, on the known validated n=24 (m=47) unbalanced two-fiber witness, three exact group-ring claims about the two-pair-swap generator on symmetric A: (1) the corrected full-support closed form for Δr_A including the +4δ0 diagonal term; (2) the abelian composition law with exact pairwise interaction term 2Σ(Q_i−P_i)(Q_j−P_j); (3) the reverse-swap inverse identity Δ(g)+Δ(g')=0. Then runs one causal positive control: damage the witness by a single swap, find a ≥2-generator (non-reverse) repair, predict the full repaired profile from the composition law before validating on the system runner. Builds reusable storage/nexus/trade_algebra.py.

evaluations.title: Is the residual-capacity state exactly the difference-multiset invariant? Homometry audit of the q=25 hard core
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Free-exploration calibration eval testing a mechanistic reframing from holiday reflection: that the residual-capacity developmental state used in Evals #1980/#1997 is exactly the difference-multiset (autocorrelation) invariant of the seam set Y, so its completability blind spot is precisely cyclic homometry (distinct sets with equal autocorrelation). The sharp specimen from Eval #1997 (depth-6 pair, identical 24-shift residual-capacity vectors, completion counts 0 vs 19, C_5 occupancies [1,1,2,2,0] dead vs [1,2,1,2,0] live) is hypothesized to be a genuine cyclic-homometric pair mod the affine group. This eval verifies that claim exactly and, if confirmed, measures across ALL relevant q=25 states whether same-residual-capacity collisions coincide with

evaluations.title: Mapping and Repairing the q=191 Sum-Kernel in Z_95 Bridge Grammar (n=48)
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Translates the near-miss Skew-Paley sum-kernel on F_191^* into the Z_95 complementary bicirculant bridge grammar. Profiles the exact residual row defects, and runs a bounded CP-SAT search within Hamming distance 2 of the sum-kernel template to surgically repair the boundary parity.

evaluations.title: Unfolding the residual state: is completion multiplicity carried by the X-layer, not the seam? (q=25 exact)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2004 falsified the seam-homometry reframing and revealed that at q=25 the folded residual-capacity state R(d)=13-1_X(d)-r_X(d)-r_P(d) hides the layer that actually governs completion: 106 of 107 informative collision classes are the identical seam P with different zero-free inverse-symmetric X-layers and mixed completion status (one class: identical P and identical C_5 occupancy, X-layers giving 194 vs 0 completions). Conditional on a fixed X-layer, residual equals the autocorrelation invariant exactly. This eval tests the formula-motivated unfolded state S_unfold=(1_X(d), r_X(d), r_P(d)) as three separate channels against the folded S2, on the exp48 benchmark: does unfolding resolve the cross-X collisions, what fraction survive (the

evaluations.title: Affine-Split Adjacency: Rescuing the Perfect Quadric Carrier
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the distance-18 degeneracy of the perfect quadric carrier from Eval 1995. Instead of an inclusive distance threshold, it introduces an affine-parity tie-breaker to strictly map the zero-character sum to exact half-density. Tests whether this corrects the Red bulk-boundary codegree explosion.

evaluations.title: Skew S/K Block Construction for n=44 via 35-Variable Block Algebra
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the baseline S/K conference construction to prime powers q=n-1=43=3 mod 4. Constructs a 35-variable block-matrix grammar over the Paley tournament matrices I, Q, and N, and uses fast local search (SA/CP-SAT) to find a valid Ramsey rule table.

evaluations.title: Does X-layer dominance transfer? Completability + seam-freeness at q=45 and q=49
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2006 established exactly at q=25 that completion multiplicity in the balanced two-layer inequality source is an X-layer autocorrelation phenomenon: the unfolded state (1_X, r_X, r_P) resolves every completion collision, either X-channel alone suffices, and the seam autocorrelation r_P does not. The seam looks nearly free. This eval tests whether that mechanism transfers to larger carriers (q=45 composite, q=49 prime power) and whether it yields the high-value structural claim that valid-source EXISTENCE is essentially determined by the X-layer with the seam Y acting as almost-always-feasible slack. It builds matched-depth partial-state trajectories at q=45/q=49, tests completability prediction by X-layer vs seam

evaluations.title: Orbit-Deconvolved Z_87 Bridge Search for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus II

This reduces the search for the symmetric bridge subset A to exactly 8 highly structured orbit combinations. Each combination is evaluated using the exact fixed-A CP-SAT completion solver to find the missing n=44 witness.

evaluations.title: Rigorous layer-flip test: which channel exactly resolves S2-collisions at composite q=45 vs q=85?
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2006 showed exactly that at q=25 completion multiplicity is resolved by the X-layer channel; Eval #2009 found the opposite observational signal at composite q=45 (seam autocorrelation more predictive than X), but that signal was non-identifying because the full-state keys were singletons. This eval makes the comparison rigorous by matching the exact #2006 collision-resolution protocol at composite carriers: deliberately construct genuine folded-S2 collision groups (partial states with identical 24-dim residual vector but different exact completability), then test which single channel resolves each group exactly. Channels tested: X-indicator 1_X, X-autocorrelation r_X, seam autocorrelation r_P, and the CRT-split seam channels r_P restricted

evaluations.title: 3-Fiber Symmetric Search over Z_58 for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a 3-fiber search grammar over the even-order group Z_58 to solve the missing gap n=44. This factorization avoids the Even-n Parity Lock of the Z_87 bicirculant by allowing the symmetric base subset A to contain the involution 29, enabling the exact balanced size of |A| = 43.

evaluations.title: Does completability factor over CRT primes? Per-factor feasibility conjunction on balanced composite pools (q=45, q=65)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: The discriminating test for the carrier-dependence reframing from Evals #2006/#2009/#2011. Eval #2011 found the folded residual state binary-completability-injective on the q=45 pool, but that pool was 92% dead and the finding is equally consistent with two explanations: (H-decouple) completability factors over the CRT primes so per-factor conditions suffice, or (H-artifact) dead states are generically easy to separate with no deep decoupling. This eval discriminates them by, on BALANCED completable/dead pools at TWO composite carriers (q=45 = Z_9 x Z_5 and q=65 = Z_5 x Z_13), testing whether exact binary completability equals the CONJUNCTION of per-CRT-factor feasibility screens. If the conjunction

evaluations.title: Class-collective trade: closure + exact cyclotomic update law + seed-side decrease test (n=52, m=103)
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract: Theorem-first test of whether the verified two-pair-swap algebra composes into a macroscopic class-collective generator with construction leverage beyond static seed selection. Declared closed state class: coset-unions of the index-e subgroup of Z_103^* plus O(1) symmetric defect (e in {17,34}, viable by size for |A|=50,|C|=51). Claimed closure/update: a coset-orbit of coordinated two-pair swaps maps a coset-union to another coset-union, with aggregate class-histogram change equal to an exact e x e cyclotomic trade matrix. evaluations.title: Pure Cayley Search on Z_158 with Involution Core for n=40
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the single-fiber Cayley architecture on the even-order group Z_158 to solve n=40. By including the involution 79, the symmetric connection set A can achieve the exact expected optimal degree of 79 without parity distortion.

evaluations.title: Uniform theorem audit for the ramified cyclic pullback atom
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Prove and independently audit the proposed repeated-prime carrier atom for all odd primes and exponents: characterize the image of Z[C_{p^{e+1}}] in Z[C_{p^e}] times Z[zeta_{p^{e+1}}] by the canonical thick seam, derive its explicit inverse and p^{p^e} index, and verify that the reconstructed output is valid input for another ramified step. This evaluation addresses the general carrier theorem before the C9/C27 biological controls.

evaluations.title: Is the composite feasibility obstruction captured by a compressed joint cross-component channel? (exp55 q=45 both-pass set)
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2013 established exactly that binary completability does NOT factor over the CRT primes on a balanced q=45 pool: the per-CRT-factor marginal screens are necessary (reverse residual 0/200) but not sufficient, leaving a 45.4% cross-component residual (166 of 366 both-screens-pass states are dead). This eval tests the decisive follow-up: is that cross-component feasibility obstruction captured by a COMPRESSED joint channel C_cross (the off-axis CRT autocorrelation of the support, plus graded low-order joint moments), or is it irreducibly high-dimensional? On the exact exp55 both-pass set (200 completable + 166 dead), it measures how much of the residual C_cross resolves and whether

evaluations.title: Ramified phase-kernel theorem and hidden C9 intervention
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Prove the fixed-lower ramified phase-kernel theorem under prime-to-p augmentation, then reconstruct the preregistered hidden C9 binary organism from only its lower packet and primitive component. Sweep every primitive root phase while preserving the lower packet, primitive norm, and radical seam, and test the prospective prediction that exact thick descent survives precisely for quotient-kernel translations.

evaluations.title: Density-Corrected 3-Fiber Search over Z_58 for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Applies the inclusion-exclusion topological insight to correct the 3-fiber search on Z_58. Sets the block sizes to the uniform optimal density |A|=29 and |C|=29, ensuring exactly the required vertex degree of 87 while bypassing the Even-n parity lock via the involution.

evaluations.title: Recursive held-out C27 reconstruction from the recovered C9 packet
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Test the hereditary output contract of the proved ramified atom by consuming the recovered C9 packet from Eval #2018 verbatim as the lower input for C9-to-C27. Reconstruct the preregistered hidden C27 lift from only that lower packet and its primitive component, verify exact norm and binary ledgers, and emit a next-step-compatible packet without reading the original C9 or C27 supports during reconstruction.

evaluations.title: Feasibility-level homometry test at q=45: is completability a function of the support autocorrelation?
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2013 showed exactly that on a balanced q=45 pool the per-CRT-factor quotient screen is necessary but not sufficient for partial-support completability (45% cross-component residual). Eval #2017 could not decide whether a compressed channel repairs this because its cohort of distinct supports was near-injective under any support statistic (a sparsity artifact). This eval runs the sparsity-proof decisive test: whether partial-support completability is a FUNCTION of the full cyclic autocorrelation (difference multiset) at all. evaluations.title: Canonical ancestry-state and truncation-minimality theorem
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Identify the ramified pullback quotient canonically as F_p[pi]/(pi^{p^e}), derive its explicit p^e-coordinate seam ledger, and prove that every strictly thinner uniformizer truncation admits exact false-positive component tuples. This formalizes the thick seam as a finite ancestry boundary state rather than an empirically chosen congruence depth.

evaluations.title: Jacobi-Dual Non-Flat Source: 8-Orbit Exhaustive Census (n=44, 47)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact attainable region of the Jacobi-Dual composite mechanism for missing targets n=44 (m=87) and n=47 (m=93). Searches all valid boolean character subsets X, Y to determine if their 8 spatial orbits strictly satisfy the two-layer inequality r_X(d) + r_Y(d) <= n - I_X(d).

evaluations.title: Paley Extension Graph on F_173 for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus II

The Paley graph inherently satisfies the n=44 Ramsey caps, reducing the problem to finding an 87-vertex neighborhood for the new vertex that avoids exceeding the intersection bounds.

evaluations.title: Replication of q=45 feasibility-homometry witnesses: second homometry family, multiple depths, balanced prevalence

evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract: Decisive high-risk test of whether exact autocorrelation trades give construction leverage beyond static seed selection, using a relational predictor that survives structure-breaking. On loaded (1,1) split-cap near-misses at missing n=52 (m=103) and n=64 (m=127), builds the relief-incidence bipartite graph (over-cap lags vs admissible trades that strictly relieve a target without lifting the tight shell, accounting for the four cap-moving rims), and tests whether a non-interfering admissible cover clears the wall. Attempts a symmetry-break-then-concentrate

evaluations.title: Versioned regenerative packet for hereditary ramified descent
evaluations.author: Vireo IV

Add an independently implemented verifier and explicit provenance labels while preserving all prior theorem artifacts and avoiding new organisms or carrier panels.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive CRT Block Grammar Search on Z_174 for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus II

evaluations.title: Focused SA Repair of the q=191 Sum-Kernel Boundary Defect for n=48

Locks the structurally perfect base subset A, and anneals only the cross-fiber subset C to resolve the exact +1 red/blue boundary defects.

evaluations.title: CRT-pruned fail-first positional completion engine on q=93 (n=47): leverage vs matched unstructured DFS
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
Stage-1 build+run of the positional completion engine for the balanced multilevel inequality source
(Archive #58 ledger) at the smallest missing composite carrier q=93=3*31 (n=47). Primary falsifiable
milestone: does CRT-factor exclusion pruning create substantial prospective leverage (fewer nodes /
faster time to a valid witness or to fixed-budget saturation) over a matched unstructured backtracker,
with CIs — or, jackpot, does it produce a valid q=93 witness (+1 score)? Exact exhaustion of a
restricted manifold is an allowed honest outcome but is NOT counted as the positive milestone.

evaluations.title: Clean-room proof and API audit of the ramified pullback packet
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Perform the single planned proof-focused reproducibility audit of ramified-pullback-packet-v1. Re-derive the theorem independently from its public statement, inspect the proof for hidden assumptions, and verify the fixed transition artifacts using a fresh implementation that does not import the packet core or prior audit modules. No new carrier, organism, or theorem claim is introduced.

evaluations.title: Exhaustive CRT Block Grammar Search on 3-Fiber Z_58 for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 3-fiber Z_58 architecture by restricting the subsets A and C to exact symmetric blocks derived from the CRT decomposition Z_2 x Z_29. Tests all 72 combinations that satisfy the required uniform-density |A|=|C|=29.

evaluations.title: Deep Exponential SA Repair of q=191 Sum-Kernel for n=48
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Continues the focused repair of the q=191 sum-kernel boundary defect. Employs a longer (1800s) simulated annealing run with an exponential energy penalty to prevent the defect from concentrating into a few local rows, forcing the stochastic search to fully flatten the boundary profile.

evaluations.title: Operational-heredity repair and adversarial release audit
evaluations.author: Vireo IV
evaluations.abstract: Apply the single permitted correction after Eval #2031: preserve the failed v1 release candidate, create a corrected v1.1 release with frozen dependency closure and semantic validation, and test deterministic byte identity across original, sibling-polluted, and relocated environments plus a preregistered adversarial mutation panel.

evaluations.title: CRT-pruned fail-first leverage on q=45 (correct ledger n-1_X(d)); stretch q=93 witness attempt

STRETCH: apply the winning arm to q=93 (n=47) at full budget as a witness attempt. Either

evaluations.title: Autocorrelation-Trade Analysis of the n=24 Tenax Positive Control
evaluations.author: Novus II

evaluations.title: Completability prevalence + homometry transfer at a squarefree semiprime carrier (held-out for R-B2)

Label completable/dead with the exact completion oracle under a stated per-instance budget. Report with CIs: (1) completability PREVALENCE among both-screens-pass supports; (2) censored fraction (with fast-decided vs censored label rates); (3) mixed-homometry class occurrence (qualitative). Also confirm the exact correlation ORDER of the existing J1/J2/J3 channels. Pre-registered decision rule (see instruction). This is a decision-gating measurement,

evaluations.title: Extended-actuator trades under an exact global ledger: valid-witness search, shortcut false-certificate rate, and tight-shell routing
evaluations.author: Nexus VI
evaluations.abstract:
Rebuild the split-cap trade formalism around an exact global validity ledger (every lag,
moving membership cap, all pairwise interactions), replacing the false on-W clearability
shortcut from the rejected draft. Enumerate an extended actuator family (matched 2-pair
trades and incidence-pruned 3-cycles) on two loaded near-miss organisms and test three
things simultaneously: whether any extended-actuator trade reaches a globally valid
witness, the false-positive rate of the old on-W shortcut against the exact ledger, and
whether coordinated cycles deposit less net load on the tight shell than single pairs.

evaluations.title: Joint-Neighborhood SA Repair of the q=191 Sum-Kernel Template for n=48
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the repair of the q=191 sum-kernel boundary defect by allowing both the symmetric same-fiber set A and the cross-fiber set C to vary simultaneously. Constrains the search to the immediate cyclic Hamming neighborhood of the algebraic sum-kernel template to preserve its macroscopic density-skew bypass.

evaluations.title: Third-order (bispectrum/triple-correlation) separation of the mixed homometry classes — is there a phase-sensitive channel R-B2 does not exclude?
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract:
R-B2 (#2021, #2037) proves no SECOND-ORDER (autocorrelation/quotient) channel separates completable from
dead partners in the mixed homometry classes at q=45 and q=33; J1/J2/J3 are all confirmed second-order.
The bispectrum / triple correlation is a THIRD-ORDER, phase-sensitive, translation-invariant statistic
that does NOT factor through the autocorrelation, so R-B2 does not exclude it. This test asks, on the
EXISTING verified mixed completable/dead pairs (q45 exp57 + q33 exp62) and a balanced pool: does the
triple correlation (support bispectrum) EVER coincide across a completable/dead pair, or does it separate
all of them? Collision-designed (not accuracy-scored) to avoid the #2017 dimensionality-injectivity trap.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT 6-Fiber Paley Block Grammar on F_29 for n=44
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact 6-fiber Paley block algebra on F_29 for n=44. Formulates a CP-SAT MILP searching the 3^(6x6) rule table defined by I, Q, and N matrices to perfectly bypass cyclic parity via field incidence intersections.

evaluations.title: Orbital Graph Basis for PGL(2, 19) on Pairs of the Projective Line
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fundamental non-abelian geometric space for n=48 (V=190) by computing the exact orbital graphs of PGL(2, 19) acting on the 190 pairs of points of the projective line P^1(F_19). Extracts the basis matrices, their sizes, and their degrees to set up a discrete union search.

evaluations.title: Correct-gauge homometry recompute + compact phase-row feature leverage on HARD roots (q45, q93 stretch)

evaluations.title: Quotient-Constrained SA Repair for n=44 Bicirculant (c_U=(16,14,14))
evaluations.author: Novus II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the complementary bicirculant grammar for n=44 by restricting the search space to the unique analytically feasible quotient occupancy vectors over Z_3. Proves that prior orbit-deconvolved failures were artifacts of the k=4 multiplier symmetry forbidding the required 0-coset size of 16.

evaluations.title: Provenance-clean matrix-convolution slack packets for Tenax bicirculants
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct the regenerated n=22 Tenax witness and a frozen n=23 held-out witness directly from compact SU/SV/SUV source residues, derive their complete source-level Seidel convolution and affine book-slack ledgers, and independently compare every displacement class with graph-level codegrees. This is a non-score evaluation establishing the first typed source and ledger packet for later matched interventions and construction search.

evaluations.title: Prospective relation-table ledger for the S/K conference construction
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Recover the S/K construction from a conference relation and its fixed chamber rule, derive the complete book-slack ledger from the small parent relation multiplication table before graph assembly, test it on n=26 with frozen n=30 held out, and perform one gauge-inequivalent chamber-rule intervention preserving declared valency nuisances. This is an independent compositional positive-control lane.

evaluations.title: Corrected O(q) phase-row brancher on q=93 (n=47) and q=129 (n=65): witness-or-failure with full node accounting
evaluations.author: Kaizen I
evaluations.abstract: Run the correct-gauge compact O(q) phase-row branch-ordering heuristic inside the exact bounded completion DFS on the two missing composite carriers q=93 (n=47) and q=129 (n=65), comparing node counts and outcomes against an autocorrelation-ordered baseline and against source-preserving co-generation. Report a complete witness-or-failure ledger. Success = either a valid witness (which scores) or a clean, node-accounted failure/exhaustion report that documents the brancher's behavior on real missing targets rather than a synthetic pool.

evaluations.title: Homometric cross-kernel intervention on the n=22 Tenax source
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Enumerate the exact cyclic norm fiber of the n=22 Tenax cross kernel from its freshly computed autocorrelation, select a gauge-inequivalent replacement before inspecting book slack, and test the prediction that diagonal fiber ledgers remain fixed while only the mixed cross block changes. This is the preregistered matched causal intervention for the matrix-convolution interface.

evaluations.title: k=3 block-signed lift n->3n-1: exact 4-channel recurrence + n=25->74 positive control build
evaluations.author: Kairos VI

witness at n to a candidate at 3n-1, keeping the 4n-2 vertex lattice exact. Derive the exact
four-channel codegree recurrence from the 3x3 block structure of the lifted Seidel matrix,

evaluations.title: Odd-k block-signed lift (k=5,7): general recurrence + witness hunt at missing 73,93,67

evaluations.title: q=85 multiplier-orbit parent transfer through the S/K compiler

evaluations.title: Conference-source tensor lift S'=E⊗S+G⊗I: anticommuting (E,G) search + witness build at missing 46,59,72

evaluations.title: CP-SAT 4-Chamber Skew-Conference Lift for n=44, 48

evaluations.title: Switched k=3 lift: per-copy Seidel switching to break the excess-1 deadlock, witness hunt at missing 80,92

evaluations.title: Cubic norm-invariant character compiler for the q modulo 24 branches

Exhaust the resulting finite type templates on frozen discovery and held-out fields, then materialize any valid missing scored rows.

evaluations.title: Alternating-path matching repair of the q equals 7 mod 8 sum kernel
evaluations.author: Vireo V

This forces balanced degree prospectively. Exhaust the small source-coordinate repair grammar on q=23, freeze all discovery hits, test q=31 and q=47 held out, and materialize any scored missing family rows.

evaluations.title: Four-vertex saturated-pair descent from two-copy Paley parents

evaluations.title: Sum-kernel bicirculant for q=2n-1 prime, q=3 mod 4: exact ledger scan at n=40, growth at n=52,64

We build explicit graphs from a small, fully-specified parameter grid and decide feasibility by DIRECT common-neighbor counting (the evaluator's exact test), not by character-sum formulas. Primary

evaluations.title: Calibration: Seidel switching as a codegree-search move — Gram-magnitude spectrum + switching sensitivity on the n=44 near-miss
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract: Gating measurement to choose the next durable construction object after the closed lift program. Seidel switching (S->DSD) preserves the Seidel spectrum (hence the multiset of Gram magnitudes |(S^2)_uv|) but changes red/blue codegrees, so it is a near-cap-preserving move — exactly the property the lineage said was needed but never used (their edge-flip moves are capacity-destroying). evaluations.title: Odd-order ratio-character modulation of the q equals 7 mod 8 sum kernel
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Refine the q=7 mod 8 sum-kernel by the inversion orbit of an odd-order multiplicative character of the endpoint ratio. Exhaust the complete fixed sign grammar for orders 3, 5, and 7 on preregistered discovery fields, freeze all valid templates, test held-out fields, and apply surviving compilers to the missing scored parameters supporting the same character order.

evaluations.title: Red-safe local repair of the (0,3) sum-kernel seed at n=40: is the blue excess a regularity defect or robust?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract:
Follow-up to Eval #2062. The best sum-kernel bicirculant at q=79 (n=40) gives red_max=n-2
(saturated) and blue_max=n+2, a conserved total excess of 3. The G-degree sequence spans
exactly 3 (76/77/78), coinciding suspiciously with the excess. This experiment tests the
boring, falsifiable hypothesis FIRST: that the blue overshoot is a near-regularity defect
localized at low-G-degree (=high-complement-degree) vertices, removable by red-safe local
edge moves, rather than a fundamental color-frustration. We (A) localize the blue-violating
pairs relative to the degree sequence, and (B) run a red-safe local search (only moves
keeping red_max<=n-2) to minimize blue_max, aiming to reach a valid (0,0) witness for n=40.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Unrestricted Vertex Exposure - Memoryless Greedy Baseline
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Implements the raw unrestricted sequential vertex-exposure process and measures the survival distribution of a memoryless greedy routing policy at n=22, providing the required state-independent comparator.

evaluations.title: Conference-matrix Seidel-switching witness search (flat-Gram source law)
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract:
Test a new durable object: the symmetric conference matrix of order N=4n-2 as a
flat-Gram Seidel seed. Since S^2=(N-1)I gives (S^2)_uv=0 off-diagonal, the exact
Archive #2 book-cap ledger reduces validity to a pure row-sum sign condition
S_uv*(r_u+r_v-2)<=0 (r_u = Seidel row sum). Seidel switching preserves the flat
Gram but moves row sums, so the switching class is an exact witness search space
with a co-generated certificate. Search it for witnesses at solved-control and
missing n; any missing-n witness is a direct +1 score and confirms the object.

evaluations.title: Generalized bilinear bicirculant at n=40: skew (difference) cross + sum within, twist, and codegree-distribution diagnostic

evaluations.title: Warm-started residue-set search on the bicirculant manifold at n=40: can full A,B,D freedom break total excess 3?

evaluations.abstract: Evals #2062/#2068 show the entire single-character bilinear bicirculant class (sum, difference, twist cross forms) robustly gives total excess exactly 3 at q=79 (n=40): red saturates at n-2, blue overshoots by 3, independent of near-regularity. These are all one mechanism: adjacency = one quadratic character of a linear form. Critically it is WARM-STARTED from the bilinear near-miss (already at total excess 3) and

evaluations.title: Full-manifold bicirculant search across all 8 bucket-(a) primes: is the (1,1) wall q-specific or universal?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Four mechanistically distinct attempts (sum/difference/twist bilinear forms, Evals #2062/#2068, and a warm-started full-manifold tabu search, Eval #2069) all stall at total book-cap excess 2-3 for q=79 (n=40), with the best a symmetric (1,1) near-miss whose violations localize at internal differences and whose within-fiber sets satisfy B = Z_q* \ A. This wall was already Kaizen I's archived q=79 incumbent, so it is established across generations for the two-fiber cyclic model. Decisive breadth question: is this wall specific to q=79, or does it hold across all 8 bucket-(a) primes q=2n-1 in {79,103,127,139,151,167,191,199} (n in {40,52,64,70,76,84,96,100})? Any prime reaching total excess 0

evaluations.title: +4-vertex extension atom: solved-n witness -> missing n+1 via mostly-linear CP-SAT completion
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract: Test a new durable object: a +4-vertex extension operator that maps a valid witness at solved n_s to a candidate at n_t=n_s+1. Adding 4 vertices grows N by 4 (4n_s-2 -> 4n_s+2) and relaxes BOTH book caps by 1, giving every existing pair one unit of fresh slack. With the backbone fixed, existing-pair codegree constraints are LINEAR in the 4 new vertices' edge variables; only the 6 new-new pairs are quadratic. This yields a ~686-variable, mostly-linear CP-SAT feasibility problem, far smaller than the full-graph completions that previously stalled. Success = a valid witness at a missing n (primary: 44 from

evaluations.title: Clean-room hereditary quotient packets along the n=67 source trajectory
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the 3x7 tensor quotient certificate from Eval #1621 can be upgraded from one-step compatibility to an operationally reusable source-state interface. Classify the entire provenance-clean 17-move n=67 trajectory in the fixed quotient algebra, implement a forbidden-data transition consumer that emits same-schema child packets, replay consecutive transitions using each emitted packet verbatim, and compare only after freezing outputs. Include the Eval #1618 matched negative control to distinguish state renewal from validity.

evaluations.title: Asymmetry-aware repair of the q=79 (1,1) bicirculant near-miss: target red<=n-2 using blue's slack
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2069 found a highly localized (1,1) near-miss at q=79 (n=40): red_max=39 (cap 38), blue_max=40 (cap 39), with violations confined to exactly two internal difference classes {25,36}, a clean cross channel, and B=Z_79*\A. Unlike the red-SATURATED excess-3 seed that resisted repair in Eval #2065, this seed has red violations on a single narrow orbit with ample slack elsewhere. This experiment attempts to repair it to a valid n=40 witness (red_max <=38 AND blue_max<=39) by a targeted, exact search over a small candidate edge set on the violating orbits, deliberately exploiting the asymmetric caps (blue cap n-1 exceeds red cap n-2

evaluations.title: Dihedral D_q Cayley construction at q=79 (n=40): do reflection-coset edges break the cyclic excess-2 wall?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: All prior bucket-(a) attempts (Evals #2062/#2068/#2069/#2070) live on the abelian two-fiber cyclic model and stall at total book-cap excess >=2. N=2q admits exactly two group structures: Z_2q and the dihedral group D_q. The dihedral Cayley graph adds a genuinely new ingredient absent from the cyclic/bicirculant model: edges within the REFLECTION coset. In the dihedral representation theory, characters pair {k,-k} into 2-dimensional irreps, giving block-off- diagonal degrees of freedom that can redistribute the codegree contribution of a single cyclic difference orbit into symmetric/antisymmetric parts - exactly the freedom a two-class ({25,36}) resonance needs. Moreover, since q=3 mod4, the reflection x->-x swaps

evaluations.title: Composite-q witness search with CRT/subgroup-refined bicirculant at n=44,47,48: does subgroup freedom break the prime excess-2 rigidity?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: At q=79 (prime, n=40) the full semiregular-Z_q bicirculant class walls at total book-cap excess 2, and Eval #2073 shows the (1,1) near-miss is a strict one-flip local minimum with a rigid four- Hamilton-cycle defect (steps 36,25). Mechanism hypothesis: prime q gives all-or-nothing Z_q symmetry (no proper subgroups), and this rigidity is what leaves excess 2. Composite q=2n-1 has subgroup/CRT structure (Z_q = product of prime-power cyclic factors), providing finer-than- circulant degrees of freedom unavailable in the prime case. This experiment tests whether that extra freedom breaks the rigidity and reaches a valid witness at the three smallest composite-q missing values:

evaluations.title: Deep single-prime bicirculant search at q=103 (n=52): does the prime excess-2 rigidity replicate off q=79?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2070's 8-prime sweep gave q=79 a uniquely clean (1,1) excess-2 near-miss while other bucket-(a) primes showed excess 4-8, but the budget was split 8 ways and q=79 alone had a warm- start incumbent, confounding depth with hardness. This experiment de-confounds by giving a single larger bucket-(a) prime, q=103 (n=52, N=206), a DEEP dedicated bicirculant search with strong warm starts, matching q=79's effective depth. Question: does the prime-q Z_q-semiregular class at q=103 also collapse to a clean localized (1,1)-type excess-2 near-miss, or does it genuinely wall higher? A replicated clean excess-2 wall would establish prime-q rigidity as a reproducible phenomenon

evaluations.title: Seidel-switching / non-transitive escape from the (1,1) bicirculant near-miss at n=40 and n=47
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Across six carriers (q=79,87,93,95,103,127) the full Z_q-semiregular bicirculant class - which provably subsumes two-copy Paley and the dihedral Cayley family (Eval #2074) - walls at total book-cap excess >=2, best case a rigid (1,1) near-miss with B=complement(A) and a clean cross channel (Evals #2069/#2070/#2075/#2076). Eval #2073 showed the (1,1) seed is a strict one-flip local minimum (every single edge flip raises aggregate excess by >=46) whose defect is four Hamilton cycles on the two fibers. The common constraint in every failed attempt is vertex- transitivity, which forces codegrees constant on each difference-orbit and locks them one unit over cap. This

evaluations.title: Feasibility gate: H_16 repair-number tooling + diverse-seed existence at a solved n
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract:
Preliminary gate for a co-design-distance study. (1) Implement the H_16 zero-slack extension filter
(Archive #27) and its minimum-constraint-deletion "repair number" R_H16 as a weighted CP-SAT
optimization reporting a bracket [lower, upper]. Validate on controls: punctured extendable witnesses
should give R_H16=0; the n=43 baseline should give R_H16>0 (H_16 infeasible). (2) Test whether several
distinct valid witnesses exist at one in-range solved n, to enable a later topology-vs-parameter
comparison. Success = validated tooling with correct controls AND confirmation that a diverse seed set
at a fixed solved n is obtainable.

evaluations.title: Dimension-reduced B=complement(A) bicirculant deep search at q=79 (n=40), informed by the working n=34 (q=67) witness structure
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: The baseline's Tenax bicirculant tabu search produced VALID (excess-0) two-fiber witnesses for n=22,23,24,28,29,32,34; among these q=43,47,67 are prime and =3 mod 4 - exactly the bucket-(a) arithmetic class. Inspection of the working n=34 (q=67) witness shows |SU|=34, |SV|=32=66-34 with SV=Z_67*\SU, i.e. B=complement(A) - the same structure my q=79 full-manifold searches converge to (Evals #2069/#2076). This refutes a fundamental-rigidity reading: excess-0 bicirculant witnesses exist for prime q=3 mod4 in-model at smaller n, so the q=79 excess-2 stall is a search-depth/local- minimum problem at larger n, not a proven wall. This experiment exploits that: FIX B=Z_q*\A (halving the search dimension to A

evaluations.title: Cospectral H_16 split test at n=41: does tight-pair topology govern extendability?
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract:
Core test of the co-design-distance hypothesis. Generate many distinct valid witnesses at the fixed
solved value n=41 via Archive #49 projective-direction halfsets (varying the free cross halfset Z),
which are cospectral with identical global codegree histograms but different fine tight-pair topology.
For each, compute the Archive #27 H_16 four-vertex-extension decision (feasible/infeasible) and, where
tractable, the repair-number bracket. If cospectral same-n witnesses SPLIT on H_16 feasibility, then
fine tight-pair topology strictly governs extendability, independent of spectrum and parameter -
filling the survey-identified gap. A null result (all identical) is also decision-changing.

evaluations.title: Capacity-profile A + exact fixed-A CP-SAT C-completion at n=40 (q=79): the proven n=36 method transported to a missing prime
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: My 9 prior bicirculant searches (Evals #2062-#2079) all JOINTLY optimize A and the cross set by tabu/SA and wall at total book-cap excess 2 at q=79 (n=40). The baseline's own generators reveal a fundamentally different, PROVEN method that cracked the hard values just below my range: n=36 (PRIME q=71) and n=38 (q=75) were solved by CAPACITY-PROFILE A-SELECTION followed by EXACT fixed-A CP-SAT C-completion, not joint SA. This decouples the problem: choose symmetric A so residual capacities cap(d)=(n-2 if d in A else n-1)-N_A(d) are favorable (high min-cap, low variance, PSD/Fourier- feasible target autocorrelation), THEN solve the cross set C EXACTLY

evaluations.title: Capacity-profile A + exact fixed-A CP-SAT C-completion at n=44 (q=87=3*29): proven method on a missing composite value
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract:
Parallel application of the proven capacity-profile-A + exact fixed-A CP-SAT C-completion pipeline
(which solved n=36 at q=71 and n=38 at q=75) to the smallest missing COMPOSITE-q value, n=44
(q=87=3*29, N=174). Composite q gives A-selection extra structure (subgroup cosets) that may make
the residual capacity profile more favorable than the prime case. My joint tabu (Eval #2075) walled
at excess 2 here; exact completion of a well-chosen A may close it. Targets a valid n=44 witness.

evaluations.title: Coupled support-atom positive gate on n=40 and q=45
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Minimal sketch-stage test of whether jointly committing one inverse pair and two directed-support points gives prospective completion information beyond sequential support placement. Freeze the atom and ranking on the provenance-clean n=40 split-cap source, then transfer unchanged to the cyclic q=45 multilevel separator. This is a positive-control gate, not a target search or interface build.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Causal Comparison of the W_2 Implication-Walk Policy
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Implements the state-dependent W_2 Implication-Walk policy and measures its causal effect on finite-horizon survival compared to the memoryless greedy baseline at n=22.

evaluations.title: Involution quotient (S,D,m) representation at q=79 (n=40): decode-validate, then search the sigma-invariant sign space
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: My two completed evals (#2081 q=79, #2082 q=87) show the proven capacity-profile + exact fixed-A CP-SAT completion reproduces but does not beat the excess-2 (1,1) wall in the complementary bicirculant (order-q circulant) representation, for both a prime and a composite carrier. The compass points at the representation itself. For N=4n-2=2q the only semiregular automorphism orders are q (circulant, exhausted, rigid) and 2 (fixed-point-free involution, untried). This eval tests the order-2 quotient: a signed super-graph on q vertices encoded by symmetric 0/1 matrices S (same-parity edges), D (opposite-parity edges), and matching bits m, giving Omega(q^2) genuine design freedom vs O(q) for

evaluations.title: Real +4 extension build: does H_16 feasibility predict actual n->n+1 buildability?
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2080 showed cospectral valid n=41 witnesses split on H_16 four-vertex feasibility, separated only by color-resolved tight degree. H_16 is a necessary-only filter. This experiment tests whether that filter predicts REAL-graph extendability: attempt an exact +4-vertex build from n=41 to n=42 on H_16-feasible seeds versus infeasible seeds, on the actual graph with correct raised caps. Success = feasible seeds build a valid n=42 witness and infeasible seeds do not. This exercises the 4-vertex extension atom as a construction object and converts a diagnostic into a tested predictor.

evaluations.title: Minimal PLP difference-cycle gate at q=21 and q=69
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Test one source-side operation for the Archive #51 pipeline: a smallest paired exchange that swaps one inverse pair in X and two points in Y while preserving the complete combined autocorrelation exactly. Exhaust the q=21 nonconference PLP, freeze this universal trade grammar, and test the independently generated q=69 field-quotient PLP. Require a non-gauge exact source transition on both controls; otherwise stop without increasing trade radius.

evaluations.title: Symmetry-free full-graph search at N=158 (n=40, q=79): is the excess-2 wall intrinsic or a symmetry artifact?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: All my prior q=79 searches imposed a group symmetry (order-q circulant #2069/#2079, dihedral #2074, and now order-2 involution #2085), and every one walls at total book-cap excess 2. This experiment removes ALL imposed symmetry: a from-scratch local search over arbitrary graphs on N=158 vertices, minimizing total book-cap excess (red edges >38 triangles, blue edges >39 triangles). It is a BUILD attempt (any excess-0 graph scores n=40) AND a calibration: if a symmetry-free search reaches strictly below excess 2, symmetry is the binding obstruction and less-symmetric objects (e.g. the involution quotient) are the right lane; if it also walls at ~2,

evaluations.title: Positive control for +4 extension: punctured n=42 S/K core vs algebraic n=41 seeds — is the one-slack shell the discriminator?
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2086 proved all six standalone n=41 seeds UNSAT for a fixed-core +4 extension to n=42, with the obstruction localized (by the coder) to the one-slack shell (pairs at codeg cap-1) that Archive #27's H16 omits, not the cap-tight shell. This experiment supplies the missing positive pole and the count-vs-arrangement test. n=42 is solved (S/K), so we puncture the n=42 witness to a valid n=41 core, which is +4-extendable by construction, and run the identical exact builder (must return SAT). We then contrast the one-slack shell structure of the extendable punctured core against the non-extendable algebraic halfset seeds at the

evaluations.title: Structural decode of the n=40 bicirculant witness and solved neighbors: extract the A=B / |A|=n-2 source law and transfer to n=44, n=52
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: My prior searches missed a valid n=40 witness because they fixed the wrong regime (|A|=n, B=complement). The inherited witness_n40.txt is a Z79-shift-invariant bicirculant with a single symmetric within-fiber set A=B of size |A|=n-2=38 and directed cross C of size n-1=39, found by the lineage joint split-cap CP-SAT (joint_cpsat.py). This experiment decodes that witness and the other bicirculant-solved small witnesses into their difference-set triples, extracts the arithmetic structure that makes the A=B, |A|=n-2 regime valid (multiplier stabilizer, coset/QR structure, and any C-to-A relation), and attempts to convert it into a source law by constructing and validating a witness for missing values

evaluations.title: Calibration: does a product-character (Jacobi-type) composition rule generate PLPs on composite squarefree orders?
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract: The only known generative construction for periodic Legendre pairs (PLPs) is field-additive quadratic residues, which requires prime-power order. Composite squarefree orders q=p*r have no known generative source law (Survey #174). This experiment tests whether a multiplicative product-character (Jacobi-type) support X on Z_p x Z_r, with an explicit axis-handling rule, produces a valid PLP. It calibrates against the known positive control q=21=3*7 (PLP exists) and the exact-proven negative q=57=3*19 (no abelian PLP), plus other small squarefree composites, to determine whether the rule reproduces the known existence pattern and thereby mechanistically explains the group-structure dependence found in Archive #53.

evaluations.title: CRT-shell internal registration gate on the n=43 positive
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Use the provenance-clean n=43 multiplier-4 source to test the first approved-proposal gate. Freeze the coarse shell as the Z5 and Z17 occupancy margins of the actual cross support C, then enumerate the smallest binary shell-preserving 2x2 CRT switches. Compare the positive registration with a lexicographically selected same-shell control using prospective exact source responses before graph materialization.

evaluations.title: Joint split-cap CP-SAT with multiplicative-orbit-restricted symmetric A at n=47 (q=93) and n=48 (q=95): correct-regime score attempt
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract:
The valid n=40 witness lives in the symmetric-A (A=B), |A|=n-2, directed-C, |C|=n-1 regime solved by
the lineage joint split-cap CP-SAT (joint_cpsat.py). Earlier joint attempts at n=47 (q=93=3*31) and
n=48 (q=95=5*19) returned UNKNOWN with fully unrestricted symmetric A. The new lever, motivated by
eval #2082 where multiplicative-orbit A gave the smallest defect, is to restrict A to unions of
multiplicative-subgroup cosets/orbits on Z_q, drastically shrinking the CP-SAT search while keeping the
arithmetically structured candidates most likely to satisfy the caps. Goal: close a new missing value.

evaluations.title: Reverse-engineer known composite-order PLPs (q=21,33) to extract the flat-spectrum generating ingredient
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract: The Jacobi product-character composition candidate collapsed (Eval #2091): it overshoots the PLP spectral bound even at the known positive q=21. The failure mechanism is spectral concentration; a PLP needs a near-flat power spectrum, which field-additive QR achieves via Gauss sums but which has no field analogue at composite order. This experiment reverse-engineers the structure of actual known composite-order PLPs at q=21=3*7 and q=33=3*11 (both exist) contrasted with q=57=3*19 (proven none): it extracts the difference-set/almost-difference-set type, exact power-spectrum profile, and any additive-quadratic or fiber-structured generating rule, to identify the correct composition ingredient and any p-condition governing existence in the 3*p family.

evaluations.title: Held-out CRT-shell registration test on n=67
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Apply the frozen n=43 shell and move definition without refitting to the held-out n=67 product source: freeze C's Z7 and Z19 occupancy margins, enumerate every binary 2x2 CRT switch, predict the exact graph response from the materialized source, and test whether selective or strong shell behavior transfers. The historical 17-move trajectory and quotient packet are forbidden inputs.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Constraint-Aware Generation and the T_3 Topological Policy
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the uniform sampler with a hybrid Tarjan SCC-checked WalkSAT generator to isolate true 2-SAT dead ends from sampling failure. Causally compares the T_3 Topological trace penalty against the greedy load-minimization policy at n=22.

evaluations.title: Two-step composition inside the frozen CRT shells
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the already frozen binary 2x2 shell move composes into a genuine source operation. Exhaust unique distance-two C registrations from the valid n=43 and n=67 controls, permitting invalid intermediates but excluding immediate reversal, and prospectively validate endpoints before graph materialization. This asks whether the positives are only one-step isolated or whether their fixed shells contain a second valid realization.

evaluations.title: Calibrate the correction-geometry hypothesis on the n=67 positive control: is the crossing low-rank/global vs local/sparse?
evaluations.author: Kairos VI
evaluations.abstract: My session established that fixed-core local vertex surgery fails to reach adjacent witnesses because the validity obstruction is a dense O(N^2) correlation-slack shell (Eval #2086/#2089). Vireo #50-5 reports the valid n=67 witness (q=133, composite non-prime-power, satisfies the validity inequality, not a PLP) was reached by a rank-one move from an invalid multilevel-slack source. This experiment calibrates the central hypothesis (correction geometry must match obstruction geometry) on that positive control: reconstruct the n=67 witness in balanced two-layer Seidel form, compute the exact combined-PAF validity ledger, and measure whether the correction taking a nearby invalid source to the valid witness is genuinely

evaluations.title: Global margin-stabilizer actuator on n=43 and n=67
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Replace the stopped local 2x2 grammar by a distinct operation arising from the frozen shell itself: swap two entire equal-occupancy CRT rows or columns of the materialized cross support C. Freeze this global margin-stabilizer generator on n=43 and transfer unchanged to n=67, testing whether the coarse shell can support a second valid global registration.

evaluations.title: Even-n split-cap lane baseline: exact joint CP-SAT at n=52 (q=103) in the correct |A|=n-2 regime, with n=40 profile-transfer warm start vs matched control
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: The abelian periodic-Legendre route is parity-closed at q=3 mod 4 (Archive #53 addendum), i.e. for even n. The 20 missing even-n values must therefore use the unbalanced complementary split-cap bicirculant instead (Archive #35), which is exactly the object my n=40 (q=79=3 mod 4) decode identified and which exact joint CP-SAT (joint_cpsat.py, Eval #1932) solved. This experiment establishes the lane baseline at the smallest untried prime-q even target, n=52 (q=103=3 mod 4), in the CORRECT regime (symmetric zero-free A of size |A|=n-2=50, directed C of size n-1=51, split cap). It runs three arms: cold; warm-hinted by the n=40 decoded autocorrelation profile

evaluations.title: Replicated, held-out causal test of n=40 autocorrelation-profile transfer: multi-seed profile-vs-matched-control at n=52 (q=103) and n=64 (q=127)
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2100 gave a single-seed signal that transferring the n=40 decoded autocorrelation profile as a warm start for exact joint split-cap CP-SAT beats a matched random-profile control (excess 22 vs 32) at n=52 (q=103). This experiment tests whether that signal is robust and transferable: it repeats the profile-vs-matched-control comparison across multiple independent seeds at n=52 AND at a held-out second order n=64 (q=127), reporting mean/spread of final split-cap excess per arm. Success is decision-grade evidence (with dispersion) about whether the n=40 profile is a genuinely causal, order-transferable construction variable, and any arm reaching zero excess yields a new witness. This

evaluations.title: Exact row-phase shell of the n=39 product positive
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Test a new fixed-shell mechanism derived prospectively from the n=39 product source geometry. Freeze each Z11 row shape of the materialized cross support C up to cyclic translation, then exhaust all relative row phases modulo common translation. This preserves actual binarity, row occupancies, and the complete pure-second-factor autocorrelation while varying mixed inter-row correlations.

evaluations.title: Witness attempt at n=52 (q=103): profile-seeded symmetric A + EXACT fixed-A directed-C completion in the correct split-cap regime
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2101 showed the n=40 autocorrelation-profile transfer reliably yields low-excess symmetric A at n=52/64, but joint min-excess CP-SAT with the A as a mere hint does not close to a witness in 50s. This experiment switches to the method that solved n=36: for each of many profile-seeded, screen-passing symmetric A (|A|=n-2=50) at q=103, FIX A and solve the exact directed-C completion (|C|=n-1=51) under the split cap r_A(d)+r_C(d) <= n-3+[d in A]. Fixed-A completion is a smaller, cleaner exact problem than the joint model, so many A candidates can be tried. Success = a directly validated n=52 witness. Uses Nexus III's

evaluations.title: A-only extension-sound cut for the split-cap packing: pruning power and phase-aware residual-capacity realizability screen
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: My proposal's central object is an extension-sound cut that prunes the symmetric-A search in the Archive #35 split-cap regime WITHOUT choosing C. Because g(d)=r_A(d)+r_C(d) with r_C(d)>=0, any A with r_A(d)>cap(d) (n-2 on A, n-3 on B) is infeasible for every C. This experiment builds that A-only cut and two strengthenings — (1) the aggregate residual-capacity budget sum_d (cap(d)-r_A(d)) >= |C|(|C|-1), and (2) a phase-aware realizability screen asking whether ANY binary directed C of size n-1 has an autocorrelation fitting under the residual capacity cap(d)-r_A(d) (Fourier-nonnegativity / PSD necessary condition on the target) — and measures pruning power on calibrated pools.

evaluations.title: Single-row homometric realization gate on n=39
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the n=39 product source admits a genuinely different internal row shape while preserving its exact pure-factor shell. For each labeled Z11 row of C, exhaust all binary subsets with the same occupancy and full periodic autocorrelation, replace exactly that row, and prospectively audit the complete mixed ledger. Separate translations and dihedral equivalents from nontrivial homometric mates before graph outcomes.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: GF(289) Exact Boundary Ledger Positive Control
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates an exact CP-SAT model for the carrier-host boundary matrix to reconstruct a 17-carrier lift on the GF(289) line-deleted host without special hints, serving as a positive control for the boundary-first paradigm.

evaluations.title: Architecture test: A-first fixed-A completion vs joint (A,C) co-generation in the unbalanced split-cap regime, with hidden-n40 positive control
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: My construction pipeline has always been A-first: choose/screen a symmetric A, freeze it, then complete the directed cross set C. The split-cap ledger g=r_A+r_C does not imply search information separates this way; prior lineage work (Archive #58/#60) indicates binary support realizability — the joint registration of A with C — is the binding layer. This experiment is a prospective architecture comparison in the unbalanced split-cap regime (Archive #35): A-first fixed-A completion versus joint co-generation of partial binary A and C with per-decision residual-capacity updates and sound pruning. It includes a hidden-n40 positive control (recover the valid n=40 source from partial

evaluations.title: Matched-control test of n=40 profile provenance: n=40 target vs non-n40 targets matched on variance, capacity, Fourier margin, and initial excess (n=52, n=64)
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2101 showed the transferred n=40 autocorrelation profile beats a RANDOM-profile control on starting excess at n=52/64. Random profiles are a weak control: Archive #58 already associates low-unbalance profiles with admissibility, so the #2101 advantage may reflect generic low-energy structure, not n=40 provenance. This experiment supplies the correct control: compare A seeded to the n=40 profile against A seeded to several NON-n40 target profiles MATCHED to the n=40 target on autocorrelation variance, minimum residual capacity, Fourier margin, and achievable initial split-cap excess. If matched non-n40 targets do as well, the n=40-provenance interpretation is demoted to "a good low-energy initializer" —

evaluations.title: Macroscopic Variance Obstruction: Exact Integer Quotient Bounds (n=40)
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the strict mathematical feasibility of various macroscopic block partitions for n=40 (V=158). By using the exact integer minimum dot-product (Cauchy-Schwarz) bound, this experiment proves whether a given partition can theoretically support the strict n=40 Ramsey bounds without violating variance limits, filtering out doomed microscopic architectures.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic feasibility probe for the unbalanced split-cap pair (A,C): can multiplier-stabilized class unions meet the split cap over GF(q), q=79/103/127?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: My two prior mechanism candidates (profile transfer, A-first vs joint architecture) were retired by matched controls (#2107, #2108). Following the supervisor's steer and the task's premium on source laws, my new central object is a GENERATIVE arithmetic coupling of the unbalanced split-cap pair (Archive #35): symmetric A (|A|=n-2), directed C (|C|=n-1) over Z_q, q=2n-1=3 mod 4, with split cap g=r_A+r_C <= n-2 on A / n-3 off. Since total slack is exactly n-4 the pair is an almost supplementary-difference-family, and the balanced PLP and skew-Paley regimes both have character-sum generators while this regime has none. This probe tests whether restricting

evaluations.title: Character-condition symmetric sets for the unbalanced split cap: is codegree flatness a character sum?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract:
The cyclotomic coset-union ansatz (Eval #2110) is exactly cardinality-excluded for the
unbalanced split-cap pair (A,C) at prime q=2n-1=3 mod 4: |A|=n-2 sits off the coset lattice
at every nontrivial order. This experiment tests the refined generative ingredient — symmetric
character-CONDITION sets, whose near-half size is automatic and whose codegree r_A(d) is a
character sum. Goal: determine whether any character-condition A of size (q-3)/2 has flat
codegree, and whether a jointly-chosen near-quadratic-residue C of size (q-1)/2 meets the exact
split cap. Outcome selects the generative principle for the proposal.

evaluations.title: Spectral-complementarity decode of the n=40 witness: is the split cap an unequal-size periodic complementary pair?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract:
Two exact negatives (#2110 coset-union cardinality exclusion; #2111 quadratic character is
symmetric-blind, flat r_A insufficient) reframe the unbalanced split cap as an ALMOST supplementary
difference family: the constant-sum value lambda=(q-3)^2/(2(q-1)) is non-integer (37.03 at q=79),
so g=r_A+r_C must be two-valued {floor(lambda), floor(lambda)+1} with +1 only on A-differences.
In Fourier this is |A^(t)|^2+|C^(t)|^2 ~ const: an unequal-size periodic complementary pair. This
experiment decodes the known n=40 witness through this lens and tests whether the coupling is
spectral anti-correlation, defining the construction target for C given A.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: GF(289) Boundary Ledger with Circulant Quotient (Positive Control)
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Compresses the 17x272 GF(289) boundary ledger model using an exact circulant block quotient derived from the affine line translation group. The goal is to recover the native 17-carrier lift as a positive control without solver hints.

evaluations.title: Provenance-clean Z3 row-response interface and bounded-exception lemma
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Build the universal materialized six-bit Z3 row-response interface, reconstruct only the formula-generated q=21 discovery source, audit its full source gauge and CRT decompositions, and prove the scaling boundary that excludes bounded exceptional-row repairs of the full-copy pure-axis defect. This is a discovery-stage non-score experiment; q=33 and later source rows must remain unseen.

evaluations.title: The Uncoupled Regular Bipartite Lift: Breaking the Parity Obstruction (n=40)
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a 2-fiber model for n=40 over Z_79 that mathematically breaks the complementary mirror parity obstruction. Theorem 1 proved the graph must be exactly 78-regular, so we enforce |A| = |B| = 39, |C| = 39. However, we abandon the mirror symmetry B = A^c. By decoupling A and B while preserving regularity, the cross-fiber profile N_12(d) naturally breaks the even-parity lock on the variance slack, theoretically allowing a valid graph for even n.

evaluations.title: Freeze the four-interval positive-density Z3 row law on q=21
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Encode and hash a compact four-interval outer mask law read directly from the canonical q=21 discovery anatomy. Prove its cardinality, inversion, and pure-axis identities for every r=4k+3, verify exact q=21 recovery and full mixed ledger, and freeze the rule before any q=33 source or candidate is generated.

evaluations.title: Conic level-set split-cap source: exact R_s(d) ledger over all valid c at q=79/103/127 (approved lane, stage 1)
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract:
First stage of the approved conic level-set source lane. The single parent is f_c(x)=chi2(x^2+c)
on Z_q (q=2n-1 prime, q=3 mod 4, -c a nonzero QR); A and C are its +1 and -1 level sets, with sizes
|A|=n-2, |C|=n-1 forced exactly by the Jacobsthal identity and 0 in C. This experiment computes the
exact split-cap ledger g(d)=r_A(d)+r_C(d) via the quartic character sum R_s(d) over ALL valid c at
q=79,103,127, honoring the exceptional displacement correction R_u(d)=q-3 at d=+/-2a, and asks
whether any c meets the split cap and whether sign(R_s(d)) tracks A-membership.

evaluations.title: Blind held-out q=33 gate for frozen four-interval law v1
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Instantiate the already hashed four-interval packet at r=11 and fix its complete candidate ledger before any authoritative q=33 source is generated. An invalid candidate closes packet v1 unopened; a valid candidate unlocks independent formula regeneration, gauge comparison, and one preregistered inverse-pair block-swap intervention.

evaluations.title: Conic split-cap ledger is an elliptic-curve trace family: exact R_s = -1 - a_E and the sqrt(q)-vs-O(1) obstruction
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract:
Stage 1 (Eval #2117) showed the conic level-set parent chi2(x^2+c) is multiplicatively rigid (one
orbit per q) with min split-cap excess 7/8/8 and sign(R_s) not tracking A-membership. This stage
tests the mechanistic reframing: R_s(d)=sum_x chi2((x^2+c)((x+d)^2+c)) is the quadratic-character sum
of a squarefree quartic, hence R_s(d) = -1 - a_{E_d}(q), the Frobenius trace of the genus-1 curve
E_d: y^2=(x^2+c)((x+d)^2+c). If confirmed, the split cap reduces to an elliptic-curve trace condition
whose sqrt(q)-scale fluctuation structurally exceeds the O(1) cap slack, explaining the exact excess
and refuting any single-conic source law with a transferable mechanism.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Fully Coupled T_L-Equivariant CP-SAT for GF(289) n=73
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Solves the exact fully coupled boundary (carrier-host) and internal (carrier-carrier) CP-SAT model for the 18-vertex replacement in the GF(289) index-12 PDS floor, testing whether the T_L-equivariant interface allows a valid complete graph.

evaluations.title: Conic parent across congruence classes of q: witness search + congruence-resolved split-cap obstruction map
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Evals #2117/#2119 tested only q=79,103,127, which are ALL q=7 mod 24. Two key features are congruence-dependent: the exceptional row d=+/-2a violates iff 3 is a nonresidue (q=7 mod 12 in my sample), and the trace-histogram symmetry was observed in one class only. This experiment sweeps the conic level-set parent chi2(x^2+c) across primes q=2n-1 in ALL residue classes mod 24 (q=3 mod 4), computing the exact split-cap ledger and elliptic-trace family per prime, to (a) SEARCH for any class where the conic reaches split-cap excess 0 (a witness for a missing even n), and (b) build a correctly-scoped, congruence-resolved obstruction map

evaluations.title: Freeze a skew-difference-set Z3 mask law on q=21
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Freeze a second, mechanistically distinct q=21 candidate in which all six outer binary masks are generated from one normalized cyclic skew Hadamard difference set D and two intersection atoms E_t=D intersect (D+t). Prove the generic structural ledger conditional on explicit source incidences, recover q=21 exactly, and keep q=33 unopened.

evaluations.title: The Uncoupled Asymmetric-Capacity Lift: Shattering the Unit Obstruction (n=40)
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a 2-fiber model over Z_79 for n=40 that satisfies exact 78-regularity while actively unbalancing the connection sizes to |A|=36, |B|=36, |C|=42. This perfectly circumvents both the Regularity Constraint (Theorem 1) and the Cyclotomic Unit Obstruction (Theorem 3). The asymmetric capacity injects 15 units of variance slack into the highly rigid cross-channel, converting an impossible exact cyclotomic Diophantine equation into an open local-search landscape.

evaluations.title: Blind r=11 gate for frozen skew-difference-set law v1
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Instantiate the already frozen skew-difference-set/intersection packet at r=11 from the fixed normalized skew difference set D={1,3,4,5,9}. Test A0, P0, and the full mixed tensor ledger before any authoritative q=33 formula source is generated. Any failure closes packet v1 without repair or hidden-source inspection.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Fully Coupled GF(17)^x Multiplicative Symmetry Model for GF(289) n=73
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: Tests a geometrically asymmetric fully coupled boundary model using the GF(17)^x multiplicative group. This isolates the geometric origin from the remaining 16 affine line vertices, breaking the fatal uniform boundary load of the T_L translation symmetry using exactly 317 base variables.

evaluations.title: Multi-Fiber Macroscopic Quotient: Shattering the Flatness Obstruction (n=44)
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Diophantine bounds for a 6-fiber quotient geometry at n=44. Theorem 4 proves that pure 2-fiber cyclic models over Z_87 are mathematically impossible due to the Autocorrelation Flatness Obstruction. This experiment searches the 6x6 inter-fiber degree matrix E over fibers of size 29 to find asymmetric macroscopic partitions that guarantee strictly positive macroscopic variance slack everywhere.

evaluations.title: Conserved-slack potential: positive control that transient-debt flow dynamics causally reach feasibility vs random/tabu on a solved order
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: The Archive #35 unbalanced split-cap ledger has an exact conservation law: for any size-correct (A,C) on Z_m (m=2n-1, |A|=n-2, |C|=n-1), the total slack Sum_{d!=0} slack(d) = n-4 exactly (a second-moment identity, rung A). Total slack is a conserved fluid; size-preserving swaps redistribute it but cannot create it, so feasibility is a transport problem: route a fixed n-4 surplus so no difference-value is in debt (negative slack). This tests whether a debt-flow dynamics that exploits this conserved potential is CAUSALLY responsible for reaching feasibility, versus null and generic baselines, on a SOLVED control order where feasibility is known. This is a

evaluations.title: Phase-domain decode of realizable split-cap witnesses: is joint integral realizability a targetable phase invariant?
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract:
Archive #41 localized the missing-even-n two-fiber wall to JOINT INTEGRAL realizability: a valid
split-cap profile g=r_A+r_C exists but does not split into two simultaneous 0/1-set autocorrelations,
with displayed component DFTs going negative. The profile carries spectral MAGNITUDE (g_hat=
|A_hat|^2+|C_hat|^2) but discards the RELATIVE PHASE between A_hat and C_hat, which is exactly the
degree of freedom that decides joint realizability. This decodes the ACTUAL realizable witnesses in
the phase domain to test whether joint realizability is a low-dimensional, targetable invariant that
a construction could reproduce. This is a decode that FORKS a build move, not a screen.

evaluations.title: Exact audit of hereditary quadratic colored-process packets
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Independently audit the completed symbolic theorem: exhaustively classify the dimension-four polar pencils, rebuild two coefficient-derived dimension-five atoms, verify every derivative and convolution row, and test materialized direct-sum renewal on a fixed input packet.

evaluations.title: Almost-supplementary-difference-set decode of composite-m split-cap witnesses and an invertible cyclotomic rule tested at missing n=44, n=48
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: The split-cap witness is exactly an ALMOST supplementary difference set: at parameters v=2n-1, k1=|A|=n-2 (symmetric), k2=|C|=n-1 (directed), the SDS counting identity forces lambda=(n-2)^2/(n-1), which is never integer, so the summed difference count is two-level straddling that value with total slack n-4 (matching Archive #35/#41 from the design-theory side). This decodes the two COMPOSITE-m realizable witnesses n=39 (m=77=7*11) and n=43 (m=85=5*17) to test whether A and C are cyclotomic/CRT class-unions with a TRANSFERABLE residue-condition rule, then INVERTS any such rule and evaluates it at missing composite targets n=44 (m=87=3*29) and n=48 (m=95=5*19). Invertibility is the pass criterion; a returned valid graph

evaluations.title: Held-out anisotropic test of the quadratic renewal operators

evaluations.title: The Boolean Lift of the 6-Fiber Geometry: Z_29 (n=44)
evaluations.author: Empirica III
evaluations.abstract: Performs the exact Boolean lift of the flat 6x6 macroscopic degree matrix (D_ii=16, D_ij=14) over the 6-fiber geometry Z_29. This architecture theoretically breaks the cyclotomic unit obstruction and guarantees strictly positive macroscopic slack everywhere, establishing a highly flexible search space for n=44. evaluations.author: Novus III

evaluations.abstract: The only realized UNBALANCED split-cap witness we own (n=40, q=79, symmetric A with |A|=n-2=38, directed C with |C|=n-1=39) uses a symmetric A that appears to be a NON-character set, unlike the Paley/conic character parents that fail in-range. Goal: a reusable unbalanced two-fiber source law (open Question #12), or a scoped structural atlas of the realized witness.

evaluations.title: q=7 causal row-class audit of commutant-twist visibility
evaluations.author: Vireo V
evaluations.abstract: Hold the q=7 generalized-dihedral source, atoms, pure axes, algebra, and conditional expectation fixed, and test the preregistered prediction that all 42 normal-subgroup rows hide the right twist while all 42 reflection-coset rows expose it.

evaluations.title: Close the q=93 (n=47) balanced-source near-miss via bounded-transient-invalidity macro-search
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Kaizen I (Archive #58/#60) reached an excess-1/1 near-miss for a valid n=47 witness in the balanced two-layer source at carrier q=93, but greedy/tabu search is trapped there because no single-step move reduces total excess without creating a new violation. This eval attempts to CROSS that shell using the bounded-transient-invalidity macro-search (depth-3 macro-words allowing +1 intermediate cap violation), warm-started from a reproduced 1/1 near-miss support. evaluations.author: Novus III

evaluations.title: Decompose split-cap feasibility: exactly decide A-only (single-set) existence at missing carriers, with a q=79 positive control

Thus a necessary condition is the single-set problem: does a symmetric zero-free A of size n-2 with r_A(d)<=cap_A(d) (cap_A = n-2 on A, n-3 off A) exist at a given carrier? Goal: relocate the wall to either the almost-difference-set A or the compatible partner C, per carrier, with

evaluations.title: Gate 1: alternating-six-cycle repair atom — mechanism realization on solved witnesses

evaluations.title: Regime-two generalized-dihedral heredity and isolated renewal audit

evaluations.title: Difference-set-anchored cross set: fix C = Paley DS on Z_q (q=2n-1=3 mod4), solve symmetric A; mask-hidden n=40 control then fire at q=103

Anchoring C to this flat difference set reduces the joint problem to a SINGLE-set target: find symmetric A (|A|=n-2) with r_A(d) ≤ (n-4)/2 + 1_A(d). This inverts the hard direction onto A. evaluations.title: Generalized S/K Skew-Conference Lift for n=44 (q=43)

evaluations.author: Empirica III

evaluations.title: Anticorrelation-anchored C: calibrate C-autocorrelation band from realized n=40, build almost-DS C matched to A's valleys, solve A blind; fire q=103
evaluations.author: Kaizen II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2147 showed fixing C to a perfectly FLAT Paley difference set does not emit a compatible A at the known-solvable n=40 (CP-SAT UNKNOWN, annealer excess 24 — worse than generic joint near-misses at ~8). This is consistent with the rung-A anticorrelation fact (#2112): the realized n=40 C spectrum is anticorrelated (−0.84) with A, so a compatible C is NOT flat — its autocorrelation peaks must fill A's autocorrelation valleys. This eval calibrates the true C-autocorrelation band from the realized n=40 witness, then implements an anticorrelation-anchored generator: given an A-only-feasible symmetric A, build a directed C whose per-shift autocorrelation targets

evaluations.title: G1b: single six-cycle atom as NET reducer on exhibited over-cap near-misses (n40, n44)
evaluations.author: Kairos VI

Single-atom entry into the approved over-cap testing gate (G3 subset) for the alternating
six-cycle repair atom. On exhibited over-cap near-misses (n40: red_max 39/cap 38, blue_max
40/cap 39; n44: red_max 43, blue_max 44; both max excess exactly 1), test whether ONE

evaluations.author: Kairos VI

The single predeclared CASE-C refinement of the six-cycle repair atom. G1b (#2152) showed the

symmetric-difference), i.e. the typed-boundary interface p.Delta~0, and check whether any such
low-footprint relieving cycle is a NET REDUCER on the exhibited n40/n44 over-cap near-misses.

evaluations.title: Explicit Algebraic 6-Fiber F_29 Block Grammar Diophantine Solver
evaluations.author: Novus III

evaluations.title: Projective Line Conference Graph Analysis for n=44 (q=173)
evaluations.author: Novus III
