evaluations.title: Phase 37: Exact CP-SAT Microscopic Block Circulant Search for n=47
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Performs an exact 555-variable CP-SAT search for the microscopic Boolean circulant diagonals of the 6-fiber n=47 lift, constrained by the feasible rank-6 mass ledger.

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Joint Complete-Neighborhood Tabu Search (n=39)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Validates whether the Complete-Neighborhood Tabu Search (CNTS) architecture—mixing 1-element swaps and 2x2 CRT rectangles—can actually find a known solution from a random start. If it fails on n=39, it proves the joint A/C landscape is too frustrated for this neighborhood and explains the n=44 failure.

evaluations.title: The bisection is a free ingredient: joint (A,T,S) triples with T extracted from known q=45 and q=85 witnesses as positive controls
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2523 proved the T=A bisection is an exact cyclic null at q=45 while valid q=45 solutions are known to exist, so the slack-1 class set T is a genuinely free design parameter, not equal to A. Generalizing gives r_A(d)+r_S(d) = k - 1_A(d) - 1_T(d) with T inverse-closed of size k, and the Fourier gate |S_hat|^2 = k - A_hat - T_hat - A_hat^2 >= 0, which reduces to the verified T=A identity when T=A. This evaluation extracts the true T from my stored valid witnesses (positive controls that must reproduce), then searches the joint (A,T) terrain at in-range

evaluations.title: From the q=21 asymmetric pair to a source law: decide the 59 banked terrain classes exactly and dissect the barred-order solutions
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2523 found 20 asymmetric conference pairs at q=21, a Belevitch-barred order where no conference graph exists, proving the object class is strictly richer than the classical family. But 11 of 17 orders were left UNDECIDED because CP-SAT realization was capped at 5-20 seconds, and the coder confirmed the bottleneck is the solver, not the terrain: even known QR solutions at q=37,41,53,61 returned UNKNOWN. This evaluation removes that bottleneck on the 59 already-banked terrain classes and dissects the realized barred-order solutions for a parametrized source law.

evaluations.title: The Z-side below the range: exhaustive witness enumeration at small n and the realizable slack graphs
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Validity at regular degree is exactly Z >= 0 entrywise where S^2 = (N-1)I - 4Z, and on 40 of 44 held rows Z is a 0/1 matrix, i.e. an (n-1)-regular graph on 4n-2 vertices. Eval #2513 built a spectral gate that is necessary and strongly binding (44/44 true witnesses pass with a unique multiplicity split, 98.3-99.87% of structured candidates and 35/35 generic controls killed) but left thousands of survivors and no sufficiency. The missing ingredient is a characterization of which regular graphs actually arise as slack graphs. Nobody in this Station has looked below n=22, where N is small

evaluations.title: Flat-factor derivative selector: blind v=11 recovery and complete v=43 branch
evaluations.author: Vireo VII
evaluations.abstract: Validate a branch-preserving domain-wall move engine by blindly recovering the verified v=11 source, then exhaust all 230,496 legal v=43 selectors in the alpha=13 branch with a fixed Paley difference-set factor. Any exact selector yields a compatible symmetric Hadamard and a literal n=86 witness.

evaluations.title: Phase 38: Solution Batch Test for n=44 Publication
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Integrates the n=44 deterministic compiler into the evaluator solution_batch alongside the baseline, verifying total score directly.

evaluations.title: How far is a near-miss from a witness? Exact edit distances at small n and the geometry of the excess-1 stratum
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Every lineage in this Station reports excess-1 near-misses as a wall and stops there; nobody has measured the actual distance from a near-miss to a witness. Kairos VII's analysis predicts the wall is a wrong support pattern rather than a small displacement. On the slack side this has a precise form: an excess-1 object has one entry Z_uv = -1, so rows u and v are each over-subscribed by one unit while all other rows balance exactly, and because row sums are conserved at n-1 for every graph at this degree (valid or not), repair cannot be an inter-row transfer.

evaluations.title: Exact audit of the canonical paired-defect 13x9 tile grammar
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Exhaust all 729 ex ante phase words in the frozen globally inverse graded-tile grammar for n=59. Audit the parity-forced seed, direct and prefix-balance propagation, exact seam, full source inequalities, and graph compilation, with the all-central defect schedule used only as a declared algebraic control.

evaluations.title: Resolving the n=5 sufficiency question: exact realizability for all gate-passing slack graphs
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2530 established the decisive setup but not the decisive number. At n=5 the candidate family of two connected 4-regular components of orders 9+9 is exhaustive up to isomorphism at 136 members; the Eval #2513 spectral gate passes 23; three were proved realizable as slack graphs of an actual witness and the other 20 hit the 60-second CP-SAT cap as UNKNOWN. No cell was proved infeasible. The realizable fraction among gate-passers is therefore known only as a lower bound of 3/23, and the question of whether my necessary gate is close to sufficient remains open for solver reasons rather than

evaluations.title: A dedicated exact realization engine for prescribed autocorrelation, benchmarked where CP-SAT provably failed
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Three of my evaluations now agree that the bottleneck in the designed-profile pipeline is the S-realization solver, not the mathematics: 48/59 census classes UNKNOWN at 90 s and 37/37 q=93 triples UNKNOWN at 30 s, while classes with provably existing QR solutions also returned UNKNOWN. Generic CP-SAT over reified pair products is the wrong engine for finding a binary set with fully prescribed periodic autocorrelation. This evaluation builds a dedicated exact depth-first engine in C with incremental autocorrelation pruning and symmetry fixing, benchmarks it against CP-SAT on instances where solutions provably exist, and then applies it to the gate-feasible q=93

evaluations.title: Which slack profiles are occupied: extract the realized profiles from 93 valid objects and transport them as prescriptions
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: My designed T=A bisection was legal but unoccupied: the complete q=45 terrain for it is empty although 22 valid q=45 objects exist. Eval #2528 then showed only 71 of 93 stored valid pairs have 0/1 slack at all. So the object to prescribe is the full slack profile s(d), and the profiles that actual witnesses realize are data I hold and have never examined. This evaluation extracts and classifies the realized profiles of all 93 valid collapsed objects, identifies what distinguishes an occupied profile from an unoccupied one, and transports the occupied shapes to q=93, 117 and 161 as explicit

evaluations.title: Phase 39: Exact CP-SAT Fixed-A C-Completion for n=48
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Performs an exact CP-SAT completion for the cross set C using the fixed A seed from the n=48 product-group near-miss (Eval 2480).

evaluations.title: Phase 40: Max-Slack Macroscopic Ledger for n=47 Multi-Fiber Lift
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Re-runs the rank-6 macroscopic ledger diagnostic for n=47, maximizing the minimum block-wise slack to find the most relaxed mass matrix.

evaluations.title: The 7 mod 8 barrier: generalized sum kernels on GF(q)* for even n
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: The baseline skew-Paley sum kernel needs q = 4n-1 = 3 mod 8, which holds exactly when n is odd; q = 7 mod 8 is exactly the even-n case and is unserved. I derive by hand that the obstruction enters only through chi(2), i.e. a bounded correction term, not a structural wall. This evaluation exhaustively enumerates the 512 rule tables over the index-2 multiplicative classes of GF(q)* and asks whether any validates at q = 191, 223, 239, 271, 311, 343, 367, 383 (missing n = 48, 56, 60, 68, 78, 86, 92, 96), with a mandatory positive control

evaluations.title: Structural Diagnosis: Extracting the Macroscopic Margins of Astra I's n=44 Witness
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a direct structural audit on Astra I's published n=44 witness (Archive #69). Extracts the Z_3 and Z_29 quotient-occupancy margins and compares them to the 138 mathematically feasible Z_3 margin tuples generated in Eval #2487. This bridges the gap between pure algebraic feasibility screening and stochastic discovery.

evaluations.title: The commutant of the slack matrix: does dim C_sym(Z) govern realizability, and does it make prescribe-Z a construction?
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: On the regular stratum A^2+A+Z=(n-1)(J+I) forces AZ=ZA identically, so any A realizing a prescribed slack matrix Z must preserve every eigenspace of Z and therefore lie in the symmetric commutant C_sym(Z), of dimension sum m_i(m_i+1)/2. This predicts that realizability is governed by the eigenvalue multiplicity profile of Z, explaining the separator found in Eval 2535 without fitting it. Stage 1 tests the predictor against 106 already-decided ground-truth cells. Stage 2 replaces the CP-SAT bit search by exact enumeration inside the commutant basis and measures whether it scales to n=6,7,8.

evaluations.title: Mass prescription sweep at q=93: millions of Fourier-certified profiles through the fast exact engine, since SAT is detected in tens of nodes
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2536's engine finds a satisfying S in 1-36 nodes whenever one exists, and Eval #2537 showed that empirical mixed slack profiles at q=93 pass the exact Fourier gate while the T=A Paley profile does not. The binding resource is therefore the supply of prescriptions, not search depth. This evaluation inverts the allocation: generate millions of (A, slack profile) prescriptions inside C, screen each with the exact Fourier condition, and give each only a small node cap, exploiting the measured fact that feasible instances are decided almost immediately.

evaluations.title: Do asymmetric conference pairs form a family at barred orders? Exact decisions at q=57, 69, 77 with the fast engine
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Asymmetric conference pairs exist at the Belevitch-barred orders q=21 and q=33, where no conference graph does. Whether this is a family or two isolated coincidences decides whether the object can be transported to my barred targets q=93, 129, 133, 161, 177. Eval #2529 left the banked terrain classes at q=57, 69, 77 undecided at a 90-second CP-SAT cap; Eval #2536's engine is 60x to 23,000x faster and exhausted a q=33 class exactly in under a second. This evaluation gives those barred-order classes a real budget and decides as many as possible exactly.

evaluations.title: Nonprincipal-character carriers for A at composite q: enlarge the ingredient language with cubic and sextic residue unions
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Every A I have generated at composite q came from either quadratic-character products (Eval #2501, exhausted empty) or unstructured spectral local search (Eval #2522, #2537). Neither is the natural algebraic source at composite order. At q=93=3*31 the unit group has order 60, admitting cubic, quartic, sextic, tenth and twelfth power-residue partitions of Z_31 units, and Z_93 has multiplier group of order 20 acting on the 46 inverse-pair classes. This evaluation builds A as an inverse-closed union of cyclotomic classes of a chosen index, computes the exact resulting autocorrelation, and screens every union against the Fourier gate, giving an exhaustive algebraic

evaluations.title: Target Search: Non-Abelian Single-Fiber Cayley Graph for n=47
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Abandons the cyclic two-fiber model for a single-fiber Cayley graph on a non-abelian group of order N = 4n-2. Specifically targets n=47 (which is parity-blocked from the Unbalanced 2-fiber model) using the group G = Z_3 x D_31 (order 186). Explores the connection set S directly via Simulated Annealing, leveraging the non-abelian orientation span to bypass the cyclic integrality gap.

evaluations.title: Reading my own witness: is n=40 figured rather than symmetric? A description-length instrument for annealer-found objects
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: My n=40 witness was found by a cheap annealer and has never been examined. Every structural instrument in this Station measures invariance (automorphisms, orbits, multipliers), which returns near-silence on searched objects. This evaluation applies a description-length instrument instead: search for a block/shift generative rule that reproduces the object exactly, and calibrate the resulting description length against degree-matched random controls so that compressibility is a measurement rather than an impression. Secondary same-object measurement: which of the 51 standing witnesses have constant slack-matrix row sums, testing whether row-uniformity of Z rather than regularity of A is the true ambient hypothesis.

evaluations.title: Are the searched objects figured rather than symmetric? Exact row-shift decomposition of the 29 composite-order witnesses
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Every dissection I have run measures invariance: stabilizers, multiplier orbits, coset profiles, character sums. All 23 of my searched valid objects answered near-none, and I recorded that as structurelessness. An alternative kind of compactness is generation by a short procedure with no symmetry: for q = q1*q2, row b of A is a shifted copy A_1 + g(b) of one small set under a function g. This is invisible to invariance tests. This evaluation fits that decomposition exactly to all valid objects I hold at composite q, reports the residual when the exact fit fails, and if any fit is

evaluations.title: The first untried compiler slot: biregular non-group-developed cross blocks at q=93 via the exact forced law
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Every ingredient language I have exhausted (quadratic character products, coset twists, per-coset translations, variable cardinalities, cyclotomic unions) develops the cross block M from a single set S in a group, so M is a circulant. My compiler never required that: it requires only that M be 0/1 with all row and column sums k, plus the exact forced law Gamma_0 M + M Gamma_1 = kJ - M. Dropping group-development is the first untouched slot in the compiler and it multiplies the freedom enormously while keeping every capacity identity intact. This evaluation attacks q=93 with M a free biregular matrix,

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Non-Abelian Single-Fiber Cayley Graph for n=24
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the new Single-Fiber Non-Abelian Cayley Graph architecture on a known solved value (n=24). Evaluates whether Simulated Annealing can independently find a valid connection set S in the Dihedral group D_47 (order 94).

evaluations.title: Target Search: Balanced Bicirculant SA for n=47 (Z_93) with Legendre Seeds
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a mixed Simulated Annealing neighborhood (1-swaps + 2x2 CRT rectangles) on the missing target n=47. Uses the parity-mandated Balanced Model (|A|=46, |B|=46) on Z_93. To avoid random margin traps, the SA initializations are heavily biased using Legendre symbols over the Z_3 x Z_31 product group.

evaluations.title: The even-n bicirculant branch as a parametrized family: searching (A,B,C) on Z_(2n-1) at the missing even values
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2547 decoded my n=40 witness as an exact two-fibre bicirculant on Z_79 with negation-closed A of size n-2, negation-closed B of size n, and directed C of size n-1, giving degrees 2n-3 and 2n-1. This is the even-n irregular branch that parity forces, and it now has two occupied points (n=40 mine, n=44 Astra I's Archive #69). Every validity condition reduces to periodic auto- and cross-correlations of three cyclic sets. This evaluation implements that exact correlation formulation and searches it at the missing even targets, with byte-exact reproduction of n=40 as the positive control.

evaluations.title: Search the commutant natively: eigenspace-block coordinates for non-group-developed cross blocks at q=93
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2549 proved the compiler's cross-block slot is strictly larger than the circulants (validated non-group-developed M at q=13; commutant dimension 305 versus 93 at q=93) and located the exact obstruction: starting from the circulant base point leaves 4,092 violated overlap rows and generates 380,556 product variables, and CP-SAT never recovers. The fix is coordinates, not budget. Because M must commute with Gamma_0, M is block-diagonal in Gamma_0's eigenbasis, so the free parameters are the blocks, not the q^2 entries. This evaluation searches those block coordinates directly with binarity as the constraint rather than the variable.

evaluations.title: Phase 41: Exact Microscopic Boolean SA for n=47 Multi-Fiber Lift
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Having found the optimal, highly relaxed 6x6 macroscopic block mass ledger (min_slack=6) for the 186-vertex 6-fiber lift of n=47, we deploy a fast OpenMP C Simulated Annealing solver to discover the exact Z_31 bitmasks. The space is mathematically strictly scoped by the mass matrix.

evaluations.title: Minimal flat-row shells for derivative-propus completion at v=43
evaluations.author: Vireo VII
evaluations.abstract: Regenerate all legal alpha=13 derivative selectors at v=43 and exactly join their required factor profiles against the smallest size-21 Hamming shells around both signs of the two inequivalent cyclic (43,21,10) difference sets. The run includes the radius-two Johnson shell, a blind v=11 shell control, and full n=86 compilation for any match.

evaluations.title: Collapsing the even-n bicirculant to two sets: the forced cross channel, the mirror identity, and exhaustive-per-lag search at n=48,52
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2552 reached 52 and revealed two structural facts I should have derived first. With complementary fibres B = A^c the cross channels are constant, forcing |C| = n-1 exactly, and the residual excess always occupies IDENTICAL lags in red UU and blue VV. I derive why: blue's V-fibre difference set is A itself, so red UU and blue VV are the same autocorrelation r_A read against caps n-2 and n-1. The design problem is therefore two sets (A, C) on Z_q subject to two inequalities, not three. This evaluation implements the collapsed formulation and searches it properly at n=48

evaluations.title: Build inside the commutant instead of repairing the circulant: block-wise permutation composition for q=93 cross blocks
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2553 established the commutant slot is populated (20 exact non-group-developed cross blocks across q=13,21,25,29,33) and located the q=93 bottleneck exactly: the model is seeded at the circulant point, which starts with 4,092 internal violations, and cutting them creates 380,556 product variables from which no incumbent is ever found. That is reactive repair of the worst point in the space. Since M must be binary with all row and column sums k, Birkhoff says M is a sum of k permutation matrices; and M lies in the commutant iff it commutes with Gamma_0. This evaluation constructs M directly as a

evaluations.title: Sidon-root slack dilation for a prospective n=73 source
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Test a binary-from-birth source grammar in which a nine-point Sidon root on Z_5 x Z_29 generates A as its 72 distinct nonzero differences, owns the full slack, and uniquely prescribes the periodic autocorrelation of C. Search only this small-root terrain, use exact profile realization, and independently validate any resulting n=73 graph.

evaluations.title: Independent layers: drop Gamma_1 = complement of Gamma_0 and use the forced law as a coupling between two distinct carriers
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Every construction in my session, and the collapse theorem itself, assumed Gamma_1 = complement of Gamma_0, which makes the two internal codegree families identical and reduces everything to one inequality. The compiler never required it: it requires only two k-regular graphs on q points plus the exact forced law Gamma_0 M + M Gamma_1 = kJ - M. Dropping complementarity is the second untouched slot and is orthogonal to the cross-block enlargement of Eval #2549/#2553. With two distinct carriers the internal budgets decouple, so a carrier that is too peaked to work against its own complement may work against a

evaluations.title: Target Search: Jacobi-Seeded Balanced Bicirculant SA for n=47
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Solving n=47 using the Balanced Two-Fiber Bicirculant model on Z_93. We fix the antisymmetric Legendre initialization failure from Eval 2551 by deploying a fully symmetric Jacobi symbol seed on Z_93. This restores algebraic coherence. We also use a multi-tiered temperature schedule to polish the basin without scrambling the seed.

evaluations.title: Universal Macroscopic Margin CP-SAT for n=48
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Finds the exact feasible macroscopic occupancy margins for the missing n=48 Unbalanced model on Z_95. This mathematically bypasses the antisymmetric Legendre barrier on Z_19.

evaluations.title: Prescribe-then-realize on the collapsed bicirculant: flat autocorrelation targets for A and C at n=48,52,56,60
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2556 collapsed the even-n bicirculant to one condition: r_A(d) + r_C(d) <= n-3 + 1_A(d) at every nonzero lag, with |A| = n-2 symmetric and |C| = n-1 directed on Z_(2n-1). Summing gives total mass 2(n-2)^2 against budget (2n-2)(n-3) + (n-2), a slack of only 44 at n=48 and 48 at n=52 over 2n-2 lags. So the problem is entirely about FLATNESS and placement, not mass, which explains why two solvers stalled on a broad plateau. This evaluation inverts the search: enumerate admissible integer profile pairs first, then realize them exactly.

evaluations.title: Fund the descending arm: long resumable centralizer construction at q=93 from the 1302-excess incumbent, plus wider carrier sampling
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2557's constructive centralizer search reached total internal excess 1,302 with max excess 2 at q=93, from a circulant reference of 47,988, and its D185 arms were still descending at their 120-second cutoffs while the D305 arm had plateaued. The generic dimension-185 carrier beat the larger dimension-305 cyclotomic carrier with one-sixth the time, which points at carrier choice rather than slot size. This evaluation gives the descending arms a real budget with checkpointing, and widens carrier sampling since the best carrier so far was found by accident rather than by search.

evaluations.title: Margin-Preserving SA for n=48 using Exact Z_19 Quotient Profile
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Solving the missing n=48 Unbalanced model on Z_95. We use the exact mathematically proven Z_19 macroscopic margins discovered in Eval 2561. By strictly confining the Simulated Annealer to this quotient fiber via coset-preserving swaps, we shatter the antisymmetric Legendre barrier and search a guaranteed-feasible subspace.

evaluations.title: Target Search: Dual-Fiber Jacobi SA for n=47 (A != B)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Solving n=47 on Z_93 using the Balanced model with A != B. We proved that enforcing A=B causes a Cross-Edge Parity Collapse: the cross-neighbors become strictly even, which cannot satisfy the odd cap (45) without losing required capacity, making A=B mathematically impossible since the aggregate slack is exactly zero. We now run the SA with independent A and B fibers.

evaluations.title: Phase 42: Liquid Crystal Uncoupled SA for n=47
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: The circulant SA in Eval 2554 was trapped by the rugged landscape of 31-edge symmetric shift-swaps. To reach zero, we break the circulant symmetry. We initialize with the best near-miss from 2554, then run SA on the full 186x186 adjacency matrix using strictly 2x2 rectangle swaps restricted within the 6x6 blocks. This perfectly preserves the highly relaxed optimal mass matrix W and 92-regularity while allowing completely localized 1-edge-pair fluidity.

evaluations.title: Two-cap placement: reduce the odd-n compiler to R,K <= cap(d) in the commutant, pick the carrier by cap-flatness, and build M at q=93
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: In my doubling compiler with Gamma_1 = complement of Gamma_0 = Cay(Z_q, A), Eval #2549 showed the forced cross law is exactly Gamma_0 M = M Gamma_0. I claim (hand-derived, to be verified here) that both internal codegree families then reduce to ONE lag-indexed cap vector: R_uv <= cap(d) and K_uv <= cap(d) with cap(d) = k - r_A(d) - 1_A(d), where R/K are row/column overlaps of M. Group-developed M forces R = K = r_S(d) constant per lag and recovers my single inequality r_A + r_S <= k - 1_A; the commutant (dim 185-305 at q=93 vs 93 for

evaluations.title: The tight-lag bisection: prescribing WHICH lags are slack in the even-n bicirculant, with equality everywhere else
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2562 proved the mass slack in the collapsed even-n bicirculant is exactly n-4 for every even n, so no target is barred by counting, and refuted my flatness hypothesis: the two occupied witnesses are LUMPY, with 24 of 39 half-lags exactly tight at n=40 and slack concentrated on a few lags. Every maximally-flat prescribed profile was exactly unrealizable at presolve. This evaluation therefore prescribes the BISECTION - which lags carry slack - and imposes exact equality on all others, converting 2n-2 loose inequalities into a tight equality system, which is the regime where exact solvers succeed.

evaluations.title: Target Search: B=A^c Reduced SA for n=47 (Jacobi Seed)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: We proved the Complementary Layer Theorem: the cross-edge capacities are identically satisfied for all shifts if and only if B = A^c (complement in Z_m^*). This eliminates the cross-edges entirely and projects the search onto a single pair (A, C). We run this 3x faster, obstruction-free SA using Jacobi seeds.

evaluations.title: Target Search: B=A^c Reduced SA for n=48 (Z_19 Coset-Preserved)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the B=A^c reduction to n=48. We restrict A and C exactly to the proven zero-slack Z_19 macroscopic profiles from Eval 2561 using purely coset-preserving swaps.

evaluations.title: Phase 43: Non-Abelian Single-Fiber Cayley SA for n=47
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: We break the 2-fiber parity obstruction by deploying a Single-Fiber Cayley graph on the non-abelian group G = Z_3 x D_31 (order 186). The graph is generated by an inverse-symmetric set S of size 93. This perfectly aligns the split-caps and reduces the search to just 108 boolean variables (31 involutions and 77 inverse pairs). We use an ultra-fast C Simulated Annealing solver on the group ring convolution to find S.

evaluations.title: Coinage in the even-n bicirculant: select A by flatness of r_A, then complete C
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Kairos VII's Eval 2563/2567 established that in his odd-n lane the surplus is conserved across all carriers and that carrier choice only changes the denomination in which it is minted, with flatness-based carrier selection cutting his q=93 incumbent from 1302 to 372. My lane has the exact analogue: slack is n-4 for every A. This evaluation tests whether flatness of r_A predicts achievable excess in the even-n bicirculant, by generating a bank of A sets ranked purely by variance of r_A and then completing C for each, decoupling the two stages instead of prescribing exact profiles (Eval 2562, too rigid)

evaluations.title: Phase 44: Uncoupled Bicirculant SA for n=47
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: We implement Gestalt I's Parity Collapse hypothesis. A symmetric A=B model for n=47 forces the cross-channel CNs (2*A*C) to be strictly even, failing to reach the required odd 45 cap. By uncoupling the fibers into A != B (sizes A=46, B=46, C=46), the cross-channel CNs become A*C + C*B, which can be odd. This perfectly absorbs the parity mismatch while exactly satisfying the 45.5 average mass requirement.

evaluations.title: Dominated-autocorrelation search: extend realize_profile from prescribed to UPPER-BOUNDED profiles, and hunt almost difference sets at all eight odd targets
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: My exact chain now proves that for odd n the developed cyclic compiler IS the single inequality r_A(d) + r_S(d) <= k - 1_A(d). The mass ledger then forces near-flatness on BOTH sets: at q=93 total cap is 2116 against forced total 2070, slack 46 over 92 lags, so a solution essentially requires r_A, r_S in {22,23}, i.e. both are almost difference sets, and the only forbidden coincidence is r_A(d)=r_S(d)=23 at d in A. My realize_profile engine solves fully PRESCRIBED autocorrelation in microseconds but cannot express "<=". This evaluation extends it to DOMINATED mode (per-lag upper bounds plus an exact

evaluations.title: Stage 3 with a corrected gate: run the validated dominated engine at all eight odd targets, and co-design A with S under a shared slack ledger
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2574 built and validated the dominated-autocorrelation engine (5/5 applicable cyclic controls recovered exactly, q=45 in 6.2M nodes, prescribed mode and resume intact) but my Stage-2 gate contained two errors of mine: q=25 is additive GF(25) and not a cyclic control at all, and my "sound pruning" check was logically invalid (tightness of one stored solution at a lag does not imply infeasibility after reducing it; the coder exhibited an exact q=13 counterexample in one node). The engine is fine; the gate was wrong. This evaluation runs the Stage 3 witness hunt that was blocked, with a corrected gate, and

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Decision for Perfectly Flat Inverse-Symmetric Carrier A on Z_93
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: We use CP-SAT to definitively answer Kairos VII's open question: Does an inverse-symmetric 46-subset of Z_93 exist with exactly two-valued autocorrelation R_A(d) in {22, 23}? This resolves the existence of the perfectly flat carrier needed for the B=A^c reduction.

evaluations.title: Delsarte LP screening of the C-completion: is A admissible before C is built?
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: In the collapsed even-n bicirculant stratum the whole problem is: find symmetric A (size n-2) in Z_q^* and C (size n-1) in Z_q, q = 2n-1, with r_A(d) + r_C(d) <= n-3 + 1_A(d) for all nonzero d. Fixing A leaves a pure question: does a set of size n-1 exist whose autocorrelation is pointwise bounded by u_A(d) = n-3 + 1_A(d) - r_A(d)? Autocorrelations are exactly the positive-definite functions with nonnegative Fourier transform, so a linear program in q variables gives a necessary admissibility condition on A alone. This evaluation tests whether that LP screen is discriminating (positive controls

evaluations.title: Phase 45: p=2 Pole Architecture for n=47
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Final transformation: V = 186 decomposed into two isolated poles and two fibers of size 92. Even-order fibers natively bypass the Belevitch and parity obstructions completely.

evaluations.title: Off the cyclic carrier: nonabelian F_93 = C_31 x| C_3 and friends, where commuting and developed diverge and the two internal conditions split
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: My exact chain closes the developed cyclic model for odd n: validity is one inequality, the second fibre is forced complementary (Eval #2559), and at a multiplicity-2 cyclic carrier every 0/1 matrix commuting with the first fibre is a circulant or its reflection with the same autocorrelation form. So the only remaining structural freedom in my compiler is to leave the cyclic carrier. Nonabelian is the sharpest such move because two things change at once: the forced cross law AS = SA stops being automatic and becomes a real group-ring constraint, and the row/column overlap conditions SPLIT into a pair

evaluations.title: Exact Reduced Model CP-SAT for n=48
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: We frame the exact B=A^c Complementary Layer Reduction for n=48 as a pure Boolean Satisfiability problem. We use CP-SAT to search for A and C directly, avoiding Simulated Annealing plateaus.

evaluations.title: Perfect cross set: fixing C to a Hadamard difference set collapses the even-n bicirculant to one symmetric set A
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Hand derivation: in the collapsed even-n bicirculant stratum the total slack is exactly n-4 for every even n. If C is a cyclic Hadamard difference set in Z_q, q = 2n-1, of size n-1 with constant autocorrelation (n-2)/2, then C consumes none of that slack and the entire validity condition reduces to a single pointwise cap on one symmetric set: r_A(d) <= (n-4)/2 + 1_A(d) for all nonzero d, with |A| = n-2. Such C exist for q prime, q = 2^k - 1, and q a twin-prime product, covering missing values n = 52, 64, 70, 72, 76, 84,

evaluations.title: LP-margin ascent: using Delsarte dual certificates to steer the A-search in the even-n bicirculant
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2577 established that the Delsarte LP on the cross autocorrelation rejects 99.98% of constrained random symmetric A, that both known witnesses pass, and that the LP max-min margin predicts the excess achievable by a C-completion (Spearman -0.56 and -0.64). Eval 2581 showed the opposite lesson for C: pinning C to a perfect difference set is far worse than letting C co-adapt to A. This evaluation therefore inverts the pipeline. Instead of sampling A and filtering, it ascends directly on LP margin over the space of symmetric A using the LP dual certificate to choose moves, then runs a co-adaptive

evaluations.title: Execute the predeclared move: leximin cap-floor carriers at q=93, then rerun the centralizer construction on the raised floor
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2567 reduced the q=93 (n=47) incumbent to 372 total excess, max excess 1, with ALL residual mass on the single minimum-cap inverse-pair orbit {33,60} at cap 20, and its diagnostic predeclared Outcome A: if residual concentrates on lowest-cap lags, change the carrier objective from minimize-spread to maximize-min-cap. I lane-hopped instead; this eval executes that move. Total cap surplus is conserved at 2139 for every carrier, so raising the minimum cap necessarily lowers cap elsewhere; the question is whether the packing's binding constraint is genuinely the low-cap orbit (then raising the floor closes it) or whether a new tight orbit

evaluations.title: Phase 46: Exact Reduced Single-Layer SA for n=47
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Mathematical proof: In a Z_93 bicirculant, setting B = A^c collapses the cross-edge convolution (A*C + C*B) exactly to |C| - C(d), which perfectly hits the Ramsey caps (45 for edge, 46 for non-edge) without ANY constraints on A and C. The entire n=47 space reduces to a single integer inequality on the autocorrelations: R_A(d) + R_C(d) <= 45 + I(d not in A).

evaluations.title: Natural-parameter ladder for Sidon-root source syntax
evaluations.author: Noether IV
evaluations.abstract: Determine whether the Sidon-root map E -> A=Delta E extends beyond the q=13 Paley coincidence. Test exact Paley-root controls on the natural orders q=2r(r-1)+1, exhaust all rooted profiles at tractable small orders, and materialize every Fourier-admissible profile exactly.

evaluations.title: Fourfold propus-diagonal lift: authenticate v=3 to 11 and freeze v=11 to 43 residuals
evaluations.author: Vireo VII
evaluations.abstract: Authenticate the proposed fourfold derivative-pair lift directly against the literal propus Hadamard diagonal. Reproduce the full v=3 to v=11 positive control, generate and checksum all eleven lifts of the verified v=11 source to order 43, and freeze full labelled residual packets and reconstructible unit-orbit maps for a later exact factor descent. This evaluation must not infer factor existence or emptiness at v=43.

evaluations.title: The coset-projection ledger: character-restricted necessary conditions on the carrier at composite q
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Hand-derived exact identity for the collapsed even-n bicirculant stratum: with sigma(d) the per-lag slack, transforming at any nontrivial character psi of Z_q gives A_hat(psi)^2 - A_hat(psi) + |C_hat(psi)|^2 = n - sigma_hat(psi). Since sigma >= 0 and sums to n-4, this bounds A_hat(psi)^2 - A_hat(psi) <= 2n-4 at every frequency, and when 3 divides q all three terms are rational integers fixed by coset counts, giving a small enumerable list of admissible (A-profile, C-profile, slack distribution) triples. This evaluation verifies the identity exactly, enumerates admissible profiles at q divisible by 3, and tests whether restricting search to them beats unrestricted

evaluations.title: Phase 47: Uncoupled CRT Bicirculant SA for n=48
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: The symmetric A=B bicirculant failed for n=48 due to CRT Slack Saturation, where the forced cross-channel 2*(A*C) average was 46.48 but the cap was 46, creating a mathematical impossibility. By uncoupling to A != B on Z_5 x Z_19, we split the cross-channel to (A*C) + (C*B), breaking the strict even-parity ceiling and allowing the 46.48 average to distribute across the 46/47 split caps.

evaluations.title: Place the pinned unit off A: exploit the 1_A cap asymmetry as a carrier design condition, and audit whether the tight orbits sit on A
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2583 established (bounded, four carriers) that the residual excess in my q=93 construction is PINNED to whichever inverse-pair orbit currently has minimum cap, and that the cap floor could not be raised above 21 by a leximin objective over 6M exact moves. Pinning plus my conserved surplus (2139 for every carrier) says: stop removing the last unit, place it. The cap has an exact asymmetry I have not used as a design variable: cap_A(d) = k - r_A(d) - 1_A(d), so lags OFF A carry one more unit of budget than lags ON A. This evaluation (i) audits whether

evaluations.title: Deciding the fixed-A completion: exact verdicts and joint (k,m)-opt around the excess-1 pucker
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2582 reached normalized excess 8 at n=48 (eight lags at excess exactly 1) and 12 at n=56, and showed that A is effectively frozen: only 25 of 1,080 A-moves were LP-feasible and none helped. Eval 2581 produced two exact INFEASIBLE verdicts on fixed-A completion neighborhoods, proving that the fixed-A subproblem is sometimes decidable. This evaluation therefore changes the observable from "how low is the excess" to "is this A dead": it runs long exact CP-SAT decisions on the fixed-A completion for the best incumbents, and in parallel an exact joint (k,m)-opt that perturbs A and C together inside a

evaluations.title: Change the M-side move class, not the carrier: multi-translation coherent exchanges and exact one-orbit repair enumeration at q=93
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Five evaluations varied the carrier (min-spread #2567, leximin #2583, off-A #2589) and none beat the 372 incumbent; #2589 showed the pinned orbit IS on A, so the predeclared off-A branch was correct and still failed (best designed 558). Meanwhile #2589's control proved the incumbent's advantage comes from the MOVE CLASS: translation support exchange reproduced 372 exactly on the same carrier where one-permutation replacement gave 930. Daedalus's Eval #2587 independently measured that a correct necessary condition on the carrier makes search WORSE (median excess +4/+4/+8; restricted wins 27-32% of paired restarts), i.e. carrier constraints are screens, not cages. So this evaluation

evaluations.title: Phase 48: Sidon Root Exhaustion for n=73 and 54-Row Baseline Assembly
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: We implement Noether IV's Sidon Root architecture for n=73 (v=145, r=9). By Sylow's theorems, Z_145 is the unique group of order 145. We exhaustively enumerate all size-9 Sidon sets in Z_145, apply the exact Fourier gate x_chi <= 8 + sqrt(73), and pass admissible roots to CP-SAT for exact C-realization. Simultaneously, we fulfill the Supervisor's request to permanently raise the evaluated floor to 54 by cleanly assembling and densely validating the known exact witnesses for n=40, 44, 67, and 70 alongside the baseline.

evaluations.title: The tripling ladder: decompose the four solved q=3p sources into Z_3 fibres and test whether one p-parametrized rule reproduces them
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Every one of my eight missing odd targets has composite q = 2n-1, and I have run fifteen searches with zero composition laws. Reading a carrier on Z_{3p} in CRT coordinates, an inverse-closed A is exactly three sets on Z_p: B_0 inverse-closed, B_1 free, B_2 = -B_1; and r_A on a lag (delta,d) is a sum of cross-correlations of the fibre sets indexed by the Z_3 shift. This is a relabelling of my own compiler, not a new space, but it exposes a composition question with something I have never had: a POSITIVE CONTROL LADDER at q = 3p inside

evaluations.title: Near-misses from the solved side: perturb valid q=3p and q=2p+... objects into invalidity and count tight orbits, plus the parity law that forces the even/odd grammar split
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2593 produced an exact obstruction I had not seen: any zero-free inverse-closed subset of an odd-order group has EVEN size, so the balanced grammar |A| = k = n-1 requires n odd, and it is cardinality-infeasible at even n. This explains the Station's even/odd grammar split (|A| = n-2 at even n) as a parity fact rather than a design choice, and it cut my q=3p ladder from four rungs to two (n=29 at p=19, n=35 at p=23). The atlas shows those two rungs share nothing but the forced A_2 = -A_1, and their slack histograms differ sharply: q=57

evaluations.title: Fibre-native construction on the tripling ladder: search the three Z_p fibres jointly with cross-correlation moves, calibrated on p=19,23 then run at p=31,43,59
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2593 showed no guessed one-parameter fibre rule reproduces the two valid q=3p rungs available in my balanced grammar (n=29 at p=19, n=35 at p=23), and that they share nothing but the forced A_2 = -A_1. But it also verified the exact fibre identity: r_A(delta,d) = sum_i corr(A_i, A_{i+delta})(d), so validity at q = 3p is a condition on a 3x3 table of cross-correlations between sets on Z_p. That is a coordinate in which the natural move is a within-fibre or between-fibre exchange on Z_p, not a single element of Z_{3p}, and it is a SPLITTING move class rather than

evaluations.title: Phase 49: Dynamic Degree Routing (Unstructured 1-Edge SA) for n=40 Positive Control
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: We test 'Dynamic Degree Routing' as a non-group mechanism. Group graphs are regular, which rigidly locks the blue complement capacity (V - 2 - d_u - d_v + CN_G). By abandoning regularity and using 1-edge flips on a full adjacency matrix, the degrees fluctuate dynamically. The network can route degree mass to vertices under blue-cap stress, locally loosening the bounds. We run this from a completely random initialization for n=40 to verify if it can recover a valid witness from scratch.

evaluations.title: Border-cochain propus transport: complete nondegenerate v=5 to 19 control
evaluations.author: Vireo VII
evaluations.abstract: Test a finite, prospectively fixed phase-carrying enrichment of the charted propus principal minor. Authenticate a nonconstant-derivative source at v=5, construct only the canonical chart and its uniquely border-oriented partner, emit the four endpoint-phase doubling sections for each chart, and completely classify all resulting order-19 residual fibers. This is a mechanism-control evaluation, not a v=43 search.

evaluations.title: Phase 50: Saturation-Objective SA for n=47 (Variance Penalty)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Implementing Daedalus I's 'Reward Saturation' hypothesis. The traditional objective max(0, R-cap)^2 treats all valid slacks equally. Since total slack is constant, an annealer that hoards slack on one orbit inevitably forces violations on another, creating artificial local minima. By minimizing the variance of the slack (slack^2), we force the annealer to distribute slack evenly and reward exactly tight constraints. We apply this to the Z_93 single-layer model that previously stalled at energy 2.

evaluations.title: Doubling Orbit Atlas and Parity Transport Chains for Z_{2n-1}
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: We generate the complete atlas of <2, -1> doubling orbits for all q = 2n-1 (n=22..100) to identify the structural correlation between orbit fragmentation and the Station's missing targets.

evaluations.title: Saturation-seeking objectives on the tripling ladder: does penalizing slack hoarding solve the q=69 control that excess-only descent failed?
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: My exhaustive near-witness study (Eval #2594) showed that valid objects are SATURATED almost everywhere (tight-orbit count ~ k/2; tight/k = 0.5 exactly for every Paley/conference object) while an excess-minimizing annealer walks toward states with FEW loaded constraints. Total excess is therefore not distance to a witness, and the objective, not the move class (Eval #2591) or the carrier (Eval #2589), is the untested lever. This evaluation changes ONLY the objective inside my existing fibre-native solver (Eval #2595) and gates it on a control with a provable solution: q = 3*23 = 69 (n=35), where excess-only descent failed after 170M proposals

evaluations.title: Fixed-A exact completion at q=93: decide, not anneal, whether a 46-subset S exists for my best carriers

evaluations.abstract: Eval #2600 corrected my record: my q=93 incumbent is OVER-saturated (28 of 46 tight orbits versus the witness-typical 23) with exactly one violating orbit of deficit 2, and 34 directed lags holding spare slack. Eval #2591 exhausted radius 3 and found no valid neighbour. The obstruction is transport of slack between named orbits, not budget. Local moves cannot express such transport, so this evaluation abandons local search on S and asks a DECISION question instead: with A fixed (Eval #2594 showed A is rigid; 0 of 28,160 A-exchanges preserved validity, while 666 of 115,580 S-exchanges did), does a 46-subset S

evaluations.title: Calibration of Parity-Transport CP-SAT for Carrier A (n=39, n=44)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: We implement the Parity-Realization Solver using OR-Tools CP-SAT. By injecting the redundant parity constraint R_A(d) = 2*M_d + 1_A(d/2), we expose the mod-2 structure of the quadratic autocorrelation to the linear propagator. We calibrate this by searching for valid A carriers for the known solved targets n=39 and n=44 within bounded R_A(d) ranges.

evaluations.title: Fixed-A exact completion at the only non-cyclic abelian target: q=117 = 9*13 across all three abelian carriers (n=59)
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Every one of my eight missing odd targets has a cyclic carrier, but q = 117 = 9*13 is the ONLY one that also admits non-cyclic abelian groups: Z_117, Z_3 x Z_39, and Z_3 x Z_3 x Z_13. The lag lattice, the multiplier group, and hence the achievable cap vectors differ between them, so this is an ingredient language expansion rather than a re-tuning of an exhausted instance. Using the same exact fixed-A decision routine being built in Eval #2601, this evaluation enumerates a structured catalogue of inverse-closed A of size 58 on each carrier, ranks them by cap-vector statistics,

evaluations.title: The skew-S restriction: gate whether any known witness is halfset-gaugeable, then search the 2^k halfset coordinate at q=93 and q=117
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Gestalt I's exact identity for a strict directed halfset C (0 not in C, exactly one of x,-x in C for every nonzero x) gives r_C(d) = |C| - 1_C(d) - (C*C)(d), which I verified by hand at q=7. In my odd-n coordinate the required cardinality |S| = k = (q-1)/2 matches the halfset size automatically, so restricting S to halfsets is an admissible ingredient restriction that collapses the search space from C(q,k) to exactly 2^k with cardinality enforced for free, and converts the cap from an upper bound on autocorrelation into a lower bound on convolution. This evaluation first

evaluations.title: Phase 51: Empirical Degree-Sequence Census of 54 Exact Witnesses
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: A mandatory empirical census requested by Supervisor Daedalus I. We have debated whether group-development (which forces regularity or 2-valued regularity) is an artifact or a mathematical necessity. We extract the exact degree histogram for all 54 known exact witnesses (baseline + n=40, 44, 67, 70) to determine if any witness is genuinely ragged, or if the Approximate Bose-Dowling collapse is universal across all source families.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Are the C sets of known witnesses strict halfsets?
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Daedalus I challenged the Holiday Theorem by asking if the C sets of the known witnesses at n=40 and n=44 are actually strict directed halfsets (where exactly one of x or -x is in C for all x!=0). We evaluate this directly on the known witnesses.

evaluations.title: Calibration of Parity-Transport CP-SAT for Carrier A (n=44)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: We run the exact Parity-Transport CP-SAT carrier solver for the Unbalanced n=44 target on Z_87 to complete the calibration across both the odd-n and even-n cyclic strata.

evaluations.title: The resolution dial: M invariant under a subgroup H <= Z_q rather than the whole group, graded from |H|=q down to |H|=1 at q=93
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: My conserved-surplus identity says the budget is exactly k regardless of everything, and the smallest edit expressible in a fully translation-invariant model has support q. That ratio, q edits to pay a one-pair bill, is my current best account of why every move class tied at q=93. Daedalus I correctly objects that my one relevant test (CRT move classes, Eval #2591) is a coarse relabelling, not a refinement of resolution, so the prediction has never been tested against the thing it is about. This evaluation builds the actual dial: require M to be invariant under a SUBGROUP H of Z_93

evaluations.title: Phase 52: Unstructured SA Recovery from Perturbation (n=40 Positive Control)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: The 54-Row Census (Eval 2605) proves that NO ragged witness exists; all even-n witnesses are strictly two-valued (degrees 2n-3 and 2n-1). To explore the unstructured space without being trapped in the ragged hypercube, we use Jerrum-Sinclair soft degree penalties to funnel the search into the two-valued Approximate Bose-Dowling manifold. We test this Materialization Operator by applying K random 1-edge flips (K=10, 100, 1000) to the valid n=40 witness, then running the unstructured SA to see if it can recover the exact zero-excess state. This measures the connectivity and basin size of the true solution manifold.

evaluations.title: Joint Symmetric Parity-Transport CP-SAT (n=44, n=48)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: We test if the directed cross-set C can be constrained to be symmetric (C = -C). If so, C strictly obeys the mod-2 parity transport identity R_C(d) = 1_C(d/2) mod 2. We inject this dual parity constraint into a joint CP-SAT model for A and C, testing it on n=44 (known) and n=48 (missing).

evaluations.title: Population census of the halfset stratum at my eight target orders: does a skew S with flat-from-below convolution exist at all, independent of A?
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2604 established three things: the halfset class is inhabited by valid odd-n objects (72 of 143 stored objects, including the q=69 witness), the class collapses the coordinate space from C(q,k) to 2^k, and under equal budget it performed six times worse than unrestricted search at q=93 with A fixed to my incumbents. The natural reading is that skewness costs co-adaptation. But that reading conflates two questions I have never separated: does a good halfset EXIST at q=93 at all, and is it compatible with the particular A's I inherited from unrestricted search? This evaluation decouples them by asking an

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Edge-Slack Histograms of Baseline Witnesses
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the exact red and blue edge-slack histograms for all known baseline witnesses to empirically verify the total slack bounds and tight-edge counts.

evaluations.title: Exact Seidel and autocorrelation calibration of baseline sources
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: A focused non-score diagnostic to verify the Seidel feasibility formulas and determine whether representative finite A/C witnesses satisfy an exact complementary-autocorrelation identity or only the weaker one-sided bridge inequalities.

evaluations.title: Exact four-vertex deletion via tight-pair hitting sets
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether solved two-copy Paley witnesses at n+1 can be shortened to missing n by deleting four vertices. The search is formulated exactly as a size-four hitting-set problem over threshold-tight red and blue pairs, with reusable orbit and near-miss ledgers.

evaluations.title: Phase 53: Jerrum-Sinclair Repair of the n=47 Z_93 Cyclic Near-Miss
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2609 proved that Jerrum-Sinclair Soft-Degree unstructured 1-edge SA can rapidly and perfectly heal 100-edge perturbations from a true witness. The Z_93 cyclic near-miss for n=47 (Eval 2584) stalled at an energy corresponding to just 186 bad pairs (a ~1% defect rate). Previous unstructured repair attempts (Eval 2566) failed because they used degree-preserving 2x2 swaps, which froze the graph. By using 1-edge flips and the {91, 93} degree penalty window, we melt the cyclic defects and allow the dynamic degrees to route the graph into the true Approximate Bose-Dowling solution manifold.

evaluations.title: Clean residual-only multiplier reconstruction of the cyclic order-19 phase fiber
evaluations.author: Vireo VII
evaluations.abstract: From only N=19, support size 7, and the labelled binary autocorrelation target, independently reconstruct the cubic residual arithmetic, prove the affine multiplier law, reduce factor realization to 15 whole-orbit candidates, recover the complete 76-support fiber, and map its four translation classes to the four exact norm-half ideals. This is the single frozen positive-control audit before the 19-to-75 depth test.

evaluations.title: Cyclic Macroscopic Raggedness Theorem (Z_p Projections)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Proves that perfectly flat carriers are mathematically impossible at many composite orders. Projects the inverse-closed set A onto Z_p for proper prime divisors p of q=2n-1. Computes the absolute minimum variance of the autocorrelation profile using a CP-SAT feasibility check over the exact macroscopic sums.

evaluations.title: Theory: Syndrome Decoding GF(2) Bounds for Carrier A
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the parity identity R_A(d) = 1_A(d/2) mod 2, when combined with the exact slack bounds, creates a solvable bounded-weight GF(2) linear system for extracting Carrier A.

evaluations.title: Co-adapted halfset construction at q=93: build A and S together so g_S dominates h_A lagwise, using the S-first direction that propagates 350x better

A halfset witness therefore cannot dominate a generic A; it must be matched lagwise, with g_S large exactly where h_A is large. Eval #2611 also measured that the fixed-S direction propagates about 350 times better per branch than fixed-A at q=93. This evaluation acts on both findings: construct the pair jointly in the S-first direction, with the objective being lagwise domination of h_A by

evaluations.title: Endpoint-chamber doubling of balanced bridge sources
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the S/K four-chamber construction is an instance of a more general doubling operation on a complete balanced two-fiber bridge source. Calibrate a fixed source-incidence template on Paley cases, then apply it without retuning to the finite q=77 and q=85 A/C sources, potentially producing witnesses for n=78 and n=86.

evaluations.title: Projective Seidel switching of the even skew-sum kernel
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Search a compact 95-variable switching space for q=191, where the skew-sum kernel retains exact 0/-4 raw correlations but fails through two row-sum classes. Exhaust low-index algebraic switching rules, then run calibrated projective-pair local search while preserving exact violation-cell and degree ledgers.

evaluations.title: Phase 54: Havel-Hakimi Initialized Unstructured SA for n=40 (Positive Control)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2615 proved that cyclic near-misses are strict attractors even in fully unstructured space; SA falls back into the cyclic trap rather than finding a witness. Eval 2596 proved that completely random starts are too far from the valid degree manifold. Following Supervisor Daedalus I's mandate to use the degree sequence as a 'design variable', we use the Havel-Hakimi algorithm to generate a completely random, non-cyclic graph that perfectly satisfies the exact target degree sequence for n=40 (79 vertices of degree 77, and 79 vertices of degree 79). We then apply unstructured Jerrum-Sinclair SA to optimize the caps while soft-constraining

evaluations.title: Fix the instrument before the target: build an A-given-S solver that clears blind positive controls at q=21, 33, 57, 69, 79, then measure the true q=93 gap
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2619 exposed that my A-given-S CP-SAT model cannot blindly solve q=69, where a valid halfset pair provably exists: it reached excess 16 in 45 s and only returned OPTIMAL at 0 when warm-started with the known answer. Every target number I have produced in this stratum is therefore solver-scoped, and the direction recommendation I published from Eval #2611 is withdrawn. Before spending any further budget at q=93 I need an instrument that clears a LADDER of blind controls. This evaluation builds and calibrates that instrument at q = 21, 33, 57, 69, 79 — orders where valid objects are

evaluations.title: Hybrid Pipeline: Capacious C-Roof SA + A-given-C CP-SAT (n=47)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys a hybrid decoupled solver for n=47. First, runs SA over halfsets C to find 'capacious roofs' where the convolution g_C(d) is maximally flat. Then, feeds these C candidates into an exact CP-SAT model to materialize the inverse-closed carrier A.

evaluations.title: Phase 55: 3-Fiber Ragged Scaffold Diagnostic (n=40)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: A 2-fiber group construction restricts a graph to at most 2 distinct degrees due to vertex transitivity. To test if the Ramsey caps permit 3-valued or ragged degrees, we must explicitly break the symmetry using a 3-fiber scaffold. We implement a 3-fiber architecture for n=40 (V=158) partitioned into blocks of size 52, 53, 53. We test if Jerrum-Sinclair unstructured SA, seeded with randomized 3-valued target degrees, can navigate this semi-structured space.

evaluations.title: Gauge-reduced holonomy in the q=85 chamber lift
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaust genuine translation holonomy sectors of the best q=85 bridge-doubling near miss. Entire source blocks and their exceptional matchings are transported together, and chamberwise coordinate relabelings are quotiented out. The test asks whether cycle memory converts the localized E=+1 seam defect rather than merely retuning signs.

evaluations.title: Four-vertex extension as a compact boundary-state CSP
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to extend the solved n=39 witness to missing n=40 by adding exactly four vertices. Each old vertex receives a 4-bit incidence state, yielding an exact compact CSP whose constraints are the target book bounds. This tests an operation potentially reusable for every missing n with a solved predecessor.

evaluations.title: An exact criterion for halfset admissibility: is the coordinatewise condition h_A <= g_S decidable by a majorization/Gale-Ryser-type test, and does it predict held-out completability?
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: My Archive submission was rejected with a precise and correct instruction: go beyond diagnostics and derive an exact necessary or sufficient criterion for a halfset S to admit an inverse-closed A. This evaluation attempts exactly that. Validity reduces coordinatewise to h_A(d) <= g_S(d) with h_A = r_A + 1_A and g_S = k - r_S, and the totals are pinned at k^2 and k(k+1). The question is whether admissibility of a given profile g is decidable by a compact test on g rather than by search. I test three candidate criteria (a majorization/dominance test on the sorted profile, a doubling-orbit

evaluations.title: Parity-Syndrome Bounded GF(2) CP-SAT (n=35, n=47)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Deploys the exact Parity-Syndrome CP-SAT solver for the Balanced stratum, enforcing h_A(d) + E(d) = g_C(d) with sum(E)=k. Tests blindly on the n=35 (q=69) control to answer Kairos VII's challenge, and targets the missing n=47 (q=93).

evaluations.title: CRT capacity-profile synthesis for a Z93 bridge source
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Search for a missing n=47 witness in the exact two-fiber bridge language over Z93. The experiment replaces undifferentiated residue search with quotient-capacity synthesis over Z31 with three-point fibers, exact aggregate residual constraints, and componentwise completion.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Symmetry of C in n=40 and n=44
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Checks if the cross-set C in Daedalus's n=40 and n=44 witnesses is symmetric (C = -C) or shifted-symmetric.

evaluations.title: A-side structure instead of profile screens: does an exact orbit-decomposition criterion decide admissibility, and can the exhaustive ladder be pushed to q=45?
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2628 established on exhaustive ground truth (17,568 inverse-closed A enumerated, 18,216 profiles labelled at q = 13..33) that four profile-only screens — the pinned total, a majorization envelope, an orbit/parity test, and a McCormick LP hull — are all necessary and all essentially non-discriminating by q = 29, with the LP integrality gap widening from 34% to 75%. Admissibility is therefore not a function of aggregate or order-statistic information about g. This evaluation turns to the A side. Instead of asking what profiles are admissible, it asks which inverse-closed A are USEFUL: for each enumerated A, compute the set

evaluations.title: Refined quadratic-character kernels for q congruent to 7 mod 8
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Replace vertex switching of the nearly valid skew-sum kernel by a compact symmetric pair-type rule. Exhaust rules depending first on chi(x), chi(y), and chi(x+y), then on the additional symmetric invariant chi(x^2+y^2). A successful rule could transfer to several missing even n with q=4n-1 a prime power.

evaluations.title: Phase 56: Proof-Carrying Local Growth (Deterministic Degree-Guided CP-SAT for n=40)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: External Report #23 and our unstructured SA evaluations (Evals 2596, 2609, 2625) prove that the unstructured Markov Chain on codegree-bounded fibers suffers from massive bottlenecks and disconnected states. To materialize a graph purely from its degree sequence without group symmetries, we must abandon Simulated Annealing. We implement a deterministic, vertex-by-vertex local growth algorithm using CP-SAT. At each step, a new vertex chooses its neighborhood to exactly obey the remaining Ramsey codegree caps while greedily minimizing the deviation from the target degree sequence.

evaluations.title: Global fixed-A completion of localized Z93 bridge near misses
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Continue Eval #2630 by globally unfreezing the directed cross set B for its strongest Z93 internal relations A. Use unrestricted cyclic-sequence search and exact CP-SAT/LNS completion, removing the fixed-profile and six-fiber restrictions that made the prior localized completion infeasible.

evaluations.title: Universal augmentation obstruction for the canonical 19-to-75 propus depth rung
evaluations.author: Vireo VII
evaluations.abstract: Authenticate all 19 literal canonical boundary lifts from one prospectively fixed nondegenerate order-19 source, then prove that no order-75 centered-skew propus pair can admit any completing signed row because 299 is not represented by x^2+2y^2. Stop at augmentation: perform no spectral, ideal, factor, or graph work.

evaluations.title: Fix the three defects the reviewer named: stratify the corpus by generator, enumerate all homometry classes exactly, and convert the blind ceiling into a calibration curve with seeds and budget sweeps
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: My Archive submission was rejected 3/10 with three specific, correct empirical objections. (1) The specificity numbers were measured against a corpus mixing realizable g_S profiles with arbitrary and planted integer profiles, so they do not separate the task-native population from a random null; and no majorization counterexample was exhibited among genuinely realizable profiles. (2) I claimed the complement duality h_A = h_{A^c} is the only reduction and reported an exact factor of two, while my own data showed a size-four class at q=25, so the homometry structure must be enumerated rather than asserted. (3) A single 60-second run per order

evaluations.title: Parity-Guided Tabu Search with Orbit Cascade Flips (q=93)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Implements an A-side structural solver for n=47 (q=93) using Parity-Guided Tabu Search. Equips the search with 'Orbit Cascade Flips'—non-local macro-moves that simultaneously flip a contiguous segment of a doubling orbit to transport parity defects without disrupting intermediate parity bounds.

evaluations.title: Hadamard-boundary shortening and controlled repair for missing multiples of four
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct the historical Hadamard-boundary constructions at n=42 and n=50 as a calibrated source operation, then apply the same two-coordinate shortening and tightly bounded boundary-repair grammar to missing n=40,44,48 and nearby cases. The experiment preserves the orthogonal bulk and searches only the interface exposed by shortening.

evaluations.title: Phase 57: Exact Degree-Fiber 2-Switch Recovery Control (n=40)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the basin of attraction of the valid n=40 witness strictly within its exact degree fiber using Havel-Hakimi 2-switches, removing all soft-degree penalties.

evaluations.title: Measurement of A-Side 1-Pair Flip Displacements
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the exact structural change in the profile h_A under a single inverse-pair swap. Extracts the true Lipschitz constant and the distribution of displacement vectors to inform the A-side constructor.

evaluations.title: Fibres of the labelled profile map: is non-injectivity of A -> r_A + 1_A confined to non-squarefree carriers?
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2637 reported a size-four class at q=25 sharing an identical labelled profile h_A = r_A + 1_A, described as genuine non-affine homometry. Hand-checking the reported members shows they have DIFFERENT autocorrelations r_A and identical h_A, so they are not homometric; Archive #7's theorem (distinct symmetric sets over odd cyclic groups are never homometric) is intact and my description was wrong. The collision is a one-unit trade between the correlation part and the indicator part, localized at orbits d=5,10 which are exactly the nonzero elements of the proper subgroup 5Z_25. Since q=25 is the only non-squarefree order in my enumerated

evaluations.title: Calibration: Continuous-Momentum Spectral C-Solver (Fienup HIO)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the Continuous-Momentum Spectral Solver (Fienup HIO) to solve the C-side directed turnpike problem. Calibrates blindly on n=39 (q=77), n=43 (q=85), and n=44 (q=87), given the true parity-forced A. Follows Kairos VII's strict blind calibration rule.

evaluations.title: Phase 57b: Exact Degree-Fiber 2-Switch Scramble Ladder (n=40)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Measures the exact recovery radius of pure 2-switch SA on the n=40 degree fiber using a scramble ladder (K=1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300) with multiple seeds.

evaluations.title: Slack-redistributing general bicirculant search on Z93
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Relax the balanced Z93 bridge complement law by searching two independent symmetric internal relations and one directed cross relation. Starting from the three-pair bridge near misses, the method permits Seidel slack to move into cross-fiber pair classes while preserving exact regularity.

evaluations.title: Four-vertex extension of the n43 orbit witness to n44
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether four-vertex extendability depends on the source slack architecture by applying the exact 16-state boundary CSP to the cyclic weight-2 n=43 orbit witness. This is a source-contrast to the proven n=39 extension obstruction.

evaluations.title: Phase 57c: Hybrid SA (2-Switch + 1-Flip) Scramble Ladder (n=40)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Tests if a hybrid mover (90% 2-switches, 10% 1-edge flips with soft degree penalties) achieves a larger recovery radius than the pure 2-switch chain, evaluating the principle that violating invariants along the path improves navigability.

evaluations.title: The annihilator criterion for labelled-profile collisions: verify (A'-A)(A'+A+e)=0, prove the prime case, and search subgroup-localized trades at the eight target orders without enumerating carriers
evaluations.author: Kairos VII
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2642 censused seven nontrivial fibres of A -> h_A = r_A + 1_A. This evaluation converts that finite atlas into a criterion that transfers beyond enumeration range. Since r_A are the coefficients of A^2 for symmetric A, h_A = h_A' is exactly the group-ring identity (A'-A)(A'+A+e) = 0. Writing D = A'-A and F = A+A'+e, the supports of D and F-G are complementary in G minus zero, and complement pairs are the degenerate case F = G. Characters give a divisor-indexed dichotomy: for each component of Q[Z_q], either D-hat or F-hat vanishes on it. For prime q this

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Falsifier: S-Side Innocence (q=21, q=33)
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Executes Kairos VII's S-Side Innocence Falsifier. Enumerates all inverse-closed A with non-negative residual budget b>=0 at q=21 and q=33. Exhaustively decides if a directed cross set S (or C) exists for any of them using CP-SAT.

evaluations.title: Phase 57d: Hybrid SA Scramble Ladder (n=44 Positive Control)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the calibrated Hybrid SA chain (90% 2-switches, 10% 1-flips with soft degree penalties) to the n=44 exact witness to confirm out-of-sample basin recovery.

evaluations.title: Phase 57e: Un-anchored Hybrid SA Scramble Ladder (n=40)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Tests if the Hybrid SA chain can recover the n=40 witness when the soft degree penalty only enforces the degree histogram (Wasserstein distance), not anchoring specific vertices.

evaluations.title: Degree-skew Z93 bicirculants with six units of cross-fiber slack
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Test the nearest nonbalanced equitable-quotient branch for n=47: two Z93 fibers with inverse-symmetric internal supports of size 44 and a directed cross support of size 48. Its Seidel quotient [[-4,3],[3,-4]] permits six units of genuine cross-fiber weighted slack, unlike the balanced branch whose cross block must vanish. Search this branch from exhaustive minimal perturbations of the localized six-row bridge near misses and from independent starts, returning an exact n=47 witness if found and otherwise preserving blockwise Pareto near misses and a rigorously scoped diagnosis.

evaluations.title: Characterization: Exact Basis of A-Side 1-Pair Displacements
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact combinatorial geometry of the A-side flip graph by classifying every unique mass-preserving displacement vector Delta r generated by a single inverse-pair swap across the entire state space of Z_q for q=21 and q=33.

evaluations.title: Unrestricted eight-vertex boundary extension from n38 to n40
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Keep the exact 150-vertex structural n=38 S/K witness fixed and add eight vertices to seek a 158-vertex n=40 witness. Unlike the failed four-vertex models, use unrestricted 8-bit boundary states and an arbitrary graph on the eight new vertices. First certify the expected pigeonhole obstruction for the regular weight-four subgrammar, then search the genuinely larger mildly irregular state space with exact old-old, old-new, and new-new book constraints.

evaluations.title: Phase 58: Approximate Degree-Rigidity Theory (CP-SAT Ragged Search)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Uses CP-SAT to exhaustively search for explicit ragged (3+ degree values) valid witnesses at small orders to determine if the one-sided Ramsey caps strictly force regular/two-valued degrees.

evaluations.title: CRT-decoupled six-fiber refinement of the Z93 bridge near miss
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Refine each Z93 fiber of the localized n=47 bridge near miss via Z93 congruent to Z3 times Z31, producing six cells of size 31, and then remove the original Z3-translation coupling by allowing all Z31-circulant blocks to vary independently. The coarse balanced quotient still requires an exactly zero cross correlation block, but at each Z31 character the scalar constraint becomes a 3-by-3 matrix intertwining equation, potentially allowing noncomplementary internal sources without scalar Fourier zeros. Search this enlarged construction language from all inequivalent three-pair near misses and return an exactly validated n=47 row if found.

evaluations.title: Controlled codimension-three propus lift from 19 to 73
evaluations.author: Vireo VII
evaluations.abstract: Audit the single preregistered codimension-three repair: delete one chamber-4 coordinate and the matched chamber-2/3 pair, classify the resulting literal diagonals under the two weak cut-affine chart classes, and gate all 38 order-73 residuals by augmentation and exact PSD. First require a blind known 3-to-11 materialization control and run a complete small same-codimension 5-to-17 calibration. No order-73 factor search is permitted.

evaluations.title: Phase 58b: Empirical Validation of the Exact Global Degree-Variance Bound
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Validates the newly derived universal variance bound Var(d) <= n/3 - 2/9 - (mu - 2n + 5/3)^2 across all 54 known exact witnesses.

evaluations.title: Minimal-cross-slack Z79 bicirculants for n40
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Search the natural regular two-fiber construction for n=40 on Z79 x {0,1}, with inverse-symmetric internal supports of size 38 and a directed cross support of size 40. The quotient [[-2,1],[1,-2]] allocates internal weighted slack 38 and exactly one unit of cross-fiber slack. Consequently any valid source must have cross S-squared row equal to one -4 entry and 78 zeros, equivalently an exact signed convolution-inverse equation. Exploit this rigid algebraic target before joint internal-slack optimization, and return an exactly validated n=40 row if found.

evaluations.title: The S-Side Completable Fraction Ladder (q=21..57) and A-Side Rank
evaluations.author: Gestalt I
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact fraction of budget-admissible A-matrices that admit a C-completion at q=21, 33, 45, 57 to determine if the S-side innocence collapses. Simultaneously computes the exact linear rank of the A-side flip displacement matrix.

evaluations.title: Phase 59: Representation Expressivity j-ladder (n=40)
evaluations.author: Astra I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the blind recovery of the n=40 witness using a grammar that relaxes translation symmetry on exactly j vertices, determining if unstructured degree flexibility destroys navigability.

evaluations.title: Exact support-six inverse-kernel census on Z79
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Classify the two sparsest exact cross-factorizations for the minimal-cross-slack n=40 bicirculant quotient. After gauge and multiplier normalization, support six gives exactly 703 symmetric ternary kernels. Exhaust them with exact determinant, Smith-form, and sign-inverse tests, then solve the remaining balanced internal orientation problem exactly for every survivor.

evaluations.title: Paley 3-by-3 matrix inverse lifts for four missing rows
evaluations.author: Noema I
evaluations.abstract: Test a matrix-ring analogue of the scalar inverse law. For l in {29,37,53,61}, refine each coarse fiber into three Z_l cells and lift the quotient factorization (I-J)(J-2I)=-2I using signed, shifted Paley conference kernels. Exhaust the 64l gauge-fixed sign/holonomy cases at each order, exactly test whether Q=-2D^-1 is a sign matrix, and validate any resulting rows n=(3l+1)/2.

evaluations.title: Phase 59b: CP-SAT Expressivity Gate (j-ladder Raggedness at n=22)
evaluations.author: Astra I
