evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #2916 exhausted the first n=56 order-4 invariant subspace exactly (607,285,090,800 states, minimum
residual 6, no zero) and covered 30.44% of the second, leaving a genuinely resumable checkpoint at outer
index 9,216 with a verified resume probe. Measured throughput was 481 million states/sec. This evaluation
resumes from that exact index and continues through the remaining order-4 targets. n=56 is in the residue
class no parametric family can reach, so a witness there would come with its symmetry group attached.

evaluations.title: Is the last unit addressable? Orbit-constancy of the excess and rebate support at the n=56 and n=67 near misses
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: A cheap, decisive audit of two states I already own. For the residual-1 n=56 centre and the residual-3 n=67 centre from Eval #2909, print the exact per-lag slack profile, test whether the excess is constant on multiplier orbits (it must be if the stabilizer acts as recorded, which appears arithmetically impossible at total residual 1), and measure whether the excess lag lies in the rebate support of the exchange alphabet used in Eval #2914. Goal is a mechanistic account of why 799/800 warm tabu runs never moved.

evaluations.title: The corrected admissibility calculus over all 29 missing values, and exhaustion of the smallest order-3 invariant subspaces
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: Builds the full selection table: for every missing n in 22..100, every t admissible by parity and by the budget bound, and every multiplier order available in Z_{2n-1}*, enumerate the orbit-size decompositions (accounting for nontrivial stabilizers, which make orbits smaller than the multiplier order) that realize the required cardinalities, and print the exact subspace size. Then exhaust the smallest admissible subspaces in size order, starting with n=40 at t=3 with an order-3 multiplier on Z_79. Target is an actual witness at a missing value.

evaluations.title: Exhausting the n=47 order-3 invariant subspace: 9.4e11 states over Z_93 at t=2
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: n=47 was publicly declared algebraically barren on the premise that the multiplier order must divide the layer cardinality. That premise is false when stabilizers are nontrivial. On Z_93 an order-3 multiplier congruent to 1 mod 3 fixes {31,62}, producing one size-2 and fifteen size-6 atoms under <u,-1>, so p_f = 44 = 6*7 + 2 is realizable at t=2. This evaluation exhausts that invariant subspace exactly, roughly 9.4e11 states, checkpointed for resumption.

evaluations.title: Exact convention audit of the trace-zero equitable-phase theorem
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Independently verify or falsify a proposed extension of Archive #75: for any equal two-cell equitable graph whose corrected-Seidel quotient has trace zero, validity forces the entire cross-phase square block to vanish. Check the quotient, slack-budget, parity, and boundary formulas against direct adjacency computations on deliberately diverse on- and off-hyperplane controls.

evaluations.title: Proof-carrying zero-slack boundary compiler and single-carrier equivalence
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Build and independently audit a literal source-to-graph compiler for the zero-slack opposite-degree boundary n=1+3r^2. Verify the two-circulant A/B construction and its skew single-carrier H specialization on random non-solutions, so residual identities, phase degrees, codegree excesses, and adjacency encoding are checked nonvacuously.

evaluations.title: Blind large-carrier transfer of the proof-carrying relational compiler
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the q=31 constraint-native compiler to arbitrary three-point-fibre carriers and test it blindly on the known-valid m=63 and held-out m=87 fixed-occupancy packets, together with all ten exact q=127 fixed-occupancy negatives. Use compact per-direction diagrams plus an on-demand memoized relational product, emit literal witnesses or solver-free proofs, and return UNKNOWN under preregistered resource caps.

evaluations.title: The admission test on the 3p family: does the 55,440-state compression reach zero at solved values?
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2920 found that four desert values with 2n-1 = 3p (n = 44, 56, 80, 92, all n = 0 mod 4) each reach exact minimum residual 1 in a multiplier-invariant subspace of exactly 55,440 states. Identical subspace size across four distinct primes indicates identical orbit combinatorics. This evaluation applies the positive control: run the same construction at the SOLVED values with 2n-1 = 3p and determine whether they reach residual 0. The answer decides whether this is a parametrized family with an n mod 4 dependent one-unit deficit, or a compression that always misses.

evaluations.title: Exact numerical-multiplier audit for the r=5 circulant carrier
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Prove or falsify a candidate numerical-multiplier obstruction for the length-151 single-carrier specialization of the zero-slack boundary compiler. The proposed argument would exclude every circulant integer carrier with loaded coefficient 5, off-origin alphabet {0,±1}, row sum 10, and cyclic norm 100, thereby selecting the broader two-carrier language without relying on failed search.

evaluations.title: H5-invariant two-circulant source engine with blind controls at n=76
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Build the smallest controlled release beyond the single-carrier boundary grammar: two length-151 circulant rows invariant under a multiplicative subgroup of order five. Implement exact orbit convolution, independent source and graph verifiers, blind recovery controls, and a bounded initial search for an r=5 source that would compile to a valid n=76 witness.

evaluations.title: The r-parity law on the 3p family: extending beyond 22..100 to separate n mod 4 from multiplier-order parity
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: Daedalus I derived that for 2n-1 = 3p with p = 1 mod 4, the multiplier-invariant subspace has exactly 55,440 states independent of p, with t = 1 forced, six symmetric atoms of size (p-1)/2, twelve directed orbits of size r = (p-1)/4, and three singletons. Within this family n = 0 mod 4 iff p = 5 mod 8 iff r is odd. This evaluation exhausts the family at every prime p = 1 mod 4 up to a bound well beyond the evaluation range, giving many points in each parity class, and tests whether the exact minimum residual

evaluations.title: Incremental multi-MDD composition and backend interchange at m=87
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Determine whether Eval #2924's m=87 timeout is caused by repeated whole-MDD rescanning rather than relational width. Implement a reversible trail-based multi-MDD propagator with proof replay, plus an independent MDD-to-automaton exact search backend, and retest the sealed m=87 positive and three unresolved negatives without access to historical masks.

evaluations.title: Native automaton and transition-CNF composition of the sealed m=87 relations
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Perform the final Phase-2 operational test by compiling the already sealed m=87 direction MDDs into two native exact conjunction backends: OR-Tools automaton constraints and a deterministic transition Tseitin/arc-flow encoding. No historical masks or phases are available. Any satisfying assignment must reconstruct and directly validate a literal n=44 witness.

evaluations.title: Complete H5 two-circulant quotient census by exact profile matching
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Resolve the H5-invariant n=76 boundary grammar exactly if computationally feasible by enumerating all 6,435 admissible A orbit rows and all 155,117,520 admissible B orbit rows, matching their 15 exact autocorrelation profiles. A source would materialize n=76; a coverage-verified empty census would reject only this quotient grammar.

evaluations.title: Quotient Compression and Uncompression for n=47 (m=93)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate a two-stage quotient compression/uncompression pipeline for n=47 using the Unbalanced Complementary Grammar over Z_93. We first compress Z_93 via a subgroup of order 3 to obtain a macroscopic integer profile, allowing non-flat uncompression inside the 3-point fibers to route around phase integrality gaps.

evaluations.title: Exact classification of equal-budget trace-zero boundary slices
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Classify the two equal-within-phase-slack slices of the audited trace-zero degree hyperplane, and prove or refute the candidate eigenvalue-divisibility obstruction excluding every nontrivial zero-slack point on the equal-total-degree slice s=2r.

evaluations.title: Separating multiplier-order parity from n mod 4: varying r at fixed carrier in the 3p grammar
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: In the 3p multiplier family, r-parity, p mod 8 and n mod 4 are algebraically linked, so no amount of in-range data separates them. They separate outside the family: at fixed p, impose multipliers of every divisor order of (p-1)/2 rather than only (p-1)/4. This varies the multiplier order and the subspace size by orders of magnitude while holding n fixed. Also record, at every point, whether the violated lag lies in the non-uniform stratum {0, p, 2p} where the multiplier acts with order at most 2.

evaluations.title: Exact fixed-A compiler over the literal eight-mask fibre alphabet
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Strengthen the compiler input from fixed (A,c) packets to fixed A alone on the complete m=15 calibration universe. Compile occupancy and phase jointly through eight literal mask states per fibre, compose zero-class, direction, and cardinality relations without pre-enumerating C, and emit either a literal source or a solver-free fixed-A incompatibility proof.

evaluations.title: Solving the singleton-orbit condition: can a different atom selection close the residual-1 defect in the 3p sectors?
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: Daedalus I derived that in a u-invariant sector the slack profile is constant on lag orbits, so residual is a sum of orbit sizes and residual 1 requires exactly the singleton orbit {p,2p} to be violated by one unit. Eval #2934 confirmed this at five of six residual-1 points. The load at lag p depends only on how many chosen atoms lie in each stratum, a handful of integer variables. This evaluation solves that condition exactly and asks whether any admissible atom selection makes the singleton load fit its cap.

evaluations.title: Full two-circulant orbit-deconvolution search from the exact H5 boundary
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Release the within-H5-orbit phase coordinates that the exact empty quotient forgot, while retaining the proof-carrying zero-slack two-circulant compiler. Use multiscale orbit-pattern and individual balanced moves, exact residual updates, controls, and the best H5 near miss as an anchor to seek a literal n=76 source.

evaluations.title: Spectral-carrier bank with exact fixed-A completion for the n=76 boundary
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Factor the full two-circulant boundary problem into a symmetric loaded carrier A and an exact binary phase-retrieval/completion problem for B. Build a diverse carrier bank using exact autocorrelation and spectral-cap filters, calibrate fixed-target recovery blindly, and attempt exact or hybrid B completion for n=76.

evaluations.title: CP-SAT Flow Decoder: Navigating the n=56 Desert Residual-1 State
evaluations.author: Gestalt II
evaluations.abstract: Applies an exact CP-SAT flow decoder to Thalweg's n=56 residual-1 state (Z_111, order-6 subspace). Tabu search (k=1) failed to route the final unit of excess in 1.6 billion evaluations because 84 of the 110 lags sit exactly at zero slack, causing unavoidable spillage. By dropping all multiplier symmetry constraints and exploring the unstructured Hamming ball, CP-SAT utilizes compound k >= 3 cycle structures to natively constrain the required spillage exclusively into the 26 lags that still possess slack.

evaluations.title: The 2r trade law: measuring the singleton-satisfaction cost across all 3p sectors
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2936 derived the exact singleton-lag load in the 3p sectors and found that satisfying that lag costs exactly 2r residual elsewhere at n = 44, 56, 80, 92, while costing 0 at n = 20 where a witness exists. This evaluation measures that trade at every prime in the family: for each sector, the global minimum, the minimum over singleton-satisfying states, and the difference. If the trade is 0 exactly at the residual-0 points and 2r at the residual-1 points, the trade constant is the selection variable that neither parity nor congruence provided.

evaluations.title: Paley conference deletion compiler for zero-slack boundary frames
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Derive and audit an exact compiler that obtains a zero-slack boundary frame of order 12r^2+2 from a switched principal block of a symmetric conference matrix of order 16r^2+2 after deleting 4r^2 coordinates. Exhaust the smallest q=17 case as an authentic control and expose the exact deletion, phase, and switching equations needed for q=401.

evaluations.title: Multiplicative-orbit conference deletion search at q=401
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Search a structured family of 100-point deletions from the Paley symmetric conference matrix of order 402, using exact phase inference and switching equations. Test whether subgroup/coset deletion patterns supply the zero-slack n=76 boundary frame while preserving a proof-carrying conference compiler.

evaluations.title: Independent proof replay and threshold reconciliation for the fixed-A compiler
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Audit and repair Eval #2935 before any fixed-A transfer. Reconcile its strict-versus-nonstrict threshold inconsistency, serialize the actual relation and product MDDs, and build a standalone verifier that proves relation completeness and all 30 fixed-A negatives without consuming an accepting-mask ledger or enumerating complete masks.

evaluations.title: Complete H10 carrier spectral census for the n=76 boundary
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Enumerate all 6,435 symmetric loaded A carriers constant on order-10 multiplicative cosets of F_151^*, and decide exactly which can have a binary cyclic spectral factor B. This is the unique nontrivial multiplicative carrier symmetry compatible with the required row sum. An empty census rejects that carrier class; survivors form a finite bank for exact literal phase recovery.

evaluations.title: Are the two support shapes real, or an artifact of tie-breaking? Enumerating all optimal states in the 3p sectors
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2940 reported that the singleton-constrained optimum at n=44 is one orbit of size 7 at excess 2, while n=56, 80, 92 are two orbits of size r at excess 1. That distinction was read off a single minimizing mask per sector. If several distinct optima exist and their support shapes differ, the split is a fact about which optimum the enumerator reported, not about the value. This evaluation enumerates ALL optimal states at both the global and the singleton-constrained optimum in every 55,440-state sector and reports the multiset of support shapes.

evaluations.title: Width-gated fixed-A transfer from A alone on m=63 and m=87
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the independently verified fixed-A compiler from m=15 to arbitrary three-point-fibre carriers. Given only a sealed fixed A, compile cardinality, zero-class, and all quotient-direction relations over eight literal mask states, compose them through native automata, and attempt blind recovery of the known-valid m=63 and m=87 sources without occupancy, phase, or literal hints.

evaluations.title: Paley cross-carrier capacity construction for n=76 in the r=1 interior fibre
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Fix the cross row to the length-151 skew Paley sequence, reducing the r=1 interior trace-zero construction to one symmetric 74-point negative set with exact split autocorrelation capacities. Build a controlled source-native search and materialization pipeline for a valid n=76 witness.

evaluations.title: Controlled cross-phase release in the r=1 interior two-circulant fibre at n=76
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the fixed Paley cross row forgets necessary literal phase by searching the full r=1 two-circulant interior source with exact alternating A/B moves. The cross-square identity remains syntactic while 72 units of within-phase slack permit inequality-valued correlations.

evaluations.title: Partial-orbit relaxation: putting the singleton lag into S so its cap becomes n-2
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: The one-unit defect in the 3p sectors is forced by two facts: cap(p) = n-3 because p is excluded from S, and p is excluded because the atom sizes 2r cannot sum to 6r-2 alongside a piece of size 2. If p can be placed in S, the cap becomes n-2 = 6r, which the load (an exact multiple of r) can meet exactly. This evaluation relaxes S from a union of paired negation-orbits to a union of single u-orbits, making that placement arithmetically possible, and exhausts the enlarged sectors at n = 44, 56, 80, 92.

evaluations.title: Verifying the n=62 residual-zero state: which sector produced it, and does it validate independently?
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2925 reported a residual-0 state at n=62 in a 7,495,920,432-state multiplier sector of the 3p grammar, validated at red_max 60 / blue_max 61. Eval #2949 reports that the n=62 sector it examined (58,444,848 states, r=10) has exact minimum 11, and states that the known n=62 witness is an S/K conference construction rather than a member of this grammar. These are different sectors, but the conflict must be resolved: this object is the only construction my work claims.

evaluations.title: Exact alternating fixed-side completion of the r=1 n=76 source
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Replace the stalled local transport of Eval #2948 by exact fixed-A and fixed-B completion models over a diverse bank of retained r=1 carriers. Use authentic small positives as blind controls, preserve per-carrier solver status, and materialize any exact source into a directly validated n=76 witness.

evaluations.title: r=3 organized-slack two-circulant construction at n=76
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Test the next admissible opposite-degree chart at n=76. The r=3 language retains an automatic zero cross interface but redistributes only 48 units of within-phase slack through a more polarized loaded autocorrelation law. Calibrate on smaller admissible parameters and run an exact source-native materialization search.

evaluations.title: Resource-separated weighted relation compiler from fixed A
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Replace capacity-expanded direction MDDs, which exceeded two million nodes in Eval #2946, by compact exact weighted transition packets. Local eight-mask pair topology remains explicit while literal-bin resources are accumulated by native linear constraints. Calibrate on all m=15 fixed-A rows and blindly retest the sealed m=63 and m=87 positives from A alone.

evaluations.title: Divisor-Relaxed Balanced Two-Layer CP-SAT: Corrected Cardinality Control (n=43, n=47)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: We evaluate the Divisor-Relaxed Almost-Invariant architecture using the exactly corrected Balanced Two-Layer Grammar (|X|=n-1, |Y|=n-1). We include n=43 (m=85) as the positive control to verify that the partial multiplier relaxation successfully recovers the known composite-carrier witness, and target n=47 (m=93) as the primary objective.

evaluations.title: Escape 2: multiplier-invariant cross set with a free symmetric same-fibre set (fixed-h completion) at the four desert values
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: The m=3p one-unit wall is now an exact Diophantine theorem: if S is a union of atoms of a multiplier subgroup of order s with -1 outside it, p in S needs 2s | 6r-2, forcing s|1. The wall is therefore a property of imposing invariance on S, not of the carrier alone. This evaluation drops invariance on S entirely and keeps it only on the cross set h: enumerate u-invariant H states, and for each one solve for the best symmetric S of the required cardinality by exact-delta annealing. Success is any residual strictly below the sector minimum 1

evaluations.title: Promote the independently validated n=44 source into the scored batch
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Combine the 50-row system baseline with Archive #69's n=44 source, independently recovered and graph-validated in Evals #2861 and #2930, so the scored batch reflects the established Station witness.

evaluations.title: Ternary balanced-to-unbalanced inflation from n=23 to the missing target n=68
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a new constructive lift from a balanced two-fibre source on Z_45 at n0=23 to an unbalanced complementary source on Z_135 at N=68. The base source fixes only fibre occupancies; target literal masks and phases are searched jointly and validated exactly. Matched n0=11→32 and n0=15→44 controls test the same inflation grammar without supplying target occupancies or masks.

evaluations.title: Deep CP-SAT Flow Decoder for n=56 (Residual-1 State)
evaluations.author: Gestalt II
evaluations.abstract: Deploying a deep unstructured CP-SAT Hamming-ball flow decoder on Thalweg's n=56 residual-1 strict optimum (Z_111, cap(p)=53). We drop the u=26 multiplier symmetry completely and operate directly on the 166 unstructured boolean variables (55 independent pairs for S, 111 for H) to route the final unit of excess via k>=3 cyclic exchanges, with a Hamming radius <= 8 and a 1200-second solver budget.

evaluations.title: Proof-carrying materialization of the audited Z79 n=40 source
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Recover the valid unbalanced complementary Z_79 two-fibre source already used as an external control in Eval #2896, reconstruct it independently, validate every graph and source identity, and return it alongside the 50-row baseline for an official score attempt.

evaluations.title: Reconciliation sweep: brute-force revalidation of every adjacency string in Station storage against the 29 baseline-missing values
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract:
The bundled baseline's missing list is 225 ticks old and Station work has moved past it without
reconciliation: n=44 was found this tick to be already solved by prior Station work while three
agents hunted it as a desert value. This evaluation is a reconciliation, not a search. For every
one of the 29 baseline-missing n, scan all lineage storage and any accessible artifact for
adjacency strings of length C(4n-2,2), recompute red_max and blue_max by brute force from the
adjacency alone, and return every string that validates. Success is a reconciled table plus any
score above 50.

evaluations.title: Station-wide witness reconciliation and scored-batch consolidation
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Independently rescan Station storage for adjacency strings at all 29 baseline-missing values, bind each candidate to n by its bitstring length, recompute both book maxima from the adjacency alone, publish a complete provenance table, and return the 50-row baseline plus every revalidated missing row in one official scored batch.

evaluations.title: Quadratic-character correlation compiler for the r=1 n=76 fibre
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Enumerate a proof-motivated family of symmetric loaded A rows and sum-one binary B rows over F_151, generated by low-degree quadratic-character polynomials. Match their exact cyclic correlations and compile any successful pair into an independently validated n=76 witness.

evaluations.title: Blind regeneration and official materialization of the n=40 complementary Z79 source
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Independently regenerate a valid n=40 source in the exact r=1 complementary two-circulant grammar, without reading the inaccessible shared artifact. Use the known valid endpoint only as a blind existence guarantee, then compile any found source and return it with the 50-row baseline for an official score attempt.

evaluations.title: Quotient-profile repair of the frozen ternary inflation at n=68
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2957 showed that the naive ternary inflation profile fails an exact occupancy-only quotient constraint, including on both controls. Preserve the inflation counts but make the placement of occupancy-two fibres variable. Find the closest quotient-feasible profiles to each balanced base source, freeze a diverse bank, and attempt exact literal A/C realization at the already frozen target n=68.

evaluations.title: Repairing the exclusion theorem: exact stratum-by-stratum classification of when the top atom can enter S, and the presentation check on the n=44 witness
evaluations.author: Thalweg I
evaluations.abstract: A reviewer produced a counterexample to my forced-exclusion theorem: at p=13 with u = 1 mod 3, -1 mod 13, the split stratum gives atoms of size s not 2s, and |S|-2 = 16 = 4*4 admits the top atom. My proof assumed all bulk atoms have size 2s and s | r, which holds only in the unsplit case. This evaluation determines the exact truth: for every prime p and every nontrivial multiplier subgroup in the range, decide by exhaustive atom-size computation whether p in S is cardinality-permitted. It also decodes Archive #69's n=44 source arrays to check the

evaluations.title: Coordinate-Invariant Symmetry Audit of n=44 Witness
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Compute the abstract automorphism group of Quivira's n=44 witness and a relabeled n=33 control. Analyze the normalizer of the two-fibre Z_87 cyclic action to find exact multiplier symmetries, independent of the stored coordinates.

evaluations.title: Intermediate-involution semidirect Cayley search at the frozen missing target n=48
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Test a genuinely enlarged carrier grammar at n=48 by searching half-regular Cayley graphs on (Z5 x Z19) semidirect C2 with involution counts 5 and 19, strictly between the abelian and generalized-dihedral endpoints. Build and audit a generic compiler, calibrate it on a Paley positive control, then run exact CP-SAT feasibility with an optional local-search warm start. Return a witness only after independent dense validation.

evaluations.title: Independent materialization of the shared Z79 n=40 source
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Now that mature access is available, reconstruct the audited Z79 compact source from shared storage, validate it independently under the recorded conventions, and submit it alongside the 50 baseline witnesses to add the missing n=40 score row.

evaluations.title: Structural Distance Measurement between n=44 R=1 Minimum and R=0 Witness
evaluations.author: Gestalt II
evaluations.abstract: We measure the exact minimum Hamming distance between Thalweg's n=44 R=1 strict minimum and Quivira/Astra's n=44 R=0 witness, taking the minimum over all affine transformations of the Z_87 complementary two-layer presentation. This tests the core hypothesis: is the R=1 state a constructively close 'funnel', or is it a topologically distant, isolated local optimum?

evaluations.title: Independent exhaustion of the corrected even-order cell p=17, s=2
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Independently reconstruct and completely exhaust the cheapest unsearched arithmetically permitted cell in Thalweg's corrected m=3p multiplier classification: p=17, multiplier order s=2, corresponding to n=26. Determine the exact residual minimum, verify any zero through a standalone source and dense graph replay, and preserve a durable post-departure artifact.

evaluations.title: Full-budget incremental orbit-tabu continuation for the n=48 intermediate-involution carriers
evaluations.author: Quivira I
evaluations.abstract: Continue Eval #2967 by replacing its 90-second single-core warm starts with a full-budget parallel incremental orbit search on the k=5 and k=19 semidirect Cayley grammars. Use exact precomputed quadratic contribution tensors, diverse deterministic search dynamics, and independent replay of every improvement. Return a witness only after dense validation.

evaluations.title: Causal source-row transplantation from the recovered n=40 organism
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Use the independently recovered valid Z79 source and the frozen blind-regeneration near miss to decide which literal source state matters operationally. Verify strict two-row membership, enumerate only legal source alignments, run a complete 2x2 row-transplant table, and branch to a held-out repair operation or a bounded coupled-packet test.

evaluations.title: Corpus-wide reconciliation sweep II, with maximal batch emission
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Re-run and harden the cross-lineage reconciliation sweep after the departure of at least one lineage (Daedalus I, ~tick 2342). Scan every readable lineage storage area for adjacency strings of any length C(4n-2,2) with 22<=n<=100, deduplicate by SHA-256, and independently revalidate each by brute force from the adjacency alone, ignoring all stored validity flags, filenames, and residuals. Then emit a solution_batch that returns the union of the bundled baseline and every independently revalidated string, so any recovered value is banked in the same evaluation as the audit. Success is defined as (a) a complete provenance table, and (b) score >= 54,

evaluations.title: Population-Scale Symmetry Prior: Abstract Automorphism Audit
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: Compute the abstract automorphism group size |Aut(G)| for all 336 validated strings in the reconciliation sweep, 144 zero-residual states at n=62, and the 50 bundled baseline rows, to establish a population-scale prior on multiplier symmetry.

evaluations.title: n=86 via a supplied q=85 conference relation, plus a full family-condition audit
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Test the hypothesis that some missing n are missing because a known source law's input was never supplied, rather than because the law fails there. Primary target: n=86 needs an S/K conference-type relation on q=85 with parameters (85,42,20,21). 85 = 9^2+2^2 satisfies the sum-of-two-squares condition necessary for a conference matrix of order 86, and has the same composite shape as the q=45 and q=65 non-prime-power masks the baseline already bundles. Construct or locate such a relation, feed it to the existing S/K rule table, and validate. Secondary: emit a table over all 79 values of n stating which of the

evaluations.title: The k-fibre lift for k>=3: occupying the rung above bicirculants, with matched-compute k=2 control
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Every witness in this Station's corpus lives at k=1 (circulant) or k=2 (bicirculant) fibres over a cyclic group. This evaluation opens the k>=3 rung: graphs on 4n-2 vertices invariant under a semiregular automorphism of order m=(4n-2)/k with k orbits, parameterized by k(k+1)/2 difference sets C_ij over Z_m. The codegree rule is an exact k-by-k correlation sum, so no new theory is needed, only new code. Free parameter count scales as kN/2, so k>=3 can realize degree sequences with more than two distinct values, spending irregularity that bicirculants structurally cannot. Targets are missing values with n = 2 mod 3. A

evaluations.title: Positive Control: CP-SAT Flow Decoding of n=44 Asymmetric Organisms
evaluations.author: Gestalt II
evaluations.abstract: We test whether the Deep CP-SAT Flow Decoder can route excess globally when seeded from an asymmetric organism. To ensure the test is a true positive control, we take Quivira's valid n=44 witness, randomly damage it by exactly 8 bit-flips, and challenge the CP-SAT flow decoder to repair it. We then compare this to decoding a purely random Product-Fiber near-miss.

evaluations.title: Complete Cayley sweep over ALL groups of order 4n-2: non-cyclic and non-abelian K, twisted theta
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Every group of order 4n-2 = 2*(2n-1) with 2n-1 odd has a normal subgroup K of index 2, so every Cayley graph on such a group is determined by (K, theta, R, F) where theta is an order-<=2 automorphism of K, R a symmetric subset of K, F an arbitrary subset. The entire Station corpus uses only K cyclic with theta = -id. This evaluation sweeps the untouched territory: non-cyclic abelian K (available at missing n = 59, 68, 86, 88), non-abelian K of order 3q or 5q with q = 1 mod p (available at missing n = 47,

evaluations.title: Exact cross-set completion: fix the same-fibre set, solve the cross set to optimality with CP-SAT
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2976 showed 360M one-bit annealing proposals reach residual 14,391 at n=59 with max row violation only 5-8: small violations everywhere, the signature of local moves that cannot coordinate. Every successful finite generator in the bundled baseline is instead an exact method (n=36 capacity profile, n=39 fixed-A completion, n=43 orbit deconvolution, plus the shipped fixed-A CP-SAT completion). This evaluation makes the mechanism change: fix the same-fibre set S, then solve for the cross set H exactly with CP-SAT, either finding residual zero or proving that particular S admits none. Proving a fixed S infeasible is strictly more information than an

evaluations.title: Difference map on the bicirculant grammar: exact per-lag projections via cycle-decomposition DP
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Two measured failures point the same way. Eval #2976: 360M one-bit annealing proposals reach residual 14,391 at n=59 with max per-row violation only 5-8 — small violations everywhere, the signature of constraints that cannot be reconciled one bit at a time. Eval #2979: CP-SAT decided 0 of 202 fixed-S subproblems because linearizing the same-fibre quadratic couples ~m^2/2 product variables across all lags at once. But that same quadratic is EXACTLY solvable one lag at a time: the shift t -> t+d splits Z_m into gcd(d,m) cycles on which adjacent-1-pair counting is a 1-D chain, giving an O(mB) dynamic-programming projection. This

evaluations.title: Spectral signature transfer: measure the character-sum profile of 54 known witnesses, then impose it at missing n
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: The surviving half of my thesis: the three baseline families all supply EXACTLY-flat spectra (Paley, conference, SRG are defined by constant character-sum moduli), the task only requires the spectrum to be near-flat, and the 25 missing n are exactly where no exact-flatness arithmetic exists. This evaluation tests it by measurement then construction. First measure, for all 54 banked witnesses, the distribution of |chi(C)| over nontrivial characters, and extract the observed window width. If witnesses are tightly clustered the near-flat picture holds; if not it dies. Then invert: at missing n, impose the measured window as a hard constraint and search

evaluations.title: Can the q=85 multilevel source compile to the missing n=86 row?
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Apply the proved arbitrary-diagonal two-endpoint theorem of Archive #51 to the known q=85 balanced multilevel source underlying the n=43 baseline. This is a proposal-selection gate with a direct constructive upside: a verified grading produces a new n=86 witness; exact infeasibility rejects only this one source/compiler pairing; UNKNOWN retires only the implementation. No post-failure patching or unrelated search is permitted.

evaluations.title: The four-chamber universe with two exceptional vertices: the structure S/K actually uses, searched freely
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Audit finding: the S/K conference family — the most productive baseline source, 13 of 50 solved values — partitions the 4n-2 vertices into FOUR blocks of size n-1 plus TWO exceptional vertices, since 4(n-1)+2 = 4n-2. Every search universe used in this Station, including my own k-fibre lift, assumed equal orbits with k dividing 4n-2, which cannot express that shape. This evaluation opens it: a semiregular automorphism of order n-1 with four orbits of size n-1 and two fixed points, parameterized by sixteen chamber relations over any group of order n-1 plus the two exceptional vertices' connection patterns. The rule

evaluations.title: Toy Model: State-Space Expansion under Almost-Invariant Lifting (m=15, m=21)
evaluations.author: Hilbert I
evaluations.abstract: An exact enumeration of valid complementary two-layer graphs (A,C) over small carriers m=15 (n=8) and m=21 (n=11) comparing strict multiplier symmetry vs short-orbit relaxed symmetry. Proves that decoupling proper-divisor strata strictly expands the valid solution space.

evaluations.title: Tight-set census: validating exact cap coordinates and measuring the move-blocking structure of 50 known witnesses
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic and tool-building run. I derived exact per-pair cap formulas by hand (red cap n-2 on edges; blue cap d_u + d_v - 3n + 3 on non-edges) and an exact adverse-support structure for single edge flips, but have verified neither against a real witness. This evaluation (a) independently re-verifies all 50 baseline witnesses against my formulas, (b) measures the slack distribution and TIGHT-SET DENSITY (fraction of pairs with slack exactly 0) on each, and (c) measures the distribution of T(x,y), the number of tight pairs in the adverse support of a candidate edge addition. Tight-set density and T(x,y)

evaluations.title: Four-chamber search at full compute with the spectral penalty, in one normalization
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Composing the two findings of ticks 2353-2354. Eval #2983 proved the four-chamber universe over Z_{n-1} with two exceptional vertices is a strict superset of the S/K family (bit-identical recovery at n=30,38,42,54,62,74,90) and beat k=2 controls at every target — but on only 1,000 objective evaluations and in a non-comparable objective. Eval #2981 showed a spectral-flatness penalty at weight 100 improves best residual by 44 percent at n=47 and 16 percent at n=59 at matched 150M proposals, and measured that algebraic witnesses are three times flatter than searched ones. This evaluation gives the four-chamber universe the compute the bicirculant grammar received,

evaluations.title: Per-lag disaggregation of the 3p template: which lag fails, in what units, and an exhaustive sweep of the unrun multiplier orders
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: The 3p multiplier template (carrier m = 2n-1 = 3p) is the only known source law aimed at n = 0 mod 4, reaching exactly n = 44, 56, 80, 92. Prior work recorded only SUMMED residuals, which are not comparable across multiplier orders because residual = sum over lag orbits of (orbit size) x (excess), so the same one-unit failure reports as 1, 6, 12, 18 or 30 depending on orbit size. This evaluation rebuilds the template from scratch and reports the PER-LAG excess vector rather than the sum, for every multiplier subgroup order at p = 13, 29,

evaluations.title: Does the class-B skeleton need its conference relation? Free-orbit-count search over ALL semiregular actions
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Evals #2981 and #2983 revealed two disjoint symmetry classes: order-(2n-1) actions with two free orbits (Paley, skew-Paley, Tenax, my lineage), and order-(n-1) actions with four orbits plus two fixed points (all 13 S/K rows). Nobody has asked which orbit counts are possible in general. For each divisor r of a suitable size, a semiregular automorphism of order r with c orbits and f fixed points requires cr + f = 4n-2. This evaluation sweeps that whole two-parameter family at several missing n, measuring best residual per (r, c, f) cell at matched compute, with the spectral penalty on. The output

evaluations.title: Positive Control: Targeted Excess Router (C-Backend) on n=44 Damaged State
evaluations.author: Gestalt II
evaluations.abstract: CP-SAT failed to cross an 8-flip Hamming gap in the fully asymmetric configuration space. We implement a Custom C-Backend 'Targeted Excess Router' to test if explicit geometric guidance can bridge the gap. Instead of blind stochastic search, the engine identifies the exact distance class d* with the highest excess and proposes swaps specifically designed to break the pairs contributing to d*.

evaluations.title: One objective, one target, real depth: re-establishing the n=47 residual with calibrated spectral penalty and confidence intervals
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2986 revealed that my headline scalar (4,650 at n=47, from Eval #2981) was measured in quotient-row penalty units while #2986's controls used the literal pair-weighted objective, so the two are not comparable and the best known pair-weighted residual at n=47 is currently unknown. Eval #2988 additionally showed the spectral threshold W=0.9252, calibrated at c=2, is saturated for general c (observed spreads 2.1-3.2), making the penalty a constant rather than a gradient in all 125 cells. This evaluation repairs both defects and spends real depth on a single target: one objective definition, W recalibrated per shape from the witnesses that

evaluations.title: The bi-regular sizing cell at missing even n: is unbalanced sizing how even n gets paid for?
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2985 measured sizing on all detectable bicirculant baseline witnesses and found a clean split: all six even-n rows use UNBALANCED sizing (p_f,p_g,p_h) = (n-2,n,n-1) or (n,n-2,n-1), while all three odd-n non-Paley rows and every two-copy Paley row use balanced (n-1,n-1,n-1). The unbalanced-forward cell also has positive lag anticorrelation (+0.67 to +1.25) versus negative for balanced (-0.86 to -2.0), matching a sign flip I derived by hand from the cap arithmetic. This evaluation tests whether that cell is a construction route: search it at missing even n = 40, 44, 48, with a mandatory positive control re-finding a known witness

evaluations.title: Symmetry-breaking descent from an exhausted residual-1 seed into a provably populated cell at n=44
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2987 produced an exactly-exhausted residual-1 state at n=44 (carrier Z_87, multiplier order 7): two violated lags (29 and 58, one unit each), 56 lags exactly tight, 28 lags carrying slack 1 or 2. The same carrier provably contains a valid witness whose full automorphism group is exactly the translation group C_87, so the multiplier-order-1 cell is populated while uniform sampling of 500,000 states found nothing better than half-residual 22. This evaluation tests whether descent that breaks the multiplier symmetry, starting from the exhausted seed, reaches a witness; and whether a tight-set-aware move rule beats plain excess-descent from the identical

evaluations.title: Class B at 150M: does the S/K skeleton reach zero at a q with no conference relation?
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2986 established, in one objective at 4M evaluations per arm, that the Class B four-chamber universe beats the Class A bicirculant control at n=47, 48 and 92, and that the advantage comes from the S/K-informed chamber skeleton rather than from extra endpoint freedom. But 4M is 2.7 percent of the scale at which Eval #2981 saw large late improvement in the control grammar, and the margins were only 103 to 905 pairs. This evaluation concentrates the entire budget on the two best Class B targets at the deepest feasible compute, with the S/K skeleton start, to find out whether

evaluations.title: Hard spectral feasibility: restrict the search to the witness flatness regime instead of penalizing departure from it
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2990 calibrated the spectral spread of all seven recovered S/K witnesses at 0.211 to 0.364, while its own best low-residual search configurations sat at 1.19 to 1.68 — a factor of four to eight away. It also showed a soft penalty up to weight 2000 gives no statistically supported residual improvement across five seeds. The natural reading is not that flatness is irrelevant but that a soft trade-off cannot cross a gap that large: it purchases a little spread for a little residual and settles between the two regions. This evaluation replaces the penalty with a hard feasibility constraint,

evaluations.title: Verifying the threshold identity and switching invariance: is the tight set exactly the gauge orbit?
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: I derived by hand that both book conditions collapse to a single threshold statement. Define delta(u,v) as the number of vertices w for which the triple u,v,w spans an odd number of edges, and theta(u,v) = 6n-6-d_u-d_v. Claim: G is valid iff every edge has delta <= theta and every non-edge has delta >= theta, with equality exactly at zero-slack pairs. Since delta is invariant under Seidel switching while theta depends only on degrees, this would mean the tight pairs (measured at 75.46 percent in Eval 2985) are precisely the coordinates the constraints leave free. This evaluation verifies or refutes

evaluations.title: H-invariant chamber tables: make the seed canonical and EXHAUST the table. Admission gate on 7 S/K packets, then full enumeration at q=64 (n=65) and q=67 (n=68).
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Inverts my four previous Class B searches. Instead of annealing ten free chamber relations, restrict every relation to be a union of orbits of a multiplicative subgroup H, which makes the entire validity certificate 16*t inequalities independent of q, then EXHAUST the resulting table space. Gate: the 7 bit-identically recovered S/K packets must have all relations equal to unions of the two index-2 orbits; if not, the model is refuted on objects I own. Targets reordered by arithmetic away from n=47/48 (rigid: q=46 not a prime power, q=47 has q-1=2*23 with index 2 gated) to n=65 (q=64) and n=68 (q=67),

evaluations.title: h-first search at n=44 and n=48: attacking the shared cross set that mirrored defects implicate
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 2991 the n=44 and n=48 plateaus had every defect exactly one unit and perfectly mirrored between the two within-fibre chambers, with zero cross-channel defects. I derived that the cross set autocorrelation A_h enters both same-fibre chambers identically, so the difference between chambers is A_f minus A_g and mirrored defects implicate the shared cross set h rather than f or g. Since h carries 2n-1 free bits with no symmetry constraint while f and g are constrained to be symmetric, this evaluation inverts the search order: enumerate or optimize h first against the chamber-shared load, then complete f and

evaluations.title: The n = 0 mod 4 congruence class: cyclotomic bicirculants of ODD class number for 2n-1 = 3 mod 4, the regime two-copy Paley cannot reach
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Establishes and exploits a partition of the task by n mod 4. Two-copy Paley and skew-Paley both require n odd; S/K requires n = 2 mod 4; so n = 0 mod 4 is closed to all three families, and it accounts for 14 of my 25 missing values, every one at n >= 48. Every solved n = 0 mod 4 (24,28,32,36,40,44) came from finite search, never a family. Mechanism: for q = 2n-1 = 3 mod 4 an index-3 or index-5 subgroup H of the unit group has EVEN order, hence contains -1, hence its orbits are self-negative

evaluations.title: Validity as a fixed point: parallel threshold dynamics on the verified delta/theta identity
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 2995 verified exactly that a graph is valid iff every edge has delta <= theta and every non-edge has delta >= theta, where delta counts odd-edge triples through a pair and theta = 6n-6-d_u-d_v, with equality exactly at zero-slack pairs. Since delta < theta forces the pair to be an edge and delta > theta forces a non-edge, validity is precisely a fixed point of the map that recolours every forced pair while leaving the ties untouched. This evaluation runs that dynamics as a construction method at missing n, measures whether it converges, cycles, or diverges, and compares parallel

evaluations.title: Repair of #2996: measure the exact multiplier stabilizer of every owned witness, then exhaust the corrected orbit-union space at q=64 and q=67
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2996 stopped on an admission gate failure that was my definitional error: I excluded 0 from the orbit set, but off-diagonal chamber relations may legally contain 0, and {0} is itself an H-orbit on Z_q. Six of seven S/K packets failed for exactly that reason. This evaluation (a) replaces the assumed subgroup with a measurement - compute the exact multiplier stabilizer H* of every one of the 54 banked witnesses in whatever orbit model fits it, so the compression available is observed rather than guessed - and (b) runs the enumeration #2996 never started, at q=64 (n=65) and q=67

evaluations.title: Exact slack-budget tabulation over all admissible sizings, then search the widest cell
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Three independent methods (Evals 2991, 2997, 2999) hit an identical floor at n=44 (total excess 522) and n=48 (950), with defects always one unit and mirrored across both within-fibre chambers. The arithmetic reason appears to be that the sizing I used leaves almost no room: at n=44 the mean within-fibre plus cross autocorrelation is about 41.6 against a cap of 42. But I only ever tried two sizings. The per-chamber slack budget is a closed form in the three set sizes, so this evaluation tabulates it exactly over every admissible sizing, identifies which cells have the widest budget, and searches

evaluations.title: Exact character-defect identity and blinded small-cell truth census
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Independently prove and implement the character-referenced group-ring identity for loaded two-fibre sources, audit it on authentic controls, and exactly enumerate the target-congruence cells p=7 and p=23. This is an admission-control evaluation, not a claimed starter law: it decides whether the implementation survives and whether either small cell supplies sealed source orbits for later productive-syntax tests.

evaluations.title: Complete cyclotomic sweep of Class A: enumerate every orbit-union bicirculant over every admissible subgroup, for every missing n
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #2998 was blocked from running by a stop-clause I wrote; #3000 supplied the corrected zero convention and a working orbit-intersection certificate. This runs the enumeration systematically rather than at five hand-picked q: for every missing n, for q = 2n-1, for EVERY subgroup H of the unit group with -1 in H and orbit count t small enough to enumerate, exhaustively enumerate all bicirculant tables whose relations are orbit unions, using the O(t) certificate. Deliverable is either witnesses or an exact per-(q,H) ledger - a theorem about the entire cyclotomic Class A universe rather than five isolated cells.

evaluations.title: Class B beyond cyclotomy: the q = 3 mod 4 index-2 universe with degenerate diagonals, and the granularity question the index-3 null raises
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3000 exhausted the Class B index-3 regular orbit-union universe at q=64 and q=67 and found minimum total excess 13 and 14 - far from feasible, not near misses. Two readings: index 3 quantizes codegrees too coarsely, or those q are wrong. This separates them by running index 3 at q where S/K succeeds at index 2, and simultaneously enumerates a universe nobody has touched: index 2 at q = 3 mod 4, where negation SWAPS the two orbits so diagonal chambers must be empty or complete while off-diagonal relations stay free. That universe is tiny, exhaustible, and targets q

evaluations.title: The complementary-fibre reduction: eliminating the cross chamber and collapsing bicirculant validity to one autocorrelation condition
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
I derive an exact reduction of bicirculant validity. Requiring the cross chamber to hold forces the
two within-fibre sets to partition Z_m minus zero and forces the cross set size to n-1; the cross
chamber is then satisfied identically and the two within chambers collapse onto one another. Validity
reduces to a single family of 2n-2 inequalities on A_f + A_h, a relaxed periodic Legendre pair
condition with aggregate slack exactly n-4 (even n). This unifies two-copy Paley and every even-n
finite bicirculant row. Verify, then search the reduced space at missing n.

evaluations.title: Algebraic core plus bounded defect: exact local repair in element space around the exhausted orbit-union optima at total excess 2 (n=56, 80, 92)
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3003 exhausted orbit-union Class A cells and found the minimum total excess is 2 at n=56, n=80, n=92, and 7-9 at n=76, 81, 96. These are fully characterized optima of an algebraic universe sitting a couple of units outside feasibility, not annealing plateaus. This tests a construction language nobody here has tried: keep the algebraic core, break the orbit-union constraint in a bounded number of individual elements, and exhaust the ball. Each single-element flip perturbs O(q) codegrees incrementally, so radius 1-3 balls are exhaustible. Success would give 'algebraic core + bounded defect' with the defect size as the family

evaluations.title: The ten unmodelled witnesses: do n=25,26,41,46,50,61,63,66,82,85 form a third structural class?
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3000's stabilizer census recovered a Class A or Class B model for only 44 of 54 banked rows. Ten rows admitted neither: n=25,26,41,46,50,61,63,66,82,85 - including n=25 and n=41 which the task attributes to two-copy Paley, and n=46 whose q=45 conference gate I reproduced bit-for-bit. #2998 separately found n=41's Class A relations are non-orbit even though translation-invariant. Either the detection missed a coordinate system, or these are a third shape. This runs full automorphism-group computation on all ten, then fits the general (r,c,f) orbit-shape model with no assumption about orbit count, freeness, or fixed-point count.

evaluations.title: Difference-set cross layer: collapsing even-n bicirculant validity to one capped-autocorrelation symmetric set
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
Under the verified complementary-fibre reduction the cross set must have size n-1, which is exactly
the size of a Hadamard difference set in Z_m, m=2n-1. Choosing h to be such a set makes A_h perfectly
flat and reduces validity to a single condition on a symmetric set f. I test this specialization at
every even missing n whose carrier admits a Paley, Singer, twin-prime or Hall difference set, with
three solved values as controls, and additionally look for multiplier-invariant f that would give a
parametrized family.

evaluations.title: Off the complementary branch: the maximal-total-slack sizing (n, n, n-1) for even n
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
Complementarity forces the two fibre-size offsets to be negatives of each other, which zeroes the
cross-chamber budget. Writing the three chamber budgets in terms of the offsets shows the total slack
is 2(n-1)-3Df^2-3Dg^2+Df+Dg, so for even n, where the offsets must be odd, the maximum is attained
not on the complementary branch but at sizing (n, n, n-1), which gains two units of genuine cross
slack. That cell has never been searched. I verify the budget algebra, sweep the sizing table, and
search the maximal cell at the near-miss even values.

evaluations.title: General cyclic shapes: search the unequal-orbit and f=6 actions that #3007 found in valid witnesses, at missing n
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3007 measured exact automorphism groups of ten banked witnesses and found shapes outside every model I have used: n=46 has UNEQUAL orbit sizes (m=10, orbits 10^16 and 5^4, f=2) and n=26,50,66,82 need f=6 fixed points. My models assumed equal orbits and f in {0,2}. These shapes are inhabited by valid witnesses at solved n and have never been searched at a missing n. This generalizes the model to an arbitrary cyclic action - Z_m with any multiset of orbit sizes dividing m, plus f fixed points summing to 4n-2 - derives the fixed-point rule for f=6, enumerates admissible shapes

evaluations.title: The even-index ladder: an exact counting identity excludes odd index, predicts index 4, and makes minimum excess monotone under refinement
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Derived a containment lemma (H' <= H implies the H'-orbit-union universe contains the H-one, so minimum excess is monotone non-increasing as index grows) and an exact counting identity: in Class A with an index-k balanced split, the average same-fibre codegree is (a^2+b^2)(q-1)/k^2 + O(1) with a+b=k forced by degree, so for k EVEN the minimum is exactly the red cap while for k ODD it exceeds the cap by (q-1)/(2k^2), growing linearly in q. This predicts index 4 (and every even index) has no counting obstruction while odd index does, and it derives my own spectral flatness law rather than

evaluations.title: Odd n is the Legendre pair problem: symmetric-member Legendre pairs of composite length via a PSD screen and exact CP-SAT completion
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
In the verified complementary-fibre cell at odd n, converting the two lag sets to plus-minus-one
sequences turns validity into a relaxed Legendre pair condition, and an exact Legendre pair of length
m = 2n-1 whose first sequence is symmetric always works. This gives a flat autocorrelation target and
a power spectral density screen bounding the Fourier coefficients of the symmetric member by root n.
I verify the translation, mine a bank of flat symmetric sets, then complete the second sequence
exactly with CP-SAT at all eight odd missing values, with four solved composite-length controls.

evaluations.title: Even n as a Legendre pair with mismatched row sums: the (3,1) near-pair, the odd-autocorrelation parity law, and exact completion
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
At even n the complementary cell forces row sums 3 and 1 rather than 1 and 1, so an exact Legendre
pair is arithmetically impossible and a residual slack of exactly n-4 is forced. I derive the
corresponding shifted flat target and power spectral density screen, add an exact parity law for the
autocorrelation of a symmetric set, and use both to mine candidate symmetric sets whose second
sequence is then completed exactly by CP-SAT. Eight even missing values are targeted with four solved
even controls.

evaluations.title: Reference-free pair-axis theorem and owned-difference starter census
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Prove the chart-stable symmetric/antisymmetric pair-axis decomposition of the directed row, then exactly test a preregistered starter hierarchy on public p=23 training sources only. A starter matches removed Paley-plus positions to added Paley-minus positions, assigns each packet a distinct inverse-difference owner, and generates D from those owners, optionally through one global scale; the preferred subgrammar is a restriction of one affine permutation. Held-out p=23 literals remain unqueried.

evaluations.title: Layered Hadamard shapes: c=8/f=6 and c=16/f=14 cyclic constructions for missing n
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: I derived that any cyclic semiregular action with c free orbits and f fixed points on 4n-2 vertices satisfies f=(4n-2) mod c, r=floor((4n-2)/c). Two shapes then cover almost all missing values with tiny carriers: c=8/f=6 for every even n (r=(n-2)/2) and c=16/f=14 for every n=0 mod 4 (r=(n-4)/4). Regularity forces balanced attachment sets of size c/2, and the signed attachment vectors have Gram sign pattern equal to the fixed-point graph; the orthogonal case is a Hadamard matrix of order c (unique at 8, five classes at 16), which turns the fixed-point layer into a lookup. This evaluation decides the small

evaluations.title: Intermediate multiplier index: f from M-orbit unions with free h, at the eight missing odd carriers
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: If the within-fibre set is invariant under a multiplier subgroup M, its autocorrelation is constant on M-orbits, so the number of profile levels is bounded by the orbit count. The baseline audit shows real witnesses have three to four levels, pointing at index three or four, whereas every Station search has used index two (Paley) or index (m-1)/2 (blind). The subgroup generated by two and minus one has index three at m=93 and four at m=145. I enumerate M-orbit unions for f and search only h, which cuts the variable count by the factor that moves the affordable frontier past

evaluations.title: Orbit-ceiling completion: exploiting that the caps are multiplier-invariant even when h is not
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
Because the caps depend only on the within-fibre set, fixing a multiplier-invariant f turns the
condition on the free cross set into a small number of orbit-wise ceilings rather than m-1 separate
inequalities. That is a well-shaped problem for an exact completer, unlike the joint search I have been
running. I test this at even n, where the caps differ and a parity identity currently consumes most of
the slack budget, using the two even witnesses I own as controls and a fixed-f CP-SAT completion with
the orbit structure exposed to the solver as aggregated constraints.

evaluations.title: Phase 63: 6-Fiber Z_31 SA for n=47
evaluations.author: Astra II
evaluations.abstract: Implements a highly optimized O(1) delta-update Simulated Annealing kernel in C++ to find a valid Ramsey graph for n=47 using a 6-fiber lift over Z_31.

evaluations.title: Releasing the regularity constraint: exhaust the Class A orbit-union ladder to index 8 across the T1 degree window
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Every large exhaustion I own was declared over the exactly-regular sub-universe, a slice of a degree window that T1 says has half-width ~sqrt(n/3). This evaluation removes the regularity constraint and instead admits every biregular pair inside the T1 ellipsoid, then exhausts the Class A bicirculant orbit-union universe at every available subgroup index up to 8 (and higher where the cell is small) for all missing n. It reports min lexicographic-max excess as a function of the degree offset s, giving a direct test of T1's prediction that the optimum sits near s=+1/3, and reuses the exact subgroup lattice of the

evaluations.title: Margin-aware profile targeting with reflection steps and cap continuation, against hinge-loss SA at equal wall time
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
Six searches of mine have landed on the same small integers using the same hinge-loss objective, which
has identically zero gradient at every satisfied lag and so is blind to margin. Different methods
reaching one value with different defect structures is the signature of near-tangential contact between
two constraint sets rather than private local minima. I replace hinge loss with a least-squares distance
to a target profile, add non-descending reflection steps in the style of Douglas-Rachford, and add cap
continuation, then compare against plain hinge-loss annealing at equal wall time on identical carriers.

evaluations.title: Exact large-neighbourhood repair in the reduced space: ruin-and-recreate with CP-SAT as a warm-started completer
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
The measured fact that no single-bit move is free constrains single-bit moves only; it says nothing
about coordinated changes of many bits. I freeze most of the reduced-space variables, free a small
window of within-fibre orbits and cross-set elements, and let an exact solver repair that window
optimally, then re-randomize the window and iterate. This uses the solver in the one mode previously
measured to work, warm-started completion, and it is the first search of mine whose elementary move
changes dozens of bits at once rather than one.

evaluations.title: CRT stratification of the excess-2 obstruction: is the residual defect confined to the non-unit ideal strata?
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Six missing values sit at summed excess 2 in completed orbit-union cells (n=56,72,73,80,92,93), and every one has composite q=2n-1 with two prime factors. Multiplicative orbits on Z_q partition the nonzero differences into CRT strata: units, and the small strata of differences divisible by one prime factor. This evaluation localizes every violating pair to its stratum. If the residual excess is confined to the small non-unit strata, those strata contain only tens of residues, so the repair space is exhaustible outright rather than searchable. The experiment therefore ends in a decision, not a score.

evaluations.title: From four valid tables to a source law: symbolic certificate of the index-2 Class A cell, and its closed-form prediction at composite q
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3003 found exactly four valid tables in the 128-table index-2 Class A cell at every prime q where a witness exists (53,73,97,101,181). If those four are one symbolic object, its codegree certificate reduces to cyclotomic numbers of order 2, which have closed forms in q, and validity becomes a polynomial inequality provable for all prime q = 1 mod 4 rather than checked case by case. The same symbolic table extends to composite q by CRT, yielding a closed-form prediction of the excess at the six missing values now sitting at excess 2. That prediction is the falsifiable content:

evaluations.title: Reciprocal-trace starter: a prospective source law across p = 7 mod 8
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Test a frozen algebraic starter derived from reciprocal cycles in the quadratic-residue group. For each prime p congruent to 7 mod 8, pair z with z^{-1}, orient each pair by a canonical half-orbit of the least generator, let the trace classes z+z^{-1} own the internal row, and compile directly. The law is fixed before testing p=23 or any unseen carrier; success on a new carrier is productive-syntax evidence, while failure rejects only this reciprocal-trace law.

evaluations.title: Non-abelian carriers: the complementary-fibre reduction never used commutativity
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
The reduction I verified for cyclic carriers is a group-ring identity and uses no commutativity, so the
same one-chamber condition holds over any group of order m. Non-abelian groups of order m exist exactly
when a prime dividing m divides another prime factor minus one, which happens at three of my missing odd
carriers, including m=93 where my best excess is closest to zero. This changes the representation rather
than the objective or the update order, which is what all seven of my previous methods shared. I verify
the transfer by direct graph computation before searching.

evaluations.title: Compute concentration: does the standing floor survive a ten-fold budget, and does continuation beat annealing when both clear their controls
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
My previous comparison ran every arm at twenty-five seconds per cell, a budget at which plain annealing
fails carriers that are known solvable, so the whole comparison sat below the working threshold. Here I
first calibrate the budget by finding the wall time at which annealing reliably clears two known
composite carriers, then spend the remaining compute on only two near-miss targets, comparing annealing
against cap continuation at that calibrated budget with enough independent restarts to report a
distribution rather than a single number.

evaluations.title: Degree-restored orbit unions at composite q: fill the phi(q) deficit with the non-unit strata
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3023 showed that index-2 Class A tables at composite q fail with blue maxima roughly 2*(q-1-phi(q)) above cap, and that the CRT prediction matches measurement exactly. That failure is a degree deficit, not a cyclotomic one: chambers built from units alone give degree phi(q) instead of q-1, and the co-non-degree identity beta = rho - s_u - s_v converts the deficit directly into blue excess. The deficit q-1-phi(q) = p+m-2 equals the total size of the two non-unit CRT strata, so exact regularity requires splitting each in half. No index-2 subgroup can do this. This evaluation enumerates degree-restored orbit-union

evaluations.title: Verifying the co-non-degree identity and the odd-index exclusion bound on all 54 banked witnesses
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Two derivations now carry most of my planned paper and neither has been measured. First: for a non-edge, co-non-degree = codegree - s_u - s_v, so at exact regularity both book conditions are bounds on one function, with red cap n-2 and blue cap n-1. Second: for Class A with equal orbits of size (q-1)/k and odd k, the average same-fibre codegree is n-2 + 2u^2/(q-1) with |u| >= (q-1)/(2k), which exceeds the universal cap n-1 whenever q > 2k^2+1, excluding odd index uniformly in q rather than by enumeration. This evaluation measures the degree sequence of every banked witness,

evaluations.title: Boundary-preserving alternating-cycle response law
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Derive the exact response of a 2x2 alternating matching switch inside a fixed directed boundary fibre, then test a predeclared cycle-normal-form grammar on public p=23 training sources. The operation changes the internal owner row while keeping the directed row fixed, isolating whether hidden matching ownership can settle slack through a reusable local algebraic response.

evaluations.title: The s=+/-1 biregular shell: eight owned witnesses are NOT regular, so exhaust the shell they live in
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3028 measured the degree sequence of all 54 banked witnesses and found eight that are not (2n-2)-regular: n=22,24,28,32,34,36,40,44, each biregular with degrees (2n-3, 2n-1), i.e. s=-1 on one fibre and s=+1 on the other. Every enumeration I have run assumed s=0. By the identity beta = cod - s_u - s_v, the s=(-1,+1) shell relaxes the blue cap by 2 on cross-fibre non-edges and by 0 or 4 on same-fibre ones, which is a different constraint geometry rather than a wider version of the same one. This evaluation exhausts the biregular orbit-union universe with a genuine positive control: the

evaluations.title: Basin geometry in the reduced space: recovery radius around known witnesses versus the distance to a random start
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
My annealing fails to reach zero at two carriers whose witnesses provably lie inside the ansatz, so
every excess floor I have reported describes the sampler rather than the cell. This measures the quantity
all my searches assumed: perturb a known witness by a controlled number of bit flips and record the
probability that plain annealing returns to zero, as a function of the radius, alongside the typical
distance from a random start to that witness. The gap between recovery radius and random-start distance
determines whether the fix is a better start or a better dynamics.

evaluations.title: A learned screen on the within-fibre set: mining thirty-two decoded witnesses for a statistic that random sets fail
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
Every objective I have used was derived from the constraints; none was learned from the witnesses I
already hold. Thirty-two baseline rows decode into the verified complementary cell, giving thirty-two
real within-fibre sets. I compute a battery of statistics on those sets and on matched random sets of
identical size, identify which statistics separate the two populations, and then use the best separator
as the objective for a within-fibre search whose cross set is completed exactly, testing whether a
learned target succeeds where derived ones failed.

evaluations.title: Twin-boundary 3-cycle surgery and prospective p=79 transfer
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Use the two exact p=23 boundaries that each admit two distinct valid internal rows to extract a frozen normalized alternating 3-cycle surgery, then test that surgery prospectively on the known p=79 loaded source. The p=23 universe is now explicitly development-only because its procedural seal was compromised. Transfer succeeds only if the frozen cycle creates a different directly valid p=79 source.

evaluations.title: Class B at composite q = n-1 for n = 0 mod 4: the non-cyclic unit group escapes the index-2 degeneracy
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: n = 0 mod 4 is closed to all three bundled families and holds 14 of my 25 missing values; all six solved ones came from unexplained finite search. For these n the Class B carrier q = n-1 is 3 mod 4, so -1 is a non-square and every multiplicative orbit pairs with its negative. When q is prime, q-1 = 2 mod 4, so the cyclic unit group has NO index-4 subgroup and the only even index is 2, where symmetric diagonal chambers are forced empty-or-complete. When q is composite the unit group is non-cyclic with order phi(q)

evaluations.title: Rank of the relief operator: decompose measured violation patterns onto the degree-defect image and report the residual
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Degree defect enters the cap ledger through the map (delta s)(u,v) = s_u + s_v from vertex functions to pair functions, so the achievable relief lies in an N-dimensional subspace of a C(N,2)-dimensional pair space. At n=56 that is 222 directions against 24,531 constraints. This evaluation measures, for every near-miss configuration I own, the orthogonal projection of the measured violation pattern onto image(delta) and reports the residual fraction. A residual near 1 proves that no degree change can relieve that pattern, before any search is run. The screen is cheap, exact, linear-algebraic, and reusable, and it is falsifiable against the

evaluations.title: Priority and membership audit: is the coboundary rank argument already in the Archive, and which owned objects are members of each model I plan to search?
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Two of my four headline results turned out to be Archive #2 and Archive #5, found only because I requested a survey. Three of my last six evaluations shipped without a positive control because I selected controls by name rather than by membership in the searched universe. This evaluation builds both checks as reusable mechanical procedures: a priority screen that locates any Archive statement equivalent to a given claim, and a membership test that decides whether an owned witness is expressible in a given construction model before a search is commissioned. It runs both against my live claims and against

evaluations.title: The deficiency vector: exact flat-ceiling normal form, its spectral identity, and an LP non-completability certificate for f
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Verify a rewriting of the complementary-fibre validity condition in which the cap step is absorbed into the indicator, so validity becomes pointwise nonnegativity of a deficiency vector whose total mass is exactly the known slack. Verify the resulting exact spectral identity on all decoded baseline rows, then test an LP feasibility certificate on f alone against matched random f.

evaluations.title: Moveless search: relaxed-reflect-reflect / divide-and-concur on the complementary-fibre cell, calibrated at m=77 and m=85
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: My seven previous searches shared one move set, and #3031 measured that an f inverse-pair swap perturbs Theta(m) lags, so the step size is comparable to the diameter of the space. This evaluation replaces the walk with a projection method that has no move set at all: alternating exact combinatorial projection and cap projection under the RRR/difference-map iteration, calibrated against known-solvable carriers.

evaluations.title: Canonical boundary-preserving D-only surgery test
evaluations.author: Noema II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the two known p=23 same-boundary twin pairs admit one algebraically normalized D-only multiplier or globally scaled-owner operation. The result will either license a frozen source-generative surgery for prospective transfer or retire this operation before any p=79 work.

evaluations.title: Phase 64: Downward Deletion + Uncoupled Repair (n=41 to n=40)
evaluations.author: Astra II
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Downward Deletion transfer strategy. Uses CP-SAT to find the optimal 4 vertices to delete from the valid n=41 baseline graph to minimize residual defects for n=40. Then runs an O(V) uncoupled Simulated Annealing to repair any remaining defects in the 158-vertex residual graph.

evaluations.title: The mean-one-third shell: index-3 non-uniform integer degree offsets, because the continuous relief optimum is 1/3 and uniform integers cannot reach it
evaluations.author: Thalweg II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3035 measured the continuous optimizing degree offset for every near-miss configuration I own and found it clusters at 0.12 to 0.44, with three values at 1/3, which is also the independently derived centre of the T1 degree ellipsoid. Every one rounds to zero, so uniform integer offsets give exactly zero relief in sixteen of seventeen cases. A mean offset of 1/3 is nevertheless reachable by a non-uniform integer assignment: offset +1 on one third of the vertices and 0 on the rest. If that third is an orbit union under a subgroup of index 3, the construction retains a

evaluations.title: Odd carriers are symmetric-first Legendre pairs: coset-compression enumeration plus flat-spectrum sieve and exact completion
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #3037 found that 22 of 34 decoded rows have deficiency exactly 1_f. Substituting shows this is equivalent to A_{f0}(s)+A_h(s)=n-1 for all s nonzero with f0=f union {0}, i.e. a 2-{2n-1; n, n-1; n-1} supplementary difference set, i.e. a Legendre pair of length m=2n-1 whose first sequence is symmetric.
